name: Like Nastya
about: Like Nastya, born Anastasia Sergeyevna Radzinskaya, is a Russian-American YouTuber who has the 5th most-viewed and 7th most-subscribed channel in the world.

name: Roger Daltrey
about:
Roger Daltrey is an English singer, best known as co-founder and lead singer of The Who. The band have had a number of hit songs, including: "My Generation," "Won't Get Fooled Again," and "You Better You Bet." 
 
Outside of The Who, Daltrey has also had a prolific solo career. He has released ten studio albums, also with a number of hits: "Giving It All Away," "Without Your Love," "Under a Raging Moon," etc.

name: Franz Boas
about: Franz Boas was a German-born American anthropologist who is often referred to as the "Father of American Anthropology." His pioneering work in the fields of cultural anthropology, linguistics, and physical anthropology laid the foundation for the discipline in the United States.

name: William S. Burroughs
about: One of the primary figures of the Beat Generation the post-war counterculture literary movement that included Allen Ginsburg and  .

name: Jack Ruby
about: Fatally shot and assassinated  , when he was in police custody after being charged with the assassination of  , on live TV.

name: Robert Henry Lawrence
about: Robert Henry Lawrence Jr. was an American astronaut and military officer. He was the first African-American to be selected as an astronaut.

name: Valery Kubasov
about: Valery Kubasov was an Soviet cosmonaut, best known for flying two missions in the Soyuz programme: Soyuz 6 and Soyuz 19. The latter, known as Apollo-Soyuz, was the first joint crewed international space mission in which an Apollo spacecraft from the United States docked with a Soviet Soyuz capsule.

name: Ronald McNair
about: Ronald McNair was an American astronaut and physicist known for being one of the first African American astronauts and for his tragic death in the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
about: The most visible and well-known leader of the Civil Rights Movement, King was a Baptist minister who helped advance civil rights through non-violent methods based on his Christian beliefs.

name: John B. Gurdon
about: John Gurdon is a British developmental biologist best known for his research in nuclear transplantation and cloning. In 2012, he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with   "for the discovery that mature cells can be reprogrammed to become pluripotent."

name: Saddam Hussein
about: A member of the Ba'ath political party, he was instrumental in its rise to power in Iraq in 1968. Throughout the 1970s he consolidated his power in the country, before formally taking over in 1979. His policies espoused a mixture of Arab nationalism and socialism.

name: Robert De Niro
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: American actor, known for many roles including the young Vito Corleone in " ", a role for which he won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. He is also highly regarded for his role in the 1990 crime film "Goodfellas".

name: Bob Packwood
about: Bob Packwood was an Oregon politician who served as a United States Senator from 1969 to 1995. A member of the Republican Party, he was first elected to the Senate in 1968 and served five consecutive terms.

name: Liz Claiborne
about: Liz Claiborne was an American fashion designer and businesswoman. She was a pioneer in the fashion industry, becoming the first woman to found and lead a Fortune 500 company.

name: Fred Rogers
about: Fred Rogers, commonly known as Mister Rogers, was an iconic American television personality. He became a widely beloved figure through his children's show, Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, which aired from 1968 to 2001.

name: Don DeLillo
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Don DeLillo is an acclaimed American author known for his vivid portrayals of American life and exploration of themes such as consumerism, technology, media, and the notion of individuality in society. DeLillo is considered one of the most influential writers in the postmodern literary movement.

name: Christopher Walken
about: Christopher Walken is known for his versatile performances and distinctive speaking style. He has appeared in over 100 films and won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

name: Malcolm McDowell
homePlace: Horsforth, West Riding of Yorkshire, England
about: Malcolm McDowell is a British actor who gained international recognition for his iconic portrayal of the sociopathic and charismatic protagonist, Alex DeLarge, in  's groundbreaking film A Clockwork Orange (1971), which was based on  's dystopian novel of the same name.

name: Margaret Smith Court
about:
The first woman during the open era to win the singles Grand Slam (all four majors in the same calendar year), she won a record 24 of those titles during her career.  
 
She also won 19 women's doubles and 21 mixed doubles titles, giving her a record 64 Major titles overall.

name: Martin Sheen
about: , Badlands

name: Bruce Crampton
about:
Bruce Crampton began playing golf at the age of eight and won his first tournament at age 11.  
 
He turned professional in 1953 and went on to win 14 PGA Tour events and was inducted into the Sports Australia Hall of Fame in 2001.

name: Carol Burnett
about: Carol Burnett is best known for creating and starring in "The Carol Burnett Show" (1967-1978), a variety program that won 23 Emmy Awards.

name: Carole King
about: Carole King began her long career in music as a songwriter, with her husband Gerry Goffin providing lyrics. Early hits included  "Chains" (for The Cookies, later recorded by the Beatles) and "The Loco-Motion" (for their babysitter "Little" Eva [Boyd]). Later in the 60s, they wrote "Take Good Care of My Baby" (for Bobby Vee); "Up on the Roof" (for the Drifters); "One Fine Day" (for the Chiffons); "Pleasant Valley Sunday" (for the Monkees); and "(You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman" (for  ).

name: Arthur Ashe
about:
Arthur Ashe was ranked number one in the world and won three Grand Slam titles. An African American, he was the first black player ever selected to the United States Davis Cup team and the only black man ever to win the singles title at Wimbledon, the US Open, and the Australian Open.  
 
He is thus considered to be one of the best tennis players from the United States in history.

name: Michael Dukakis
about:
Michael Dukakis is an American politician who served as Governor of Massachusetts first from 1975 to 1979 and then from 1983 to 1991. This makes him the longest serving governor in Massachusetts history. 
 
While Dukakis was nominated for the 1988 presidential elections by the Democratic Party, he ended up losing to  . He is known within Massachusetts for overseeing a period of economic growth since called the 'Massachusetts Miracle.'

name: Joe Namath
about: Super Bowl 1969; Super Bowl MVP 1969; Pro Bowl 1972; NY Jets

name: Václav Havel
about:
With his Civic Forum party, Havel was a major figure in the Velvet Revolution that overthrew communist rule in Czechoslovakia in 1989. Also well known for his plays, essays and memoirs. 
 
After the Czech-Slovak split in 1993, he served as the President of the Czech Republic from 1993-2003.

name: John Howard
about: John Howard is the second-longest serving Australian politician, in power 1996-2007 and leader of the Liberal Party. Howard was Prime Minister for four terms, his first administration was a coalition government with the National party in 1996. Howard's government oversaw the introduction of a goods and services tax, and a constitutional referendum on whether the country should become a republic in 1999.

name: Ethel Kennedy
about: Ethel Kennedy was an American human rights advocate and the widow of Senator  , who was assassinated in 1968. As a prominent member of the Kennedy family, she was involved in various social and political activities, as well as maintaining her late husband's legacy of public service.

name: Richard Harris
about: Best known for his role as Frank Machin in "This Sporting Life" and as King Arthur in the 1967 film "Camelot".

name: Richard Kuklinski
about:
Given the nickname "Iceman" for his method of freezing a victim to mask the time of death, he was a contract killer for Newark's DeCavalcante crime family and New York City's Five Families of the American Mafia.  
 
He claimed to have murdered from over 100 to 250 men between 1948 and 1986.

name: John Gotti
about: John Gotti was the boss of the Gambino crime family in New York City. He was known for his flamboyant style and frequent media appearances, which earned him the nicknames "The Dapper Don" and "The Teflon Don."

name: Jim Brown
about:
Best known for his exceptional and record-setting career as a running back for the Cleveland Browns.  
 
Sporting News named him the greatest professional football player ever. Brown is considered to be one of the greatest professional athletes in the history of the United States.

name: Sydney Pollack
about: Sydney Pollack was an important Hollywood filmmaker, whose fame rests on his work as both a director and producer but also as an actor and screenwriter.

name: Anthony Hopkins
about: Best known for his portrayal of Hannibal Lecter in "The Silence of the Lambs" (1991), for which he won both Oscar and BAFTA awards, and its sequel "Hannibal" (2001).

name: Tony Sheridan
about: Tony Sheridan helped shape the sound of early British rock 'n' roll and mentored a young band that would become The Beatles. Known as "The Teacher," his influence on popular music extended far beyond his own recordings.

name: Dionne Warwick
about: Dionne Warwick is an American singer, actress, and television show host. She is one of the most-charted female vocalists of all time, with over 50 of her singles making the Billboard Hot 100 between 1962 and 1998.

name: Loretta Lynn
about: Loretta Lynn was raised in poverty in rural Kentucky yet went on to become the most successful and acclaimed female country music singer-songwriter.

name: Steve Sabol
about:
Together with his father Ed, he helped develop NFL Films which allowed fans to get a closer look at the game of American football. Steve starter as a cameraman and writer, and took over as president at his father's retirement. 
 
He went on to win 35 Emmy Awards and play a part in the founding of the NFL Network.

name: Sandy Koufax
about: Koufax is considered one of the greatest pitchers in baseball history, perhaps the greatest left-hander of all-time. He pitched 12 seasons for the Brooklyn/Los Angeles Dodgers from 1955 to 1966 before arthritis in his left elbow ended his career prematurely at age 30

name: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
about: Appointed to the Supreme Court by   in August 1993, she was the 1st Jewish female justice and the second female justice.

name: Waylon Jennings
about: Waylon Jennings was an American musician who pioneered the outlaw movement in country music. He released several major albums: Lonesome, On'ry and Mean (1973), Honky Tonk Heroes (1973), Dreaming My Dreams (1974), and Are You Ready for the Country (1976).

name: Ted Kaczynski
about:
Known as the "Unabomber", he engaged in a nationwide bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995.  
 
His targets were people involved with modern technology. He killed a total of three people and injured 23 others.

name: Jerry Springer
homePlace: Highgate tube station, London, England, United Kingdom
about: Jerry Springer was a British-American television presenter, lawyer, and politician. He is best known as the host of the tabloid talk show The Jerry Springer Show, which debuted in 1991 and became known for its controversial and often sensational content.

name: Al Kaline
about: Al Kaline was an American baseball player who played his entire 22-season career with the Detroit Tigers in Major League Baseball (MLB). Known affectionately as "Mr. Tiger," his skill in the outfield was acknowledged with ten Gold Glove Awards and his constant presence at the All-Star Games, being selected 18 times.

name: Cillian Murphy
about: Cillian Murphy is an Irish actor who came to fame with his performance in the 2002 horror film "28 Days Later" and 2005 comedy-drama "Breakfast on Pluto," which earned him his first Golden Globe Award nomination.

name: Thomas A. Steitz
about: Thomas A. Steitz was an American biochemist. He is best known for his work on the ribosome, which is a part of cells that makes proteins. Steitz, along with   and Ada Yonath, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009 for this research.

name: Ian Dury
about: Ian Dury was a British singer-songwriter and actor. He is best known for his work with the band Ian Dury and the Blockheads and for hits such as "Sex & Drugs & Rock & Roll" (1977) and "Hit Me with Your Rhythm Stick" (1978).

name: Raquel Welch
about:
First won attention for her role in "Fantastic Voyage", after which she won a contract with 20th Century-Fox, but is perhaps most recognized for her role in "One Million Years B.C.".  
 
Although she had only three lines in the film, the doe-skin bikini she wore became a best-selling poster that turned her into an iconic sex symbol and catapulted her to stardom.

name: Richie Benaud
about: The first player to reach 200 wickets and 2,000 runs in Test cricket, he has been described as the most influential cricket personality since World War II.

name: Jean-Paul Belmondo
about: One of the most popular actors working in French film Belmondo's career began in the 1950s. It was  's French New Wave film "Breathless" (1960), opposite Jean Seberg, that made him a star.

name: Peter Benchley
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Peter Benchley wrote a novel about a shark that terrified millions and created a Hollywood blockbuster. His novel "Jaws" not only created the summer blockbuster but also sparked a complicated legacy that would lead him to become a passionate defender of marine life.

name: Omar Sharif
about: Omar Sharif is best known for his roles in the epic films " " (1962) and " " (1965). Sharif had a long and successful career that lasted over 50 years and included more than 100 films.

name: Brian Epstein
about: After being discharged from the army, in part due to his homosexuality, and then pursuing training as an actor, Brian Epstein joined his family's retail business, running their North End Music Store (known as NEMS).  He expanded the inventory from pianos and radios to include records, while also writing a column in 'Mersey Beat' a local music magazine.

name: Maximilian Schell
about: Maximilian Schell won an Academy Award for Best Actor for his role in "Judgment at Nuremberg" (1961). He was known for his versatile performances, often in films dealing with World War II and Nazi themes, and had a career spanning over 60 years in theater, film, and television.

name: Phil Spector
about: One of the most influential figures in music history, Spector pioneered a production technique known as "Wall of Sound", which used the recording studio as an instrument to create a dense orchestral sound.

name: Gerd Müller
about:
Scored 68 goals in 62 appearances for West Germany.  
 
Also played 453 games for Bayern Munich, scoring 398 goals.

name: Craig Breedlove
about: Craig Breedlove was an American race car driver and a five-time world land speed record holder. He gained worldwide attention in the 1960s for his daring attempts to break land speed records in jet-powered vehicles. His most famous vehicle, the Spirit of America, set multiple records at the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah.

name: Steve McQueen
about:
Called "The King of Cool", his "anti-hero" persona made him a top box-office draw of the 1960s and 1970s.  
 
Best known for "The Sand Pebbles", "The Thomas Crown Affair", "The Magnificent Seven", and "The Great Escape".

name: Billy Cannon
about: Heisman Trophy 1959, LSU; AFL Championship 1960, 1961 and 1967; AFL All-Star 1961 and 1969; Houston Oilers, Oakland Raiders

name: Fran Tarkenton
about: Fran Tarkenton is a former American football quarterback who played primarily for the Minnesota Vikings, as well as a short stint with the New York Giants. He was a nine-time Pro Bowl selection and one of the most prolific passers in league history. He led the Vikings to three Super Bowls, although they never secured a championship win.

name: Elgin Baylor
about:
Played 13 seasons as a forward in the NBA for the Minneapolis/Los Angeles Lakers, appearing in eight NBA Finals.  
 
A gifted shooter, strong rebounder, and an accomplished passer, he was renowned for his acrobatic maneuvers on the court, regularly dazzling Lakers fans with his trademark hanging jump shots.

name: Wes Craven
about: Wes Craven was an American film director, best known for his work in horror and slasher films. He created the A Nightmare on Elm Street franchise (1984-2010), which featured the classic character Freddy Krueger. Craven wrote and directed the original, which was also  's film debut.

name: Allen Toussaint
about: Allen   was an American musician, best known for his influence on the New Orleans rhythm and blues movement for several decades from the 1950s. He was regarded by those that knew of him, for he was not well known outside of the scene, as "one of popular music's great backroom figures."

name: Ernie Davis
about: Ernie Davis was an American football player, best known as the first African-American recipient of the Heisman Trophy which he won in 1961. He played college football for Syracuse University before joining the NFL.

name: Ursula K. Le Guin
homePlace: Berkeley, California, United States of America
about: Ursula K. Le Guin is a prolific science fiction and fantasy author with a career spanning from the early 1960s until she died in 2022. Le Guin is the first female author to win both the Nebula and Hugo Awards for Best Novel in 1970 with her work "The Left Hand of Darkness."

name: Michael Hill
about: Sir Michael Hill is one of New Zealand's most well-known entrepreneurs as the founder of global jewellery retailer Michael Hill Jeweller. There are currently over 300 stores in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada.

name: Bob Simpson
about: 62 Tests @ 46.81, 10 x 100s; Wisden Cricketer of the Year 1965

name: David Geffen
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA

name: Bob Turley
about: Played for the NY Yankees and 3 other teams between 1951-63.

name: Hubert Dreyfus
about: Hubert Dreyfus was an American philosopher who made significant contributions to the fields of phenomenology, existentialism, and the philosophy of artificial intelligence. He was best known for his critiques of AI, particularly for his skepticism about the ability of computers to exhibit human-like intelligence, which he outlined in his influential book, What Computers Can't Do (1972).

name: Donald Sutherland
about: One of Canada's most well known actors and a prolific performer, Donald Sutherland's career spanned over decades. Earning him a Primetime Emmy Award, an Honorary Academy Award, and two Golden Globe Awards.

name: Harry Reid
about: Reid was an American lawyer and politician, best known as senator for Nevada (1987–2017) and Senate Majority Leader (2007–2015).

name: Octavia E. Butler
about: Octavia E. Butler is a prolific science fiction and speculative fiction author who has won several awards for her works. Her first novel, "Patternmaster", was published in 1976, and her breakout novel, "Kindred", was published in 1979. Butler has published over 20 novels and works, including short story collections, essays, and non-fiction.

name: John Stamos
about: Starred in General Hospital,   and ER.

name: James May
about: James May is a British television presenter and journalist, best known as "Top Gear" co-host alongside   and   from 2002 to 2015.

name: Rob Reiner
about: Stand By Me; When Harry Met Sally; This Is Spinal Tap; The Princess Bride

name: Moses Malone
about: Moses Malone is regarded as one of the best centers in ABA / NBA history.

name: Matti Nykänen
about: Won four Olympic gold medals between the 1984 and 1988 games.

name: Roddy Piper
about: 'Rowdy' Roddy Piper was regarded as one of professional wrestling's most recognisable and influential stars.

name: Tom Kite
about: Tom Kite is known for his consistent performance on the PGA Tour and winning the 1992 U.S. Open. He is recognized as a pioneer in golf technology and training methods, and has been inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame.

name: Uri Geller
about: Uri Geller is best known for his claims of psychic abilities, particularly spoon bending. He gained international fame in the 1970s through television performances showcasing his supposed paranormal powers.

name: Moon Jae-in
about: Coming from a family of North Korean refugees, Moon studied law and then became involved in human rights activism—once even being arrested during a protest. As a result of this, he was selected to help with Roh Moo-hyun's successful 2002 presidential campaign. Roh had long been a mentor to Moon, and his presidency saw Moon serve in a variety of official roles.

name: P. J. O'Rourke
about: A regular correspondent for The Atlantic Monthly, The American Spectator and The Weekly Standard, O'Rourke has written a number of books including "Parliament of Whores: A Lone Humorist Attempts to Explain the Entire U.S. Government" and several notable articles for various magazines.

name: Walter Payton
about: Walter Payton is regarded as one of the most prolific running backs in NFL history.

name: Wolfgang Güllich
about: Wolfgang Güllich was a German rock climber considered the strongest climber in the world during his era. He also established some of the hardest grade climbs of his time and for pioneering training techniques that remain central to the discipline. Güllich's legacy includes the creation of innovative equipment such as the campus board, which is still widely used among climbers today.

name: Peggy Lipton
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Peggy Lipton was an American actress, model, and singer, best known for her role in The Mod Squad (1968-73) and her appearance in   (1990-91, 2017). She began her career as a model before moving on to television, eventually becoming a Golden Globe-winning actress.

name: Abdul Qadir
about:
Abdul Qadir was an Pakistani cricketer who bowled for Pakistan. During the 1970s and 1980s he was regarded as a legendary leg spinner and model for many that sought to emulate his success. 
 
Over his career, Qadir played 67 Tests and 104 One Day International matches. He also served as the captain for Pakistan in 5 of the One Day matches and played with the Pakistani national team for the 1983 and 1987 Cricket World Cups.

name: Diane von Furstenberg
about: Diane von Furstenberg is a Belgian fashion designer, best known for the iconic wrap dress design, which became a symbol of female empowerment in the mid-1970s. Having started her career in fashion with a modest line of jersey dresses, she quickly revolutionized women's apparel with her innovative and versatile dress design.

name: James Comey
about: James Comey is an American lawyer and public official, best known as the 7th director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation. He served in this post until he was dismissed by President   in 2017.

name: Curtis Strange
about: Curtis Strange is an American professional golfer and broadcast analyst.

name: Mike Pompeo
about: Pompeo served first as  's Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (2017–2018), then as Secretary of State (2018–2021).

name: Anita Baker
about:
Anita Baker is an American singer-songwriter, best known for her soulful ballads especially those released during the 1980s. She first came to fame with her album Rapture (1986), which was Platinum-certified and features "Sweet Love" as a Grammy-winning single. 
 
Over her career, Baker has released four Platinum-certified and two Gold-certified albums. She has also won a total of eight Grammy Awards.

name: Virginia Ruzici
about: Most notable for winning the 1978 French Open singles championship. She won 12 singles titles in total.

name: Pavlo Lazarenko
about: Prime Minister of Ukraine from 1996-97. Convicted and sentenced to prison (money laundering, wire fraud and extortion) in 2006, he embezzled approximately $200 million from the government of Ukraine.

name: Dan Quisenberry
about: Dan Quisenberry was an American baseball pitcher, best known for the time spent playing for the Kansas City Royals. He had a record number of saves, leading the American League in saves five times; and retiring with 244, which was the fifth highest in major league history.

name: Arnoldo Aleman
about: Arnoldo Alemán is a Nicaraguan politician who served as the President of Nicaragua from 1997 to 2002. Ultimately he fell from power and was convicted of various financial crimes, although his sentence was overturned under suspicious circumstances.

name: Lee Daniels
about: Lee Daniels is an American film director, producer, and screenwriter who first gained prominence as a producer with the film "Monster's Ball" (2001), for which   won the Best Actress Oscar, making Daniels the first African-American to solely produce an Oscar-winning film.

name: Imad Mughniyeh
about: Imad Mughniyeh was a senior member of Hezbollah known for his role in organizing numerous attacks against Western and Israeli targets.

name: Ben Bernanke
about: Chairman of the Federal Reserve during the Financial crisis of 2007–08.

name: David Cone
about: David Cone is a American professional baseball pitcher. Over his 17-year career, Cone played for five Major League Baseball teams, earned five All-Star selections, won the   Award, and was part of five World Series championship teams. After retiring, he became a commentator and co-authored a New York Times Best Selling autobiography.

name: Tōru Iwatani
about: Tōru Iwatani created Pac-Man, one of the most famous arcade games in history.

name: Lars Ulrich
about: Lars Ulrich is a Danish-American musician, songwriter, and actor. He is best known as the co-founder and drummer of the heavy metal band  , which he formed in 1981.  He comes from a family of professional tennis players, includiing his father Torben Ulrich and grandfather Einer Ulrich.

name: Katey Sagal
about:
Katey Sagal is an American actress and singer best known for her role as Peggy Bundy on Married... with Children (1987-1997). She also voiced the character of Leela on Futurama (1999-2003, 2008-2013, 2023) and played Gemma Teller Morrow on Sons of Anarchy (2008-2014).  
 
In 2011, Sagal won a Golden Globe for her performance in Sons of Anarchy. She has also had a musical career, releasing a series of solo albums and even contributing to the Sons of Anarchy soundtrack.

name: Steve Buscemi
about: Steve Buscemi is an American actor known for his prolific television and film career, including noteworthy roles in  's Reservoir Dogs (1992) and as Enoch "Nucky" Thompson in Boardwalk Empire (2010-2014).

name: Yuji Horii
about: Yuji Horii is best known for creating the Dragon Quest series which shaped the role-playing game genre and influenced a generation of game developers.

name: Kevin Anderson
about: Kevin Anderson is an American stage and film actor. He was a member of the renowned Steppenwolf Theatre Company, which has also featured notable actors like  ,  , and Laurie Metcalf.

name: Li Keqiang
about:
Premier of the State Council of China, a leading figure behind Chinese economic policy, and the second-ranked member of the Politburo Standing Committee.  
 
Named the World's 12th Most Powerful Person by Forbes in 2015 and 2016.

name: Jeff Sessions
about: Sessions served as Attorney General for the United States from 2017 to 2018, under President  . Prior to this he had served as U.S. Attorney in Alabama and then as Senator for Alabama, from 1997 to 2017.

name: Gary Carter
about: Gary Carter was an American baseball player, primarily recognized for his time as a catcher for the New York Mets and Montreal Expos in Major League Baseball (MLB). His illustrious career in baseball earned him the nickname "The Kid" for his enthusiasm and love for the game.

name: Lawrence Taylor
about:
Nicknamed "L.T.", he played his entire professional career as a linebacker for the New York Giants in the NFL.  
 
Considered one of the greatest defensive players in the history of football, Taylor was named the league's Most Valuable Player in 1986.

name: Vivienne Westwood
about: Vivienne Westwood was a British fashion designer known for her significant contributions to the punk and new wave fashion movements of the 1970s and 80s. Her designs, often described as provocative and rebellious, have played a pivotal role in shaping modern fashion.

name: Etta James
about: Jamesetta was the product of a broken home, and found solace in song. First as a member of her church choir, and then bitten by the doo-wop bug.  As a teenager, she was discovered and championed by bandleader and impresario Johnny Otis.  Otis suggested the stage name of Etta James and produced her early hit "The Wallflower" with her girl group, The Peaches.

name: Ray Dolby
about: Ray Dolby was an American engineer and inventor best known for his work in noise reduction and surround sound technology that transformed the audio quality of music, movies, and television.

name: Al Davis
about: Al Davis was an American football coach and executive, best known for his tenure as the principal owner and general manager of the Oakland Raiders. From his association with the team in 1972 until his passing in 2011, Davis was key to the franchise's success.

name: Jack Brisco
about: Jack Brisco was an American professional wrestler known for his technical prowess and his status as a two-time NWA World Heavyweight Champion. He transitioned from a celebrated amateur wrestler to a central figure in professional wrestling.

name: John Gutfreund
about: Former CEO of Salomon Brothers Inc, named 'King of Wall Street' by Business Week in 1985. Also featured prominently in the book Liar's Poker by Michael Lewis.

name: Don Cherry
about: Don Cherry is a Canadian ice hockey commentator and former professional ice hockey player and NHL coach. Cherry co-hosted the "Coach's Corner" intermission segment during the first intermission of the Canadian "Hockey Night in Canada" television broadcasts, along with broadcaster  , from 1986 to 2019.

name: Norman Schwarzkopf
about: Schwarzkopf served as the commander of the United States Central Command from 1988 to 1991. In this position he served as the commander of all US and coalition forces during the First Gulf War in 1990-1991. He became known as 'Stormin' Norman' for his aggressive military leadership style and fiery temper.

name: Jack Welch
about: Welch was Irish American and Catholic, as a businessman he was best known as the CEO of General Electric from 1981 to 2001. His severance package upon retirement is infamous for being the largest of its kind at $417 million.

name: Chuck McKinley
about: Chuck McKinley is best known for his win at Wimbledon in 1963. He was a key figure in American tennis during the 1960s, helping to break Australia's dominance in the sport.

name: Roone Arledge
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
President of ABC Sports from 1968 to 1986 and ABC News from 1977 until 1998, Arledge was a key part of the company's rise to equal status with the other two main US television networks, NBC and CBS.  
 
Arledge created many programs still airing today, including  "Monday Night Football", "20/20" and "ABC World New Tonight".

name: Anton Geesink
about:
First non-Japanese world champion in Judo, Geesink also won an Olympic gold medal in the sport in 1964. 
 
Geesink won a record 21 European Judo Championships during his career.

name: Sparky Anderson
about:
Managed the National League's Cincinnati Reds to the 1975 and 1976 championships, then added a third title in 1984 with the Detroit Tigers of the American League, making him the first manager to win the World Series in both leagues.  
 
He was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2000. He was named American League Manager of the Year in 1984 and 1987.

name: Alex Johnson
about: Alex Johnson was an American baseball outfielder that played for a variety of teams between 1964 and 1976.

name: Tom Snyder
about: Tom Snyder was an American television personality, news anchor, and radio host. He was best known for his pioneering role in late-night television with Tomorrow with Tom Snyder"(1973-1982) and his distinctive interview style with on-air smoking.

name: Harold Bloom
about: Harold Bloom was a professor at Yale University best known for his ideas about the Western canon, which is a grouping of books, plays, and poems that have been influential in Western culture.

name: Teri Garr
about: Primarily know for offbeat comedic roles, Teri Garr was nominated for  the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her work in the 1982 film "Tootsie".

name: Chandra Bahadur Dangi
about: Chandra Bahadur Dangi held the record for being the shortest man in recorded history. He measured 54.6 cm (1 ft 9+1⁄2 in), breaking the previous record set by Gul Mohammed.

name: René Préval
about:
Préval served as President of Haiti from 1996 to 2001 and again from 2006 to 2011.  
 
His first term saw attempts to reform the economy and investigate human rights abuses while his second term saw the destruction wrought by the earthquake in Haiti on January 12, 2010, which killed between 100,000 to 316,000 people.

name: Colin Meads
about: Colin Meads was a New Zealand rugby union player, best known for his career with the New Zealand national team, the All Blacks, where he played from 1957 to 1971. He played as a lock forward, and was fielded in a total of 55 test matches over his career.

name: Earl Anthony
about: Earl Anthony was an American professional bowler who took 43 Professional Bowlers Association (PBA) titles and was the first bowler to earn over $100,000 in a single season. His career highlights included ten major titles, membership in multiple Halls of Fame, and earning the title of "Bowler of the Millennium."

name: Colin Chapman
about: Colin Chapman started the Lotus car company and earned enduring fame for his innovative designs which increased the pace of Formula One racing and helped to give the cars their famous shape.

name: Phil Everly
about:
Phil was one half of the Everly Brothers, along with brother Don Everly, a rock-and-roll harmony group that gained success in the 1950s and 1960s. He would sing the tenor part of their harmony, while Don sang the baritone. 
 
Songs such as "Bye Bye Love" and  "Wake Up Little Susie," "All I Have to Do Is Dream," "Bird Dog," and "Problems" had significant success.

name: Arthur Kopit
about: The avant-garde playwright is credited with shaking up off Broadway in the 1960s with such plays as "Oh Dad, Poor Dad, Mamma’s Hung You in the Closet and I’m Feelin’ So Sad” (1962) and "Indians" (1969), know for their satirical and absurdist qualities.

name: Sani Abacha
about: A Nigerian Army general and politician who served as the de facto President of Nigeria from 1993 to 1998. His regime, although it saw dramatic economic growth, also saw widespread human-rights abuse.

name: Rolf Harris
about: Rolf Harris is an Australian entertainer, formerly a beloved television personality whose image was dashed in 2014 when he was convicted of indecent assaulting a series of underage girls. He was stripped of his honors and publicly reviled, with there being a sense of betrayal in the distance between his earlier image and these actions.

name: Carol Mann
about: Carol Mann was an American professional golfer best known for her career on the LPGA Tour. She began playing golf at age 9 and demonstrated early talent by winning the Western Junior and the Chicago Junior in 1958. Mann secured her first professional victory at the Women's Western Open in 1964, and her career amassed 38 LPGA Tour event wins, including two major championships. She was inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame in 1977.

name: John Polanyi
about: John Polanyi is a German-born Canadian chemist who made a significant impact on the field of chemical kinetics, a contribution that led to his receipt of the 1986 Nobel Prize in Chemistry​ which he shared with   and

name: Robert McFarlane
about: Robert McFarlane was an American government official known for his role as National Security Advisor under President   and his involvement in the Iran-Contra affair. McFarlane's career spanned various administrations, and his military service in the Marine Corps, including time in Vietnam, set a foundation for his later political roles.

name: Kris Kristofferson
about: Kris Kristofferson was an American singer-songwriter and actor best known for his influential country music career and performances in films such as "Pat Garrett &  " (1973) and "A Star Is Born" (1976). Kristofferson's work has earned him significant recognition, including a Lifetime Achievement Grammy Award in 2014.

name: August Wilson
about: Best known for his series of 10 plays, collectively called The Pittsburgh Cycle (or The Century Cycle), produced between 1984 and 2005. Each play is set in a different decade of the 20th century, most in the African-American community known as the Hill District of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, his childhood home.

name: Albert Finney
about:
Albert Finney was an English actor who came to fame with his film debut in The Entertainer (1960), which was directed by Tony Richardson. Subsequently Finney, having previously worked in theatre, became known for his many film roles. 
 
Finney was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actor four times:   (1963), Murder on the Orient Express (1974), The Dresser (1983), and Under the Volcano (1984). He won a BAFTA, Golden Globe, and an Emmy.

name: Terry Sawchuk
about: Played 21 seasons in the NHL for five different teams, but was best known as a member of the Detroit Red Wings. He is widely considered to be one of the best if not the best goaltenders of all-time, and set the standard for measuring goaltenders.

name: Doug Sahm
about: Doug Sahm was a musical polyglot who combined western swing, power pop, rock, country, and Tejano music into his sound.  His notable groups include the Sir Douglas Quintet and the Texas Tornados.

name: Jacques Plante
about:
During a career lasting from 1947–1975, he was considered to be one of the most important innovators in hockey.  
 
Plante played for the Montreal Canadiens from 1953 to 1963; during his tenure, the team won the Stanley Cup six times, including five consecutive wins. 
 
He was the first NHL goaltender to wear a goaltender mask in regulation play on a regular basis.

name: Sebastián Piñera
about: Sebastián Piñera is a Chilean businessman and politician who served as the President of Chile twice, from 2010 to 2014 and again from 2018 to 2022. As a member of the right-wing National Renewal party, he was the first conservative leader to be elected in Chile since its return to democracy in 1990.

name: Howard Stern
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Stern is one of the most famous and controversial figures in US radio.  
 
Often labelled a 'shock jock' for his comments on air, he outraged the Hispanic community in 1995 over his comments after the death of the singer Selena.  
 
Stern's shows were syndicated nationally 1986 to 2005 and were No. 1 in New York over a 7 year period.  
 
Stern has also published 2 best-selling autobiographies, hosted tv shows and been a judge on "America's Got Talent".

name: Paula Yates
about:
Paula Yates had a career as a music journalist and TV presenter on UK television, appearing on "The Tube" and "The Big Breakfast". 
 
Yates was married to The Boomtown Rats singer   for ten years before getting together with INXS singer  . She died of a heroin overdose in 2000.

name: George R. R. Martin
about: Author of the epic fantasy series "A Song of Ice and Fire," which was adapted into the Primetime Emmy Award-winning television series " ."

name: Ray Liotta
about: Ray Liotta was an American actor, film producer, and voice actor. Liotta is known for his roles in Goodfellas (1990), Hannibal (2001), and Field of Dreams (1989). He has also appeared in many other films and television series.

name: Edward Lee Howard
about: CIA case officer who defected to the Soviet Union after allegedly giving away CIA secrets during the Cold War.

name: John Carpenter
about:
American film director of horror and science fiction classics such as "Halloween" (1978), "The Fog" (1980) and "Escape from New York (1981). 
 
"Halloween" is credited as the first slasher film and began a film franchise with 7 sequels and a reboot in 2007.

name: Jennifer Higdon
about: Higdon is a an winning composer of contemporary classical music and music educator. She was awarded a Pulitzer Prize in 2010 and has  won three Grammy Awards for Best Contemporary Classical Composition (2010, 2018, and 2020).  She was a professor of composition at Philadelphia's prestigious Curtis Institute of Music for over 25 years.

name: Ozzie Smith
about: Ozzie Smith is a former outstanding baseball shortstop who played for the San Diego Padres and St. Louis Cardinals 1978-1996.

name: Mark Messier
about:
Played 25 years in the NHL with the Edmonton Oilers, New York Rangers, and Vancouver Canucks.  
 
Considered one of the greatest NHL players of all time, he won six Stanley Cups (five with the Oilers and one with the Rangers) and is the only player to captain two different professional teams to championship victories.

name: Nancy Lopez
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1977. She won 48 LPGA Tour events during her LPGA career and three major championships.

name: Kim Hughes
about: Cricket batsman who played for Australia between 1977 and 1984 and captained the side in 28 Test matches.

name: Pete Maravich
about: Considered perhaps the greatest creative offensive talent in history, he played 10 seasons in the NBA before his career was cut short because of injuries.

name: Wes Unseld
about: Wes Unseld was an American basketball player and executive who first gained prominence for winning both the NBA MVP and Rookie of the Year awards in the same season. He would later lead the Baltimore Bullets to an NBA Championship and was ultimately inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame.

name: Nawaz Sharif
about: Prime Minister of Pakistan three times between 1990 and 1993, 1997 and 1999 and 2013 and 2017.

name: Ismail Haniyeh
homePlace: Al-Shati refugee camp, Egyptian-occupied Gaza Strip
about: Ismail Haniyeh is the former leader of Hamas, an Islamist political and militant group that governs the Gaza Strip. He has played a significant role in shaping the political landscape of Palestine and the ongoing conflict with Israel.

name: John Leguizamo
about: Mambo Mouth, Whispers in the Dark

name: Lorenzo Lamas
about:
Lorenzo Lamas is well known for his role in the US prime time soap opera "Falcon Crest" (1981-90) opposite his real life stepmother  . 
  
 After "Falcon Crest" he has starred in such TV shows as "Renegade" (1992–1997) and the daytime soap opera "The Bold and the Beautiful" (2004–2006).

name: Gilbert Gottfried
about:
Gilbert Gottfried is an American stand-up comedian and actor, best known for his peculiar voice. He is primarily a stand-up comic, but has also starred in several major films and television series.  
 
Gottfried was the voice of Iago in Aladdin (1992), and also voiced Digit LeBoid in Cyberchase (2002-2004) and Kraang Subprime in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012-2017).

name: Eugene Jarvis
about: Eugene Jarvis is best known for producing pinball machines and video games at Williams Electronics and Atari respectively.

name: Randy Savage
about: Randy "The Macho Man" Savage is regarded as one of the greatest professional wrestlers in history, best known for his time in the World Wrestling Federation (WWF) and World Championship Wrestling (WCW),

name: Gregg Allman
about: Gregg Allman was an American musician, singer-songwriter, and a founding member of the Allman Brothers Band. He is best known for songs like "Whipping Post" and "Midnight Rider."

name: Sylvester James Jr.
about: Sylvester James Jr.'s father, Sylvester James Sr., was a musician who played the trumpet and his mother, Lillian James, was a homemaker. James Jr. began playing the trumpet at the age of five and by the time he was eight, he was playing in his father's band.

name: Nick Price
about: Won three major championships in his career: the PGA Championship twice (in 1992 and 1994) and The Open Championship in 1994. He reached the number one ranking in the world in the mid-1990s.

name: Rush Limbaugh
about: Limbaugh was a controversial American media personality, known for his long running and highly rated conservative talk radio show "The Rush Limbaugh Show".

name: Dino Ciccarelli
about: Played 19 seasons in the NHL, primarily with the Minnesota North Stars. He scored 1,200 points in his NHL career.

name: Ivan Reitman
about: Ivan Reitman was a Czechoslovak-born Canadian who worked in film and television as a director, producer, and screenwriter. He directed a number of major comedy films in the 1980s and 1990s, including " " (1984), "Twins" (1988), and "Dave" (1993).

name: Annie Lennox
about: Annie Lennox is a Scottish singer-songwriter, activist, and philanthropist who achieved international fame as half of the duo   in the 1980s before embarking on a successful solo career. With her distinctive voice and androgynous style, Lennox has become an iconic figure in the music industry, known for her powerful performances and emotive songwriting.

name: Hassan Nasrallah
about: Hassan Nasrallah was the leader of Hezbollah, a Lebanese political and military organization. He was known for his role in Lebanese politics and his opposition to Israel.

name: Kirby Puckett
about: Spent his entire 12-year career playing for the Minnesota Twins, and currently is the Twins' all-time leader in career hits, runs, doubles, and total bases.

name: Luther Vandross
about: Luther Vandross was an American singer, songwriter, and record producer whose soulful voice and heartfelt lyrics made him one of the most successful R&B artists of his time. He began his career as a background vocalist and songwriter before breaking through as a solo artist in the early 1980s.

name: Ray Bourque
about:
Considered one of the best defenceman in NHL history, he currently holds records for most career goals, assists, and points by a defenceman.  
 
Bourque played 21 seasons with the Boston Bruins franchise, before finishing his career with the Colorado Avalanche, with whom he won his only Stanley Cup in his final NHL game.

name: Florence Griffith Joyner
about: Florence Griffith Joyner, commonly known as Flo-Jo, was an American track and field athlete who still holds the world records for the 100 meters and 200 meters sprints. This is the longest-held of any such record, possibly due to an unrecorded tailwind on the day.

name: Ralph Fiennes
about: Fiennes first found success onstage as a performer of   at the Royal National Theatre.

name: Gabrielle Carteris
about: Gabrielle Carteris is best known for her role as Andrea Zuckerman in the television series " " (1990-1995) and for her leadership in  , where she served as president from 2016 to 2021.

name: Ryne Sandberg
about: Ryne Sandberg was drafted by the Philadelphia Phillies in the 1978 MLB draft and made his debut with the team in 1981.

name: Niki Lauda
about: Niki Lauda was an Austrian Formula One driver, best known for winning the F1 World Drivers' Championship three times (1975, 1977, 1984). During this time he raced for Ferrari and McLaren, and he is the only driver to have won a championship with both of these prestigious teams.

name: Vitas Gerulaitis
about: Vitas Gerulaitis was one of the more flamboyant players on the WCT Tour in the late 1970's and 1980's.

name: Mohamed Morsi
about: Mohamed Morsi was an Egyptian politician and engineer that served as the fifth President of Egypt (2012-2013). He was elected in the 2012 presidential election and then deposed in the 2013 coup d'état by General Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.

name: Ray Romano
about:
Romano is best known for his role as Raymond Barone on the CBS comedy Everybody Loves Raymond (1996-2005), which made him at one point the highest-paid actor on US television. 
 
In addition to that role he played Manny in the Ice Age film series, and created the TNT series Men of a Certain Age (2009-11).

name: Ben Crenshaw
about:
Ben Crenshaw is an American golfer known for having won 19 PGA Tour events, and in particular for having won the Masters Tournament in both 1984 and 1995. 
 
Crenshaw is regarded as an excellent putter, having been mentored by Harvey Penick. His seconds masters win came only two weeks after Penick's death.

name: Rand Paul
about: Serves as the junior United States Senator for Kentucky, in office since 2011. He is a member of the Republican Party. A member of the Tea Party movement, he supports a widespread reduction in federal spending and taxation.

name: Mike Bossy
about:
Played for the New York Islanders for his entire career and was a crucial part of their four-year reign as Stanley Cup champions in the early 1980s.  
 
Bossy is the only player in NHL history to score consecutive Stanley Cup winning goals (1982 and 1983).

name: Liu Xiaobo
about: Liu first came to prominence in the 1980s as a literary critic while outside China.

name: Bobby Murcer
about: Bobby Murcer was an American professional baseball player and broadcaster best known for his time as an outfielder with the New York Yankees, as well as for his later career as a Yankees broadcaster. Over the course of his career, Murcer was a five-time All-Star as well as a Gold Glove winner.

name: Michael Flynn
about: Originally a general who served in the US Army for 33 years, Flynn was picked by   to serve as his National Security Advisor. Between 2012 and 2014 he served as the Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency.

name: Ina Garten
about: Best known for designing recipes with an emphasis on fresh ingredients and time-saving tips, she has been noted by   and   for her cooking and home entertaining.

name: Terry Fox
about: Terry Fox was diagnosed osteogenic sarcoma, with a form of cancer at just 18 years old and his leg was amputated above the knee. Motivated by the suffering of others with cancer and realising that there was not enough funding for cancer research, so he formulated a plan to fundraise by running across Canada with his artificial leg.

name: Grete Waitz
about: 9 x NYC Marathon titles; World C'ship gold 1983; 5 x gold World Cross Country; WR x 4

name: Susan Lucci
about: Susan Lucci is best known for her role as Erica Kane on the soap opera "All My Children" (1970-2011). Her career was characterised by a long-running Emmy nomination streak, and then crowned with her eventual win.

name: Darrell Waltrip
about: Darrell Waltrip is one of the best NASCAR drivers in motor sports history.

name: Martin McGuinness
about: McGuinness is known as an Irish politician, but also for his involvement in the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA).

name: Chris Haney
about: Chris Haney was a Canadian journalist best known as a co-creator of the popular board game, Trivial Pursuit. After dropping out of school at 17, Haney began his career in journalism as a photo editor for the Montreal Gazette, but his life would soon take an unexpected turn.

name: David Lynch
about: A major American filmmaker whose work was known for its often surrealist quality.

name: Charles Taylor
about: Charles Taylor is a Liberian politician and war criminal, who was convicted of aiding and abetting war crimes in Sierra Leone during the 1990s and 2000s. He served as the 22nd President of Liberia from 1997 to 2003. Taylor is the first former head of state to be convicted by an international criminal court since the Nuremberg Trials in 1945.

name: Syd Barrett
about: Best known as one of the founding members of the band  , Barrett was the lead singer primary songwriter, from 1965 until 1967.  He was responsible for two hit singles, "Arnold Layne" and "See Emily Play", and the successful debut album "The Piper at the Gates of Dawn".

name: Paul Reubens
about:
Best known for creating and portraying the character Pee-wee Herman.  
 
Most famously in the adventure comedy film "Pee-wee's Big Adventure and the Saturday-morning children's program "Pee-wee's Playhouse".

name: Dale Earnhardt
about: Winner of seven NASCAR Winston Cup Series championships.

name: Tony Greig
about: The captain of England from 1975-77, he is considered by some to be one of England's leading international all-rounders and helped start World Series Cricket.

name: Sissy Spacek
about: Coal Miner's Daughter (1980), Heart Beat (1980) and The River (1984).

name: David Baszucki
about: David Baszucki is best known as the co-founder and CEO of Roblox Corporation, a popular online gaming platform.

name: Steve Garvey
about: Holds the National League record for consecutive games played, a staggering 1,207.

name: Christopher Reeve
about: Christopher Reeve was best known for his portrayal of Superman and his advocacy for spinal cord research. He transformed from a Hollywood star to a leading voice for disability rights after a life-changing accident.

name: Bill Pullman
about:
Pullman has starred in numerous high profile films, including  Spaceballs (1987), The Accidental Tourist (1988), Sleepless In Seattle (1993), While You Were Sleeping (1995), Casper (1995),   (1996), Lake Placid (1999), and Lost Highway (1997). 
 
In addition to numerous other television series he has appeared in, he is the main cast on the highly rated Netflix show The Sinner.

name: Paul Alexander
about: Paul Alexander was an American lawyer who became known for living with polio and using an iron lung. Contracting the disease in 1952, he survived thanks to an iron lung, continuing to face challenges and achieve notable milestones in education and career. His life story culminated in the publication of a memoir and his recognition by Guinness World Records.

name: Eduardo Romero
about: Eduardo Romero rose from modest beginnings in Argentina to become one of Latin America's most successful golfers. Known as "El Gato" (The Cat), his warm personality and competitive spirit helped him amass over 80 professional tournament wins across three decades.

name: Jean-Claude Duvalier
about: Jean-Claude Duvalier, also known as "Baby Doc," was a Haitian politician who served as the President of Haiti from 1971 to 1986. He was the son of François "Papa Doc" Duvalier, and his presidency was marked by the continuation of the Duvalier family's authoritarian rule over Haiti.

name: Tony Gwynn
about: Tony Gwynn was an American baseball player, best known for his 20-year career with the San Diego Padres. Nicknamed "Mr. Padre," he is regarded one of the all-time greatest hitters in the history of baseball. Gwynn was an outfielder who excelled in batting, earning eight batting titles and finishing his career with a .338 average.

name: Stan Smith
about:
Stan Smith is an American tennis player who was once world number one in 1971, who won two major singles championships (1971 US Open, 1972 Wimbledon), and who was a member of one of the all-time great men's doubles teams alongside Bob Lutz.  
 
Despite all this, he is best known as the namesake of a popular brand of tennis shoes made by Adidas.

name: Dilma Rousseff
about: Dilma Rousseff is a Brazilian economist and politician who became the first woman to serve as the President of Brazil. Her tenure ran from 2011 until 2016, when she was impeached on charges of fiscal mismanagement. Her rise in politics, however, was marked by a long history of resistance and activism, including her fight against the military dictatorship in Brazil during the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Jonathan Pryce
about: Jonathan Pryce was a successful stage actor before he began an equally successful film career. After studying at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art he acted in local productions before gaining more national roles.

name: Michael Hutchence
about: Founding member and the lead singer and lyricist of rock band INXS from 1977 until his death in 1997.

name: Alan Rickman
about: Alan Rickman was an English actor, best known for his performed as the antagonist Hans Gruber in Die Hard (1986). He achieved an entirely new level of fame when he played Severus Snape in the   series (2001-2011).

name: James Gandolfini
about: James Gandolfini was an American actor, best known for his iconic portrayal of Tony Soprano, the complex mob boss and protagonist of the acclaimed HBO television series The Sopranos. This role, which he played from 1999 to 2007, earned him widespread acclaim and multiple awards, including three Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series.

name: John Lydon
about:
Lead singer of the 1970s punk band  , Lydon has gone from causing moral panic to becoming something of a national icon since the heady days of the punk explosion.  
 
With the band he penned singles such as "God Save the Queen" and "Anarchy in the U.K." 
 
After the break-up of the   in 1978 Lydon formed a new band called Public Image Ltd.

name: Jimmy Buffett
about: Jimmy Buffett was an American singer-songwriter, musician, author, and businessman.

name: Bob Forsch
about: Bob Forsch was an American baseball pitcher who played for the St. Louis Cardinals (1974-1988) and Houston Astros (1988-1989). Forsch was a member of the 1982 World Series Champion team, as well as a National League pennant winner in 1985 and 1987.

name: Haruki Murakami
about: Haruki Murakami is a Japanese writer best known for his novels, essays, and short stories, which have gained international acclaim, been translated into multiple languages, and awarded several literary prizes.

name: Shelley Duvall
about: Shelley Duvall was known for her distinctive appearance and performances in critically acclaimed films. She later became a pioneer in children's television programming.

name: Hakeem Olajuwon
about:
From 1984 to 2002, he played the center position in the NBA for the Houston Rockets and Toronto Raptors.  
 
Olajuwon led the Rockets to back-to-back NBA championships in 1994 and 1995, winning the Finals MVP Award both times.

name: Barbara Mandrell
about:
With a series of major hits during the 70s and 80s, Mandrell was one of the most successful female vocal artists of her era. During her career she won two Grammy Awards and seven American Music Awards, among many others. 
 
Her first number-one hit was 'Sleeping Single in a Double Bed,' which was followed by '(If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to be Right.' She continued with a streak of Billboard number-one hits, with one each year from 1981 to 1983.

name: Malcolm McLaren
about: Malcolm McLaren had a huge influence of late 20th century pop culture. He was the founder of the famous S&M clothing boutique SEX with his girlfriend the designer   in London, a center for the emerging Punk scene.

name: Bill Rodgers
about: Despite never winning an Olympic medal, Rodgers is one of the biggest names in marathon history.

name: William Hurt
about: American stage and screen actor won Academy Award for Best Actor for hi role in "Kiss of the Spider", the first of 3 consecutive nominations (followed by "Children of a Lesser God" and "Broadcast News").

name: Yoon Suk-yeol
about: Yoon Suk Yeol is a South Korean politician, currently serving as the 13th President of South Korea. He has held this role since the 2022 presidential election, in which he ran for the right-wing People Power Party and defeated the Democratic Party nominee, Lee Jae-myung.

name: Trevor Berbick
about: Trevor Berbick was one of the leading heavyweight boxers in the 1980's, considered to be a golden era in the sport.

name: Kapil Dev
about: Captained the Indian cricket team which won the 1983 Cricket World Cup, and was named as the Indian Cricketer of the Century in 2002. He was one of the greatest all-rounders of all time.

name: Johnny Ramone
about:
Lead guitarist and songwriter for influential American punk band the Ramones.  
 
Ramone was one of the founding members of the band in Queens, New York in 1974. Band members all took the surname Ramone and weren't related.  
 
The band played together for 22 years before disbanding in 1996. Now regarded as one of the all-time greats, the Ramones are the recipients of a Lifetime Grammy award and have also been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

name: Bobby Bonds
about: Bonds was an a baseball right fielder, mainly with the San Francisco Giants, from 1968 to 1981. His record of five seasons with 30 home runs and 30 stolen bases was matched only by his son,  .

name: Val Kilmer
about: Val Kilmer is an American actor who first came to fame with his roles in Top Secret! (1984), Real Genius (1985), and Top Gun (1986). He starred in the latter alongside   and Kelly McGillis.

name: Chi-Chi Rodríguez
about: Chi-Chi Rodríguez won eight PGA Tour events and 22 Senior PGA Tour events during his career.

name: Jacques Anquetil
about: First 5-time winner of the Tour de France with tour victories in 1957 and 1961-64.

name: Curtis Mayfield
about: Curtis Mayfield was an American singer-songwriter, guitarist, and record producer who came to fame as a member of The Impressions and as a solo artist, with songs like "People Get Ready" (1965) becoming anthems of the civil rights movement. Despite a tragic accident that left him paralyzed, Mayfield continued to create music until his death in 1999.

name: Stan Mikita
about: Stan Mikita is regarded as the best ice hockey centre of the 1960s era.

name: Mary Mills
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1962 and won three major championships and nine LPGA Tour victories over her career.

name: Ingemar Johansson
about: Ingemar Johansson was a Swedish professional boxer known for his surprise victory against   in 1959, with which he won the world heavyweight championship. This made him the first European to take the title from an American since 1933.

name: Bill Walsh
about: Walsh is credited with inventing the West Coast offense, which revolutionized the game of football. As head coach of the San Fransisco 49ers, he won three Super Bowls and was named NFL Coach of the Year twice.

name: Mike Ilitch
about:
Ilitch co-founded Little Caesar's Pizza, the third-largest pizza chain in the United States, with his wife Marian. 
 
He also owned the Detroit Red Wings of the Major Hockey League and the Detroit Tigers of Major League Baseball.

name: T. Boone Pickens
about: An American oil and gas tycoon and corporate raider who rose to prominence in the 1980s for his attempts to overtake major American oil companies.

name: Ray Nitschke
about: A fierce competitor, he was the heart of the great Packers defense of the 1960s. He was the first defensive player from the Packers’ dynasty years to be elected to the Hall of Fame.

name: Jackie Wilson
about: "Lonely Teardrops"; "Higher And Higher": "I Get the Sweetest Feeling"

name: V. S. Naipaul
homePlace: Chaguanas, Colony of Trinidad and Tobago
about:
V.S. Naipaul is the recipient of the 2001 Nobel Prize for Literature.  He has published more than 30 books both of fiction and nonfiction over 50 years.  
 
Naipaul's best-regarded works include "A House for Mr Biswas" (1961), "In a Free State", which won the 1971 Booker Prize and "A Bend in the River" (1979). He was knighted in 1990.

name: Paul Arizin
about: Paul Arizin was a super athletic, high-scoring small forward who dominated the NBA in the 1950s and early 1960s.

name: Willis Reed
about:
Spent his entire professional playing career (1964–1974) with the New York Knicks, winning the NBA Championship twice.  
 
In 1997, he was voted as one of the 50 Greatest Players in NBA History.

name: Bobby Unser
about: Bobby Unser pioneered new frontiers in American auto racing, becoming one of only ten drivers to win the Indianapolis 500 three or more times and the first to win it across three decades (1968, 1975, 1981). Together with his brother Al, they became the only siblings to win the prestigious race, contributing to the Unser family's record nine Indianapolis 500 victories.

name: John Turner
about: John Turner was a Canadian politician who served as the 17th Prime Minister of Canada, holding office for a brief period in 1984. Turner's tenure as Prime Minister was notably short, but his career in Canadian politics spanned several decades and included significant roles in the cabinets of Prime Ministers   and  .

name: Al Unser
about: Al Unser was an American automobile racer, known as the younger brother of Jerry Unser and  , who were both also racing drivers. His son,  , was also a race car driver.

name: Chet Baker
about: Chet Baker is an American jazz trumpeter and vocalist who was born in Yale, Oklahoma in 1929. He began playing the trombone in his high school jazz band, and eventually switched to the trumpet. He developed a unique, lyrical style of playing that often featured a fragile beauty and melodic inventiveness.

name: Bob Guccione
about: Bob Guccione was an American magazine publisher and founder of Penthouse magazine. He was born in Brooklyn, New York, in 1930, and raised in Bergenfield, New Jersey. After high school, he served in the U.S. Air Force and then attended the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, where he studied painting.

name: Jean-Luc Godard
about: Jean-Luc Godard was a French-Swiss film director, screenwriter, and critic, often associated with the 1960s French film movement known as the Nouvelle Vague, or New Wave. His innovative approach to narrative structure, visual style, and the use of sound transformed the conventions of cinema and made him one of the most influential filmmakers in the history of the medium.

name: Roberto Suárez Gómez
homePlace: Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia
about: Roberto Suárez Gómez played a key role in expanding cocaine trafficking from Bolivia and had close ties to the powerful Medellín Cartel.

name: A. Bartlett Giamatti
about: A. Bartlett Giamatti was an American professor who served as the president of Yale University (1978-1986) and as the seventh Commissioner of Major League Baseball (1989). His tenure as Commissioner of Baseball ended abruptly with his sudden death of a heart attack in September of 1989.

name: Cormac McCarthy
about: Cormac McCarthy was known for his deeply immersive, vividly descriptive, and often dark and violent storytelling. His works often explore themes of morality, survival, and the human condition, set against the backdrop of the American Southwest and Mexico.

name: Frank Rosenblatt
about: Frank Rosenblatt was an American psychologist and computer scientist who made significant contributions to the early development of artificial intelligence, particularly in the field of neural networks. He is best known for his invention of the perceptron, a type of artificial neural network that laid the foundation for modern machine learning algorithms and techniques.

name: James Caan
about: James Caan was a respected American actor known for his wide-ranging roles in film and television. In the early stages of his career, he appeared in various television series before landing his breakthrough role as Brian Piccolo in the TV movie Brian's Song (1971), earning critical acclaim for his performance.

name: Jean Chretien
about: Jean Chrétien served as Prime Minister of Canada for over a decade. He was known for his working-class background and straightforward approach to politics.

name: Fred Stolle
about: Won the French Championship in 1965 and the US National Championship in 1966.

name: Franz Beckenbauer
about: Franz Beckenbauer is a German former professional footballer and manager, nicknamed "Der Kaiser" ("The Emperor") and generally counted among the all-time best players. He was named European Footballer of the Year twice, and in 2004 was listed in the FIFA 100.

name: Ornette Coleman
about: Ornette Coleman revolutionized jazz by freeing it from conventional harmony, chord changes, and fixed rhythms. Now known as the principal founder of free jazz, he was initially regarded as a frivolous interloper and even a fraud.

name: Clive Granger
about: Clive Granger was a British economist who won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 2003. He shared the award with   for their use of statistical methods in the analysis of time series data. Granger's contribution, known as Granger causality, has become a standard tool for testing causal relationships in economic data.

name: Ollie Matson
about:
Ollie Matson was an All-American running back from the University of San Francisco. He was also a sprinter, winning a bronze medal in the 400-meters at the 1952 Summer Olympics. 
 
He was drafted by the Chicago Cardinals in the first round of the 1952 NFL Draft, and went on to play for the Cardinals, Los Angeles Rams, Detroit Lions, and Philadelphia Eagles.  
 
Matson was a six-time Pro Bowl selection and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1972.

name: Maury Wills
about: Maury Wills was an American professional baseball player who is best known for his time with the Los Angeles Dodgers as a shortstop during the 1960s. Wills was an exceptional base runner and fielder, and his speed and agility on the field helped revolutionize the game. He is widely regarded as one of the most successful base stealers in the history of Major League Baseball (MLB).

name: Ashley Cooper
about: Played his best year in 1958, when he won three of the four Grand Slam events (and lost in the finals in the other), becoming one of only 11 men to win three Grand Slam events in the same year.

name: Plácido Domingo
about: One of the three tenors, Domingo has performed over 150 operatic roles, most notably the title role of Verdi's "Otello".

name: Jim Clark
about: Winner of Indianapolis 500 in 1965 and F1 World Champion in 1963 and 1965.

name: Manmohan Singh
about: India's first Sikh Prime Minister, Manmohan was also the first since   to be re-elected for a second full term.

name: Stirling Moss
about: Won 16 Formula 1 Grands Prix races and came runner-up in the World F1 Drivers Championship between 1955 and 1958.

name: Ray Stevens
about: Ray Stevens is an American country and pop singer-songwriter. He is known for his comedic novelty songs such as "The Streak" and "Gitarzan," and his serious country hits such as "Everything Is Beautiful" and "Misty."

name: Emile Griffith
about: Emile Griffith was an American boxer from the U.S. Virgin Islands who achieved significant fame in the 1960s. He is best known for his three fights with Benny Paret, which culminated in a bout where Paret tragically died from injuries sustained during the match.

name: Andrei Tarkovsky
about: Andrei Tarkovsky was a Soviet Russian film director and screenwriter, commonly regarded as one of the all-time greatest to work in film. He is widely renowned for his critically-acclaimed films, including Andrei Rublev (1966), Solaris (1972), Mirror (1975), and Stalker (1979).

name: Marsha P. Johnson
about: As one of the most prominent advocates for gay rights from the 1960s-90s, Johnson was a pioneering transgender activist best remembered for her calls for socio-economic justice and support for marginalised groups in society.

name: Isaac Hayes
about: Isaac Hayes was an American musician and composer, best known as a pioneer of Southern soul music at the label Stax Records. He worked there in a successful partnership with David Porter during the mid-1960s. The two were inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2005 for this work.

name: Colin Cowdrey
about: Colin Cowdrey was known for his batting and long career in Test cricket. He became the first player to appear in 100 Test matches and the first to score 7,000 Test runs.

name: Joe Morgan
about: Morgan is considered one of the greatest second basemen in Major League Baseball history.

name: Don Shula
about:
Best known as coach of the Miami Dolphins, the team he led to two Super Bowl victories, and to the NFL's only perfect season.  
 
Shula currently holds the NFL record for most career wins with 347, and only had two losing seasons in his 36-year career of coaching in the NFL.

name: Mary Travers
about: Mary Travers was a member of the very successful and influential folk group Peter Paul and Mary that also included Peter Yarrow and Noel Paul Stookey.

name: Larry Hagman
about: The American actor had a long career in film and on television but is best remembered for two starring role on the small Screen.

name: Alex Olmedo
about:
Alex Olmedo won the Australian Open and Wimbledon in 1959, as well as the U.S. Pro Championships in 1960. He was also on the United States' winning team for the 1958 Davis Cup. 
 
Olmedo was born and raised in Peru but moved to the United States and attended the University of Southern California, where he won the National Collegiate Athletics Association Singles and Doubles Championships in 1956 and 1958.

name: Peter Bogdanovich
about: Peter Bogdanovich is an American film director, writer, actor, producer, critic and historian. Bogdanovich has directed or produced over 70 motion pictures.

name: Dolph Schayes
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
A top scorer and rebounder, he was a member of the 1955 NBA champion Syracuse Nationals and played his entire Hall of Fame career with the Nationals and their successor, the Philadelphia 76ers.  
 
In his 16-year career, he led the team into the post-season 15 times and became a player-coach near the end of his playing career. 
 
After retiring from playing, he transitioned into a pure coaching role with the 76ers, earning NBA Coach of the Year honors in 1966.

name: Yao Wenyuan
about: Yao Wenyuan was a Chinese literary critic and a prominent political figure during the Cultural Revolution in China, which lasted from 1966 to 1976. He was a member of the Gang of Four, a political faction that played a significant role in this period and was known for its radical influence on Chinese politics and culture.

name: Peter Boyle
about: Best known for his role as Frank Barone on the sitcom "Everybody Loves Raymond", and as a comical monster in  ' film spoof "Young Frankenstein".

name: Ben Kingsley
about: Ben Kingsley is best known for his Oscar-winning portrayal of   in "Gandhi" (1982) and has received numerous accolades throughout his career. Kingsley was knighted in 2002 for his contributions to the British film industry.

name: Max Von Sydow
about: Made 11 films with Swedish director  , beginning with  "The Seventh Seal" in 1957. He was awarded the French Legion of Honor in 2012.

name: Betty Shabazz
about: The wife of  , Shabazz was a civil rights activist and educator in her own right.

name: Raymond Kopa
about: Raymond Kopa was considered one of football's elite attacking midfielders during the 1950s. He was nicknamed 'the   of football'.

name: Jimmy Page
about:
Achieved international success as the guitarist and leader of the rock band Led Zeppelin.  
 
Widely considered to be one of the greatest and most influential guitarists of all time.

name: Debbie Reynolds
about: Debbie Reynolds was an American actress, singer, and entertainer who rose to prominence during the 1950s. She is best known for her role as Kathy Selden in the iconic musical Singin' in the Rain (1952) alongside   and Donald O'Connor.

name: Earl Weaver
about: Weaver played minor league baseball, then managed minor league teams; while he never played Major League Baseball himself, he would later go on to manage the Baltimore Orioles for 17 years (1968-1982; 1985-1986).

name: Edward Albee
about:
As one of America's greatest modern playwrights, Albee is most known for "The Zoo Story" (1958), "The Sandbox" (1959),  "The American Dream" (1961), and "Who's Afraid of  ?" (1962).  
 
Albee has received numerous theatrical honors including a Tony Award and three Pulitzer Prizes.

name: Eric Carle
about: Eric Carle's most famous work is "The Very Hungry Caterpillar", the classic  children's story of a caterpillar that munched its's way through a lot of food to become a beautiful butterfly. Although the book has sold over 50 million copies and has been translated into 66 languages, since its publishing in 1969, it is just one of the seventy books he wrote for very young children.

name: Gale Sayers
about: Gale Sayers was an American football halfback who played for the Chicago Bears in the National Football League (NFL) for seven seasons. Known as "The Kansas Comet," Sayers is renowned for his elusiveness and agility on the field.

name: Don Drysdale
about: Drysdale, who went to school with  , started his career as a right-handed pitcher with the Brooklyn / Los Angeles Dodgers in 1956. In 1962 he won 25 games and the   Award, recognising for best pitcher in Major League Baseball.

name: Jacques Brel
about: Jacques Brel was a Belgian singer-songwriter and actor who became famous for his emotional, poetic, and often melancholic songs. His music, which encompassed a wide range of themes, from love and death to social commentary, has influenced many major artists including  ,  , and  .

name: Bobby Allison
about: Bobby Allison won 85 official Cup Series races, including three Daytona 500 victories, and claimed the 1983 Winston Cup Championship. Allison was also a founding member of the Alabama Gang, a group of drivers who helped shape NASCAR's competitive landscape.

name: Joe Lieberman
about: Joe Lieberman was a United States politician who served as Democratic Senator from Connecticut. Lieberman's most notable accomplishments include his vice-presidential candidacy in the 2000 election and his role in the repeal of the "Don't Ask, Don't Tell" policy on homosexuality in the military.

name: Frank Lucas
about: Frank Lucas was an American drug lord from New York City who controlled the heroin trade in the late 1960s and early 1970s. He made a deal directly with sources in Southeast Asia which allowed him to cut out the middleman, allegedly smuggling heroin back in the coffins of dead American soldiers.

name: Tom Brookshier
about: A starting defensive back for the Philadelphia Eagles for seven seasons from 1953 to 1961, he is best known for his pairing with   on the primary broadcast team for NFL games on CBS during the 1970s.

name: Gordon Moore
about: Gordon Moore co-founded the Intel Corporation in 1968 with Robert Noyce and made significant contributions to the semiconductor industry. He is best known, however, for proposing Moore's law, which states that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit doubles about every two years.

name: Wilma Rudolph
about: Wilma Rudolph was an American athlete known for her achievements in track and field. Overcoming childhood polio, she became the first American woman to win three gold medals in a single Olympic Games, and later worked as a civil rights and women's rights advocate.

name: Bob Hawke
about: The 23rd Prime Minister of Australia and the Leader of the Labor Party from 1983 to 1991.

name: Gary Kildall
about: Gary Kildall was an American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur who founded Digital Research, Inc. (DRI). He is best known for creating the CP/M operating system, which played a significant role in laying the groundwork for the personal computer revolution.

name: Cale Yarborough
about: Cale Yarborough won three consecutive NASCAR championships and 83 races over the course of his career, as well as claiming victory in the Daytona 500 four times.
