name: David Lange
about: Lange served as the Prime Minister of New Zealand from 1984 until his resignation in 1989. Prior to this he served as the MP for Mangere, in Auckland.

name: Peter Jennings
about: Peter Jennings was one of the most trusted news anchors in the United States. He served as the sole anchor of ABC World News Tonight for over two decades.

name: Sofia Muratova
about: Sofia Muratova was a Soviet gymnast best known for her performances at the 1956 and 1960 Olympics. She was one of the most successful gymnasts of her time, winning a total of 8 medals across these two games.

name: Jalal Talabani
about: Jalal Talabani was a Kurdish politician in Iraq, also known as Mam Jalal ("Uncle Jalal"), who served as the President of Iraq from 2005 to 2014, a position that made him one of the key figures in the post-  era. Talabani's presidency was a landmark in the history of Iraq, as he was the first non-Arab to become President of the country.

name: Lou Brock
about:
6 × MLB All-Star and winner of the World Series in 1964 and 1967.  
 
Brock was also the 8 × NL stolen base leader during his 16 year career with the St Louis Cardinals.

name: Gaylord Perry
about: Gaylord Perry was an outstanding right-handed pitcher who played for eight different teams in Major League Baseball from 1962 to 1983.

name: Peter O'Toole
about: Peter O'Toole was a stage actor before he was cast as the lead in  's epic film "Laurence of Arabia" (1962). O'Toole was nominated for an Oscar and went on to achieve a record eight best actor nominations without a win. In 2003 the Academy awarded him a Lifetime Achievement Academy Award.

name: Al Arbour
about: Al Arbour was a Canadian ice hockey player, but he is best known as a coach. He guided the New York Islanders to four consecutive victories in the Stanley Cup in the period of 1980 to 1983.

name: Alberto Fujimori
about: Alberto Fujimori is a Peruvian statesman that served as President of Peru from 1990 to 2000. While many describe him as a dictator, he has also been lauded for defeating the Shining Path insurgency which had plagued Peru for so long and for restoring the country's macroeconomic stability.

name: Nathan Lane
about:
Known for his stage and screen roles during a career which began on Broadway in the 1980s. His screen debut was in 1987 and he has worked consistently in film and television since. 
 
Lane has been nominated six times for a Tony Award, of which he has won three: for A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum (1996), The Producers (2001) and Angels in America (2018).

name: Dave Kingman
about: Dave Kingman is an American former professional baseball player. The three-time All-Star played as an outfielder and first baseman in Major League Baseball (MLB) from 1971 to 1986.

name: Emerson Fittipaldi
about: Emerson Fittipaldi is a Brazilian former professional racing driver and team owner who is one of the few motorsports legends to have achieved considerable success in both Formula One and IndyCar racing. His aggressive driving style and technical talent set him apart in the racing world and made him a dominant force during his career.

name: Walter Becker
about: Along with  , Becker was the co-founder of the jazz rock group  , with which he has sold more than 40 million albums.

name: Martin Crowe
about:
Martin Crowe was regarded as one of the best batsman of his day, renown for his elegant, classical style of play.  
 
A teenage prodigy, Crowe scored 17 centuries for his country, including a then world record of 299 in 1991 against Sri Lanka.  
 
Crowe also famously captained New Zealand during the 1992 World Cup and was named "man of the series".

name: Kevin Smith
about:
A New Zealand actor remembered for his roles in two TV fantasy series "Hercules: The Legendary Journeys" (1995-1999) and "Xena: Warrior Princess" (1995-2001) opposite  .  
 
Smith died tragically as the result of a fall in China in 2002.

name: Johan Cruyff
about:
A proponent of Total Football Cruyff won the Ballon d'Or three times, in 1971, 1973 and 1974. 
 
After his playing career he took up coaching and coached FC Barcelona between 1988 and 1996.

name: John Belushi
about: SNL; Animal House; The Blues Brothers

name: Eddie Van Halen
about:
Best known as the lead guitarist, keyboardist and co-founder of the hard rock band Van Halen.  
 
Ranked as one of the world's greatest guitarists, Van Halen is considered one of the most influential rock guitarists of the 20th century.

name: Billy Preston
about: Keyboard prodigy Billy Preston played the organ for gospel singer  ,  and piano as a guest on "The   Show" before he was a teenager.  He toured with   and released his own debut album at 16.

name: Steve Austin
about: Steve Austin is regarded as one of the greatest and most influential professional wrestlers of all-time.

name: Wendy Wasserstein
about: Wendy Wasserstein was an American playwright, best known for her play The Heidi Chronicles (1988) which in 1989 received the Tony Award for Best Play and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama.

name: Rickey Henderson
about: Nicknamed "The Man of Steal", he was widely regarded as the sport's greatest leadoff hitter and baserunner. He spent half of his 24-year career with the Oakland A's, where he won his first World Series in 1989. He won a second World Series during a brief stint with the Toronto Blue Jays in 1993.

name: Stephen Hillenburg
about: Hillenburg turned his passion for marine biology into one of the most successful and acclaimed cartoons in history, SpongeBob SquarePants, which is the fifth-longest running animated series in American history.

name: Carl Weathers
about: Carl Weathers was an American actor and former football player known for his roles in film and television, as well as his accomplishments on the football field. His most iconic role was the character Apollo Creed in the Rocky film series.

name: Reggie White
about: Star defensive end for the Philadelphia Eagles and Green Bay Packers, who was twice named NFL Defensive Player of the Year and was a 13-time Pro Bowl.

name: Chris Farley
about: Chris Farley was an American actor and comedian who started out with Chicago's Second City Theatre and was later a cast member with Saturday Night Live from 1990 to 1995. Subsequently Farley acted in a number of films, including Airheads (1994), Black Sheep (1996), and Almost Heroes (1998).

name: Will Wright
about: Will Wright is best known for creating SimCity and The Sims, a video games in which players manage simulations of individuals, families, and cities.

name: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo
about: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, known as "El Jefe de Jefes" (The Boss of Bosses), co-founded the Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s. He played a significant role in shaping the drug trafficking landscape in Mexico and along the United States border.

name: Peter Sutcliffe
about: Peter Sutcliffe, better known as the Yorkshire Ripper, was an English serial killer found guilty of murdering 13 women between 1975 and 1980 in Manchester and West Yorkshire. For these murders, and for the attempted murder of 7 more women, he received 20 concurrent life sentences.

name: Fernando Valenzuela
about: Fernando Valenzuela is a Mexican baseball pitcher who gained fame in the 1980s with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

name: Seve Ballesteros
about: Seve Ballesteros was one of the most influential and charismatic figures in golf. He won five major championships and played a key role in elevating European golf on the world stage.

name: Leon Spinks
about:
Best known for his victory over   in 1978, which is considered one of the biggest upsets in boxing history.  
 
Spinks had an overall record of 26 wins, 17 losses and three draws as a professional, with 14 of those wins by knockout.

name: David Boon
about: David Boon scored over 7,000 runs in Test cricket and played a key role in Australia's 1987 World Cup victory. He is also recognized for his stocky build and distinctive mustache.

name: Mark O'Meara
about: Mark O'Meara is an American professional golfer who enjoyed a successful career on the PGA Tour, winning numerous tournaments and major championships. He is known for his consistent play, exceptional short game, and sportsmanship.

name: Dick Wolf
about: The television writer and producer is responsible for both the Law & Order Franchise, which started in 1990 and the Chicago franchise which began in 2012.

name: Christine Lagarde
about: Christine Lagarde is one of the most influential figures in global finance. She currently serves as the President of the European Central Bank, the first woman to hold this position.

name: Bob Saget
about: Saget was an American comedian best known for playing Danny Tanner, the father on the ABC sitcom Full House which ran from 1987 to 1995; and then its Netflix sequel Fuller House which ran from 2016 to 2020. This role had him play father to   and  , who shared the role of daughter Michelle Tanner.

name: Axl Rose
about: Axl Rose founded the band Guns N' Roses in 1985 with Tracii Guns in Los Angeles. The band was made up of former bandmates and eventually included lead guitarist Slash, guitarist Izzy Stradlin, bassist Duff McKagan, and drummer Steven Adler.

name: Donna Summer
about: Donna Summer was an American singer and songwriter that came to fame in the 1970s during the disco era. She came to be internationally known, which led to her being acclaimed the 'Queen of Disco.'

name: Stevie Ray Vaughan
about: Stevie Ray Vaughan was a highly influential electric guitarists and blues musician. He bridged the gap between blues and rock, and was one of the foremost figures in the blues resurgence of the 1980s.

name: Peter Blake
about: Sir Peter Blake was near the top of the long list of great New Zealand sailors.

name: Temuera Morrison
about: Temuera Morrison is a New Zealand actor who first came to fame after playing Dr. Hone Ropata on Shortland Street from 1992 to 1995. He then progressed to more serious work with his acclaimed role as Jake "The Muss" Heke in Once Were Warriors (1994).

name: Nikki Sixx
about:
Sixx, born Frank Feranna Jr., is an American musician best known as a founding member of the Mötley Crüe, alongside  , Mick Mars, and Vince Neil.  
 
The band has since sold over 100 million albums worldwide, as well as a number of chart-topping hits.

name: Crystal Gayle
about: Crystal Gayle is best known for her hit song "Don't It Make My Brown Eyes Blue," her floor-length hair, and her crossover success as a country star in pop music.

name: Rodney Brooks
about: Rodney Brooks is an Australian-American roboticist, computer scientist, and entrepreneur who has made significant contributions to the fields of artificial intelligence and robotics.

name: Natalie Cole
about: Natalie Cole was the daughter of jazz and pop singer  . Her first recording was on her Father's Christmas album aged 6.

name: Hamid Karzai
about: Hamid Karzai was President of Afghanistan from 2001 to 2014. He is also khan of the Popalzai Durrani Pashtun tribe of the Kandahar Province; a role which he took over after his father's assassination in 1999.

name: Kenneth Branagh
about: Kenneth Branagh is a British actor, director, producer and screenwriter. He is best known for his film adaptations of  's plays, as well as his work in the Marvel Cinematic Universe having directed Thor (2011).

name: Toby Keith
about: Toby Keith was an American country music singer, songwriter, and producer who started out performing as a child in the house band at his grandmother’s supper club in Oklahoma. He went to a series of chart-topping singles, starting with his debut "Should've Been a Cowboy" (1993), and several gold-certified albums.

name: Sid Vicious
about: Best known as the bassist and vocalist for the " ."

name: Nicolas Sarkozy
about: Life long politician served as the 23rd President of France from 16 May 2007 until 15 May 2012.

name: Robin Gibb
about: Best known as a member of the  , which was co-founded with his fraternal twin brother   and older brother  .

name: John Paul Jones
about: John Baldwin, stage name John Paul Jones, had a successful career as a session musician arranging and performing with such acts as  ,   and Dusty Springfield before joining The Yard Birds, later Led Zeppelin.

name: Patrick Swayze
about: Patrick Swayze was an American actor, dancer and singer-songwriter best known for his role in Dirty Dancing (1987). He also starred in Ghost (1990), among other films, and had a hit song with "She's Like the Wind" (1987).

name: Jane Geddes
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1983 and won two major championships and 11 LPGA Tour events overall.

name: Nolan Ryan
about: Nicknamed "The Ryan Express", he pitched in 1966 and from 1968 to 1993 for four different teams: the New York Mets, California Angels, Houston Astros, and Texas Rangers during a major league record 27-year baseball career. His 5,714 career strikeouts rank first in baseball history by a significant margin, and he is the all-time leader in no-hitters with seven.

name: Wayne Gretzky
about:
Nicknamed "The Great One", he has been called the "greatest hockey player ever" by many sportswriters, players, and the NHL itself. He is the leading point-scorer in NHL history, with more assists than any other player has points.  
 
He is also the only player to total over 200 points in one season, a feat he accomplished four times. He won four Stanley Cup championships as a member of the Edmonton Oilers.

name: Glenn Frey
about: Glenn Frey was an American singer and guitarist, best known as a founding member of the Eagles. He wrote most of the band's material with Don Henley and sung lead vocals on many of their songs, including "Take It Easy" (1972) and "Tequila Sunrise" (1973).

name: Eugene Levy
about: Eugene Levy is a Canadian actor, comedian, producer, director, and writer. He is best known for his work in the   film series, as well as the CBC sitcom Schitt's Creek, which he co-created with his son Daniel Levy.

name: Donald Fagen
about: Along with  , Fagen is the co-founder of the jazz rock group  , with which he has sold more than 40 million albums.

name: Laffit Pincay Jr.
about: Laffit Pincay Jr. once held the record for most wins in horse racing history and today still holds third place even decades after his retirement. He is known for his exceptional career in the United States, where he won numerous prestigious awards and competed against some of the greatest horses in history.

name: Payne Stewart
about:
Won 11 PGA Tour events, including three major championships: the 1989 PGA Championship, the 1991 U.S. Open, and the 1999 U.S. Open.  
 
A popular golfer with spectators, Payne was known for his distinctive clothing.

name: Eric Holder
mainType: Attorney General of the United States
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Eric Holder is an American lawyer who served as the 82nd Attorney General of the United States from 2009 to 2015. Appointed by President  , Holder became the first African American to hold the position, marking a significant milestone in the history of American politics.

name: Patty Duke
about: Patty Duke was an American actress and, after being diagnosed with bipolar disorder in 1982, was a mental health advocate and public educator. As an actress, Duke won an Academy Award, two Golden Globes, and three Primetime Emmy Awards.

name: André the Giant
about: André René Roussimoff was a French professional wrestler, known for his size which resulted from an excess of growth hormone caused gigantism. This led to his being known internationally as André the Giant, and called by some "The Eighth Wonder of the World."

name: Tracy Austin
about: A child tennis prodigy, Tracey Austin was the youngest woman to win the US Tennis Open in 1979, when she 16 years and 9 months. She won the US Open title again in 1981, defeating Martina  Navratilova in the final. In 1980 she attained the ranking of No. 1 in the world.

name: Tim Russert
about:
Tim Russert was the longest-serving moderator of NBC's "Meet the Press" show, appearing from 1991, going on to appear for 16 years. 
 
Russert was also a senior vice president at NBC News and chief of its Washington bureau.

name: Michael Houser
about: Michael Houser was an American guitarist best known as founding member and lead guitarist of the band Widespread Panic. He performed with the band for 16 years, from 1986 until his untimely death in 2002.

name: Phil Hartman
about:
Became famous in the late 1980s when he joined the sketch comedy show "Saturday Night Live", and is best known for his impressions, particularly of former President  .  
 
Also known for providing the voices for Troy McClure and Lionel Hutz, two characters on " ".

name: Bret Saberhagen
about: Bret Saberhagen was an American professional baseball pitcher who made a notable impact in Major League Baseball (MLB). Known for his precise control and powerful fastballs, he enjoyed a successful career that spanned nearly two decades, primarily with the Kansas City Royals.

name: Samuel L. Jackson
about: Amos & Andrew, White Sand,

name: Bill Walton
about: Achieved superstardom playing for John Wooden's powerhouse UCLA Bruins in the early '70s,  before having a prominent career in the NBA where he was a league MVP and won two NBA championships.

name: Robbie Coltrane
about: Born Anthony Robert McMillan, Robbie Coltrane took the stage name Coltrane in tribute to the jazz legend John Coltrone.

name: Natasha Richardson
about: Natasha Richardson was a member of the English Redgrave acting dynasty, her mother was the actress Vanessa Redgrave her father the director and producer Tony Richardson.

name: Mariska Hargitay
about: Best known for her role as New York City sex crimes Detective Olivia Benson on the NBC television drama Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, a role that has earned her multiple awards and nominations, including an Emmy and Golden Globe.

name: Mark Spitz
about: Mark Spitz won an unprecedented seven gold medals at the 1972 Munich Olympics. Even more remarkably they were all won in world record time. He had previously won two gold relay medals, a silver and a bronze at the 1968 Mexico City Olympic Games.

name: Danny Glover
about: Danny Glover's career began in theater but he has gone on to be  successful in film, TV and theater. His  most famous role is opposite   in the "Lethal Weapon" film series. Other prominent roles include the Oscar nominated films "The Color Purple" (1985) directed by Stephen   and "Witness" (1985).

name: Lee Hsien Loong
about: Serving as the Prime Minister of Singapore since 2004, Lee is one of only three heads of government in modern Singaporean history, the others being Goh Chok Tong and  , Lee's father.

name: Eddie Vedder
about: Eddie Vedder is an American singer, songwriter, and musician best known as the lead vocalist, one of three guitarists, and the primary lyricist of the American rock band Pearl Jam. Vedder's rise to fame began in 1990 when Pearl Jam's debut album, Ten, was released and spawned the hit singles "Alive," "Even Flow," and "Jeremy."

name: Michelle Obama
about:
A lawyer by profession she became the first African-American First Lady of the United States when   was sworn in as  President in 2009. 
 
An advocate for poverty awareness, nutrition, physical activity, and healthy eating Obama has become a strong role model for women.

name: Ken Starr
about: The lawyer who investigated the Clinton administration.

name: Yahya Sinwar
homePlace: Khan Yunis refugee camp, Egyptian-occupied Gaza Strip
about: Yahya Sinwar is the leader of Hamas in the Gaza Strip, a position he has held since 2017. He is regarded as the mastermind behind the 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel, which resulted in the deadliest attack in Israeli history.

name: Greg Louganis
about: Greg Louganis is an American Olympic diver and LGBT activist, widely considered one of the greatest divers in history. He is known for his remarkable performances in the Olympics and for his advocacy work in the LGBT community and HIV awareness.

name: Geoffrey Hinton
about: Geoffrey Hinton is a British-born Canadian cognitive psychologist and computer scientist who has made groundbreaking contributions to the fields of artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning. He is often referred to as the "  of deep learning" due to his pioneering work in developing neural network architectures and learning algorithms, which have laid the foundation for the modern era of AI.

name: Tom Petty
about: Tom Petty, working chiefly with his band the Heartbreakers, but also as a member of the supergroup the Traveling Wilburys, and as a solo artist sold an estimated 80 million records during his life time. He won 3 Grammy Awards, one with each group, and one by himself.

name: Chris Evert
about: Chris Evert is a former professional tennis player from the United States who was one of the game's most dominant figures in the 1970s and 1980s. Known for her powerful baseline play and remarkable consistency, Evert won 18 Grand Slam singles titles during her career, making her one of the most successful players in the history of the sport.

name: Brad Pitt
about:
Award-winning star and film producer of numerous Hollywood blockbusters including "Thelma & Louise", "Se7en", "12 Monkeys", "Fight Club" and " ". 
 
Pitt is considered one of the most influential and powerful people in entertainment. He also frequently appears on various "most attractive" lists.

name: Benny Andersson
about: Benny Andersson began his music career in 1964 as keyboardist and composer for the Swedish pop band Hep Stars. He met folk singer-songwriter Bjorn Ulvaeus in 1966 and began writing with him, including songs that were recorded by Andersson's band.  During the 1969 Swedish Eurovision Song Festival, for which he co-wrote a song, he met jazz vocalist Anna-Frid Lynsgstad, and they began a relationship.

name: Richard Lewis
about: Richard Lewis was an American stand-up comedian and actor known for his dark sense of humor which focused on his personal struggles and neuroses.

name: Michael Milken
about: Michael Milken is an American financier known for his central role in developing the high-yield bond market, also known as the junk bond market, his legal troubles related to securities violations, and his subsequent philanthropic activities.

name: Yannick Noah
about:
Best remembered for winning the French Open in 1983 and as a highly successful captain of France's Davis Cup and Fed Cup teams.  
 
He is also the father of Joakim Noah, who plays for the Chicago Bulls in the NBA.

name: Paul Coffey
about: Known for his speed and scoring prowess, he ranks second all-time among NHL defencemen in career goals, assists, and points. He won three Stanley Cups with the Edmonton Oilers and one with the Pittsburgh Penguins.

name: Jim Hines
about:
The first person to run 100 meters in under 10 seconds Hines won two Olympic gold medals.  
 
One in the 100m and one in the 4x100m relay, both at the 1968 Olympic Games in Mexico City.

name: Jeffrey Dahmer
about: Jeffrey Dahmer was an American serial killer and sex offender who committed the murders and dismemberments of seventeen young men between 1978 and 1991. His later murders also involved necrophilia, cannibalism, and the permanent preservation of body parts, typically all or part of the skeleton.

name: Uhuru Kenyatta
about: Uhuru Kenyatta is the current President of Kenya, in office since 2013. He is also the Chairman of the Jubilee Party of Kenya and was previously the Member of Parliament for Gatundu South constituency.

name: Carrie Fisher
about: Carrie Fisher was best known for her role as Princess Leia in the original " " film trilogy.

name: Guy Lafleur
about:
First player in the NHL to score 50 goals and 100 points in six straight seasons.  
 
Lafleur played 17 seasons, most of which for the Montreal Canadiens, and won five Stanley Cups.

name: Paul Allen
about: Paul Allen was an American businessman and computer programmer, known for co-founding the Microsoft Corporation with his childhood friend   in 1975. After the microcomputer revolution of the 1970s and 1980s, Microsoft went on to become the largest such company in the world for a while.

name: Anthony Albanese
about: Anthony Albanese is an Australian politician who is the current Prime Minister of Australia, having defeated  's Liberal-National Coalition in the 2022 election. Albanese is the leader of the Australian Labor Party, a position which he has held since 2019, as well as being the member of parliament for Grayndler since 1996.

name: Amy Alcott
about: Amy Alcott is an American golfer, a member of the LPGA Tour known for having won five major championships along with a total of 29 LPGA Tour events. She has further been inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame.

name: Russell Coutts
about: Sir Russell Coutts is an outstanding New Zealand yachtsman.

name: Brigitte Macron
about: Brigitte Macron is a French teacher and the wife of  , the President of France. She became a globally recognized figure after her husband's election in 2017.

name: Ron MacLean
about: Best known as the host of Hockey Night in Canada with   from 1987 to 2014, and is also a hockey referee.

name: Prince Rogers Nelson
about:
Prince was a major figure in popular music for over three decades. 
 
The singer-songwriter was known for his eclectic work, flamboyant stage presence and wide vocal range.  
 
Prince sold over 100 million records worldwide and has won seven Grammy Awards, a Golden Globe and an Academy Award.

name: Ken Norton
about:
Held the WBC heavyweight title in 1978.  
 
Best known for his trilogy of fights with  , in which Norton won the 1st by split decision, lost the 2nd by split decision and lost the final in a controversial unanimous decision.

name: David Rumelhart
about: David Rumelhart was an American cognitive psychologist and computer scientist who made significant contributions to the fields of artificial intelligence (AI), cognitive science, and neural networks. He is best known for his work on the development of the backpropagation algorithm, an essential learning technique used in training artificial neural networks, along with   and Ronald J. Williams.

name: Melvin Van Peebles
about: Peebles was an American actor and filmmaker, whose debut film was "The Story of a Three-Day Pass" (1967).

name: Brian Jones
about: Brian Jones was an English musician and singer, best known as the founder and original leader of  . He started the band in 1962, though   and   would later come to exert a greater influence over the band's sound.

name: David Pearson
about: David Pearson is regarded as one of the best NASCAR drivers of all-time.

name: Bruno Sammartino
about: Bruno Sammartino was an Italian-born American wrestler, regarded as one of the all-time greatest professional wrestlers. He worked with the World Wide Wrestling Federation, now known as the WWE, during which time he held the World Heavyweight Championship for a total of more than 11 years.

name: Dietrich Mateschitz
homePlace: Sankt Marein im Mürztal, Styria, Austria
about: Dietrich Mateschitz is an Austrian businessman who co-founded the energy drink company Red Bull. An entrepreneur with a knack for marketing, Mateschitz transformed a Thai energy drink called Krating Daeng into a global phenomenon, introducing Red Bull to the world market in 1987.

name: Willie Stargell
about: Willie Stargell was a Baseball Hall of Fame left-fielder and first baseman who spent all of his 21 seasons in Major League Baseball with the Pittsburgh Pirates (1962–1982).

name: Krzysztof Penderecki
about: Krzysztof Penderecki was a Polish composer, best known for a number of major works including Threnody to the Victims of Hiroshima (1961), Symphony No. 3 (1988-1995), Polish Requiem (1984), and Anaklasis (1960). His compositions spanned operas, symphonies, various orchestral pieces, instrumental concertos, and choral settings.

name: Vaughn Meader
about:
Famous for his impersonation of  , his 1962 comedy album The First Family became the fastest-selling record in history at the time, with more than a million copies a week sold at its height. 
 
Meader faded into obscurity after Kennedy was assassinated on November 22, 1963.

name: Billy Casper
about: Won the US Open in 1959 and 1966 and the US Masters in 1970.

name: Jerry West
about: Played his entire professional NBA career for the Los Angeles Lakers, from 1960 to 1974.

name: Bob Pettit
about: Bob Pettit was the first NBA player to score 20,000 points and is one of only four players named to all four NBA anniversary teams.

name: Seamus Heaney
about:
Seamus Heaney won the 1995 Nobel Prize in Literature - "for works of lyrical beauty and ethical depth, which exalt everyday miracles and the living past". 
 
Some of his best regarded collections of poetry include his first "Death of a Naturalist" (1966) and "The Spirit Level" (1996), which won the Whitbread Book of the Year Award.

name: Henri Richard
about:
The brother of Montreal Canadiens legend Maurice "The Rocket" Richard, he played twenty years for the Canadiens and is considered one of the greatest players in NHL history.  
 
Given the nickname "The Pocket-Rocket", he won 11 Stanley Cups.

name: Christine McVie
about: Christine McVie is best known for her work with the rock band  . She wrote and performed many of the group's hit songs, playing a major part in their global success.

name: David Koch
about: David Koch was an American businessman, philanthropist, political activist, and chemical engineer. He joined the family business, Koch Industries, in 1970 and served as its executive vice president until his retirement in 2018. David and his brother   expanded the business into one of the largest privately held companies in the United States.

name: Lew Hoad
about: Won four majors as an amateur, and won the 1959 Tournament of Champions as a professional. He has been ranked as the greatest player of the 'Past Champions' era of tennis.

name: Roger Maris
about: Maris hit a Major League record 61 home runs during the 1961 season for the NY Yankees to break the then record, set by  's single-season of 60 home runs in 1927.

name: Jack Kevorkian
about: Better known as 'Dr. Death,' Kevorkian was an American pathologist and public advocate for euthanasia. He claimed to have assisted at least 130 patients, of which he said: "My aim in helping the patient was not to cause death. My aim was to end suffering. It's got to be decriminalized."

name: Sonny Ramadhin
homePlace: St. Charles Village, British Trinidad and Tobago
about: Sonny Ramadhin was perhaps West Indian cricket's dominant spin bowler of the 1950s.

name: Harmon Killebrew
about: Hall of fame first baseman who hit 573 home runs in his 22 year career, mostly with the Minnesota Twins.

name: Helmut Kohl
about: Helmut Kohl served as Chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998, making him the longest-serving German Chancellor since  . He played a crucial role in the reunification of Germany and the creation of the European Union.

name: George Steinbrenner
about:
During his 37-year ownership from 1973 to his death in July 2010, the longest in club history, the Yankees earned seven World Series titles and 11 pennants.  
 
His outspokenness and role in driving up player salaries made him one of the sport's most controversial figures. He had a tendency to meddle in daily on-field decisions, and to hire and fire managers.

name: Roberto Clemente
about: Roberto Clemente spent 18 seasons with the Pittsburgh Pirates in Major League Baseball. He was known for his exceptional hitting and fielding skills, as well as his humanitarian work. Clemente was a 15-time All-Star, won 12 Gold Glove Awards, and was the first Latin American and Caribbean player inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame.

name: Roger Miller
about: Best known for his chart-topping honky-tonk influenced novelty hits "King of the Road", "Dang Me" and "Kansas City Star".  The singer-songwriter garnered 11 Grammy Awards between 1964 and 1965.

name: Marty Schottenheimer
about:
Served as head coach of the Cleveland Browns, Kansas City Chiefs, Washington Redskins and San Diego Chargers.  
 
Schottenheimer has the most wins of any NFL coach since 1966 to never coach a team in a Super Bowl.

name: Spalding Gray
about: He is known for the autobiographical monologues that he wrote and performed for the theater in the 1980s and 1990s.

name: Jackie Mason
about: Found fame for his series of one-man shows on Broadway such as the "World According to Me!" and for his various roles on TV shows like "The   Show" and the sitcom "Chicken Soup".

name: Fay Vincent
about: Fay Vincent is an American attorney and sports executive who served as the eighth Commissioner of Major League Baseball from 1989 to 1992. Taking the helm after the sudden death of his predecessor,  , Vincent inherited a league faced with numerous challenges ranging from labor relations to drug scandals.

name: Ralph Boston
about: Won Olympic gold in 1960 and was the first to break the 27 feet (8.2m) barrier.

name: Merle Haggard
about: Haggard is a American country music star of the sixties, seventies and eighties, although he has continued to release albums into the 2000's.

name: Ziaur Rahman
homePlace: Bagbari, Bogra District, Bengal Presidency, British India
about: Ziaur Rahman was a Bangladeshi statesman and military officer who served as the President of Bangladesh from 1977 until his assassination in 1981. A prominent figure in the country's struggle for independence from Pakistan in 1971, Rahman rose through the military to play a key role in shaping Bangladesh's early years as a sovereign nation.

name: Gene Littler
about: Gene Littler was an American professional golfer known as "Gene the Machine." He won the 1961 U.S. Open, as well as 29 PGA Tour events. Littler also played on seven Ryder Cup teams and was inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame in 1990.

name: Wang Hongwen
about: Wang Hongwen was a Chinese political figure best known for his involvement in the Cultural Revolution and as a member of the Gang of Four. The Gang of Four was a political faction within the Communist Party of China that played a significant role in this violent period of Chinese history.

name: Darlene Hard
about: Known for her strong serves and volleying ability, she captured singles titles at the French Championships in 1960 and the U.S. Championships in 1960 and 1961.

name: Anita Ekberg
about: Anita Ekberg was a Swedish actress renowned as a beauty in American and European cinema. She initially came to fame after winning Miss Sweden in 1950, and then starred in  's iconic film La Dolce Vita (1960).

name: Jim Bakker
about: Jim Bakker, along with his then wife Tammy Faye, hosted the PTL Show on TV from 1974-1987. Jim Bakker based his PTL ministries in the Carolinas where he also built a theme park Heritage USA and him and his wife were known for their lavish lifestyle.

name: Dave DeBusschere
about: Won two NBA Championships with the New York Knicks (1970, 1973) and in 1996 was named as one of the Top 50 players in NBA history.

name: Hobart "Hobie" Alter
about:
A surfing and sailing entrepreneur and pioneer, Hobart Alter is considered the   of the surfboard industry for his manufacturing innovations.  
 
He also created the popular Hobie Cat, a lightweight sailboat that skims the waves like a surfboard to give surfers something to do when the wind blows.

name: Jerry Herman
about: Jerry Herman created some of Broadway's most popular musicals. He was known for his upbeat, optimistic shows with memorable tunes.

name: Pat Summerall
about:
Played nine years in the NFL before moving to the booth, where he announced a wide variety of sports, including football, golf, and tennis.  
 
In total, he announced 16 Super Bowls, 26 Masters Tournaments, and 21 US Opens.

name: James Garner
about: James Garner was an American actor known for his roles in television series such as Maverick (1957–60) and The Rockford Files (1974–80). He had a long and successful career, working alongside names such as  ,  ,  , and  .

name: Burt Bacharach
about: Considered one of the most important composers of 20th-century popular music, Bacharach has written dozens of hits songs, many in collaboration with lyricist Hal David. Over 1000 artists have covered their work, the most successful being their collaborations with  .

name: Fred Ebb
about: American theater lyricist Fred Ebb, along with his songwriting partner composer  , have created 16 Broadway productions, including such classics as Cabaret and Chicago, and are the winners of three Tony awards, an Emmy and two Emmys.

name: Ted Kennedy
about: Kennedy was an American lawyer and senator from the Kennedy family, younger brother to   and   and father of Patrick J. Kennedy. He was senator for Massachusetts from 1962 until death in 2009, a total of 49 years.

name: John Havlicek
about: John Havlicek is considered one of the best small forwards in basketball history.

name: John Wayne Gacy
about: Gacy was convicted of the sexual assault and murder of at least 33 teenage boys and young men in a series of killings committed between 1972 and 1978 in Chicago, Illinois. Gacy was known as the Killer Clown because of his habit of dressing as a clown at charity events,

name: Joe Pesci
about: Although Joe Pesci began his career as a child actor he didn't achieve fame until his role in "Raging Bull" (1980), the first of a number of films with director   and actor  , who became a friend. He won a BAFTA and was nominated for an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for the part.

name: Ken Holtzman
about: Holtzman was an MLB pitcher who played for the Athletics' dynasty that won three consecutive World Series championships between 1972 and 1974. A two-time All-Star, Holtzman was a 20-game-winner for the Athletics in 1973.

name: Edward Feigenbaum
about: Edward Feigenbaum was an American computer scientist who made significant contributions to the field of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in the development of expert systems. He is often referred to as the "father of expert systems" due to his pioneering work in creating programs that can replicate the decision-making abilities of human experts.

name: Luis Suárez Miramontes
about: Suárez was a midfielder considered one of the all-time greats in Spanish football.

name: Henry Hill
about: Between 1955 and 1980, Hill was associated with the Lucchese crime family. He turned FBI informant in 1980, inspiring the   movie Goodfellas.

name: Chuck Noll
about: Chuck Noll led the Pittsburgh Steelers to four Super Bowl victories. He transformed the Steelers from a struggling team into a dynasty during his tenure as head coach from 1969 to 1991.

name: Jon Voight
about: Jon Voight won an Academy Award for Best Actor for his role in "Coming Home" (1978) and has received three other Oscar nominations.

name: Graham Hill
about:
Often referred to as "Mr. Monaco" due to his five wins at the Monaco Gran Prix (1963-65, 1968 & 1969).  
 
He was also a two time Formula One World Champion (1962 and 1968), and winner of the Indianapolis 500 (1966), and the 24 Hours of Le Mans (1971)

name: Wilson Pickett
about: Recorded over 50 songs which hit the US R&B charts (In the Midnight Hour, Land of 1,000 Dances, Mustang Sally, and Funky Broadway).

name: Jim Bunning
about: Jim Bunning was an American baseball pitcher who went on to be a politician, serving as senator for Kentucky. This makes him the only Major League Baseball player to have been elected to both the United States Senate and the Baseball Hall of Fame.

name: Dawn Wells
about: The American actress is famous for her role as Mary Ann on the 1960s US TV series "Gilligan's Island" alongside  ,   and Jim Backus. The show ran for three seasons, with three TV film sequels.

name: Johnny Ventura
about: Johnny Venturea was christened the “Elvis of Merengue” for the way he was able to incorporate the sounds of rock n roll and other modern influences into the traditional Merengue music of the Dominican Republic. Throughout his long career he released more than 100 albums and won six Latin Grammy awards. In 2006 he was awarded a Latin Grammy Lifetime Achievement award.

name: Alex Trebek
about:
Alex Trebek was a Canadian-American game show host, best known for hosting the quiz show 'Jeopardy!' for 37 seasons (1984-2020). His role as host ended with his death in 2020. 
 
Trebek also hosted a number of other game shows in his career, including "The Wizard of Odds", "Double Dare", and "High Rollers". Beside this, he frequently featured in films and television shows in cameo roles.

name: Richard Pryor
about: Richard Pryor was a hugely influential African American comedian. He also had a successful career as a film actor, writer and presenter.

name: Gene Wilder
about: Gene Wilder was famous for his collaborations with writer and director  , featuring in "Blazing Saddles" and "Young Frankenstein". He is perhaps best remember for his portrayal of Willy Wonka in "Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory".

name: Cass Elliot
about: "Mama" Cass gained fame as part of the 1960s folk-pop vocal quartet the Mamas & the Papas.  The group was together from 1965 until 1968, before personal issues tore them apart.  They released 4 albums and had 6 Top-Ten singles, including "California Dreamin'" and "Monday, Monday".

name: Tom Lester
about: Lester was best known for his role as Eb Dawson on "Green Acres."

name: Willie McCovey
about: 6 x MLB All Star; NL MVP 1969; NL home run leader 1963, 1968 and 1969;

name: Betsy Rawls
about:
LPGA Tour professional golfer who won eight major championship and 55 LPGA Tour career events.  
 
Rawls is a member of the World Golf Hall of Fame.

name: Don Sutton
about: MLB All-Star in 1972, 73, 75, 77; MLB ERA leader 1980; LA Dodgers

name: Loretta Swit
about: Loretta Swit was an American actress known for her role as Major Margaret "Hot Lips" Houlihan on the television series M*A*S*H (1972-1983). She won two Emmy Awards for her performance and became a television icon of the era. Swit also had a notable presence on stage and was a passionate animal rights activist.

name: Johnny Unitas
about: American football player in the 1950s through the 1970s. Spent the majority of his career playing for the Baltimore Colts. A record-setting quarterback who was the National Football League's most valuable player in 1959, 1964 and 1967. For 52 years he held the record for most consecutive games with a touchdown pass.

name: Bill Shoemaker
about: Won 8,833 career victories including winning the Kentucky Derby in 1955, 1959, 1965 and 1986.

name: Ricky Nelson
about:
Younger son in his parents' radio program and TV series "The Aventures of Ozzie and Harriet", became a teen singing idol with such songs as "Poor Little Fool", "Travelin' Man" and "Hello, Mary-Lou".  
 
His last hit record was "Garden Party".

name: Bob Denver
about: Known for his roles as   on the television series "Gilligan's Island" and the beatnik Maynard G. Krebs on the 1959–1963 TV series "The Many Loves of Dobie Gillis".

name: Carolyn Jones
about: Carolyn Jones was an American actress who gained fame for her role as Morticia Addams on the popular 1960s television series The Addams Family. With her elegant demeanor and unique sense of style, Jones captivated audiences and became an iconic figure.

name: Abdelaziz Bouteflika
about: Abdelaziz Bouteflika was an Algerian politician and diplomat, serving as the country's seventh President from 1999 to his resignation in 2019. He was pivotal in ending the Algerian Civil War and improving the national economy, but his reputation was marred by corruption and significant public dissent that eventually led to his stepping down.

name: Larry King
about:
One of the most recognizable American television and radio hosts, King came to prominence in the 1970s and 80s as an all-night talk show host on radio. Prior to that he worked as a journalist. 
 
From 1985 to 2010 he hosted The Larry King Show on CNN and now hosts Larry King Now on Hulu.

name: Whitey Ford
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Spent his entire 16-year career with the New York Yankees, winning the World Series 6 times.  
 
He was voted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1974.

name: Jessye Norman
about: Jessye Norman was an American opera singer whose career spanned several decades, during which she became renowned for her performances in a variety of operatic roles and recitals. Notable achievements include winning multiple Grammy Awards, receiving the National Medal of Arts, and being decorated with the Légion d'honneur.

name: Davy Jones
about: Davy Jones came to fame famous as a member of The Monkees, a pop rock band created for television. He sang lead vocals on the band's hit single "Daydream Believer" and appeared in their television series, which aired from 1966 to 1968.

name: Garry Marshall
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Garry Marshall was an American director, producer, writer, and actor who is best known for creating Happy Days (1974-1984) and directing Pretty Woman (1990).

name: Elston Howard
about: Elston Howard was an American professional baseball player known for breaking barriers in Major League Baseball (MLB). He was the first African American player to join the New York Yankees, debuting with the team in 1955.

name: Hanif Mohammad
about: Hanif was considered one of the best batsmen in the world despite playing at a time when Pakistan played very little Test cricket.

name: Bill Withers
about:
Wrote and performed "Ain't No Sunshine" and "Lean On Me". 
He was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2005 and Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2015.

name: Patsy Cline
about: As a country music legend and leading Nashville vocalist, Cline was a pioneer of the genre. Her success promoted female headline performers and helped break down gender barriers in the male dominated industry.

name: Nicky Hopkins
about: One of rock's greatest studio musicians, Hopkins played piano and organ on  hundreds of popular British and American artists records from the 1960s to the 1990s. Most notably, he was featured on songs by  , the Kinks, the Who, the Beatles, the   Group, and Jefferson Airplane. His resume also includes   ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  , Peter Frampton,  , Graham Parker, and  , among others.

name: Cy Coleman
about: Cy Coleman began as a child prodigy, performing classical piano at Carnegie Hall before he was ten years old. He ended his career as a composer and pianist famous for his Broadway musicals and popular songs

name: Rocky Colavito
about: A baseball outfielder and nine-time All-Star. Colavito played for the Cleveland Indians, Detroit Tigers, Kansas City Athletics, Chicago White Sox, Los Angeles Dodgers, and New York Yankees during his long career.

name: Joe Pepitone
about: Played the bulk of his career for the New York Yankees, where he was thrice-named to play in the All-Star Game and also won three Golden Glove awards, and he became a cultural icon.

name: Earl Lloyd
about:
The First black person to play a game in the National Basketball Association, when he debuted for the Washington Capitols in the 1950-51 NBA season. 
 
Lloyd later played a major part in helping the Syracuse Nationals win the NBA Championship in 1955. He was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 2003.

name: Robert Duvall
about: , The Great Santini and Tender Mercies.

name: Willie Randolph
about: Willie Randolph is a former professional baseball player, coach, and manager, recognized for his long tenure as a second baseman and his leadership roles in Major League Baseball. During an 18-year baseball career, he played from 1975 to 1992 for six different teams, most notably the New York Yankees.

name: Ken Kutaragi
about: Ken Kutaragi is known as the "Father of the PlayStation" for creating Sony's video game console and revolutionizing the gaming industry.

name: Fred Lynn
about: Fred Lynn was an American baseball player known for his potent combination of hitting ability and defensive prowess, he was a vital player for several teams, most notably the Boston Red Sox and the California Angels.

name: Dorothy Hamill
about:
Dorothy Hamill won the Olympic gold medal for Women's Figure Skating in 1976. She was also the World Champion that year and the runner-up in 1974 and 1975. 
 
Hamill is credited with developing the camel spin move in her routines. After turning professional Hamill was a star performer in the travelling Ice Capades show from 1977-84.

name: Frank Bainimarama
about: Frank Bainimarama is a Fijian naval officer who served as the Prime Minister of Fiji from 2007 until 2022. He initially came to power through a military coup in 2006, claiming it was necessary to restore stability after years of racial tensions and corruption. This marked the beginning of a transitional period in Fiji's government, leading to a shift in the political landscape.

name: Denzel Washington
about: Denzel Washington has won two Academy Awards and is considered one of the greatest actors of his generation.

name: Wayne Grady
about: Best known for his PGA Championship win, one of golf's four majors, in 1990.

name: Gabe Newell
about: Gabe Newell, known affectionately as "Gaben" among gamers, co-founded Valve Corporation, a company that has created popular games such as the Half-Life series as well as the Steam digital distribution platform.

name: Sylvia Hanika
about: Sylvia Hanika reached the world's top five ranking in tennis and is best known for her appearance in the 1981 French Open final, as well as her victory in the 1982 Year-End Championships.

name: Ellen DeGeneres
about:
The star of the popular sitcom "Ellen" from 1994 to 1998.  
 
She has also hosted her own syndicated talk show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show" since 2003.

name: Mark Cerny
about: Mark Cerny is best known for his work on several PlayStation consoles and his innovative approach to game development.

name: Olaf Scholz
about: Olaf Scholz is the current Chancellor of Germany, a position he has held since December 2021. As a prominent member of the Social Democratic Party, Scholz has had a long and distinguished career in German politics.

name: Mike Weaver
about: Won 41 of 60 career fights and between March 1980 and December 1982 held the WBA  World Heavyweight Championship.

name: Bill James
about:
Since 1977, he has written numerous books devoted to baseball history and statistics.  
 
His approach, which he termed sabermetrics, scientifically analyzes and studies baseball, often through the use of statistical data, in an attempt to determine why teams win and lose.

name: Julius Erving
about: Helped launch a modern style of basketball that emphasizes leaping and play above the rim, and helped legitimize the American Basketball Association. He was the best-known player in that league when it merged with the NBA after the 1975–76 season. He won three championships and four Most Valuable Player Awards.

name: Rex Tillerson
about: Diplomat and former energy executive for ExxonMobil, Tillerson is the 69th US Secretary of State under President  .

name: John Candy
about:
Rose to fame as a member of the Toronto branch of The Second City, and through his appearances in comedy films, including "Cool Runnings" and "Spaceballs".  
 
Perhaps best known as Del Griffith, the loquacious salesman in "Planes, Trains and Automobiles".

name: Marina Sirtis
about: Marina Sirtis is a British actress best known for her role as Counselor Deanna Troi on the popular science fiction television series Star Trek: The Next Generation (1987-1994). Her character, a half-human, half-Betazoid empath, served as a bridge officer and ship's counselor, and Sirtis reprised the role in several subsequent Star Trek films and TV series.

name: Hideo Kojima
about: Hideo Kojima is best known for creating the Metal Gear series.

name: Loretta Lynch
about: Served as the 83rd Attorney General of the United States from 2015 to 2017, Lynch is a Harvard educated lawyer who as worked as both a government prosecutor and in the private sector.

name: Brian Cox
about: Brian Cox is a Scottish actor who is classically trained in the Shakespearean tradition but has also performed major roles in film and television. Most recently he has played Logan Roy in the series Succession since 2018, for which role he has received a Golden Globe and been nominated for an Emmy.

name: Stephen Harper
about: Harper was a Conservative Party politician and the 22nd Prime Minister of Canada, serving between 2006 and 2015.

name: Dave Cowens
about: Played 13 seasons in the NBA, twelve of them with the Boston Celtics, where he won Rookie of the Year (1971), League MVP award (1973), and two NBA Championships (1974 & 1976). He served as player-coach during most of the 1978-79 season, relinquishing the coach position for his final season before retiring in 1980.

name: Nelson Piquet
about: Three-time Formula One champion in 1981, 1983 and 1987.

name: Brad Garrett
about:
Best known for his role as the tall, deep voiced Robert Barone on Everybody Loves Raymond (1996-2005). 
 
Outside of this role Garrett starred in the sitcom 'Til Death from 2006 to 2010, and is prominent within the stand-up comedy and professional poker scenes.

name: Ray Nagin
about: Nagin served as the Mayor of New Orleans from 2002 until 2010. During his time in office, he became an international figure as a result of Hurricane Katrina and the devastating effects of the storm on the city.

name: Kim Campbell
about: Served as the 19th Prime Minister of Canada from June 1993 to November 1993. She was the first, and to date, only female Prime Minister of Canada.

name: Nils Lofgren
about: Nils is best known for his association as a guitarist for   and  , but is also adept at piano and accordion and has maintained a solo career as a singer-songwriter.

name: Christa Johnson
about: Christa Johnson is best known for her success on the LPGA Tour and Legends Tour. She won nine LPGA tournaments, including one major championship, and later found continued success in senior golf competitions.

name: Marcel Dionne
about: Played 18 seasons in the NHL for the Detroit Red Wings, Los Angeles Kings and New York Rangers, scoring over 700 goals.

name: Henri Leconte
about: Best known for reaching the men's singles final at the French Open in 1988. His career-high singles ranking was World No. 5.

name: Yoshihide Suga
about:
Yoshihide Suga was first elected to Japan's House of Representatives in 1996. After becoming a close ally of Shinzo Abe Suga was elected to cabinet in 2006 when Abe became Prime Minister.  
 
Suga served the country's longest-ever term as Chief Cabinet Secretary from 2012-2020, after which when he succeeded Abe as Prime Minister and as head of the Liberal Democratic Party.

name: George Gervin
about: Widely regarded to be one of the greatest shooting guards in NBA history, averaging at least 14 points per game in all 14 of his ABA and NBA seasons.

name: Zina Garrison
about: Best known for making the Wimbledon finals in 1990. She was also a three-time Grand Slam mixed doubles champion, and a women's doubles gold medalist at the 1988 Olympic Games.

name: Sherri Turner
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1984 and won three LPGA Tour events, including one major championship.

name: Jeffrey Hawkins
about: Jeff Hawkins is an American entrepreneur and neuroscientist, best known for his work in founding Palm Computing and creating the original Palm Pilot, a device that led the way in personal digital assistants (PDAs). His contributions significantly advanced handheld computing technology.

name: Bryan Stevenson
about: Bryan Stevenson is an American lawyer, social justice activist, and author who has made a significant impact in the fight against mass incarceration and racial inequality. He is the founder and executive director of the Equal Justice Initiative (EJI), a non-profit organization based in Montgomery, Alabama, that provides legal representation to prisoners who may have been wrongly convicted of crimes, poor prisoners without effective representation, and others who may have been denied a fair trial.

name: Hans Moravec
about: Hans Moravec is an Austrian-born American roboticist and computer scientist who has made significant contributions to the fields of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI). He is particularly known for his work in computer vision, robot perception, and the development of autonomous robots capable of navigating complex environments.

name: Haider al-Abadi
about: Haider al-Abadi is an Iraqi politician who served as Prime Minister of Iraq from 2014 to 2018. Before this he had served as Minister of Communication (2003-2004) in the first Iraqi government following the fall of  .

name: David Mamet
about:
Mamet is an American playwright and film director. His work begun first with a trio of plays in the 1970s, including 'The Duck Variations.'  
 
Later he has come to direct feature films: 'House of Games' (1987), 'Homicide' (1991), and 'The Spanish Prisoner' (1997).  
 
He is perhaps best known for 'Heist' (2001), which starred  ,  , and Delroy Lindo.

name: Vijay Singh
about: Singh is the only Fijian golfer to be successful on the PGA and European Tours.

name: Tony Fernandes
about:
Founder of Tune Air Sdn. Bhd., who bought a struggling AirAsia and turned it into the first budget no-frills airline in Malaysia with the now famous tagline "Now everyone can fly", 
 
He also helped arrange the open skies agreement with neighboring Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore.

name: Prince Edward
about: Prince Edward is the fourth and youngest child of   and Prince Phillip,  . His oldest brother is King  , and this places Edward at 13th in line of succession to the British throne.

name: Shelley Long
about: Played Diane Chambers on the long-running sitcom Cheers.

name: Steve Irwin
about: Steve Irwin was known as "The Crocodile Hunter." He gained worldwide fame for his wildlife documentaries and his hands-on approach to interacting with dangerous animals, often exclaiming "Crikey!" during close encounters.

name: Richard Jenkins
about:
Richard Jenkins is an American actor best known for playing Nathaniel Fisher on   (2001-2005). He has starred in a number of films, from The Witches of Eastwick (1987) and Little Nikita (1988) to Burn After Reading (2008) and The Last Shift (2020). 
 
Jenkins has been nominated for a variety of awards, from an Academy Award to a Screen Actors Guild Award, and has won an Emmy Award in 2014 for Olive Kitteridge.

name: Laura Davies
about: She has 84 professional wins worldwide, with 20 on the LPGA, including four majors, and is England's most accomplished modern female golfer.

name: Roger Deakins
about: English cinematographer Roger Deakins was nominated numerous times for the Academy Awards for Best Cinematography, the first was in 1994 for "The Shawshank Redemption". Deakins has won twice, at his 14th nomination for Denis Villeneuve's "  2049" and for  ' war epic "1917" in 2019.

name: Jim Carrey
about:
One of the most successful and recognizable American performers, Carrey's success began in the 1990s with leading roles in Ace Ventura: Pet Detective (1994), Dumb and Dumber (1994), Liar Liar (1997) and serious films such as The Truman Show (1998) and Eternal Sun of the Spotless Mind (2004). 
 
Other notable films include Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events (2004), Fun with Dick and Jane (2005), Yes Man (2008), Horton Hears a Who! (2008) and A Christmas Carol (2009).

name: François-Henri Pinault
about: François-Henri Pinault is the Chairman and CEO of Kering, a global luxury group. He has played a key role in transforming the company, formerly known as PPR, into a leading player in the luxury fashion industry.

name: Sunil Gavaskar
about: Sunil Gavaskar is one of cricket's most accomplished batsmen. He set numerous records and helped establish India as a major force in international cricket.

name: Corey Pavin
about: Corey Pavin was an American golfer known for his PGA Tour success and his role in the Ryder Cup. He secured a major victory at the 1995 U.S. Open and topped the PGA money list in 1991.

name: Fred Funk
about: Fred Funk is an American professional golfer who won the PGA Tour 8 times and now plays on the PGA Tour Champions. He is best known for winning the 2005 Players Championship, for which he was the oldest winner at 48 years, 9 months, and 14 days.

name: Viktor Orbán
about: Viktor Orban was born in Hungary in 1963. He earned a law degree at Péter Pázmány Catholic University in Budapest. After the fall of communism in Hungary, Orban became active in politics. He was elected to Hungary's parliament in 1990 and served as the country's Prime Minister from 1998 to 2002.

name: Jimmy Lai
about:
Founder of Giordano, an Asian clothing retailer and Next Digital, the largest Hong Kong listed media company.  
 
Among his publications is the popular newspaper Apple Daily known for its support of pro-democracy groups in Hong Kong.

name: Meg Mallon
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1987 and won 18 LPGA Tour events during her career, including four major championship.

name: Elizabeth Warren
about:
A member of the Democratic Party, Warren is currently the senior US Senator from Massachusetts.  
 
Prior to politics she was a Harvard Law School professor that specialized in bankruptcy law.

name: Ron Hextall
about:
Played 13 NHL seasons, 11 of which were for the Philadelphia Flyers.  
 
His mobile style of play, in which he provided support to his defencemen by coming out of the goal area to play the puck was revolutionary.  
 
Hextall was also known for being one of the NHL's most aggressive goaltenders, setting records for the number of penalty minutes by a goalie.

name: Bobby Flay
about: Bobby Flay is an American celebrity chef, restaurateur, and reality television personality. He is the owner and executive chef of several restaurants, including the eponymous Bobby Flay Steak in Atlantic City. He has appeared on numerous cooking shows, including Iron Chef America and Beat Bobby Flay.

name: Ilie Năstase
about:
One of the five players in history to win more than 100 ATP professional titles.  
 
Năstase won seven grand slam titles, two in singles, three in men's doubles and two in mixed doubles.

name: Mima Jausovec
about: Best known for winning the 1977 French Open singles championship.

name: Mikael Pernfors
about: Mikael Pernfors is a former professional tennis player from Sweden, known for his inventive baseline play and tactical style. He gained international recognition by winning consecutive NCAA singles titles in collegiate tennis in the United States.

name: Mike Shanahan
about: He has been the head coach of the Los Angeles Raiders, Denver Broncos and Washington Redskins. He led the Broncos to back-to-back Super Bowl victories in 1997 and 1998.

name: Shirin Ebadi
about: Shirin Ebadi was Iran's first female judge and the first Muslim woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Garth Brooks
about: Brooks is one of the greatest country music singer/songwriter successes of the early-1990s. His music blends rock and country influences.

name: Jamal Khashoggi
about: Jamal Khashoggi was a Saudi Arabian journalist, author, and a former general manager and editor-in-chief of the Al-Arab News Channel. He also served as editor for the Saudi Arabian newspaper Al Watan, turning it into a platform for Saudi progressives. Khashoggi gained international prominence for his outspoken and critical views on the Saudi government's policies, advocating for progressive reforms in the country.

name: Graham Norton
about:
Known for his flamboyant and innuendo-laden comedic style, Norton has hosted his eponymous BBC chat show since 2007. For his role as host he has won five BAFTA TV Awards. 
 
In addition to his television role he is a host on BBC Radio and is the BBC commentator for the Eurovision Song Contest.

name: Mo Yan
about:
Won the 2012 Nobel Prize in Literature for his work as a writer "who with hallucinatory realism merges folk tales, history and the contemporary" 
 
His famous works include the "Red Sorghum Clan" and "The Republic of Wine".

name: Michel Platini
about:
Platini is regarded as one of the all-time greatest football players, having won the Ballon d'Or three times (1983, 1984, 1985). He was also seventh in the FIFA Player of the Century vote.  
 
After retiring from football, Platini was the French national coach for four years and was later elected president of the UEFA. During his club career, Platini began with Nancy (1972–1979), then Saint-Étienne (1979–1982), and finally Juventus (1982–1987).

name: Dolly Parton
about: Dolly Parton, who was born one of 12 children to a poor sharecropper in Tennessee's Great Smoky Mountains, went on to build a career as one of the most beloved singer-songwriters in country music.

name: James Worthy
about:
Named as one of the 50 Greatest Players in NBA History, he played 12 seasons for the Los Angeles Lakers.  
 
During this career Worthy was a seven-time NBA All-Star, a three-time NBA champion and the 1988 NBA Finals MVP.

name: Eiji Aonuma
about: Eiji Aonuma is best known for his leading role in the development of "The Legend of Zelda" series.

name: Adam Yauch
about: Adam Nathaniel Yauch was an American rapper, bassist, and filmmaker, best known as a founding member of the hip hop group Beastie Boys.

name: Jack Morris
about: Jack Morris is a former outstanding professional baseball starting pitcher (1977-1994), mainly for the Detroit Tigers (1977-90).

name: Akio Toyoda
about: Akio Toyoda is a Japanese businessman who currently serves as president of the Toyota Motor Corporation. He is the great-grandson of  , the Japanese industrialist, and grandson of Kiichiro Toyoda, who founded Toyota Motors.

name: Hassan Rouhani
about: Hassan Rouhani is an Iranian politician who served as the seventh president of Iran, from 2013 to 2021. He is also a sharia lawyer, academic, former diplomat, and Islamic cleric.

name: Ozzy Osbourne
about: Rose to prominence in the early 1970s as the lead vocalist of the pioneering band Black Sabbath, whose dark and heavy sound has often been cited as key to the development of the heavy metal genre.  Following the band's break-up, he had a successful solo career.

name: Steve Elkington
about: Steve Elkington is best known for winning the 1995 PGA Championship and two Players Championships, as well as his smooth swing and putting ability.

name: Carl XVI Gustaf
about: Carl XVI Gustaf is the King of Sweden and the longest-reigning monarch in Swedish history. He became king in 1973 and has since worked to modernize the monarchy.

name: Nikolay Zimyatov
about: Won 4 Olympic gold and 1 silver medal at the 1980 and 1984 Olympic games.

name: Betsy King
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1977 and won six major championships and 34 LPGA Tour victories in all.

name: Miloslav Mečíř
about: Won the men's singles gold medal at the 1988 Olympic Games, and also played in two Grand Slam singles finals.

name: Tracy Chapman
about:
Multiple Grammy Award-winning folk-rock artist known for her stand-out performance at the London celebration concert for  's 70th birthday, and her song "Fast Car" and "Give Me One Reason".  
 
Chapman is also a human rights activist, working closely with Amnesty International and amfAR.

name: Guillermo Vilas
about: Considered one of the greatest South American tennis players ever, he won the U.S. Open, the French Open, and the Australian Open twice.

name: Helen Clark
about:
Clark was the 37th Prime Minister of New Zealand (1999-2008), and the second woman to hold that title. 
 
After her term in office, Clark served as the Administrator of the United Nations Development Programme (2009-2017).

name: Helen Hunt
about: Twister (1996), As Good as It Gets (1997) and The Sessions (2012).

name: Yun Fat Chow
about: Famous for his starring role in blockbuster films such as "The Killer", "Hard Boiled", and " ".

name: Kevin Costner
about: American actor who has won two Academy Awards, three Golden Globe Awards, and one Emmy Award, and has been nominated for three BAFTA (British Academy of Film and Television Arts) Awards.

name: Martin Short
about: Best known for his comedy work, particularly on the TV programs SCTV and Saturday Night Live, and for starring in many comedic films.

name: Cal Ripken Jr
about: Cal Ripken Jr. played 2,632 consecutive games for the Baltimore Orioles, breaking  's long-standing record of 2,130 games.

name: Johnny Bench
about:
Bench played in the MLB for 16 years with the Cincinnati Reds.  
 
A 14-time All-Star selection and a two-time National League Most Valuable Player, he was a key member of The Big Red Machine, which won six division titles, four National League pennants, and two World Series championships.  
 
He is widely considered to be the best catcher in MLB history.

name: Andrew Cuomo
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Andrew Cuomo is an American lawyer and politician, best known for serving as Governor of New York from 2011 to 2021. Where Andrew Cuomo was the 56th individual to serve in this position, his father Mario Cuomo had been the 52nd serving from 1983 to 1994. His brother, Chris Cuomo, was also a long-time news anchor with CNN.

name: Miranda Hart
about: Miranda Hart is an English actress, comedian, and writer best known for starring in her self-titled semi-autobiographical BBC sitcom "Miranda" (2009-15).

name: Brandon Sanderson
about: With over 40 published novels, Brandon Sanderson is one of the most successful fantasy and science fiction authors. He is best known for his Cosmere fictional universe, notably the Mistborn series and The Stormlight Archive. Through his expansive world-building, he created Sanderson's Laws of Magic, popularising the idea of "hard magic" and "soft magic" systems in the fantasy genre.

name: Mark Carney
about: As the second-youngest person to serve as governor of the Bank of Canada from 2008-13, Mark Carney has earned a reputation as a great economist and crisis manager. He led Canada through the 2008-9 recession and later became the first non-British governor of the Bank of England (2013-20).

name: Ashens
about: Stuart Ashen, known online as Ashens, first gained popularity for his reviews of low-quality products on his YouTube channel.

name: Rahul Dravid
about:
Widely regarded as one of the greatest batsmen in the history of cricket, Dravid was captain of the Indian team between 2004 and 2007.  
 
He was named player of the year by the ICC in 2004. He is the fourth-highest run scorer in Test cricket, and one of only three cricketers to score 10,000 runs in Tests and ODIs.

name: Bradley Cooper
about: Bradley Cooper is an actor, director and producer whose breakthrough role came in the 2009 film "The Hangover". He also  starred in its two sequels.

name: Ronnie O'Sullivan
about:
Widely considered the greatest natural talent and as one of the greatest players in the history of the game. He is the youngest person to win a ranking title - the 1993 UK Championship at age 17 - and the youngest to win the Masters, in 1995. 
 
O'Sullivan is known for his rapid playing style, ambivalence toward the sport, his proficiency with both left and right handed shots and his mercurial temperament.

name: Katie Holmes
about:
Katie Holmes is an American actress known for her roles in the TV series "Dawson's Creek" (1998-2003), and for film roles that include "Wonder Boys" (2000) and "Batman Begins" (2005).  
 
Holmes had a high profile marriage to fellow actor   before their divorce in 2012.

name: Todd Phillips
about: The film director, screenwriter and producer rose to fame as the director and co-producer of The Hangover trilogy of films. The films starred  , Ed Helms, Zach Galifianakis with the first film going on to win the Golden Globe for best comedy or musical film.

name: Drew Brees
about: Brees was born in Dallas, Texas, in 1979. His father, Eugene Wilson "Chip" Brees II, was a prominent trial lawyer; his mother, an attorney.

name: David Toms
about: David Toms is an American professional golfer best known for his success on the PGA Tour, with a record which includes 13 victories and a major title at the 2001 PGA Championship. He spent considerable time in the top 10 of the Official World Golf Ranking and played in team events like the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup.

name: Marat Safin
about: Marat Safin is a Russian professional tennis player and former politician. He has held the world No. 1 ranking and won two Grand Slam titles. Following his retirement from tennis, Safin transitioned into politics, serving as a member of the Russian Parliament before resigning.

name: Charlie Day
about: Charlie Day is an American actor, best known for his role as Charlie Kelly in the television series It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia (since 2005). Day co-created this show with Rob McElhenney and Glenn Howerton, who also feature in the roles of Mac and Dennis.

name: Isla Fisher
about: Began her acting career on Australian television, and has since been known for her comedic roles in "Wedding Crashers" (2005), "Hot Rod" (2007), and "Definitely, Maybe" (2008).

name: January Jones
about: January Jones is an American actress and model, best known for playing the role of Betty Draper in Mad Men (2007-2015). In this role she was the wife of Don Draper, played by  . This earned her an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series.

name: Jeremy Renner
about: Jeremy Renner is an American actor, best known for his role as Hawkeye in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He had a successful and critically-acclaimed film career prior to this, including his early work in independent films such as Dahmer (2002) and his Academy Award nomination for Best Actor in The Hurt Locker (2008).

name: Brian O'Driscoll
about: Brian O'Driscoll is an Irish rugby union player, best known as outside centre for Leinster and the Irish national team. He captained the latter team between 2013 and 2012, as well as serving as captain of the British & Irish Lions during their 2005 tour of New Zealand.

name: Kate Moss
about:
Kate Moss rose to fame in the early 1990s as part of the heroin chic fashion trend, and a reaction to the supermodels then dominating fashion. 
 
She is best known for her waifish figure and her campaigns for designers include  , Gucci, Dolce & Gabbana, Calvin Klein, Chanel and Rimmel. 
 
Moss has gone on to launch her own clothing lines,  perfume and work as a fashion director.

name: Tiësto
about: Tiësto is a Dutch DJ and record producer, known by many as the "  of EDM" and often found at the top of lists for the best DJ of all time. His career launched in earnest with his first solo album, In My Memory (2001), which gave rise to a number of major international hits.

name: Rick Astley
about: Rick Astley is an English singer-songwriter, best known for his hit song "Never Gonna Give You Up" (1987). The music video for this song became an internet meme in 2007, with "Rickrolling" referring to its unexpected appearance. This meme revitalized Astley's career, and he has since released a number of singles and albums.

name: Steve Nash
about: Point guard in the NBA known for his excellent passing skills. He was named the league's Most Valuable Player in 2005 and 2006.

name: Pedro Sánchez
about: Pedro Sánchez is a Spanish politician and, since 2018, the Prime Minister of Spain. He has also held the office of Secretary-General for the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party since 2017 (and from 2014 to 2016).

name: Alexander Huber
about: Alexander Huber is a German rock climber best known for scaling some of the world's toughest routes. He has made significant impacts in a variety of disciplines, ranging from sport climbing to big wall and free solo climbing.

name: Glenn McGrath
about: Glenn McGrath redefined fast bowling with his relentless accuracy and consistency. Nicknamed the "bowling machine," he helped establish Australia's cricket dominance through the 1990s and 2000s while setting records that still stand today.

name: Ben Ainslie
about: Ben Ainslie is a British sailor and the most successful Olympic sailor of all time. He has won five Olympic medals, including four golds, and is the only person to have won gold medals at five different Olympic Games. He has also won 11 world championships, more than any other sailor.

name: Lei Jun
about:
Considered the   of China, he is best known for founding Xiaomi Inc, one of China's largest technology companies. 
 
Jun has also been involved with several other successful Chinese companies such as Kingsoft and YY.

name: Andrew Symonds
about: Andrew Symonds, also known as "Roy," was an Australian cricketer known as an excellent all-rounder but particularly renowned as an aggressive batsman and as a fieldsman.   considered him the best fielder that he had ever seen, ranking Symonds even above Herschelle Gibbs and Jonty Rhodes.

name: Xavi
about: Xavier Hernández Creus, better known as Xavi, is a Spanish football player who has served as manager for the club Barcelona since 2021. Prior to this he was a renowned midfielder in his own right, still lauded for his passing and positioning.

name: Hansie Cronje
about:
Scored 3,714 runs and took 43 wickets over a 68 game test career for South Africa. Cronje also played in 188 ODIs. 
 
He received a life ban for match-fixing in 2000 and retired in disgrace.

name: Kid Rock
about: Devil Without a Cause

name: Kiefer Sutherland
about: Lost Boys, 24

name: Ricky Ponting
about: Ricky Ponting is one of the most successful captains in cricket history. He led the Australian national team to numerous victories, including two World Cup wins, and is considered one of the greatest batsmen of all time.

name: Christina Aguilera
about: Christina Aguilera has sold over 100 million records worldwide over the course of her career. She rose to fame in the late 1990s and has since become one of the best-selling music artists of all time.

name: Richard Hammond
homePlace: Solihull, West Midlands, England, United Kingdom
about: Richard Hammond is a British television presenter and journalist. He is best known for his work on the popular motoring show Top Gear, which he presented from 2002 to 2015.

name: Scott Weiland
about:
Weiland is Best known as the two-time lead singer of the Stone Temple Pilots (1989-2002, 2008-13).  
 
He was also a member of Velvet Revolver (2003-08), as well as having a solo and collaborative career before his tragic death.

name: Kenneth Mitchell
about: Kenneth Mitchell was a Canadian actor best known for his performance in Star Trek: Discovery (2017–2020), alongside efforts to raise awareness about health issues following his own diagnosis with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as  's Disease.

name: Jamie Foxx
about:
Starred in the films "Collateral", "Ray" and "Django Unchained". 
 
Foxx is also a Grammy Award-winning musician who has produced four top ten albums, Unpredictable (2005), Intuition (2008), Best Night of My Life (2010) and Hollywood: A Story of a Dozen Roses (2015).

name: Stéphane Charbonnier
about: Stéphane Charbonnier was editor of the French weekly satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo when he was killed in a terrorist attack by Islamic extremists on the newspaper's office in Paris in January 2015.

name: Jason Bateman
about:
Bateman is known for his roles as Michael Bluth on the comedy series Arrested Development (2003-6, 2013-present), for which he won a Golden Globe award.
