His numerous film roles include Up in the Air (2009), Extract (2009) The Switch (2010), Paul (2011) and Horrible Bosses (2011). More recently he has appeared on the Netflix series Ozark (2017-present).

name: Sergio García
about: Sergio García Fernández is a Spanish professional golfer who plays on both the PGA Tour and the European Tour.

name: Hristo Stoichkov
about: Hristo Stoichkov is a Bulgarian football player who is regarded as one of the best forwards of his generation, as well as the all-time best Bulgarian football player. He won the Ballon d'Or in 1994, as well as being runner-up for the FIFA World Player of the Year award in 1992 and 1994.

name: Junichi Masuda
about: Junichi Masuda is best known for his work on the Pokémon series, which he helped create and shape over many years.

name: Patrick Dempsey
about: Patrick Dempsey is best known for his role as Dr. Derek Shepherd on the television series "Grey's Anatomy" (2005-2015) and for starring in romantic comedies. Dempsey is also an accomplished auto racing competitor who has participated in the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

name: Arantxa Sánchez Vicario
about: Arantxa Sánchez Vicario achieved world No. 1 rankings in both singles and doubles, won 14 Grand Slam titles across various categories, and is the only tennis player to compete in five Olympics, winning four medals.

name: Ja Rule
about: Ja Rule is an American rapper known for his many singles between 1999 and 2005, including Between Me and You (2000), Always on Time (2001), and Mesmerize (2002). During this period he collaborated with Christina Milan,  , and Ashanti.

name: Jude Law
about: Jude Law is an English actor who first came to recognition for his role in The Talented Mr. Ripley (1999), for which he was nominated for an Academy Award and won a BAFTA Award. He would then go on to a number of other major roles, including in Enemy at the Gates (2001) and A.I. Artificial Intelligence (2001).

name: Ted Cruz
about: Ted Cruz is an American politician currently serving as United States senator from Texas. He has been involved in several high-profile controversies and legislative battles, including the 2013 government shutdown and the 2020 presidential election certification.

name: Richie McCaw
about: Richie McCaw is one of the greats of New Zealand Rugby Union.

name: DMX
about: DMX, born Earl Simmons, was hugely successful and influential rapper who produced a series of No. 1 albums in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

name: Sarah Paulson
about: Sarah Paulson is an American actress who has been active in the entertainment industry since 1994. She is best known for her roles in the television series American Horror Story,   Story, and Ratched, and the films   (2013), Ocean's 8 (2018), and Bird Box (2018).

name: Tommy Morrison
about: An American heavyweight boxer (nicknamed The Duke) and a former World Boxing Organization champion. He lost only three out of a total of 52 professional fights. Also appeared in the 1990   boxing film "Rocky V".

name: Shonda Rhimes
about: A film and TV showrunner, writer, producer and director Shonda Rhimes is one of the most influential figures in American entertainment.

name: Laurent-Désiré Kabila
about: Laurent-Désiré Kabila was a Congolese rebel leader and politician. He played a pivotal role in overthrowing the longtime dictator,  . Kabila subsequently became the country's president, serving from 1997 to 2001.

name: Jana Novotna
about: Played a serve and volley game, an increasingly rare style of play among women during her career, which helped her win the women's singles title at Wimbledon in 1998.

name: Susan Wojcicki
about: Susan Wojcicki played a key role in Google's growth and led YouTube as its CEO.

name: Luke Perry
about:
Luke Perry rose to fame in Aaron Spelling's teenage drama "Beverly Hills 90210", becoming a popular teen idol.  
 
Perry also appeared in "The Fifth Element" (1997) and the movie "Buffy the Vampire Slayer" (1992).

name: Karrie Webb
about: Won 14 LPGA Tour titles and 7 major titles including the US Open in 2000 and 2001.

name: Big Show
about: Big Show, born Paul Wight, is an American professional wrestler and actor, a seven-time world champion across World Championship Wrestling (WCW), the World Wrestling Federation (WWF), and World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE). He has been heavyweight champion twice each with the WCW and WWF/WWE.

name: Dave Matthews
about:
Songwriter, guitarist and lead vocalist of the Grammy Award-winning Dave Matthews Band since 1991, whose concerts have attracted over 20 million fans.  
 
Matthews was born and raised in South Africa, as well as in the United States and England.  
 
In 2001, he became a board member of "Farm Aid", an organization that uses music to raise awareness and provide benefits for agricultural causes.  
 
He is also a winemaker.

name: Kurt Angle
about: Kurt Angle is an American professional wrestler, actor, and retired amateur wrestler. He is a six-time world champion, having won the World Wrestling Federation/WWE Championship four times and the World Heavyweight Championship once. He is also a one-time United States Champion and a one-time Intercontinental Champion.

name: Mary Pierce
about: Won four Grand Slam titles, two in singles and two in doubles, including the 1995 Australian Open and the 2000 French Open.

name: Keith Flint
about:
Keith Flint was the frontman for the electronic music dance band The Prodigy. The group was a leading player in the UK rave scene in the 1990s.  
 
Flint started as the group's dancer on stage before contributing vocals from their third album. His vocals feature on many of the bands biggest hits including "Firestarter", and "Breathe".  
 
Flint was famous for his physical appearance, his horned hairstyle, piercings, tattoos and for his fierce vocal delivery.

name: Harold Pinter
about: Harold Pinter was the most influential British playwright of the second half of the 20th century. He was also a significant screenwriter, actor and director. In 2005 he was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature.

name: Rip Taylor
about: Comedian Rip Taylor's career started while he was in the US army and he performed for the troops during the Korean War. Afterwards he became a successful night club performer before first appearing on television on the   show in 1961.

name: Muhammadu Buhari
about: Muhammadu Buhari is a politician and former military leader who currently serves as the President of Nigeria. He is known for his long career in public service and his anti-corruption stance.

name: George A. Romero
about: George A. Romero was an influential American-Canadian filmmaker, writer, and editor, regarded by many as the "Father of the Zombie Film." He is best known for his series of gruesome and satirical horror films about a zombie apocalypse, beginning with the now-classic Night of the Living Dead (1968).

name: Ariel Sharon
about: Ariel Sharon was an Israeli general and politician, best known as the 11th Prime Minister of Israel (2001-2006). He began his career as a soldier and then an officer in the Israeli Army, described by   as "the greatest field commander in our history."

name: Nora Ephron
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Nora Ephron was born in New York City to playwrights and screenwriters Phoebe and Henry Ephron (Desk Set; Carousel; There's No Business Like Show Business), and raised in Beverly Hills, California.

name: Ross Perot
about: Ross Perot founded Electronic Data Systems (EDS) and ran for President of the United States as an independent candidate twice.

name: Sally Ann Howes
about: Sally Ann Howes is best known for her role as Truly Scrumptious in the movie "Chitty Chitty Bang Bang" (1968).

name: Jean Béliveau
about: Jean Béliveau was one of the most respected figures in ice hockey. He played for the Montreal Canadiens in the National Hockey League (NHL) for 20 seasons.

name: Burt Reynolds
about: A Hollywood heartthrob who starred in television series such as "Gunsmoke" and movies notably "Deliverance", "Smokey and the Bandit" and "Boogie Nights".

name: Bill Bixby
about:
Best known for his role as scientist Dr. David Banner on the CBS sci-fi drama series "The Incredible Hulk".  
 
Also starred in the television series' "My Favorite Martian", "The Courtship of Eddie's Father" and "The Magician".

name: Hayao Miyazaki
about: Hayao Miyazaki is a Japanese animator, filmmaker, and manga artist, recognized for his significant contributions to the animation industry. As the co-founder of Studio Ghibli, his compelling storytelling and unique artistic vision have made an international impact through his feature films.

name: Gordon Lightfoot
about: Achieved international success in folk, folk-rock, and country music, and has been credited for helping define the folk-pop sound of the 1960s and 1970s. Referred to as Canada's greatest songwriter and is known internationally as a folk-rock legend.

name: Gilberto Rodríguez Orejuela
about: Gilberto Rodríguez Orejuela co-led the Cali Cartel, which controlled much of the world's cocaine trade in the 1990s. Known as "The Chess Player" for his strategic thinking, Rodríguez Orejuela built a vast criminal empire all while keeping a low profile.

name: Kofi Annan
about: Annan served as the Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1997 until 2006. In 2001 he and the UN were recipients of the Nobel Peace Prize, and he served as chairman of The Elders, an organization founded by  .

name: Fela Kuti
about: Fela Kuti, also known as Abami Eda, was a Nigerian musician known for his early contributions to the Afrobeat genre which combined West African and American influences, notably funk and jazz.

name: Grace Kelly
about: Golden Globe and Oscar winning American stage and film actress who retired at age 26 to marry Price  , the absolute monarch of  Monaco.

name: Dennis Hopper
about: True Grit, Blue Velvet, Easy Rider

name: José Mujica
about: José Mujica is a former President of Uruguay (2010-15) known for his humble lifestyle and transformation from guerrilla fighter to national leader. He is often referred to as the "world's humblest president" due to his modest way of living and generous donations of his salary.

name: Sam Cooke
about: Sam Cooke was a prolific cross-genre singer, starting in gospel music and later turning to pop and becoming a pioneer of soul music.  He was also a songwriter and involved and invested in publishing, a rarity for artists of his era. He also used his popularity to advocate for civil rights.

name: Mike Nichols
about: Nichols  was a versatile entertainer, both o  stage and behind the scenes. He is one of 17 people to have won all four of the major American entertainment awards: Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony (EGOT).

name: Sheldon Adelson
about:
One of the richest people in the world with a net worth near $35 billion, Adelson is the founder and CEO of Las Vegas Sands, a casino and resort company. 
 
Adelson's company owns the Marina Bay Sands resort in Singapore, the Venetian Resort in Las Vegas, and a host of other luxury properties around the world.

name: Ernie Banks
about: Ernie Banks was an American professional baseball player who spent his entire 19-year Major League Baseball (MLB) career with the Chicago Cubs. He was a 14-time All-Star and won two Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards, known for his signature phrase, "Let's play two!"

name: Louise Fletcher
about: Gained international prominence for her performance as Nurse Ratched in the 1975 feature film "One Flew over the Cuckoo's Nest", for which she won the Academy Award for Best Actress.

name: Mel Stottlemyre
about: Mel Stottlemyre was a star pitcher in high school and was drafted by the Baltimore Orioles in 1959. He opted to play college ball at the University of Missouri instead.

name: Neil Diamond
about: American singer-songwriter with a career that began in the 1960s. His early success came as a songwriter, when his songs "I'm A Believer" and "A Little Bit Me, a Little Bit You" became hits for the Monkees.

name: Sergio Leone
about: Sergio Leone was widely regarded as one of the most influential film directors in history.  He was credited as the pioneer of the 'spaghetti Western' genre, with what became known as “The Dollars Trilogy” — “A Fistful of Dollars” (1964), “For a Few Dollars More” (1965) and “The Good, the Bad and the Ugly” (1966), all worldwide hits starring  .  The genre redefined the depictions and motivations of both heroes and villains in the American Old West.

name: Frank Robinson
about: Frank Robinson was a Baseball Hall of Fame outfielder who enjoyed a 20-year playing career with most notably the Cincinnati Reds (1956-65) and Baltimore Orioles (1966-71).

name: Malcolm Fraser
about: Malcolm Fraser was a three term Prime Minister of Australia (1975-83) and head of the Liberal Party for eight years.

name: Conway Twitty
about: Conway Twitty was an American country music singer and songwriter who enjoyed immense success in the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s. Known for his deep, resonant voice and heartfelt lyrics, Twitty released numerous chart-topping hits during his career and became one of the most popular country artists of his time.

name: David Frost
about: David Frost was a British television host, journalist, and writer known for his incisive interviews and engaging personality. He gained prominence in the United Kingdom during the 1960s as the host of the satirical television show That Was the Week That Was (1962-1963).

name: Anthony Perkins
about:
Best known for playing Norman Bates in  's "Psycho" and its three sequels.  
 
Perkins was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his second film, "Friendly Persuasion".

name: Billy Martin
about: Martin was a controversial Major League Baseball infielder and manager whose success was most famously linked with the New York Yankees, whom he managed for 5 stints.

name: Jeff Beck
about: Jeff Beck  was considered a guitarist's guitarist, widely respected for his innovative work with the English blues-rock band The Yardbirds, and his own Jeff Beck Group.

name: Alan Alda
about: Alan Alda's most famous role and the one that made him famous is as Hawkeye Pierce, a medic in the phenomenally successful and popular TV series M*A*S*H, adapted from the   movie. Alda starred in the series from 1973-1983, winning five Emmy awards and six Golden Globes. Alda eventually became part of the show's writing team, contributing to 19 episodes as well as directing 32 episodes.

name: Ennio Morricone
about: Ennio Morricone was a prolific composer across many genres, from classical to pop, but became internationally famous for his film scores, particularly for his former schoolmate  ’s 1960s so-called 'spaghetti westerns'.  What came to be known as “The Dollars Trilogy” — “A Fistful of Dollars” (1964), “For a Few Dollars More” (1965) and “The Good, the Bad and the Ugly” (1966), all starring   were worldwide hits.

name: Peter Thomson
about: Peter Thomson was an Australian professional golfer who is widely regarded as one of the greatest golfers to emerge from his country. He is remembered not only for his remarkable playing career but also for his contributions to the sport as a course designer, administrator, and writer.

name: Larry Flynt
about: American publisher and the president of Larry Flynt Publications (LFP), which mainly produces sexually graphic videos and magazines, most notably Hustler.

name: Ferguson Jenkins
about: Ferguson Jenkins was a Canadian baseball player, widely recognized as one of the finest pitchers in the history of Major League Baseball (MLB). Born in Canada, Jenkins stands out as the first Canadian to be inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame.

name: Jim Bouton
about: Jim Bouton transformed baseball literature and culture with his controversial book "Ball Four." While others saw him as a solid pitcher who adapted to injury, history remembers him as the man who pulled back the curtain on baseball's carefully crafted public image.

name: Willie Mays
about: Spent the majority of his MLB career as a center fielder with the New York and San Francisco Giants. He won two MVP awards and played in 24 All-Star Games.

name: Glen Campbell
about:
Campbell was one of the leading figures of country-pop during the 1960s and 1970s.  
 
Having established himself as a commercially successful solo artist by the late '60s he transitioned into acting with his debut on "The Glen Campbell Good Time Hour," making him an international star.

name: Michael Parkinson
about:
Described by The Guardian as "the great British talkshow host" he interviewed dozens of high profile celebrities over many decades. 
 
Parkinson was the host of his eponymous chat show from 1971 to 1982 and again from 1998 to 2007. He also ventured into other chat shows both internationally and nationally.

name: Elizabeth Montgomery
about: Film and TV actress with several Emmy nominations to her credit, but best remembered for playing the witch with the twitchy nose, Samantha, in Bewitched.

name: Stephen Hawking
about: Stephen Hawking made significant contributions to our understanding of black holes and the universe. He also became a well-known public figure, making complex science accessible to many people.

name: Joe Cocker
about: Joe Cocker found success with his 1968 cover of The Beatles song "With a Little Help from My Friends", which he sung at Woodstock in 1969 and became a soul anthem.

name: Maureen Connolly
about: Connolly is best known as the first woman to win all 4 Grand Slam tennis tournaments (Australian, French, US and Wimbledon) during the same calendar year (1953).

name: John Kerry
about: The 68th United States Secretary of State. He was also the candidate of the Democratic Party in the 2004 presidential election, losing to incumbent President  . He has served in the United States Senate, and was chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

name: Whitey Bulger
about: James "Whitey" Bulger led the Winter Hill Gang in Massachusetts. He spent 16 years on America's most wanted list, often as the No. 2 behind  .

name: Charles Strouse
about: The American composer and lyricist is most famous for his Broadway productions, including his first Broadway musical "Bye Bye Birdie" written with his long-time collaborator Lee Adams, which opened on Broadway in 1960. The musical about a teen singing idol joining the army, featured  , Chita Rivera, and Paul Lynde, and went on to win four Tony Awards including Best Musical.

name: Christopher Plummer
about: Christopher Plummer was known for his work in theater, film, and television over a career spanning seven decades. He notably achieved the Triple Crown of Acting, winning an Oscar, Emmy, and Tony Award.

name: Maria Bueno
about: First women to win all four Grand Slam double titles in one calendar year. She won 19 major titles, including the US Open Singles four times and Wimbledon Singles three times.

name: Samuel C. C. Ting
about: Samuel C. C. Ting shared the 1976 Nobel Prize in Physics with Burton Richter for discovering a new subatomic particle called the J/ψ meson. He currently leads the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS) experiment on the International Space Station, a major project searching for antimatter, dark matter, and studying cosmic rays.

name: Curt Flood
about: Flood was a baseball center fielder who played variously for the Cincinnati Redlegs, St. Louis Cardinals, and Washington Senators. During this time he was an All-Star three times and won the Gold Glove for seven seasons in a row.

name: Pervez Musharraf
about: Seized power in a bloodless coup in 1999 and later was elected President of Pakistan, ruling between 2001 and 2008.

name: Tom Seaver
about: Tom Seaver spent most of his 20-year career with the New York Mets. He was known for his exceptional pitching skills, which earned him three   Awards and led to his induction into the Baseball Hall of Fame with a record-breaking vote percentage at the time.

name: Lynn Redgrave
about: Lynn Redgrave was an English actress who performed on Broadway and in several films, including   (1963) and Georgy Girl (1966). She won two Golden Globe Awards, one for her role in Georgy Girl for which she was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress.

name: Nate Thurmond
about:
Dominant at both center and power forward, he is one of the greatest rebounders and shot blockers in NBA history.  
 
He was a seven-time All-Star and the first player in NBA history to record an official quadruple-double.

name: Kurt Nielsen
about: The only Danish tennis player ever to have played in a Men's Singles final in a Grand Slam tournament when he reached the singles finals of Wimbledon in 1953.

name: Mickey Wright
about:
Wright turned professional in 1954 and became a member of the tour in 1955, winning thirteen major championships throughout her career with a total of 90 professional wins. 
 
Wright currently holds the record for the most victories in the Women's PGA Championship with 4, and holds the second most LPGA Tour wins after  , with 82 wins.

name: Willie Davis
about:
Davis played Major League Baseball for most of his career as a center fielder for the Los Angeles Dodgers.  
 
During this time, he won a variety of awards (including Gold Gloves from 1971–1973) and established himself in major league history (seventh in putouts and total chances in the outfield, third in games in center field).  
 
Most notably, he achieved a 31-game hitting streak in 1969—the longest by a Dodger, beating Zack Wheat’s previous record of 29.

name: Stephen Sondheim
about: , Company, A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum

name: Tony Trabert
about: Considered one of the greatest tennis players of all time, Trabert won five Grand Slam singles titles, including the French Open twice and the U.S. Open twice.

name: Rod Taylor
about: The Australian actor moved to Los Angeles in 1954 and when on to become a Hollywood star with lead roles in "The Time Machine" and  's film "The Birds" opposite Tippi Hedren.

name: Kathy Whitworth
about:
Whitworth won 88 LPGA Tour tournaments, more than anyone else has won on either the LPGA Tour or the PGA Tour.  
 
She also became the first woman to reach career earnings of $1 million on the LPGA Tour.

name: Bernardo Bertolucci
about: Bernardo Bertolucci was the son of a poet and initially became a poet himself winning an Italian literary prize.

name: Gnassingbé Eyadéma
about: Gnassingbé Eyadéma was a Togolese political leader who served as the President of Togo from 1967 until his death in 2005. His tenure of nearly 38 years made him one of the longest-serving heads of state in modern African history. Eyadéma's rule was characterized by a strong personalistic regime and was marked by allegations of authoritarianism and human rights abuses.

name: Dick Cheney
mainType: Vice President of the United States
about: Cheney served Vice President of the United States under   (2001-2009). In this position he was crucial to the conduct of both the War in Afghanistan and the Iraq War, as well as coordinating operations associated with the Global War on Terror.

name: Abebe Bikila
about: Abebe Bikila was an Ethiopian marathon runner renowned for winning two Olympic marathons in a row. Bikila is regarded as a national hero in Ethiopia, as Africa's first world record breaking athlete in any sport and the first sub-Saharan African Olympic gold medallist.

name: William Safire
about: He is best known as a long-time syndicated political columnist for the New York Times and the author of "On Language" in the New York Times Magazine.

name: Bob Cleary
about: A member of the American 1960 Winter Olympics team that won the gold medal. He was inducted into the United States Hockey Hall of Fame in 1981.

name: Shirley Temple
about: Shirley Temple was Hollywood's most famous child star. In films such as "Bright Eyes" (1934), "Curly Top" (1935) and "Heidi" (1937) she dominated the box office in the 1930s. From 1935-1938 she was the leading Hollywood star.

name: Brooks Robinson
about: Robinson played for the Baltimore Orioles for his entire 23-year MLB career (1955-77). He was appeared in 18 All-Star games, won 16 Gold Glove Awards for his fielding., and was American League MVP in 1964.  He set 7 team records - all later surpassed by  , Jr.

name: Corazon Aquino
about: Named the “Mother of Philippine Democracy”, Aquino was the 1st woman to become President of the Philippines and the most prominent figure of the 1986 People Power Revolution that toppled the 20-year authoritarian rule of  .

name: Dick Clark
about:
Best known for hosting "American Bandstand" from 1957 to 1987.  
 
Also hosted the game show "Pyramid" and "Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve, which transmitted Times Square's New Year's Eve celebrations", and was well known for his trademark sign-off, "For now, Dick Clark. So long!", accompanied with a military salute.

name: Anne Bancroft
about: An American actress associated with the method acting school, which she had studied under Lee Strasberg. Respected for her acting prowess and versatility, she was often acknowledged for her work in film, theatre and television.

name: Little Richard
about: Little Richard was one of rock n' roll's most influential early performers. His sound and music went on to have a strong influence of such artists as The Beatles,   and  .

name: Donna Caponi
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1965 and won four major championships and 24 LPGA Tour career events.

name: Arnold Palmer
about:
Considered one of the greatest players in the history of golf, Palmer was one of the Big Three - along with   and   - who greatly popularized golf in the 1950s and 60s. 
 
In his career he won 62 PGA Tours and was one of the original 13 inductees to the World Golf Hall of Fame.

name: Phil Niekro
about: No-hitter 1973; 5 x MLB All Star; 5 x Gold Glove; Milwaukee / Atlanta Braves

name: Maggie Smith
about: Maggie Smith achieved success as an actress on stage, in film, and on television over a career spanning more than seven decades. She came to global fame with her roles as Professor McGonagall in the   film series and Violet Crawley in " ."

name: Tammy Wynette
about: Tammy Wynette was a country music singer known as the "First Lady of Country Music." She rose from poverty to become one of the genre's most influential voices.

name: Emmett Till
about: Emmett Till was a young African American who was brutally murdered in Mississippi at the age of 14 after being falsely accused of offending a white woman in her family's grocery store. The brutality of his murder and the fact that his killers were acquitted drew attention to the long history of violent persecution of African Americans in the United States.

name: Carlos Slim
about: Carlos Slim has built a business empire spanning telecommunications, retail, and other industries, becoming one of the world's richest people.

name: Philippe de Broca
about:
French film director of mostly comedic adventure style films such as "That Man from Rio" (1964) with  . It was one of six films he would make with Belmondo. 
 
His film King of Hearts (Le Roi de Cœur)(1966) wasn't well received upon release but has gone on to become a cult favourite.

name: Buddy Holly
about: Although only 22 when he died in a plane crash during a tour of the midwest US,  Buddy Holly remains one of the most influential rock and roll musicians.

name: Richard Belzer
about: Richard Belzer is an American stand-up comedian and actor best known for his role as Detective John Munch. He first played this character on the NBC police drama Homicide: Life on the Street (1993-1999) and then later on Law & Order: Special Victims Unit (1999-2016).

name: Ted Hughes
about: One of the best poets of his generation, he was British Poet Laureate from 1984 until his death. He was also well known for being married to American poet  .

name: Joe Frazier
about:
Emerged as the top contender in the late 1960s, defeating multiple opponents en route to becoming Undisputed Heavyweight Champion in 1970.  
 
In 1971, he defeated   by unanimous decision in the highly anticipated "Fight of the Century".

name: Hank Aaron
about:
Played 21 seasons for the Milwaukee and Atlanta Braves (1954-1974) and 2 final years for the Milwaukee Brewers as a right fielder and a star hitter.  
 
In 1974 he bettered  's home run record amid some racist attacks and held it for 33 years. Aaron continues to hold the record for the most seasons as an All Star (21).

name: Leonard Nimoy
about: Commander Spock (Star Trek); not to be confused with Dr  .

name: Vidal Sassoon
about: Vidal Sasson grew up in poverty in London before going on to become one of the world's first celebrity hairdressers. He is remembered for championing short hair for woman in a new easy-care style and popular cuts associated with him include the bob, the five-point cut and the pixie cut worn by the likes of  , Grace Coddington and  .

name: Dale Murphy
about: Dale Murphy was an outstanding American professional baseball utility who had a highly credentialed 18-year career in the major leagues.

name: Geoffrey Rush
about: Geoffrey Rush is an Australian actor known for his extensive work in theatre and film, from "Pirates of the Caribbean" (2003) to "The King's Speech" (2010). He began acting in local Australian theatre, gaining experience in ensemble productions and developing a disciplined, collaborative approach to performance.

name: Ice-T
about:
Ice-T is an American rapper known for his hip-hop and heavy metal music and also for playing Odafin Tutuola on Law & Order: Special Victims Unit since 2000.  
 
He started out as an underground rapper in 1980s and was often controversial, particularly for his release of "Cop Killer" (1992) with the heavy metal band, Body Count.

name: Mike Babcock
about: One of the winningest coaches in hockey history, he is the only coach to gain entry to the Triple Gold Club: winning the Stanley Cup in 2008, Olympic Gold in 2010 and 2014, and the IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship in 2004. He is the only coach to win five national or international titles.

name: Imran Khan
about: Khan started his career as one of the most successful and admired cricketers in Pakistan, played international cricket for two decades and such was his popularity was elected Prime Minister of Pakistan 2018.

name: Yoshua Bengio
about: Yoshua Bengio is a Canadian computer scientist and artificial intelligence (AI) researcher who has made significant contributions to the field of deep learning, particularly in the development of neural network architectures and learning algorithms. He is a co-founder of the Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms (MILA) and a leading figure in AI research, with a focus on deep learning techniques and their applications.

name: Evo Morales
about: Morales was President of Bolivia from 2006 to 2019, in which he was the first indigenous Bolivian to hold this office. His administration was characterized by their left-wing politics, which sought to push back against American and corporate influence in Bolivia.

name: Graham Gooch
about: In 2000 Graham Gooch became the highest scoring batter of all time with  67,057 runs in first class and limited-overs cricket. Gooch is also one of only 25 players to hit over 100 first-class centuries.

name: John Key
about: Key served as Prime Minister of New Zealand from 2008 to 2016. Elected amidst the global financial crisis, much of Key's first term was marked by attempts to stabilize the economy and reduce the fallout from the credit crunch.

name: Larry Bird
about: Larry Bird led the Celtics to three NBA championships and is considered one of the greatest players in NBA history. He is the only person in NBA history to be named Most Valuable Player, Coach of the Year, and Executive of the Year.

name: Grant Dalton
about: Grant Dalton is a New Zealand businessman and yachtsman. He is the CEO of Emirates  , a professional sailing team that competes in the America's Cup.

name: Edie Falco
about: Edie Falco is an American actress who came to fame with her portrayal of Carmela Soprano in the critically acclaimed HBO series The Sopranos (1999-2007), a role that earned her multiple Emmy Awards. Her portrayal of Carmela, the wife of mob boss Tony Soprano played by  , was a standout performance.

name: Maria Ressa
about:
Ressa is a Filipino-American journalist, known for founding Rappler—a Philippines-based newspaper. She came to the world's attention after being convicted of cyberlibel in 2020.  
 
Since then she has come to symbolize the perils of press freedom in an age of growing authoritarianism.  
 
Prior to her conviction, Ressa was named among Time magazine's 2018 Person of the Year as one of a cohort of journalists worldwide dedicated to the fight against fake news.

name: Shinzō Abe
about: Shinzo Abe served as Prime Minister of Japan for nearly nine years, the longest tenure in the country's history. He was known for his economic policies and efforts to strengthen Japan's military position.

name: Tsai Ing-wen
about: Tsai Ing-wen became Taiwan's first female leader upon her election in 2016. She was re-elected to a second term in 2020.

name: John Elway
about: One of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history, he led the Denver Broncos to five Super Bowl appearances and two victories. He was known for performing his best in the clutch, thanks in large part to the 1987 AFC Championship Game against the Cleveland Browns where he helped engineer a 98-yard, game-tying touchdown drive, which would become known as "The Drive".

name: Mike Eruzione
about: Best known as the captain of the 1980 Winter Olympics United States national team that defeated the Soviet Union in the famous " " game, in which he scored the game-winning goal.

name: Howard Johnson
about: Best known for playing for the New York Mets in the MLB, where he is third on the Mets' all-time lists for home runs, runs batted in, doubles, and stolen bases.

name: Eric Heiden
about: Eric Heiden is an American speed skater and physician who won an unprecedented five gold medals in speed skating at the 1980 Winter Olympics, setting four Olympic records and one world record in the process. His feat of winning gold in every distance, from the 500 meters to the 10,000 meters, remains unmatched in the history of Olympic speed skating.

name: John F. Kennedy Jr.
about:
Son of U.S. President   and First Lady  , and a nephew of Senators   and  .  
 
He died in a plane crash along with his wife Carolyn Jeanne Bessette and her elder sister Lauren on July 16, 1999.

name: Jane Campion
about: Jane Campion is a New Zealand screenwriter, producer, and director. She is the second of five women ever nominated for the Academy Award for Best Director and is the first New Zealand director to be nominated for the award. Campion is also the only female director to win the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival.

name: Nate Archibald
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Nate Archibald spent 14 years playing in the NBA, and was a willing passer and an adequate shooter from midrange.  
 
He was however best known for his quickness and speed that made him difficult to guard in the open court.  
 
He is the only player to lead the league in scoring and assists in the same season.

name: Bill Maher
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Bill Maher is an American political commentator and comedian. Maher's career in the entertainment industry spans several decades, during which he has established himself as one of the leading voices in American political comedy.

name: Jari Kurri
about: A five-time Stanley Cup champion, he played 21 seasons in the NHL with five different teams. In Edmonton he played on the same line as  , and the duo became one of the most prolific scoring tandems ever to play in the NHL.

name: Melanie Griffith
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: The daughter of   actress Tippi Hedren, Melanie Griffith forged her own path, becoming a successful actress by the 1980s.

name: Larry Fink
about: Larry Fink is the co-founder, chairman, and CEO of BlackRock, the world's largest money-management firm. He has become a significant figure in global finance, known for his influence on corporate governance and investment strategies.

name: Bo Jackson
about: Bo Jackson was one of the greatest multi-sport athletes of all time.

name: Paul O'Neill
about:
Won five World Series while playing for the Cincinnati Reds (1985–1992) and New York Yankees (1993–2001).  
 
He is the only player to have played on the winning team in three perfect games.

name: Richard Linklater
about:
His films typically revolve around personal relationships and the passage of time, and sometimes even include the same actors filmed over several years, such as the film "Boyhood".  
 
Also known for "Dazed and Confused", the romantic drama film trilogy "Before Sunrise", "Before Sunset", and "Before Midnight", and "School of Rock".

name: George Foreman
about: George Foreman was a surprise winner at the 1968 Olympic Games when he won the heavyweight gold medal at age 19. After turning professional he quickly fought his way through the ranks, winning the heavyweight title in 1973 against  . He successfully defended his title twice before losing for the first time professionally to   in a famous bout known as "the Rumble in the Jungle" in Zaire in 1974.

name: Dianne Wiest
about: Dianne Wiest is an American actress who first gained prominence in the 1980s, appearing in several   films, including Hannah and Her Sisters (1986) and Radio Days (1987).

name: Peter Molyneux
about: Peter Molyneux is best known for his highly innovative games, including "Black and White" (2001) and "Fable" (2004).

name: Gary Sinise
about: Gary Sinise is an American actor, director, and musician. He co-founded the Steppenwolf Theatre Company and is celebrated for his roles in films such as Forrest Gump (1994) and Apollo 13 (1995), as well as his Emmy-winning performances in Truman (1995) and   (1997).

name: Rosanna Arquette
about: Rosanna Arquette is part of an acting family that includes her siblings Patrica, David and Alexis Arquette. She won a BAFTA award for her supporting role in the 1985 hit film "Desperately Seeking Susan" opposite  . She has also featured in films such as   's "After Hours and  's " ".

name: Robert Parish
about: Robert Parish was an outstanding and imposing basketball center who played 21 seasons in the NBA, tied for second most behind Vince Carter with 22.

name: Mukesh Ambani
about: Mukesh Ambani is an Indian business tycoon known for his role as the chairman and managing director of Reliance Industries, one of India's most significant conglomerates. As of 2024, he is the richest person in Asia and ranks 11th globally with a net worth of $112.1 billion.

name: Dennis Lillee
about: Dennis Lillee is an Australian cricketer who is widely regarded as one of the greatest fast bowlers in the history of the sport. His fearsome pace, impeccable accuracy, and aggressive playing style made him a formidable opponent during his international career, which spanned from 1971 to 1984.

name: Pat Sajak
about: Host of the American television game show "Wheel of Fortune", a position he has held since 1981.

name: George Galloway
about: George Galloway is a British politician, broadcaster, and writer. His career is marked by his tenure as a Member of Parliament, leadership of the Respect Party, and frequent media appearances. Notable for his opposition to the Iraq War, Galloway has been involved in various international issues and has encountered significant political and public backlash for his views.

name: Danny Meyer
about: Danny Meyer is an American restaurateur, author, and business executive best known as the founder and CEO of Union Square Hospitality Group (USHG), which manages a diverse portfolio of award-winning restaurants in New York City.

name: Joe Carter
about: Former MLB outfielder who played from 1983 to 1998. Most famous for hitting a walk-off home run to win the 1993 World Series for the Toronto Blue Jays.

name: Grant Fuhr
about:
Best remembered for a decade of stellar play for the Edmonton Oilers in the 1980s.  
 
Fuhr backstopped the team to four Stanley Cups in five seasons.  
 
He is the first black hockey player to be inducted into the Hall of Fame.

name: Condoleezza Rice
about: Condoleezza Rice is an American diplomat, particularly during the administration of President  . She held multiple high-ranking positions, including National Security Advisor from 2001 to 2005 and Secretary of State from 2005 to 2009. She was the first African-American woman to hold either position.

name: Tom Lehman
about: Tom Lehman was the first golfer to earn Player of the Year honors on all three PGA Tour circuits: the regular PGA Tour, the developmental Korn Ferry Tour, and the Champions Tour.

name: Liam Neeson
about:
Neeson gained fame when he starred as   in  's 1993 film  's List. This performance garnered him an Academy Award for Best Actor nomination. 
 
He then went on to lead roles in   Episode I: The Phantom Menace (1999), the Taken film series (2008-14) and the historical drama Silence (2016).

name: Oprah Winfrey
about: Winfrey began her media career in radio before becoming a news anchor and launching her show 'The Oprah Winfrey Show' in 1986. It ran until 2011 and is credited with popularizing the talk show format and introducing a new confessional style.

name: Gordon Brown
about: Brown served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Labour Party from 2007 until 2010. Prior to assuming this position, he was Chancellor of the Exchequer in the government of  .

name: James Woods
about:
James Woods is an esteemed actor who often portrays villains. His major film roles include "Once Upon a Time in America" (1984), "Casino" (1995), both with  . 
 
Woods has won three Emmy awards for television movies and for the animated series "Hercules". Woods also won a Golden Globe in 1987 for his role in "Promise".

name: Peggy Fleming
about: Won an Olympic gold medal in 1968 and the World Ladies Figure Skating Championship three times.

name: John Stockton
about: Spent his entire NBA career as a point guard for the Utah Jazz, from 1984 to 2003. Regarded as one of the best point guards of all time, he holds the NBA records for most career assists and steals by considerable margins.

name: Jamie Lee Curtis
about: American actress who made her name as a "scream queen" in such horror films as  's "Halloween" (1978). Curtis then went on to broaden her range, appearing in such comedic films as "A Fish Called Wanda" (1988) and True Lies" (1994), for which she won a Golden Globe award.

name: Doug Flutie
about: Heisman Trophy 1984, Boston College; Grey Cup MVP 1992, 96, 97; Pro Bowl 1998, Buffalo Bills

name: Christopher Meloni
about: Christopher Meloni is an American actor known for his work in both television and film. He gained prominence for his role as Detective Elliot Stabler on the long-running NBC crime drama series Law & Order: Special Victims Unit (1999-2011, 2021-present), for which he earned an Emmy nomination.

name: Keith Hernandez
about:
The starting first baseman on two World Series championship teams: the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982 and the New York Mets in 1986.  
 
Hernandez was known for his ability to hit the ball in all parts of the ballpark, especially the opposite way, and for his terrific defense.

name: Sitiveni Rabuka
about: Sitiveni Rabuka is a Fijian politician, best known as the Prime Minister of Fiji since 2022. He has served as Prime Minister of Fiji once prior, from 1992 to 1999, as well as serving variously as Chairman of the Great Council of Chiefs (1999-2001) and Chairman of the Cakaudrove Provincial Council (2001-2008).

name: Diane Keaton
about: Diane Keaton came to fame in the 1970s through her collaborations with   and maintained a successful career in film for over five decades.

name: Naruhito
about: Naruhito is the current Emperor of Japan, reigning in the Reiwa era, which began on the day of his accession, May 1, 2019. He succeeded his father Emperor   who announced his abdication on April 30, 2019, the first emperor to do so since 1817.

name: Valerie Bertinelli
about: Played Barbara Cooper Royer in the sitcom "One Day at a Time" and as Melanie Hope Moretti in the sitcom "Hot in Cleveland".

name: Thomas Hearns
about: The first boxer to win world titles in 5 different weight divisions.

name: Nick Faldo
about:
A top player of his era, renowned for his single-minded dedication to the game, he was ranked No. 1 on the Official World Golf Ranking for a total of 97 weeks.  
 
He won 40 events in total including six major championships (three Open Championships and three Masters).

name: Sally Little
homePlace: Cape Town, Western Cape Province, South Africa
about: Sally Little is regarded as one of the finest female golfers from South Africa.

name: Brendan Gleeson
about: Brendan Gleeson is an Irish actor known for his versatile performances across various film genres, from dramas and comedies to action-packed blockbusters.

name: Farrah Fawcett
about: Farrah Fawcett was one of the original cast of TV crime drama "Charlie's Angels", alongside   and  . She left the series in a shock move after one season, and was replaced by Cheryl Ladd.

name: Cathy Moriarty
about: Cathy Moriarty is an American actress whose career has spanned over four decades in both film and television. She made an unforgettable debut at the age of 19, playing the role of Vickie LaMotta in  's boxing film   (1980), a performance that earned her an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress.

name: Kevin Spacey
about: Began his career as a stage actor during the 1980s, before being cast in supporting roles in film and television. Best known for his roles in "The Usual Suspects", " ", and " ".

name: David Bowie
about: One of the most popular musicians for over five decades, Bowie sold over 140 million records worldwide and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. In his career he released eleven number-one albums.

name: Susan Boyle
about: Susan Boyle is a Scottish singer who gained worldwide fame after her unforgettable audition on the reality show Britain's Got Talent in 2009. Her powerful rendition of "I Dreamed a Dream" from the musical Les Misérables stunned the judges and audience, quickly becoming a viral sensation.

name: Zaheer Abbas
about: Zaheer Abbas was a Pakistani cricketer known for his prolific scoring and stylish play. His distinguished career included achieving the milestone of three consecutive centuries in one-day internationals.

name: Marilu Henner
about: Marilu Henner is an American actress, producer, radio host, and author. She gained fame for her role as Elaine O'Connor Nardo in the popular television sitcom Taxi (1978-1983), which earned her five Golden Globe nominations. Henner has appeared in numerous other TV shows and films, including Evening Shade (1990-1994) and L.A. Story (1991).

name: Sridevi Kapoor
homePlace: Sivakasi, Madras State (present-day Tamil Nadu), India
about:
Sridevi is one of Indian cinema's most popular actresses who hit first the screens in the 1960s at the age of 4.  
 
While she appeared in about 300 films over her career, some of Sridevi's best known films include Chaalbaaz, Himmatwala, Mr. India, Chandni, and English Vinglish.  
 
In 2013 she was awarded India's fourth-highest civilian award, the Padma Shri, for her services to the film industry

name: Robert Carlyle
about: Known for variety of roles in films such as  , The Full Monty, and The World Is Not Enough.

name: Sean Penn
about: Fast Times at Ridgemont High (1982), Dead Man Walking (1995), Mystic River (2003), Milk (2008)

name: Bryan Trottier
about: Played 18 seasons in the NHL for the New York Islanders and Pittsburgh Penguins. He won four Stanley Cups with the Islanders, two with the Penguins and one as an assistant coach with the Colorado Avalanche. He holds the NHL record for points in a single period with 6.

name: Maurice Gibb
about:
Achieved international fame as guitarist of the  .  
 
Although his brothers   and   were the band's primary lead vocalists, most of the group's albums included at least one or two of his compositions.

name: Janet Yellen
about: Janet Yellen is an American economist who was the first woman to serve as Chair of the Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States, from 2014 to 2018. Her term as Chair followed a long career in academia and public service, and she is widely respected for her understanding of economic issues.

name: Allan Border
about: Allan Border is a former outstanding left-hand opening batsman and long-term captain of the Australian cricket team.

name: Carlos Lehder
about: Carlos Lehder co-founded the Medellín Cartel known for revolutionizing the cocaine trade in the 1970s and 1980s. He pioneered the use of small aircraft to transport cocaine from Colombia to the United States, a method that transformed the drug smuggling industry.

name: Roberto Benigni
about: Roberto Benigni is an Italian actor and comedian best known for writing, directing, and starring in the Holocaust comedy-drama film "Life Is Beautiful" (1997), which earned him Academy Awards for both Best Actor and Best International Feature Film.

name: Pat Bradley
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1974. She won 31 tour events and six major championships.

name: Gary Oldman
about: Gary Oldman rose to fame on the British stage in roles for the Royal Court Theatre from 1984 and the Royal   Company 1985-1986. Oldman's breakthrough film role came in the 1986 film "Sid and Nancy' in which he portrayed Sex Pistol musician  .

name: Nigel Mansell
about: World Formula 1 champion in 1992 and Indy Car World Series in 1993.

name: Pat Day
about: Pat Day is a National Museum of Racing and Hall of Fame jockey with an illustrious 32-year career spanning 1973 to 2005. Known as a patient rider he often came with late runs in big spots and had a reputation for saving horse for the stretch.

name: Brett Hull
about:
Known as one of the game's greatest snipers, his career total of 741 goals is the third highest in NHL history, and he is one of five players to score 50 goals in 50 games.  
 
Hull was a member of two Stanley Cup winning teams, and his championship winning goal for Dallas in overtime of game six of the 1999 Stanley Cup Finals is one of the most controversial in league history.

name: Eddie Murray
about:
Spending most of his MLB career with the Baltimore Orioles, he ranks fourth in team history in both games played and hits.  
 
Murray was elected into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2003.

name: Alfonso Cuarón
about: Alfonso Cuarón is a Mexican film director, screenwriter, producer, and editor. He is best known for his films Y Tu Mamá También (2001),   and the Prisoner of Azkaban (2004), Children of Men (2006), and Roma (2018).

name: Curtly Ambrose
about: Curtly Ambrose is an Antiguan cricketer who is regarded as one of the best fast bowlers in the history of the game. Standing at 6’7”, his height allowed him to generate a steep bounce which combined with his unerring accuracy made things very difficult for the batsmen he opposed.

name: Ken Dryden
about:
Although Dryden only played nine seasons in the NHL, he won the Vezina Trophy five times, and his statistical percentages are unparalleled.  
 
He won six Stanley Cups with the Montreal Canadiens. 
 
Dryden later entered politics, becoming a Liberal Party MP and later Minister of Social Development.

name: Colin Montgomerie
about: Colin Montgomerie is known for his dominance on the European Tour and his exceptional Ryder Cup record. He is considered one of the best players never to win a major championship.

name: Larry Nelson
about: Won numerous tournaments at both the PGA Tour and Champions Tour level, including the 1983 U.S. Open and 1981 and 1987 PGA Championships.

name: George Strait
about: George Strait is an American country music singer, songwriter, and music producer. Known as the "King of Country Music," Strait is credited with bringing a traditionalist revival to country music in the 1980s, which stood in stark contrast to the more pop-oriented sound prevalent in the genre at the time.

name: Alfre Woodard
about: Considered one of the most acclaimed actress of her generation, Alfre Woodward is both an activist and an award-winning actress.

name: Shane Gould
about: Shane Gould is an Australian competitive swimmer who achieved incredible success during her brief but remarkable career. She is best known for her outstanding performance at the 1972 Munich Olympics, where she won five medals, including three golds, and set multiple world records.

name: José Canseco
about:
Canseco was one of the top Major League Baseball power hitters, though since leaving the game he has often remained in the limelight.  
 
Perhaps most notably, Canseco courted controversy after admitting to having used performance-enhancing drugs throughout his MLB career and, moreover, claimed that the vast majority of players do so also.  
 
This was published in his autobiographical tell-all book: 'Juiced: Wild Times, Rampant 'Roids, Smash Hits & How Baseball Got Big.'

name: Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo
about: Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo is the Philippines 2nd female President (2001-2010) and the daughter of former President Diosdado Macapagal (1961-1965).

name: Mel C
about:
Mel C, born Melanie Chisholm and nicknamed "Sporty Spice" was a member of the phenomenally successful British girls group the  . The group song sold over 85 million records worldwide and achieved 9 No. 1 UK singles titles. 
 
Mel C has gone on to have her own solo career, releasing her solo debut album "Northern Star" in 1999.

name: Olivia Colman
about: In addition to numerous other awards, Colman has won an Academy Award, four BAFTA Awards and two Golden Globe Awards.

name: Anne Heche
about:
Film credits include "Six Days Seven Nights", "Return to Paradise", "I Know What You Did Last Summer", "John Q" and "Volcano".  
 
Her relationship with comedienne   and the events following their breakup became subjects of widespread media interest.

name: Jonah Lomu
about: The youngest All Black ever, Jonah Lomu remains the official, all-time Rugby World Cup top try scorer with 15 tries.

name: James Blake
about: James Blake is an American tennis player who won 10 singles finals, and appeared at 24 in his career. His highest ranking during this time was world No. 4. Blake also played a key role in the United States' 2007 Davis Cup victory.

name: Stefan Edberg
about:
Stefan Edberg is a Swedish tennis player, known for winning 6 Grand Slam men's singles titles and 3 Grand Slam doubles titles in the 1980s and 1990s.  
 
He holds the honor of being one of only two men, alongside  , in recent tennis history to have held the number one rank in both singles and doubles. 
 
During his retirement from professional tennis, Edberg briefly coached  .

name: Dave Grohl
about: Dave Grohl was only 17 when joined the punk rock band Scream, having lied about his age. After Scream broke up in 1990, Grohl joined guitarist   and bassist Krist Novoselic as drummer in their band, Nirvana, and first appeared on the band's second album, the worldwide hit "Nevermind" in 1991. Their style of alternative rock spearheaded a new musical style and their single "Smells like Teen Spirit" became an anthem for  .

name: Shane Warne
about: Played 145 test matches for Australia, taking 708 wickets. Also played in 194 ODIs.

name: Sinead O'Connor
about: Sinead O'Connor rose to fame in the late 1980s with her debut album “The Lion and the Cobra” and achieved worldwide success in 1990 with a new arrangement of Prince's song "Nothing Compares 2 U".

name: Jonathan Brandis
about: Jonathan Brandis was an American actor best known for his work as a child and teen star in the late 1980s and 1990s. He began his career at a young age, finding success as a child model and actor in projects like the soap opera "One Life to Live" (1982) and the miniseries " 's It" (1990).

name: Lisa Lopes
about: Lisa "Left Eye" Lopes was an American rapper and singer who was a key member of the Grammy-winning R&B trio TLC, which sold more than 65 million records worldwide, making them one of the best-selling girl groups in history. Renowned for her rap verses, she also lent her songwriting talents to many of the group's hits, including "Waterfalls," which topped the Billboard Hot 100 chart for seven weeks.

name: Jennifer Connelly
homePlace: Cairo in the Catskill Mountains, New York, USA
about: Jennifer Connelly is an American actress who began her career as a child actor with Once Upon a Time in America (1984). She went on to star in a number of major films, including Labyrinth (1986), Dark City (1998), and Requiem for a Dream (2000).

name: Salman Khan
about: One of the most influential and successful actors in Indian cinema, Khan is one of the most popular exponents of Bollywood in both India and the rest of the world. His film appearances include Hum Aapke Hain Koun..! (1994), Karan Arjun (1995), Biwi No.1 (1999) and Hum Saath-Saath Hain (1999). A number of his movies have been among the highest-grossing Indian films.

name: Zooey Deschanel
about: Almost Famous, (500) Days of Summer

name: Heath Ledger
about: Heath ledger was one of cinema's brightest stars before his tragic accidental death from a prescription drug overdose at 28.

name: Albert Pujols
about: Albert Pujols is a Dominican-American baseball player, nicknamed 'The Machine,' that plays for the St. Louis Cardinals. As a first baseman and designated hitter, Pujols is regarded by many as an all-time great. He is currently the oldest active player in Major League Baseball.

name: François Pienaar
about: François Pienaar is a South African rugby union player best known as captain of South Africa national team, the Springboks, in their 1995 Rugby World Cup.

name: Dan Wheldon
about: Two-time winner of the Indianapolis 500, in 2005 and 2011.

name: Heather Mills
about: Mills gained a degree of fame after losing her left leg in a car accident in 1993, during which time she was a model. She continued to model after the accident with a prosthetic limb and wrote a book titled Out on a Limb in 1995.

name: Shawn Michaels
about: Shawn Michaels is considered one of the all-time greats in  professional wrestling history.

name: Holly Madison
about: Madison moved to Los Angeles in 2001 to pursue her career in modeling and acting. In 2003, she was selected as Playboy's Playmate of the Month and was featured on the cover of the July issue of the magazine. She then starred in the reality television series The Girls Next Door, which aired on the E! Network from 2005 to 2009.

name: Justin Trudeau
about: Justin Trudeau began his rise to power in 2008 when he was elected the Member of Parliament for Papineau, Montreal.

name: George Floyd
about: George Floyd was a 46 year old bouncer whose violent death at the hands of police officers in Minneapolis ignited huge Black Lives Matter protests in America and around the world.

name: Dido
about: British singer who attained international success in 1999 with her debut album "No Angel", selling over 21 million copies. Also known for featuring on Eminem's "Stan".

name: Felipe VI
about: Felipe VI is the reigning King of Spain, ascending to the throne in June 2014 following the abdication of his father, King  . Educated in various institutions including Georgetown University in the United States, he was groomed for the throne from a young age and held the title of Prince of Asturias prior to his coronation.

name: Milla Jovovich
about: American model, actress, musician, and fashion designer who has appeared in numerous science fiction and action-themed films.

name: Seth Meyers
about:
Seth Meyers rose to fame as a cast member of "Saturday Night Live", becoming co-head writer in 2006. He is also the host of "Late Night" succeeding  .  
 
Meyers has been credited with writing  's infamous sketches of Sarah Palin during the 2008 Presidential election and in 2014 hosted the Primetime Emmy awards show.

name: Lin-Manuel Miranda
about: Lin-Manuel Miranda is an American actor and composer, best known for creating the Broadway musical Hamilton (2015) as well as In the Heights (2005). He also composed the soundtrack for the Disney film Encanto (2021).

name: Tim Sweeney
about: Tim Sweeney founded Epic Games, a video game and software company best known for creating "Fortnite." He is also the creator of Unreal Engine, a widely used game development system.

name: Ashton Kutcher
about: Known for his portrayal of Michael Kelso in the Fox sitcom "That '70s Show". He also created, produced, and hosted "Punk'd" and had lead roles in the Hollywood films "Jobs", "Dude, Where's My Car?", "Just Married", "The Butterfly Effect", "The Guardian", and "What Happens in Vegas".

name: Chen Kun
about: Chen Kun is one of the most popular celebrities in China, with an active following of over 90 million people on Weibo, one of China's most popular social networking websites.

name: Cuba Gooding Jr.
about: Cuba Gooding Jr. is an American actor who first came to fame with Boyz n the Hood (1991) after which he starred in several major films including Jerry Maguire (1996), for he received the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

name: Philip Seymour Hoffman
about: Won an Academy Award for Best Actor for the 2005 biographical film Capote. Also starred in a number of other films including Moneyball, The Master and Twister.

name: Ricky Martin
about: Best known for solo pop hits as "Livin' La Vida Loca" and "She Bangs."

name: Laura Dern
about: Laura Dern was born into the acting profession as the daughter of actors Bruce Dern and Dianne Ladd.

name: John Legend
about: The second-youngest person to win an EGOT (Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony), Legend gained prominence in the industry as a collaborator on songs such as "Encore" by Jay-Z and "You Don't Know My Name" by  .

name: Jenni Rivera
about:
Began recording music in 1998, and incorporated themes of social issues, infidelity, and relationships into her songs.  
 
Her tenth studio album, Jenni (2008), became her first #1 record in the Billboard Top Latin Albums chart in the United States.

name: Kevin McCarthy
about: Kevin McCarthy was an American politician who served as the 55th Speaker of the United States House of Representatives. His career spanned various positions within the government, from a local college district trustee to holding one of the highest political offices. He faced numerous challenges and controversies, including his relationship with   and his stance on the 2020 election results.

name: Michael Schumacher
about: Michael Schumacher won a record seven World Drivers' Championships and held numerous Formula One records at the time of his retirement. Schumacher is widely regarded as one of the greatest Formula One drivers in the history of the sport.

name: Matteo Salvini
about: Matteo Salvini is an Italian politician who served the Deputy Prime Minister of Italy and the Minister of the Interior. Salvini has been a member of the European Parliament and the Italian Chamber of Deputies. He is also the leader of the right-wing, anti-immigrant Lega Nord party.

name: Chris Metzen
about: Chris Metzen is known for his role in shaping the worlds of Warcraft, Diablo, and StarCraft at Blizzard Entertainment.

name: Pat LaFontaine
about:
Spent his entire career playing for the league's New York State-based teams (New York Islanders, Buffalo Sabres, and New York Rangers).  
 
He retired in 1998 because of concussion problems, finishing with 468 goals and 1,013 points, and is considered one of the best American-born players in NHL history.

name: Markus Persson
about: Markus Persson, known as "Notch," created Minecraft, the best-selling video game in history. He founded Mojang Studios and later sold it to Microsoft for $2.5 billion.

name: Nikki Haley
about: Nikki Haley is an American politician, best known for her time serving as governor of South Carolina (2011-2017) and as United States ambassador to the United Nations (2017-2018). She also served three terms in the South Carolina House of Representatives (2004-2010).

name: Perez Hilton
about:
Founded the blog Perezhilton.com, which is known for posts covering gossip items about celebrities. He is also known for posting tabloid photographs over which he has added his own captions or "doodles".  
 
His blog has garnered negative attention for its attitude, its former outing of alleged closeted celebrities and its role in the increasing coverage of celebrities in all forms of media.

name: Jaromír Jágr
about: Jágr is a Czech ice hockey right winger known for having the second highest points in NHL history, behind  . During his time with the Pittsburgh Penguins, they won the Stanley Cup twice in a row.

name: Ryan Seacrest
about: Ryan Seacrest is an American television and radio host, producer, and entrepreneur. He is best known for hosting the "American Idol" singing competition television series from 2002 to 2016, and its re-boot, since 2018.

name: Maria Menounos
about: Maria Menounos is a Greek-American television host and actress, best known for hosting entertainment news shows like Extra and E! News. She is also the CEO of the online podcast network AfterBuzz TV, which she co-created, and has been involved with WWE as an ambassador and occasional in-ring performer since 2009.

name: Psy
about: Psy is known for his huge YouTube hit "Gangnam Style". The song, which Psy first released in 2012, referenced the wealthy lifestyle in the Gangnam district in Soul, South Korea and showcasing Psy characteristic humor and dance moves .

name: Christy Turlington
about: Christy Turlington Burns is a former supermodel who became a maternal health advocate. She is known for her work in fashion and her efforts to improve healthcare for mothers worldwide.

name: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi
about: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi was an Iraqi militant who served as the first caliph of the Islamic State. He declared the organization a caliphate in 2014 and served in this role until his death in 2019.

name: Chadwick Boseman
about: Chadwick Boseman gained worldwide fame for his role as T'Challa in " " (2018).

name: Chris Ofili
about: Chris Ofili is a British painter known for his unconventional and often controversial art. He rose to prominence in the 1990s as one of the Young British Artists (YBAs), a group who set out to challenge traditional ideas of what art should be.

name: Liz Truss
about: Before succeeding   as British Prime Minister in September 2022 and as head of the Conservative Party, Lis Truss served as Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs for a year. She was originally elected to the British parliament in 2010 as the MP for south west Norfolk.

name: Daddy Yankee
about: Daddy Yankee is a Puerto Rican singer, songwriter, rapper, actor, and record producer who is widely regarded as one of the pioneers of the reggaeton genre. He initially aimed to be a professional baseball player, but an injury after being hit by a stray round from an AK-47 led him to focus on music.

name: LL Cool J
about: LL Cool J has released 14 studio albums, won two Grammy Awards, and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021. LL Cool J is also known for his long-running role on the TV series "NCIS: Los Angeles" (2009-2023).

name: Mellody Hobson
about: President of Ariel Investments and the Chairman of Dreamworks Animation. Married to  .

name: Elizabeth Banks
about:
Elizabeth Banks has appeared in wide range of films including  "Seabiscuit" (2003) Sam Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy (2002–2007) and "The Lego Movie" (2014). Her role in "The Hunger Games" (2012-15) trilogy is perhaps her most well known. 
 
In 2014 Banks made her directorial debut with "Pitch Perfect 2", in which she also starred. It earned $69 million in its opening weekend, a record for a first time director.

name: Rebel Wilson
about: Rebel Wilson is an Australian actress, best known for her role as Fat Amy in the   film series (2012-2017) for which role she won the MTV Movie Award for Best Breakthrough Performance.

name: Emmanuel Macron
about: Emmanuel Macron is the President of France, having taken office in May 2017. A former investment banker, he served as Minister of the Economy, Industry, and Digital Affairs under President  . His election as President was notable for his relative youth and his founding of the political movement En Marche!

name: Anna Nicole Smith
about: Anna Nicole Smith was an American model, actress, and television personality. She first gained attention as a Playboy model before rising to fame in 1993 after her marriage to billionaire J. Howard Marshall and her appearance on The   Show.

name: Stephenie Meyer
about: Best known for her " " series of books which sold over 100 million copies.

name: Tiger Woods
about:
Woods was a golf child prodigy before turning pro in 1996.  
 
He won his 1st major in 1997 and became the No.1 ranked player shortly after. He dominated golf throughout the 2000s and is one of only 4 players to win the Career Grand Slam.  
 
Woods has the lowest career scoring average and the most career earnings of any player.

name: Claire Danes
about: Claire Danes is an American actress best known for her award-winning performances in My So-Called Life and Homeland. She has won several Emmy and Golden Globe Awards, as well as being involved in theater and various charitable efforts.

name: Emma Bunton
about: Emma Bunton is an English singer, songwriter, actress, and media personality, best known for her time with the popular girl group, the  . With the group, Bunton became an international sensation in the 1990s, as well as later carving out a successful solo music career.

name: Samantha Bee
about: Samantha Bee is best known for her work in political satire. She was the first woman to host a late-night satirical news show in the United States.

name: Kristi Yamaguchi
about: Won an Olympic gold at Barcelona in 1992 and World Championship gold in 1991-92.

name: Valentino Rossi
about: Valentino Rossi is an Italian professional motorcycle road racer who is widely considered one of the greatest of all time. He began his professional racing career in 1996 and has since accumulated numerous world championship titles.

name: Cedric Pioline
about: Cedric Pioline is best known for his Grand Slam final appearances—he reached the finals of the US Open and Wimbledon, losing both to  —and his Davis Cup victories.

name: Mark Ruffalo
about: Mark Ruffalo was an American actor who had a breakthrough with the 2000 film You Can Count on Me. Ruffalo's portrayal of Bruce Banner/Hulk in the Marvel Cinematic Universe has since gained him international recognition. He has earned accolades such as Academy Award nominations for The Kids Are All Right (2010), Foxcatcher (2014), and Spotlight (2015).

name: Randy Orton
about: Randy Orton is an American professional wrestler who has won the WWE Championship ten times and the World Heavyweight Championship four times, among countless other titles and awards. He is the grandson of Bob Orton and the nephew of Barry Orton.

name: Ken Jeong
about: Ken Jeong is an American actor and stand-up comedian who came to fame in The Hangover (2009) and its sequels, in which featured as Leslie Chow alongside  , Ed Helms, and Zach Galifianakis. He went on to star in Community (2009-2015) and then to write and produce his own original sitcom, titled Dr. Ken (2015-2017).

name: Kim Rhode
about: Kim Rhode is an American double trap and skeet shooter. She is the most successful female shooter at the Olympics, being the only triple Olympic Champion and the only woman to have won two Olympic gold medals for Double Trap.

name: Robert Lopez
about:
Robert Lopez is an American songwriter known for his musicals, particularly for The Book of Mormon and Avenue Q. He has also worked as a songwriter for film alongside his wife Kristen Anderson-Lopez, including Frozen (2013), Frozen II (2019), and Coco (2017).  
 
Lopez is the youngest person to receive an EGOT, and in fact holds more than one of each of necessary awards: two Oscars, three Tonys, three Grammys, and four Emmys.

name: Jonny Wilkinson
about: Jonny Wilkinson is an English rugby union player who played for the Newcastle Falcons and Toulon. He also represented England with the national team, as well as playing for the British and Irish Lions.

name: David Justice
about: Played for the Atlanta Braves (1989–1996), Cleveland Indians (1997–2000), New York Yankees (2000–2001), and Oakland Athletics (2002), and hit 305 career home runs.

name: Triple H
about: “Triple H” is recognised as one of the best professional wrestlers of all-time who has moved on to becoming a successful business executive in the wrestling industry.

name: Michael Chang
about: The youngest male player to win a Grand Slam singles title when he won the French Open in 1989 at the age of 17 years and 4 months, he was best known for his on-court speed and fighting spirit. He is considered by many observers to have been one of the best defensive baseliners of all time and introduced the jumping two-handed backhand.

name: Matthew Perry
about: Perry became a household name in the 1990s with his starring role as Chandler Bing on the sitcom Friends (1994-2004), which became one of the most popular television shows of all time.

name: Chris DiMarco
about: Chris DiMarco is an American golfer whose career highlights include three PGA Tour wins and several close finishes in major tournaments.

name: David Duval
about:
David Duval is an American professional golfer known for his 2001 win at the Open Championship. He has also won 13 PGA Tour tournaments. 
 
While Duval's golfing career declined after his 2001 win, since then he has been successful as a commentator and analyst for the Golf Channel and ESPN.

name: Brendan Greene
about: Brendan Greene, known as PlayerUnknown, is best known for creating PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds (PUBG). He pioneered the battle royale genre in video games, which involves many players competing to be the last one standing.

name: Martin McDonagh
about: Martin McDonagh is an Irish playwright, screenwriter, and director, celebrated for his darkly comedic and often violent works in both theatre and film.

name: Regina King
about: King's career first came to attention in the 1980s, with a part on the NBC series 227, before landing major roles with films like Friday (1995) and Jerry Maguire (1996).

name: Oscar Isaac
about: Oscar Isaac is a Guatemalan-born American actor who had a breakthrough performance with Inside Llewyn Davis (2013). He has since played a number of major film roles, including Ex Machina (2015) and Dune (2021).

name: David Blaine
about: David Blaine renovated magician for modern audiences. He emphasised endurance in particular, thus including elements inspired by Houdini incorporated with standard card magic and illusions. This was paired with an ordinary style, gone were the tails and top-hat.

name: Yulia Navalnaya
about: Yulia Navalnaya is a Russian activist known primarily for her role in supporting her husband, opposition leader  , and her involvement in Russian politics. Since marrying Navalny in 2000, she has been a visible presence alongside her husband, earning the moniker "First Lady" of the Russian opposition.

name: Angela Stanford
about: Angela Stanford is an American golfer who turned professional in 2000 and currently competes on the LPGA Tour. She has seven LPGA Tour wins, including the Evian Championship in 2018.

name: Kevin Hart
about:
Appeared in several films in the early 2000s, including "Paper Soldiers" and "Scary Movie 3".  
 
Hart also gained widespread recognition for the release of his stand-up album "I'm a Grown Little Man" in 2008.

name: Koji Igarashi
about: Koji Igarashi is best known his work on the Castlevania series.

name: Javier Bardem
homePlace: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Canary Islands, Spain
about: Javier Bardem is a Spanish actor whose role as Anton Chigurh in   (2007) earned him an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor, making him the first Spaniard to win in this category. Bardem's career spans diverse roles, including his portrayal of a Cuban poet in Before Night Falls (2000) and a Bond villain in Skyfall (2012).

name: Kurt Browning
about: Browning began skating at the age of three and soon began winning local competitions. When he was eleven years old, he placed second in the novice division at the Canadian Championships.

name: Moises Alou
about: Moises Alou had a successful career in Major League Baseball (MLB), during which he was known for his consistent hitting, resilience in the face of injuries, and for being part of a prominent baseball family.

name: Jon Favreau
about:
Jon Favreau is an American actor and director who has featured in numerous popular films including Daredevil (2003), The Break-Up (2006), and The Wolf of Wall Street (2013).  
 
As a filmmaker, he is best known for his work in the Marvel Universe. Most notably, Favreau directed Iron Man (2008) and Iron Man 2 (2010). He has also directed a number of other films, including The Jungle Book (2016) and   (2019).

name: Jensen Ackles
about:
Known for his roles in television as Eric Brady in "Days of our Lives", which earned him several Daytime Emmy Award nominations, as well as Alec/X5-494 in "Dark Angel" and Jason Teague in "Smallville". 
 
Since 2005 Ackles has played Dean Winchester on the cult CW series "Supernatural".

name: Vijay
about: One of the highest-paid actors in Tamil cinema, he is affectionately referred to as "thalapathy" (commander) by his fans. He has appeared in 61 films as a lead actor, notably in Poove Unakkaga (1996), Thirumalai (2003) and Thuppakki (2012).

name: Alex Rodriguez
about: Alex Rodriguez was born on July 27, 1975, in New York City. He is of Dominican and Puerto Rican descent. Rodriguez began playing baseball at a young age, and he was signed by the Seattle Mariners when he was just 17 years old.

name: Selma Blair
about:
Blair initially rose to fame after starring in "Zoe" and "Cruel Intentions". She later achieved international fame as Liz Sherman in the fantasy film series "Hellboy".  
 
In 2014, she won a Grammy award for her narration of the Holocaust-related audio documentary, "The Diary of  ".

name: Pavel Bure
about: Called "The Russian Rocket" for his blazing speed, he spent 12 seasons in the NHL where he scored 437 goals and 779 points in 702 career games.

name: Lindsay Davenport
about: Won three Grand Slam titles and an Olympic gold medal in 1996.

name: Leonard Cohen
about:
Leonard Cohen was an influential singer-songwriter whose career spanned 50 years.  Cohen began as a poet before, frustrated at his lack of success became a professional musician. 
 
Cohen's musical style was often haunting and evocative. This is evidenced in "Hallelujah" his most well known song, famously covered by Jeff Buckley. Such Cohen standards as "I'm Your Man", "Death of Ladies Man" and "Suzanne" were often covered by other musicians.

name: Michael King
about: Michael King was a New Zealand historian, author, and biographer. Although not himself Māori, he was known for his knowledge of Māori culture and history, and for his writing in an accessible way that resonated with the public.

name: Jerry Lee Lewis
