about: American rock and roll and country music singer-songwriter and pianist, known by the nickname "The Killer" and is often viewed as "rock & roll's first great wild man".

name: Maya Angelou
about: Revered globally for her poetry and her commitment to civil rights Maya Angelou was best known for her series of seven autobiographies, which focused on her childhood.

name: Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
about: King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is the reigning King of Saudi Arabia, having ascended to the throne in 2015. As the 25th son of King Abdulaziz, the founder of Saudi Arabia, Salman is part of the powerful Al Saud dynasty that has ruled the kingdom since its establishment.

name: Casey Kasem
about: Casey Kasem created and hosted "American Top 40," a long-running weekly radio program that counted down popular songs. Kasem also provided the voice for Shaggy in the "Scooby-Doo" animated series.

name: Michael Landon
homePlace: Forest Hills, Queens, New York, USA
about: Raised in Collingswood, New Jersey, Orowitz was a promising track and field athlete and won a scholarship to University of Southern California.  A shoulder injury ending his sports career, and being in Hollywood he considered show business.  He was discovered while working as gas station attendant near Warner Brothers Studios. His agent suggested a name change,

name: Sonny Liston
about: Known for his toughness, punching power and intimidating appearance, he became World Heavyweight Champion in 1962, but failed to live up to his fearsome reputation when he lost the title in 1964 to 7-1 underdog  .

name: Max Robinson
about:
The first African-American broadcast network news anchor in the United States when he became a co-anchor of ABC News World News Tonight. 
 
Robinson was a founder of the National Association of Black Journalists and one of the first television journalists to die of AIDS.

name: Bo Diddley
about: Bo Diddley was an iconic American singer-songwriter, guitarist and music producer, whose sound was influential in the development of rock and roll and rhythm and blues in the 1950s. He was given the nickname “Bo Diddley” by his friends at an early age, and it became his stage name.

name: Faye Dunaway
about: Faye Dunaway is an American actress who came to fame in the late 1960s with her role in the film Bonnie and Clyde (1967), for which she received her first Academy Award nomination. She followed this with critically acclaimed performances   (1974) and Network (1976), with the latter earning her an Academy Award for Best Actress.

name: James Dean
about: Rebel Without a Cause, East of Eden

name: Robert Wagner
about: The American actor achieved his greatest success as the star of a number of successful TV shows including It Takes a Thief, Switch and   with Stephanie Powers.

name: Winnie Mandela
about: A controversial figure in South African history and a staunch anti-apartheid activist, Winnie Madikizela married   in 1958. When he was sent to prison in 1963 after the Riviona Trial, she became the public face of Mandela through his 27 years imprisonment. On numerous occasions she was arrested, tortured and exiled.

name: Mobutu Sese Seko
about: Dictator and President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (which Mobutu renamed Zaire in 1971 and his own name to Mobutu Sese Seko) from 1965 to 1997.

name: Barry White
about: You're the First, the Last, My Everything and Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe

name: Keith Richards
about: Richards co-founded   with frontman  , one of the most commercially successful and musically influential groups in the history of music.

name: Penny Marshall
about: Penny Marshall made her name as an actress in the TV sitcom "Laverne and Shirley" (1976-83), created by her brother  . The series, a spin-off from "Happy Days" was successful on its own terms and by its third season was the most popular series on US TV.

name: Kim Jong-il
about: The eldest son of North Korean supreme Leader  , Kim Jong-il had been groomed to succeed his father from an early age.

name: Michael Crichton
about: Michael Crichton was an author, screenwriter, and filmmaker most known for his " " novels, which have been adapted into a major movie franchise. His books have sold over 200 million copies worldwide.

name: Hafez al-Assad
about: Hafiz al-Assad was born in Syria into an Alawite family. He attended military training schools and rose up the ranks of the Syrian Air Force, eventually becoming Air Force Commander. Assad also became an active member of Syria's Ba'ath Party, an Arab nationalist political party.

name: Ray Charles
about:
Known professionally as Ray Charles, he helped pioneer soul music with hits such as "Hit the Road, Jack", "Georgia on My Mind" and "I Can't Stop Loving You". 
 
Ray started to lose his sight at the age of four or five, and was completely blind by the age of seven, apparently resulting from glaucoma. 
 
Among friends and fellow musicians he preferred being called "Brother Ray" but was often referred to as "The Genius".

name: Don Estridge
about: Don Estridge was a key figure in the development of the personal computer. He led the team at IBM that created the IBM PC, which helped make personal computers common in homes and offices.

name: Hissène Habré
about: Hissène Habré was dictator of Chad from 1982 to 1990 when he was deposed by rebel forces. A later commission of inquiry found his government was responsible for the deaths of 40,000 people and the torture of 200,000 people.

name: Jacques Chirac
about: Jacques Chirac served two terms as President of France 1995-2007. Prior to that he served two terms as French Prime Minister (1974-76, 1986-88) and was Mayor of Paris from 1977 to 1995.

name: Martin Lee
about: Lee is an activist and lawyer from Hong Kong who is renowned for his involvement in the pro-democracy movement. This began with Lee participating in talks for the handover of Hong Kong by the British to China, and for his continued activity since he has been called the "Father of Democracy" in Hong Kong.

name: Jerry Lucas
about: Named one of the 50 greatest players in National Basketball Association history, he is an Olympic Gold Medal winner (1960), an NCAA National Champion (1960 Ohio State Buckeyes), and an NBA Champion (1973 New York Knicks).

name: Paul Keating
about: Paul Keating was elected to the Australian House of Representatives at the young age of 25 and went on to serve through 10 terms. He rose through the ranks in opposition before being appointed Treasurer in  's 1983 Labor government.

name: Francis Gary Powers
about: Powers is best known as the pilot of the CIA U-2 spy plane that was shot down over the Soviet Union in 1960. His plane was equipped with a state-of-the-art camera intended to take high-resolution photographs of military installations and other sensitive sites from an extremely high altitude. As the U-2 spy plane flew and took photographs from the stratosphere, the Soviet Union initially lacked any effective way to respond.

name: Douglas Hofstadter
about: Douglas Hofstadter is an American computer scientist best known for his influential book "Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid" (1979).

name: Joan Rivers
about: Famous for her sometimes controversial comedic persona, Rivers came to prominence in 1965 as a guest on "The Tonight Show" with  , who became her mentor.

name: Imre Kertész
about: Hungarian author, Holocaust concentration camp survivor, and recipient of the 2002 Nobel Prize in Literature, “for writing that upholds the fragile experience of the individual against the barbaric arbitrariness of history”.

name: Wilma Mankiller
about: Wilma Mankiller was a Cherokee Nation leader and the first female Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation. Engaging in activism and social work early in her life, Mankiller was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by   in 1998 and in 2021 was named to the United States Mint's "American Women Quarters" program.

name: Charles Manson
about: Charles Manson was a notorious American criminal and cult leader. In the late 1960s, he formed what became known as the Manson Family, a quasi-commune based in California. Manson's followers committed a series of nine murders at four locations over a period of five weeks in the summer of 1969. The crimes captivated the public due to their gruesome nature and the seemingly random and senseless violence they entailed.

name: Carl Icahn
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Carl Icahn is best known for his aggressive investment strategies and corporate activism. He is recognized for taking large stakes in companies and pushing for changes to increase their value.

name: John C. Bogle
about: John C. Bogle was an American investor, business magnate, and philanthropist, widely known as the founder of The Vanguard Group. Bogle's most revolutionary contribution to the investment industry was the creation of the first index mutual fund, which allowed investors to buy into a broad market index at a low cost.

name: Floyd Patterson
about: Floyd Patterson was an American professional boxer who in 1956 became the youngest heavyweight champion of the world at the age of 21. His win against reigning champion   also made him the first Olympic gold medalist to win a professional heavyweight title.

name: Roberta Flack
about: Roberta Flack revolutionized popular music by blending classical training with soul, jazz, and folk to create an unmistakable sound. She remains the only solo artist to win the Grammy Award for Record of the Year in consecutive years, achieving this feat with "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" and "Killing Me Softly with His Song."

name: Nancy Richey
about: She won two Grand Slam singles titles: the 1967 Australian Championships and 1968 French Open, to go with four Grand Slam women's doubles titles. She won 69 singles titles in total.

name: John Denver
about:
One of the most popular acoustic artists of the 1970s and one of its best-selling artists. By 1974, he was firmly established as America's best-selling performer, and AllMusic has described Denver as "among the most beloved entertainers of his era". 
 
Throughout his life, he recorded and released approximately 300 songs, about 200 of which he composed, with total sales of over 33 million.

name: Anthony Fauci
about: Anthony Fauci was appointed Director of America's National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NAIAD) in 1984. There he has overseen research into such established diseases as HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria as well as emerging diseases such as Ebol and Zika.

name: Nursultan Nazarbayev
about: Nursultan Nazarbayev is a Soviet and Kazakh politicians, known as the first President of Kazakhstan. He served in this role from the country's independence until 2019, when he resigned from the office.

name: Steve Carlton
about:
Steve Carlton is an American baseball pitcher, best known for playing with the Philadelphia Phillies. He was the first pitcher to win four   awards in his career, which are granted yearly to the best pitcher. 
 
Carlton has held a number of records, including the lifetime strike out record; although he was overtaken in this by his contemporary,  .

name: Khun Sa
about: Khun Sa dominated the opium trade in the Golden Triangle region of Southeast Asia from the 1970s to the 1990s. He was known as the "Opium King" and he was described as "the worst enemy the world has" by an American ambassador to Thailand.

name: Linda McCartney
about:
Linda Eastman became Linda McCartney on March 12, 1969, when she married  , then a member of the Beatles. Their marriage would last 29 years, before her death from breast cancer.  
 
In her lifetime she was a photographer, particularly of celebrity portraits, and was a noted vegetarian, forming the company Linda McCartney Foods with her husband.

name: Jane Fonda
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Rose to fame in the 1960s with films such as "Barbarella" and "Cat Ballou". She has won two Academy Awards, an Emmy Award and seven Golden Globe Awards.  
 
She has been an activist for many political causes; her counterculture era opposition to the Vietnam War and associated activities were controversial. She has protested the Iraq War and violence against women, and describes herself as a feminist.

name: Evel Knievel
about: Evel Knievel was a daredevil stunt performer whose stunts made him a famous pop culture figure in the 1960s and 1970s. His outrageous jumps on a motorcycle were as famous for their failure as their success.

name: Alan Ayckbourn
about:
Alan Ayckbourn is a British playwright and director, who has written and produced more than 80 plays. He was also the artistic director of the Stephen Joseph Theatre in Scarborough between 1972 and 2009. 
 
Ayckbourn's plays have won numerous awards and been translated into over 35 languages, with 10 of his plays being also performed on Broadway. He has been nominated for two Tony Awards, one of which he won.

name: Alain Delon
about: Alain Delon is a French actor and filmmaker, known for his leading roles in European cinema from the 1960s to the 1980s. His performances earned him a César Award for Best Actor for his role in Notre histoire (1984) and distinguished honors such as an honorary membership in France's Legion of Honour, an Honorary Golden Bear at the 45th Berlin International Film Festival, and an Honorary Palme d'Or at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival.

name: Ted Cassidy
about: Ted Cassidy is best known for his role as Lurch in the television series "The Addams Family."

name: David Suzuki
about: David Suzuki is Canada's most well-known scientist and environmental activist, hosting CBC's "The Nature of Things" from 1979-2023. He has sounded early and constant warnings about climate change.

name: Jerry Brown
about: Jerry Brown served as the 34th and 39th Governor of California, making him the longest-serving governor in the history of the state. A member of the Democratic Party, Brown's political career spans several decades and is marked by a mix of progressive and pragmatic policies.

name: Omar al-Bashir
about: Omar al-Bashir came to power in Sudan after leading a group of military officers in a coup in 1989, then went on to win three controversial and allegedly corrupted elections.

name: Sean Connery
about: Sean Connery was most famous for his portrayal of James Bond. He was further known for his distinctive voice and rugged charm, which made him a leading man in Hollywood for decades.

name: Nina Simone
about:
A prominent figure in the Civil Rights movement in America, Simone was also a noted jazz and soul singer. Her famous recording include versions of "I Loves You, Porgy," "My Baby Just Cares for Me" and her own civil rights anthem "Mississippi Goddam". 
 
Angered by racism in America, she permanently left the country in 1973.

name: Robert Munsch
about:
Famous for his exuberant storytelling methods, with exaggerated expressions and acted voices.  
 
His most loved story books include "Love You Forever", "The Paper Bag Princess" and "Smelly Socks". 
 
Munsch is known for making up his stories in front of audiences and refining them through repeated storytelling.

name: Bob Newhart
about: Newhart was noted for his deadpan and slightly stammering delivery, and one-sided phone call routines, where the audience only hears his half of a conversation.. Reaching a global audience in the 1960s, Newhart's comedy album "The Button-Down Mind of Bob Newhart" became an international best-seller and was number one in the United States. The album won 3 Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year and Best New Artist.

name: Raúl Castro
about:
Brother of  , Raúl has been the President of Cuba since 2008.  
 
He is also the Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces (Army, Navy, and Air Force) and is the nation's highest ranking general.

name: Roald Hoffmann
about: Roald Hoffmann is the Frank H. T. Rhodes Professor of Humane Letters Emeritus at Cornell University.

name: Jackie Collins
about: Jackie Collins was a British novelist known for her romance novels centered on the lifestyles of the rich and famous. With over 500 million copies of her books sold internationally, she was one of the world's best-selling writers.

name: Walt Frazier
about: Led the New York Knicks to their only two NBA Championships in 1970 and 1973. He is currently a colour commentator for the Knicks on MSG Network.

name: John Astin
about: John Astin is an American actor and director, best known for playing Gomez Addams in The Addams Family (1964-1966) as well as voicing the same character in the animated series The Addams Family (1992-1993).

name: Kenny Rogers
about:
A country music icon with 120 hit singles across various music genres and three Grammy awards. 
 
Kenny Rogers dominated the country and pop album charts during the 1970s and 1980s spending more than 200 individual weeks on top of those charts in the United States alone.  
 
In all Rogers sold over 120 million records worldwide, making him one of the highest-selling artists of all time.

name: Mickey Mantle
about:
Regarded by many as one of the greatest players in baseball history.  
 
Mantle played center fielder and first baseman for the New York Yankees for 18 seasons, from 1951 through 1968.  
 
He appeared in 12 World Series, his team winning 7 of them, and holds numerous World Series batting records.

name: Robert Lefkowitz
about: Robert Lefkowitz is an American physician and biochemist renowned for his significant advancements in the field of cell biology. Lefkowitz shared the 2012 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with   for their transformative work on G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), a large family of proteins that play a crucial role in numerous biological processes.

name: George Akerlof
about: George Akerlof is an American economist and university professor, known for his work in the field of behavioral economics and his exploration of asymmetric information and its effects on markets for which he earned a Nobel Prize in 2001.

name: Jim Davis
about: Best known as the creator of the highly successful comic strip Garfield, which has been published since 1978 and grew to become the world's most widely syndicated comic strip.

name: Bert Campaneris
about: Bert Campaneris began his professional baseball career in 1961 with the Kansas City Athletics. He is one of only a handful of players to hit two homeruns in his first game.

name: Juan Marichal
about: 10 × MLB All-Star; NL wins leader 1968; MLB ERA leader 1969; no-hitter 1963; SF Giants

name: Roch Carrier
about:
Among the best known Quebec writers in English Canada.  
 
His most famous short story is "The Hockey Sweater", which is considered an iconic work of Canadian literature. The story has sold over 250,000 copies and has been republished in numerous anthologies. It exemplifies the nation's passion for hockey, and it is considered an allegory of the relationship and tensions that exist between francophones and anglophones.

name: Roger Bannister
about: The first person to run a mile in under four minutes.

name: Sepp Blatter
about: Sepp Blatter is a former football administrator who served as the eighth President of FIFA between 1998 and 2015.

name: Sonny Bono
about: Sonny dropped out of high school to pursue a career as a songwriter, landing work as promotion man and staff writer at Specialty Records, and then with Phil Specter.  Early works were recorded by Don and Dewey, the Righteous Brothers, and  . His biggest hit came with the Searchers covering "Needle and Pins".

name: Dave Stockton
about: His two majors, both of which were PGA Championships, came in 1970 and 1976, and he had 25 professional wins in total. He had the reputation of being one of the best putters.

name: Joe Torre
about: Joe Torre is an American former professional baseball player, manager, and executive. He is known for his career in Major League Baseball (MLB), where he was a nine-time All-Star and the National League (NL) Most Valuable Player (MVP) in 1971.

name: Yuan T. Lee
about: Yuan T. Lee is a Taiwanese chemist known for his pivotal role in the development of advanced molecular beam techniques. His contributions to the field of physical chemistry, particularly the dynamics of chemical reactions, earned him the 1986 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, which he shared with   and  .

name: Ivan Sutherland
about:
Widely regarded as the 'father of computer graphics', Sutherland's teachings, inventions and students at the University of Utah spawned the foundation of computer graphics. 
 
In 1963 he invented the Sketchpad program, revolutionary in its time, and a direct predecessor to modern-day graphical user interfaces and computer-aided design programs. For this invention he received the Turing Award in 1988.

name: Quincy Jones Jr
about: "Q" was a prolific composer and record producer, working in both the jazz and pop genres.  He produced albums for legendary artists such as  ,  , Sarah Vaughan Lesley Gore,  ,  , Dinah Washington, Billy Eckstine,  , Dizzy Gillespie, and the Brothers Johnson. He arranged and produced the all-star charity single "We Are World".

name: Robert Goulet
about: Robert Goulet first came to fame for his role as Lancelot in the Broadway musical "Camelot" in 1960. He was known for his rich baritone voice and had a career spanning nearly six decades in stage, screen, and recording. His signature song was "If Ever I Would Leave You" from "Camelot."

name: Denny McLain
about: Denny McLain was an outstanding American baseball pitcher in the 1960s and 70s.

name: Robin Knox-Johnston
about: Robin Knox-Johnston is a British sailor known as the first person to complete a solo non-stop circumnavigation of the globe, which he completed as part of the Sunday Times Golden Globe Race.

name: Ibrahim Babangida
about: Babangida, known as IBB, by others as 'The Evil Genius' is a Nigerian general that ruled Nigeria from 1985 to 1993 after displacing   in a coup d'ètat. Prior to this, Babangida had served the Nigerian Army during the Nigerian Civil War; during which time he was also involved with various coups.

name: Rudy Giuliani
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Rudy Giuliani is best known as  ’s personal lawyer, although previously he was known for being mayor of New York City during the September 11, 2001 attacks. He began his career in law enforcement and later entered politics, becoming a prominent figure in the Republican Party.

name: Helen Mirren
about: Gosford Park (2002), The Queen (2007) and The Last Station (2010).

name: Elvin Hayes
about: Elvin Hayes is a American professional basketball player renowned for his remarkable skills and endurance on the court. Standing at 6'9", Hayes was known for his scoring ability, rebounding prowess, and shot-blocking, establishing himself as one of the dominant big men of his era.

name: Billy Cunningham
about: Nicknamed the "Kangaroo Kid", he played most of his career with the Philadelphia 76ers, and winning two NBA Championships (one as a player and one as a coach).

name: Dan Rather
about: Dan Rather is an American journalist and news anchor. Rather rose to fame in the 1960s when he became a correspondent for CBS News. He was assigned to the White House after his early work, including reporting on the assassination of President  .

name: Bob Charles
about: Won the British Open in 1963, becoming the first left-handed player to win a golf major.

name: Ralph Nader
about:
Came to prominence in 1965 with the publication of his book "Unsafe at Any Speed", which critiqued the safety record of American auto-mobile manufacturers.  
 
He is also a five-time candidate for President of the United States.

name: Jerry Garcia
about: Jerry Garcia co-founded the band Grateful Dead, for which he was the principal songwriter, lead guitarist, and vocalist. The band is known for being at the forefront of the 1960s counterculture.

name: Alan Sugar
about: Alan Michael Sugar is a British business magnate, media personality, and political figure known for his rags-to-riches story. He gained recognition after founding the electronics company Amstrad and later, for his role as host of the BBC series The Apprentice. By 2021, Sugar's net worth was estimated at £1.21 billion, making him one of the UK's wealthiest individuals.

name: Rosa Mota
about: The Association of International Marathons and Distance Races (AIMS) has distinguished Rosa Mota as the greatest female marathon runner of all time.

name: Sylvester Stallone
about: Sylvester Stallone is best known for creating and starring in the "Rocky" and "Rambo" film franchises. He has become an icon of action cinema and popular culture.

name: Alice Cooper
about: Alice Cooper is an American rock singer, best known as the "  of Shock Rock." His career has spanned five decades, throughout known for his raspy voice and excessive stage shows featuring fireworks and stage illusions from fake blood and dueling swords to guillotines and electric chairs.

name: Najib Razak
about: Razak served as the Prime Minister of Malaysia from 2009 to 2018, when he was ousted following the general election that bought   to power.

name: Danny Boyle
about: The English director's first success was the film thriller "Shallow Grave" (1994) starring   which won Best British film at the BAFTAs. He followed it up with   (1996) and the zombie horror film "28 Days Later" (2002).

name: Douglas Lenat
about: Douglas Lenat is an American computer scientist and artificial intelligence researcher who has made significant contributions to the fields of knowledge representation, machine learning, and automated reasoning. He is best known for his work on the Cyc project, a long-term endeavor aimed at creating a comprehensive knowledge base and reasoning system that captures the breadth of human common sense knowledge and understanding.

name: Yevgeny Prigozhin
about: Yevgeny Prigozhin was a Russian mercenary leader and former restaurateur. While he started his career in restaurants and catering, and before that as a convict in the Soviet Union, he ultimately became known as the founder the Wagner Group. This was a group of pro-Russian mercenaries that served as a paramilitary force in Syria, Africa, and Ukraine.

name: Dave Righetti
about:
Began his career as a starting pitcher before converting to a closer with the New York Yankees. Won the American League (AL) Rookie of the Year Award in 1981.  
 
As a starter, he threw a no-hitter, and as a closer, he was twice named the AL Rolaids Relief Man of the Year, the first player in history to both pitch a no-hitter and also lead the league in saves in his career.

name: Alan Menken
about: Alan Menken is an American composer best known for his work with   Animation Studios. He has written music for The Little Mermaid (1989), Beauty and the Beast (1991), Aladdin (1992), and   (1995). For each of these projects, Menken won an Oscar each for Best Score and Best Song.

name: Lloyd Blankfein
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Lloyd Blankfein is an American investment banker who served as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Goldman Sachs from 2006 to 2018. He led the bank through the 2007-2008 financial crisis, navigating the challenges of this period and establishing Goldman Sachs as the second-largest investment bank in the U.S.

name: Andre Dawson
about:
Andre Dawson, also known as "The Hawk" and "Awesome Dawson," is an American baseball player. He had a 21-year career in Major League Baseball, during which time he played mostly for the Montreal Expos (1976-1986) and the Chicago Cubs (1987-1992). 
 
Dawson was the league's Rookie of the Year in 1977, won eight Gold Glove Awards, was an 8-time All-Star, and won the Most Valuable Player Award in 1987. He was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2010.

name: Gilbert Perreault
about: Played for seventeen seasons with the Buffalo Sabres of the NHL. Known for his ability to stickhandle in close quarters, he is regarded as one of the most skillful play-making centres of all time, and was the centre man for the prolific trio of Sabres forwards known as The French Connection.

name: Steve Young
about:
Played in three Super Bowls with the San Francisco 49ers in 1988, 1989 and 1994, the last of which he was MVP. 
 
Also played in the Pro Bowl between 1992 and 1998 and was the NFL passing touchdown leader between 1992 and 1994 and again in 1998.

name: Tim Burton
about: Tim Burton is known for the distinctive visual style and dark fantasy themes of his films. He has directed numerous critically acclaimed and commercially successful films.

name: Dennis Martínez
about: First Nicaraguan baseball player (pitcher or position player) to play in the majors.

name: Greg LeMond
about: Three time Tour de France winner in 1986, 1989 and 1990.

name: Donovan
about: Donovan Philips Leitch, better known simply as Donovan, is a Scottish musician known for his many hit singles, including "Catch the Wind" (1965) and "Sunshine Superman" (1966).

name: Steve Carell
about: Steve Carell became a household name for his role as regional manager Michael Scott in the US version of the mockumentary "The Office" (2005-2013). Carell won a Golden Globe award and received six Emmy nominations for the part.

name: Paul Molitor
about: Paul Molitor is a Baseball Hall of Fame infielder / designated hitter.

name: Jeb Bush
about: John Ellis "Jeb" Bush is an American politician and businessman who served as the 43rd Governor of Florida from 1999 to 2007. A member of the Republican Party and the Bush family, he is the second son of former President   and former First Lady  , and a younger brother of former President  .

name: Sergey Lavrov
about: Sergey Lavrov is Russia's Foreign Minister and a prominent figure in international diplomacy. He is known for his long career representing Russian interests on the global stage.

name: Miguel Induráin
about: Miguel Induráin is a former Spanish professional cyclist renowned internationally for his significant achievements in stage racing and time trial events. He is a five time winner of the Tour de France, wining consecutive titles between 1991 and 1995.

name: Cyndi Lauper
about: Cyndi Lauper is an American singer, songwriter, actress, and activist who achieved widespread fame in the 1980s with her distinctive voice, colorful style, and infectious pop hits. Known for her unique fashion sense and quirky personality, Lauper became a symbol of individuality and self-expression, inspiring countless fans and fellow artists throughout her career.

name: Cecil Fielder
about: Cecil Fielder was one of the premier baseball power hitters in the 1980s and 1990s.

name: Karl Malone
about: Karl Malone is regarded as one of the greatest power forwards in basketball history.

name: Kevin Kline
about: Won two Tony Awards for his work in Broadway musicals, winning Best Featured Actor in a Musical for the 1978 original production of "On the Twentieth Century" and Best Actor in a Musical for the 1981 revival of "The Pirates of Penzance". His other stage roles include Falstaff in the 2003 Broadway production of " ", for which he won the Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Actor in a Play.

name: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan
about: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is an Indian-born British-American biologist best known for his work on the structure and function of ribosomes, which earned him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009. He won this award together with   and   "for studies of the structure and function of the ribosome."

name: Charo
about: Charo is a Spanish-American musician, singer, comedian, and actress. She is perhaps best known for her flamboyant stage presence, her proficient guitar skills, and her catchphrase "Cuchi-Cuchi," which endeared her to American television audiences.

name: Craig Ferguson
about: Craig Ferguson is best known for his time as the host of "The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson" from 2005 to 2014.

name: Jean-Claude Van Damme
about: Belgian martial artist, actor, and director best known for his martial arts action films.

name: Roberto Durán
about: Was the world champion at different times in 4 different weight divisions.

name: Chanda Kochhar
about: Chanda Kochhar was the CEO of ICICI Bank, one of India's largest private banks. She is known for her role in expanding ICICI's retail banking operations but later faced allegations of fraud.

name: Joss Whedon
about: Joss Whedon is an American screenwriter, director, and producer best known for creating the television series Buffy the Vampire Slayer (1997-2003) and for his work on blockbuster films including The   (2012) and Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015).

name: Olivia Newton-John
about: Olivia Newton-John had a long and successful career as a singer, straddling both country and pop music. Her five number one US hits including "Physical", "You're The One That I Want" and "Magic". She won four Grammys, including Record of the Year for "I Honestly Love You" in 1974.

name: Arlo Guthrie
about: Arlo Guthrie is an American folk singer-songwriter best known for his song "Alice's Restaurant Massacree" and his rendition of "City of New Orleans." Continuing the legacy of his father,  , he has been a significant figure in music and social activism.

name: Richard Hadlee
about: Regarded as one of the greatest fast bowlers and all-rounders in cricketing history.

name: Reza Pahlavi
about:
Reza Pahlavi was the Crown Prince of Iran prior to the 1979 Islamic Revolution. While he was sworn in as Shah of Iran after the revolution in Egypt in 1980, he has remained in exile ever since and has had little success in reclaiming the throne. 
 
Since the 1980s, Reza Pahlavi has shifted towards calling for human rights in Iran and demanding a secular parliamentary democracy. He is mostly popular with the generation of Iranian expatriates that left following the Islamic Revolution.

name: Tim Raines
about: Best known for his 13 seasons (of 23 total) with the Montreal Expos. He is regarded as one of the best leadoff hitters and baserunners in baseball history.

name: Marco van Basten
about: Marco van Basten is a Dutch professional football player renowned for his success with Ajax, AC Milan, and the Netherlands national team, as well as being a three-time Ballon d'Or winner. Van Basten's career was prematurely ended by an injury, but he remained a significant figure in football both as a coach and technical director.

name: Ahmad Shah Massoud
about: Ahmad Shah Massoud was an Afghan military commander and politician. He was a powerful figure in the resistance against the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan in the 1980s, and later became the Minister of Defense after the Soviet withdrawal.

name: Andrej Babiš
about: Andrej Babiš is a Czech politician and businessman who served from 2017 to 2021 as the Prime Minister of the Czech Republic.

name: Billy Crystal
about: Billy Crystal is an American actor, comedian, writer, producer, and director who came to fame with roles in television and film, particularly for "Soap" (1977-1981), "When Harry Met Sally..." (1989), and as the voice of Mike Wazowski in the "Monsters, Inc.: franchise. He was also known for hosting the Academy Awards, Comic Relief, and for his autobiographical one-man Broadway show "700 Sundays".

name: Carlos Santana
about: Carlos Santana first gained fame as the leader of the band Santana and has since influenced generations of musicians with his distinctive guitar style.

name: Arsenio Hall
about:
Arsenio Hall was the host of his own popular late-night talk show "The Arsenio Hall Show" from 1989-1994 and then again from 2013-14. He came to public attention after guest hosting Joan River's talk show.  
 
Hall has also featured in a number of popular films; including "Coming To America" (1988) and "Harlem Nights (1989) alongside his friend  .

name: Rosanne Cash
about: The eldest daughter of county legendary music musician   and his first wife Vivian, Rosanne Cash has gone on to forge a significant career of her own that includes 11 No. 1 country hit singles.

name: Mandy Patinkin
about: A versatile performer comfortable working in musical theater, film, television, and the recording studio, Mandy Patinkin has won both an Emmy and a Tony award. He is widely recognized for his role of the tormented swordsman Inigo Montoya in "The Princess Bride".

name: Jair Bolsonaro
about:
Bolsonaro took office as President of Brazil in January 2019 after a controversial presidential campaign the previous year. Many of Bolsonaro's comments, described as far-right or populist, have been highly controversial, including opposing abortion, drug liberalization, LGBT rights and affirmative action. 
 
During his presidential campaign he survived an assassination attempt when he was stabbed in the stomach at a campaign rally. He went on to win the election with 55% of the vote.

name: Wanda Sykes
about: Wanda Sykes acreer in entertainment began appearing as a stand-up comedienne in the late 1980s. She has since appeared in a number of her own televised comedy specials. In 2009 she was the featured entertainer for  's White House Correspondents Association Gala dinner.

name: Bill Cowher
about: In 15 seasons as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers, he led the team to eight division titles and 10 playoff appearances, which resulted in two Super Bowl appearances and one victory. He is the second coach in NFL history to reach the playoffs in each of his first six seasons as head coach. He is currently a studio analyst for The NFL Today.

name: Darryl Sittler
about: Played in the NHL from 1970 until 1985 for the Toronto Maple Leafs, the Philadelphia Flyers and the Detroit Red Wings. He set an NHL record for most points scored in one game when he recorded ten points against the Boston Bruins.

name: Rosemary Casals
about:
Earned a reputation as a rebel in the tennis world during the 1960s.  
 
She won more than 90 tournaments and worked for the betterment of women's tennis, and became a motivating force behind many of the changes that changed tennis in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Adam Silver
about: Adam Silver is an American lawyer and sports executive, best known as the current commissioner of the National Basketball Association. He began his career as an associate with the law firm Cravath, Swain & Moore in New York before joining the NBA in 1992.

name: Denis Potvin
about: He served as captain for the New York Islanders where he won four Stanley Cups in the early 1980s. He was also a three-time James Norris Memorial Trophy winner as the NHL's top defenseman.

name: Laura Harring
about:
Laura Harring is a Mexican-American actress, best known for her roles in  's film Mulholland Drive (2001). She was also the first Hispanic woman to be crowned Miss USA, which she won in 1985. 
 
Harring has played a number of other film roles, including The Forbidden Dances (1990), The Punisher (2004), and Love in the Time of Cholera (2007).

name: Mike Gartner
about:
Played 19 seasons in the NHL for five different teams. Best known for his blazing speed, he was a consistent performer throughout his career.  
 
Despite this, he never won the Stanley Cup or played in the Cup Finals, and never won an NHL award.

name: Sebastian Coe
about: As a track and field athlete Sebastian Coe won four Olympic medals, including two gold medals for the 1500 meters in 1980 and 1984. Throughout his career he set nine world records for outdoor events and three for indoor events.

name: Ric Flair
about: Ric Flair's career spanned over forty years, and he is regarded by many as one of the all-time best professional wrestlers—known, since the 1970s, as 'The Nature Boy.' He has been WWE world champion at least 16 times, with others claiming up to 25 wins—he himself claims to have won the world championship 21 times.

name: Patrick Ewing
about: Best known for winning gold medals in men's Olympic basketball team in 1984 and 1992.

name: Bernard Hinault
about: Bernard Hinault is a French road cyclist who over a lengthy career amassed 147 professional victories, including 5 in the Tour de France. He is regarded by many as one of the greatest cyclists of all time. Of the thirteen Grand Tours which Hinault entered, he won 10; only   has won more with 11.

name: Anatoly Karpov
about: Anatoly Karpov became a grandmaster in 1970 after attending  's chess school and winning a series of tournament as a teenager including the 1969 World Junior Championship.

name: Suze Orman
about: Suze Orman is a successful financial advisor whose unconventional approach is aimed at helping ordinary people through her finance company, books, TV appearances and podcasts.

name: Rita Wilson
about: Rita Wilson is an American actress, producer, and singer best known for her roles in film and television. She is married to actor   and has survived breast cancer, which has influenced her philanthropic efforts, particularly in cancer research.

name: Ivan Lendl
about: One of the game's most dominant players in the 1980s and remained a top competitor into the early 1990s, and is considered to be one of the greatest tennis players of all time. He won eight Grand Slam singles titles.

name: Martin Dempsey
about: Martin Dempsey is an American military officer and four-star general in the United States Army who served as the 18th Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2011 to 2015.

name: François Hollande
about: François Hollande was the President of France from 2012 to 2017, serving as the nation's head of state after defeating incumbent   in the 2012 election. He is a member of the Socialist Party, and his presidency was marked by attempts to stimulate economic growth and reduce unemployment in France amidst the backdrop of the Eurozone crisis.

name: Lyle Lovett
about: From his start as a folk singer-songwriter while earning degrees in journalism and German at Texas A&M, to an internationally celebrated musician, Lovett does not fit neatly into any genre category. While generally considered a country artist, his songs include large doses of blues, jazz, western swing, folk, rock and gospel.

name: Ron Guidry
about: Ron Guidry is an American former professional baseball pitcher who played 14 seasons in MLB, all for the New York Yankees (1975-88).

name: Wynonna Judd
about: Wynonna Judd is an American country music singer, known for her 19 No. 1 singles. She first attained fame in the 1980s as part of a country music duo with her mother, Naomi Judd, known as The Judds. Together they released seven albums, with fourteen No. 1 hit singles.

name: David Campese
about: David Campese is an Australian rugby union player, considered one of the sport's finest. His career is distinguished by his unique playing style, record-breaking try count, and his role in Australia's 1991 Rugby World Cup victory.

name: Alberto Salazar
about: Alberto Salazar is a Cuban-born American long-distance runner and track coach. He is best known for winning the New York City Marathon three times (1980, 1981, 1982) and the 1982 Boston Marthon.

name: Roger Clemens
about:
Played 24 seasons in the MLB for four teams and was one of the most dominant pitchers in MLB history, tallying 354 wins, a 3.12 ERA, and 4,672 strikeouts, the third-most all time.  
 
Clemens also won seven   Awards during his career, the most of any pitcher in MLB history.

name: Isabella Rossellini
about:
Isabella Rossellini is the daughter of Swedish actress   and Italian Director  .  
 
Rossellini  began her career as a model. She was the face of  Lancôme from 1982-1996. 
 
Rossellini came to prominence in the 1980s as a film actress appearing in "White Nights" (1985) and  's "Blue Velvet" (1986).

name: Viv Richards
about: West Indian cricketer Viv Richards is considered one of the greatest batsmen of all time. He played for the West Indies from 1974 to 1991 and is one of the most prolific run-scorers in Test and ODI cricket.

name: David Gower
about:
David Gower was one of the most capped English cricketers of his era. A Left-handed batsman, known for his graceful style, he appearing in 117 Tests, scoring 8,231 runs. He also played in 114 one day internationals scoring 3170 runs. 
 
Gower was captain of the English team in 1985 and led a successful Ashes campaign against Australia. He was replaced in 1986 after loses against the West Indies. Gower retired from international cricket in 1993.

name: Mark Burnett
about: Mark Burnett is a British-born American television producer, entrepreneur and author. He is best known for producing hit shows such as Survivor, The Voice, Shark Tank, and The Apprentice. He has been credited with creating and producing some of the world’s most popular television shows.

name: Björn Borg
about: Former world #1 tennis star who won 11 Grand Slam singles titles between 1974 and 1981.

name: Charles Simonyi
about: Charles Simonyi is best known for his pioneering work at Xerox PARC and Microsoft, as well as his many feats as a space tourist.

name: Ian Botham
about: Ian Botham, also known by his nickname "Beefy," is a cricketer widely renowned for his exceptional all-round abilities and larger-than-life personality.

name: Roger Goodell
about: The current NFL Commissioner, succeeding Paul Tagliabue on August 8, 2006. Commentators have described him as "the most powerful man in sports".

name: Bonnie Blair
about: Bonnie Blair is an American retired speed skater, one of the most decorated athletes in Olympic history. She was known for her exceptional speed and agility on the ice, and her career spanned several Olympic Games from 1984 to 1994.

name: Charles Barkley
about: Charles Barkley was an American professional basketball player who played for the Philadelphia 76ers, Phoenix Suns, and Houston Rockets, earning 11 NBA All-Star appearances and an MVP award in 1993. Barkley won two Olympic gold medals and after retiring became a successful NBA analyst, winning four Sports Emmy Awards.

name: Annette Bening
about: A four-time Oscar nominee for her roles in "The Grifters", " ", "Being Julia", and "The Kids Are All Right".

name: Salman Rushdie
about: The Indian-born British writer is known for his allegorical works on historical subjects often set on the Indian subcontinent.

name: Michelle Bachelet
about: The first woman to serve as President of Chile. She previously served as President from 2006–2010, making her the first person since 1932 to win the presidency of her country twice in competitive elections.

name: Jane Curtin
about: Jane Curtin is an American actress and comedian who first gained recognition as an original cast member on the TV sketch comedy series "Saturday Night Live" in 1975, where she anchored the "Weekend Update" segment and created memorable characters like Prymaat Conehead and Enid Loopner.

name: Janeane Garofalo
about:
Janeane Garofalo is an American comedian, known for starting her career as a stand-up comedian and then a cast member on The   Show, The Larry Sanders Show, and Saturday Night Live.  
 
Garofalo's television career gave way to a consistent sting of film productions, including Wet Hot American Summer (2001) and The Matchmaker (1997). She has also since starred in television shows including Wet Hot American Summer: First Day of Camp and 24.

name: Keith Moon
about: Explosive drummer for the British rock group "The Who" from 1964-78, Moon's penchant for drugs, alcohol, and detonations earned him a reputation as a horrible hotel guest. His drug experimentation sometimes led to his passing out during shows.

name: Jackie Joyner-Kersee
about:
Jackie Joyner-Kersee is an American track and field athlete, best known for her performance in the heptathlon and long jump. She won a total of six medals over four Olympic Games in her career: three gold, one silver, and two bronze. 
 
Joyner-Kersee is now known as a philanthropist, and is still regarded as an inspiration for having overcome asthma to succeed in athletics. She was inducted into the International Sports Hall of Fame in 2023.

name: Stephen Fry
about: A significant figure in modern British culture, Fry began his career primarily as a comedian, noted for his collaboration with  . This produced "A Bit of Fry & Laurie" and their adaptation of "Jeeves and Wooster". He then performed as an actor on productions such as " ", "Kingdom", "Bones" and "V for Vendetta".

name: Carl Lewis
about: Carl Lewis is one of the most successful Olympians in history, winning nine gold medals and one silver medal across four Olympic Games.

name: Robert Smith
about: Lead singer, guitar player, lyricist and principal songwriter of rock band The Cure.

name: Kurt Russell
about: American actor who has starred in a number of   cult film classics including "Escape from New York" (1981), "The Thing" (1982) and "Big Trouble in Little China" (1986).

name: Caitlyn Jenner
about: Caitlyn Jenner is a media personality and retired Olympic gold medal-winning decathlete.

name: Rosie O'Donnell
about: A TV sitcom and a series of movies introduced her to a larger national audience and from 1996 to 2002, she hosted "The Rosie O'Donnell Show", which won multiple Emmy awards.

name: Patty Sheehan
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1980 and won 35 LPGA Tour events and six major championships.

name: Ang Lee
about: Ang Lee's's films are known for exploring the conflict between tradition and the modern world. His early three films, called his "Father Knows Best" trilogy established these themes and examined the tensions between East and West. The last of the trilogy "Eat Drink Man Woman" (1994), a global hit, was like Lee's previous film nominated for Best Foreign Film at the Academy Awards.

name: Rick Hansen
about:
After a pick up truck accident paralyzed him from the waist down at the age of 15, he became a paralympian athlete and won three gold medals.  
 
He is most famous for his Man in Motion World Tour, and was one of the final torch-bearers in the 2010 Winter Olympics.

name: Emma Thompson
about: Emma Thompson is a British actress, screenwriter, and author who has achieved fame in both film and television. She is one of the UK's most respected and accomplished performers, having received numerous accolades, including Academy Awards for her roles in Howards End (1992) and her screenplay adaptation of Sense and Sensibility (1995).

name: Tucker Carlson
about: Tucker Carlson is a right-wing journalist and political commentator and the host of "Carlson Tucker Tonight", the most watched cable news program in US history.

name: Clarence Seedorf
about: Clarence Seedorf is a Dutch footballer, widely regarded as one of the best midfielders. He holds the record for only player to have won the UEFA Champions League with three different clubs: Ajax (1995), Real Madrid (1998), and AC Milan (2003, 2007).

name: Mahershala Ali
about: Ali first came to prominence with roles in The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (2008) and a recurring role in   (2013-2019).

name: Lou Bega
about: Lou Bega is a German singer, best known for his 1999 hit single "Mambo No. 5." The song, a remake of the mambo and jazz dance song originally recorded by Pérez Prado in 1949, topped the charts across Europe and was nominated for a Grammy Award.

name: Mark Rutte
about: Mark Rutte is a Dutch politician who has been Prime Minister of the Netherlands since 2010. He has also been Leader of the People's Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) since 2006.

name: Patrice Désilets
about: Patrice Désilets is best known for creating the "Assassin's Creed" series.

name: Brock Lesnar
about: Brock Lesnar is an American professional wrestler and former mixed martial artist, currently signed to WWE. He is also a former NCAA Division I heavyweight wrestling champion, and a two-time WWE Universal Champion.

name: Yahya Jammeh
about: Jammeh, a former Gambian military officer, lead Gambia from 1994 to 2017—first as the head of a military junta, then as elected president.

name: Brandon Boyd
about: Brandon Boyd is an American singer, songwriter, musician, and visual artist. He is best known as the lead vocalist of the rock band Incubus.

name: Brett Kavanaugh
about: Brett Kavanaugh is American judge, now an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States. Previously he served on the United States Court of Appeal before being appointed to the Supreme Court by President  .

name: Alyson Hannigan
about: Alyson Hannigan is an American actress best known for her roles as Willow Rosenberg in the television series Buffy the Vampire Slayer (1997–2003) and Lily Aldrin in the sitcom How I Met Your Mother (2005–2014). She has also starred in the   film series, portraying Michelle Flaherty in four installments between 1999 and 2012.

name: Demis Hassabis
about: Demis Hassabis is a British computer scientist, neuroscientist, and entrepreneur known for his groundbreaking work in artificial intelligence (AI) and the development of advanced machine learning systems. He is the co-founder and CEO of DeepMind Technologies, a leading AI research company that focuses on developing general-purpose learning algorithms and artificial general intelligence (AGI).

name: John Daly
about: Known primarily for his driving distance off the tee, his non-country club appearance and attitude, and his rough-and-tumble personal life. His two greatest on course accomplishments are his "zero to hero" victory in the 1991 PGA Championship, and his playoff victory in the 1995 Open Championship.

name: Thierry Henry
about: Thierry Henry is a French footballer and coach best known for his time at Arsenal where he became the all-time leading scorer. Henry won major titles both at club and international levels, including the 1998 FIFA World Cup. After retiring as a player, he moved into coaching and media punditry.

name: Terrell Owens
about: Terrell Owens is an American former professional football player who played in the National Football League (NFL) for 16 seasons, mostly as a wide receiver.

name: Manny Pacquiao
about:
Rated as one of the best pound-for-pound boxers in the world Pacquiao was the first eight-division world champion. He has won ten world titles and the championship in four different weight classes. 
 
Wildly popular in his home country, Pacquiao was elected in May 2010 to the House of Representatives in the Congress of the Philippines, representing the province of Sarangani. He was re-elected in 2013.

name: Alexis Tsipras
about: Alexis Tsipras is a Greek politician who served as Prime Minister of Greece from 2015 to 2019 and now serves as Leader of the Opposition. He is a member of the Coalition of the Radical Left – Progressive Alliance, better known as SYRIZA; a party which he has led since 2009.

name: Randy Moss
about: Randy Moss is an American football player, best known for spending fourteen seasons as a wide receiver with a variety of teams: Minnesota Vikings (1998-2004; 2010), Oakland Raiders (2005-2006), New England Patriots (2007-2010), Tennessee Titans (2010), San Francisco 49ers (2012).

name: Eva Longoria
about: Eva Longoria is an American actress, producer, director, and businesswoman who achieved fame through her roles in both television and film.

name: Ben Mendelsohn
about: Ben Mendelsohn is an Australian actor who came to fame with The Year My Voice Broke in 1987, later coming to global awareness with Animal Kingdom in 2010. Since then he starred in   Rises (2012), Starred Up (2013), and Ready Player One (2018).

name: Chris Gayle
about: One of the great batsmen of Twenty20 cricket, Gayle plays for the West Indies, and has also played domestic cricket in his native Jamaica.

name: Chris Pratt
about: Chris Pratt first gained fame for his portrayal of Andy Dwyer in the TV show "Parks and Recreation" (2009-2015) and later became a leading man in Hollywood.

name: Riddick Bowe
about:
Two-time world heavyweight champion and the first fighter to defeat   when he beat him in 1992 for the undisputed world heavyweight title.  
 
Later became the first fighter to knock Holyfield out. His professional boxing record stands at 43–1–0 (1 no contest).

name: Pedro Martínez
about: Pedro Martínez was a Dominican-American professional baseball player known for his time as a pitcher in Major League Baseball (MLB). His career spanned from 1992 to 2009, during which he was recognized for his impressive winning percentage, low ERA, and high strikeout rate. Martínez was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2015 and is considered one of the greatest pitchers in MLB history.

name: Jon Cryer
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
The actor is most well known for his starring role in the long-running Chuck Lorre CBS sitcom "Two and a Half Men" opposite  . Cryer won two Emmy awards for the part, in 2009 and 2012. 
 
Before this, his break-out role was in the 1986 John Hughes scripted romantic film "Pretty in Pretty" with Molly Ringwald.

name: Miroslav Klose
about: Miroslav Klose is a German football player and manager, best known as a striker with the all-time highest number of goals scored for Germany. He also scored 16 goals in the FIFA World Cup tournament between 2002 and 2014, with which he holds the record for the most goals scored by any single player in the tournament.

name: Joe Thornton
about: He was selected first overall by the Boston Bruins in the 1997 NHL Entry Draft, and currently serves as captain of the San Jose Sharks. His on-ice vision, strength on the puck, deft passing ability, and power forward style of play have led to him becoming one of the league's premier top line centers.

name: Elvis Stojko
about: Elvis Stojko is a Canadian figure skater who achieved significant milestones in his career, including three World Championship titles, two Olympic silver medals, and seven Canadian National titles. Renowned for his technical prowess, Stojko was the first to land a quadruple-double jump combination in competition.

name: Neil Patrick Harris
about:
Best known for playing Barney Stinson in the television comedy series "How I Met Your Mother", for which he was nominated for four Emmy Awards.  
 
He has also played the title characters in "Doogie Howser, M.D." and  's musical "Dr. Horrible's Sing-Along Blog", and a fictional version of himself in the "Harold & Kumar" film series.

name: Deion Sanders
about: Played football primarily at cornerback, but also as a kick returner, punt returner. He won the Super Bowl with both the 49ers and the Cowboys.

name: Orlando Bloom
about: After having his breakthrough by starring in the "The  " trilogy, he rose through fame by further appearing in epic fantasy, historical epic and fantasy adventure films.

name: Alyssa Milano
about: Alyssa Milano started her acting career aged 7 in a touring production of "Annie". She went on to become a successful child and adult actor, appearing on TV alongside Tony Danza in "Who's the Boss,” as a guest star on "Melrose Place," and starring in “Charmed."

name: Abiy Ahmed
about: Abiy Ahmed was elected Prime Minister of Ethiopia in 2018 by a ruling coalition and began reforms to open up the country. He lifted a ban on opposition parties and released thousands of political prisoners.

name: Amélie Mauresmo
about:
Amélie Mauresmo is a French tennis player, best known for having reached world number one ranking. She has won two major titles, winning the women's singles in 2006 at both the Australian Open and at Wimbledon.  
 
Mauresmo, who also won a silver medal in singles at the 2004 Summer Olympics, was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2015.

name: Marcus Luttrell
about: Marcus Luttrell is a retired U.S. Navy SEAL known for being the lone survivor of Operation Red Wings in Afghanistan in 2005. He has since become an author and advocate for veterans.

name: Omar Camporese
about: Omar Camporese is an Italian tennis player who won two singles titles and five doubles titles on the ATP Tour. He achieved his highest rankings in 1992, when he was World No. 18 in singles and World No. 27 in doubles.

name: Mary Lynn Rajskub
about: Mary Lynn Rajskub is an American actress and comedian best known for her role as Chloe O'Brian on the action-drama television series "24."

name: Reese Witherspoon
about: Rose to fame with the breakout role as Elle Woods in the box-office hit "Legally Blonde". She received worldwide praise and an Academy Award for her role in "Walk the Line".

name: Paul Rudd
about: Paul Rudd is an American actor best known for his roles in "Clueless" (1995), "The 40-Year-Old Virgin" (2005), and his recurring role as Scott Lang in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

name: Jennie Garth
about: Played Kelly Taylor in the teen TV franchise "Beverly Hills 90210" (1990-2000) alongside   and  .

name: Cliff Bleszinski
about: Cliff Bleszinski, also known as CliffyB, is best known for his work on the Unreal and Gears of War game series at Epic Games.

name: Bobby Cannavale
about: Bobby Cannavale is an American actor who is perhaps best known for his role as Joe Oramas in Will & Grace from 2004 and 2006. For this part alongside Eric McCormack and Debra Messing, in 2005 he received the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series.

name: Sandra Oh
about: Sandra Oh is a ground-breaking Asian-Canadian American actress. She is the first Asian woman to be nominated for an Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress for her role in the TV drama " ". She is also the first Asian woman to win two Golden Globe awards for Best Actress in a TV series, also for "Killing Eve".

name: Kate Hudson
about:
Came to prominence in 2001 after winning a Golden Globe and receiving several nominations, including one for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, for her role in "Almost Famous".  
 
Hudson then starred in the hit film "How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days" in 2003, and has since appeared in numerous romantic comedies.

name: Volodymyr Zelensky
about: Zelensky began his career as an actor and comedian, known particularly for playing the President of Ukraine in Servant of the People (2015–2019). Following the popularity of this show, a political party was founded and then, on the 31st of December 2018, Zelensky announced that he was running for President.

name: Patrick Roy
about:
Nicknamed "Saint Patrick", he is regarded as one of the greatest goaltenders of all time. He split his professional career between the Montreal Canadiens and the Colorado Avalanche, winning two Stanley Cups with each franchise. 
 
He is widely credited with popularising the butterfly style of goaltending,which has since become the dominant style of goaltending around the world.

name: Tina Fey
about: Saturday Night Live, 30 Rock

name: Adrien Brody
about: Adrien Brody is an American actor whose Władysław Szpilman in The Pianist (2002) earned him an Academy Award for Best Actor, marking him as the youngest recipient of the award at the time. Brody is known for his collaborations with director Wes Anderson and his work on series such as Peaky Blinders and Winning Time: The Rise of the Lakers Dynasty.

name: Jennifer Capriati
about: Jennifer Capriati and is generally considered one of the greatest tennis players of all time.

name: Julianna Margulies
about:
Best known for portraying Nurse Carol Hathaway in "ER" and Alicia Florrick in "The Good Wife".  
 
She has won eight Screen Actor Guild Awards.

name: Keri Russell
about: Keri Russell is an American actress who gained recognition for her starring role as Felicity Porter in the television series Felicity (1998-2002). The show, created by   and Matt Reeves, earned her a Golden Globe in 1999.

name: Chris Rock
about: Chris Rock is an American comedian, actor, writer, producer, and director. He started his career as a stand-up comedian in the 1980s and has since appeared in numerous television shows and films. Rock has also been nominated for and won several prestigious awards, including four Emmy Awards and three Grammy Awards.

name: Michael Dell
about:
Dell is the founder and namesake of the Dell computer company, which he started in 1984. 
 
With a net worth around $24 billion, Dell is also one of the richest people in the world.

name: Jason Koumas
about: Jason Koumas is a Welsh footballer known for his time with clubs such as Tranmere Rovers, West Bromwich Albion, and Wigan Athletic, as well as for his role on the Wales national team.   is his son.

name: Michael Moorer
about: One of only four men to win one or more versions of the world heavyweight championship on three separate occasions, as well as being a former world light-heavyweight champion. Also one of only four men to win world titles at both light-heavyweight and heavyweight.

name: Andrew Scott
about: Andrew Scott is an Irish film and on-stage actor, best known for his roles as Moriarty in the BBC series "Sherlock" (2010-17) and as the priest in "Fleabag" (2019).

name: Mario Lemieux
about: Widely acknowledged to be one of the best players of all time, he was a gifted playmaker and fast skater. He often beat defencemen with fakes and dekes, and led Pittsburgh to two consecutive Stanley Cups in 1991 and 1992. He is the only person to have his name on the Cup as both a player and an owner (2009 Stanley Cup).

name: Norah Jones
about:
Five-time Grammy Award winner for her debut album, "Come Away with Me". Certified diamond the album sold over 26 million copies. 
 
She is the daughter of Indian sitar master and composer  ,

name: Ron Gant
about: Played for the Atlanta Braves from 1987–1993 before finishing his career in 2003 after playing for several other teams. He joined the 30-30 club (30 steals and 30 home runs) in 1990 and 1991.

name: Keiji Inafune
about: Keiji Inafune is best known for his work on the Mega Man series.

name: Tim Duncan
about:
Played his entire NBA career for the San Antonio Spurs. He is a five-time NBA champion, two-time NBA MVP, and three-time NBA Finals MVP.  
 
Basketball experts consider him to be one of the greatest players in NBA history.

name: Kobe Bryant
about:
Professional basketball player for the Los Angeles Lakers of the National Basketball Association (NBA).  
 
Bryant entered the NBA directly from high school, and has played for the Lakers his entire career, winning five NBA championships. 
 
He is a 16-time All-Star.

name: Ben Feldman
about: Ben Feldman is an American actor who gained recognition for his role as Fred in the television series Drop Dead Diva (2009-2014). He achieved further acclaim through his performance as Michael Ginsberg in the iconic television series Mad Men (2012-2014), for which he was nominated for an Emmy Award.

name: Pierre Turgeon
about: Played 20 seasons in the NHL for six different teams. During the 1992-93 season with the New York Islanders, he scored 58 goals.

name: Sterling K. Brown
about: Sterling K. Brown is an American actor who has garnered critical acclaim for his performances in television and film. He rose to fame for his role as Christopher Darden in the anthology series   Story: The People v.  , for which he won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Limited Series or Movie.

name: Liv Tyler
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Liv Tyler is the daughter of Aerosmith's lead singer,  , and model Bebe Buell.

name: Mary J. Blige
about: Billboard ranked her as the most successful female R&B artist of the past 25 years, sold more than 50 million albums and 15 million singles worldwide.

name: Anna Faris
about: Anna Faris is an American actress, comedian, and producer. She rose to fame after starring in the Scary Movie franchise (2000-2006) and has since established a successful career in comedy films. Faris is also known for her starring roles in films such as The House Bunny (2008) and Mom (2013-2019).

name: Vaughan Gething
about: Vaughan Gething is a Welsh politician and the current First Minister of Wales. Notably, he is the first black person to serve as the head of any country within the United Kingdom. He also served as Health Minister during the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: Amanda Peet
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Amanda Peet is an American actress, best known for a number of television and film roles. She first came to widespread recognition with her performance alongside   and   in The Whole Nine Yards (2000).

name: Cam Neely
about: Cam Neely is the current president of the Boston Bruins. He is known for his powerful playing style, which combined scoring ability with physical toughness, earning him the nickname "Bam-Bam Cam."

name: Kal Penn
about: Kal Penn is an American actor, author, and former White House staff member. He is best known for his roles as Lawrence Kutner on "House" (2007-2009), Kumar Patel in the "Harold & Kumar" film series, and Seth Wright on "Designated Survivor" (2016-2019).

name: Marc Webb
about: Webb began his directorial career with a series of music, beginning with small local bands and then ultimately directing for major bands such as Good Charlotte, My Checmical Romance, and  .

name: Jim Furyk
about:
Won 17 PGA Tour titles and the US Open in 2003.  
 
Also became the 1st player to shoot 58 in a PGA Tour event and the 1st PGA Tour pro to card 2 sub-60 rounds.

name: Iva Majoli
about: She upset   to win the women's singles title at the French Open in 1997, her only Grand Slam victory.

name: Boris Becker
about: Former World No. 1 professional tennis player and six-time Grand Slam singles champion. He is the youngest-ever winner of the men's singles title at Wimbledon at the age of 17.

name: Melissa Joan Hart
about: Known for her title roles in the television series "Clarissa Explains It All", the live action version of "Sabrina, the Teenage Witch", and "Melissa & Joey".

name: Jason Aldean
about: Jason Aldean is an American country music singer and songwriter who rose to prominence in the mid-2000s with his distinctive blend of country, rock, and pop influences.

name: Willem-Alexander
about: Willem-Alexander has been the reigning King of the Netherlands since the succeeded his mother, Beatrix, on 30 April 2013.

name: Marlee Matlin
about: American actress and the only deaf performer to win the Academy Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role, which she won for "Children of a Lesser God". Deaf since she was 18 months old, she is also a prominent member of the National Association of the Deaf.

name: Vanessa Lachey
about: Vanessa Lachey is known for hosting MTV's Total Request Live and starring in "NCIS: Hawaiʻi" (2021-2024) as Jane Tennant, the first female lead in the NCIS franchise. Lachey has also co-hosted Netflix's "Love Is Blind" with her husband, Nick Lachey, since 2020.

name: Todd Martin
about: Best known for reaching the Men's Singles final at the 1994 Australian Open and the 1999 US Open. His career-high singles ranking was World No. 4.

name: Goran Ivanišević
about: Goran Ivanišević is a Croatian tennis player, best known for being the only wildcard to win the Wimbledon men's singles championship. He was admitted to the competition in 2001 despite being ranked number 125 in the world, but this was because of his having suffered a shoulder injury.

name: Luis Miguel
about: Luis Miguel is a Mexican singer and record producer who is one of the most successful artists in Latin American history. Known as "El Sol de Mexico," Luis Miguel has been recognized for his contributions across various musical genres, including pop, ballads, boleros, tangos, jazz, big band, and mariachi. He has won multiple Grammy and Latin Grammy Awards, sold around 60 million records worldwide, and has established a record-breaking legacy as a live performer.

name: Pat Cash
about:
Won the Men's Singles title at Wimbledon in 1987, and won a total of six titles in his career.  
 
In May 1988, he reached his career-high singles ranking of World No. 4.

name: Kelly Robbins
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1992 and won nine LPGA Tour events, including one major championship.

name: Noah Wyle
about: Noah Wyle rose to fame as one of the original cast member of the TV medical drama "ER". He has gone on to star in other TV series such as "Falling Skies". Wyle has also featured in movies like " ".

name: Ben Stiller
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Ben Stiller is an American actor, producer, screenwriter and director. Born into a comedic family as the son of   and Anna Meara, the younger Stiller went on to make a name for himself as a member of the "Frat Pack" group of actors.

name: Ramin Djawadi
about: Ramin Djawadi is an Iranian-German film score composer, best known for his work on the HBO series,  , and its prequel, House of the Dragon. He was nominated for a Grammy Award for his work on Game of Throne threes times: in 2009, 2018, and 2020. He won two Emmy Awards for Game of Thrones (2018, 2019).

name: Andrew Ng
about: Andrew Yang is a British-born American computer scientist known for his work in artificial intelligence, particularly for his time as co-founder and head of Google Brain. He also served as Chief Scientist for the Chinese technology company Baidu, where he oversaw the development of their Artificial Intelligence Group.

name: Lleyton Hewitt
about: Won the US Open in 2001 and Wimbledon in 2002.

name: Hozier
about: Grammy-nominated Irish singer-songwriter Hozier is known for blending folk, gospel, blues, and soul music. He gained international popularity with his debut single, "Take Me to Church," which brought attention to the repression and persecution faced by the LGBTQ+ community. Hozier's music explores themes of love, religion and social justice.

name: Charlie Cox
about: Charlie Cox is best actor known for his portrayal of Matt Murdock, the blind lawyer who moonlights as the superhero Daredevil in Marvel productions.

name: Evan Peters
about: Evan Peters is an American actor, best known for his various roles in the American Horror Story series. He started acting in the early 2000s, landing minor roles in television shows and films. It was his role in the popular anthology series American Horror Story, however, that brought him widespread recognition and critical acclaim.

name: Adam Peaty
about: Adam Peaty is a British competitive swimmer, best known for his breaststroke. He won the 100-meter breaststroke gold at both the 2016 and 2020 Summer Olympics, making history as the first British male swimmer to gain an Olympic gold in 24 years, and the first ever to successfully defend an Olympic title.

name: Tori Kelly
about:
Tori Kelly is an American singer-songwriter who first came to fame as a teenage YouTube star, then as a participant in the 2010 edition of American Idol.  
 
In 2012, Kelly reduced her debut EP and then, in 2013, was signed by Capital Records. She released her debut studio album, Unbreakable Smile, in 2015 which reached number two on the Billboard 200 chart.

name: Ellie Goulding
about: Ellie Goulding is an English singer, songwriter and record producer. She rose to fame in 2010 after her debut album Lights topped the UK albums chart and spawned a number of hit singles, including "Starry Eyed" and "Lights."

name: Jamie Vardy
about: Jamie Vardy is an English professional footballer who currently plays as a striker for Leicester City in the English Premier League. He began his career playing for non-league teams such as Stocksbridge Park Steels and Halifax Town.

name: Alice Eve
about: Alice Eve is an English actress whose breakthrough role came in 2010 when she starred in the comedy film She's Out of My League. She went on to appear in several other successful films, including Star Trek Into Darkness (2013), Before We Go (2014), and Bombshell (2019).

name: Peter Sagan
about: Peter Sagan is a Slovak cyclist known for a wide array of victories in the cycling world including three consecutive World Road Race Championships (2015, 2016, 2017) and a European Road Race Championship (2016).

name: Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce
about: Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce is a Jamaican sprinter, nicknamed "Pocket Rocket," who has won multiple Olympic gold medals and numerous World Championships titles.

name: Krysten Ritter
about: Krysten Ritter is an American actress and author. She is best known for her roles in Jessica Jones (2015–2019),   (2009–2011), Don't Trust the B---- in Apartment 23 (2012–2013), and Big Eyes (2014).

name: JoJo [Joanna Levesque]
about: JoJo is an American singer, songwriter, and actress. She is best known for her hit single "Leave (Get Out)", which topped the Billboard Pop Songs chart in 2004 and earned her a nomination for an MTV Video Music Award.

name: DaBaby
about: DaBaby is an American rapper that came to fame in 2019 after being signed with Interscope on the back of a series of mixtapes. He has since released three studio albums, with Kirk (2019) and Blame It on Baby (2020) charting at number one.

name: Jodie Sweetin
about:
Jodie Sweetin is an American actress best known for her role as Stephanie Tanner in   (1987-1995).  
 
From this early fame as a child star, Sweetin progressed into work as a television personality before returning to the resume her role as Stephanie Tanner in the Netflix sequel Fuller House (2016-2020).

name: Nicola Peltz
about: Nicola Peltz is an American actress, best known for various television and film roles including The Last Airbender (2010) and Bates Motel (2013-2015). She married Brooklyn Beckham, the son of   and  , in 2022. Her father is Nelson Peltz, a billionaire businessman and investor.

name: Dwyane Wade
about: Dwyane Wade spent the majority of his career with the Miami Heat, with whom he won three NBA championships. He is a 13-time All Star, 8-time All NBA team member, and 3-time NBA champion.

name: Luis Suárez
about:
Suárez is renowned as one of the greatest strikers of all time, having scored over five-hundred goals in national and club football.  
 
An often controversial player, nicknamed 'El Pistolero' (The Gunman), Suárez has been accused of biting opposing players three times.  
 
Despite these issues, he has won an incredible array of awards including two European Golden Shoes and a Premier League Golden Boot.

name: Bob Morley
about: Bob Morley is an Australian actor, best known for playing Bellamy Blake in The 100 (2014-2020). He previously played Drew Curtis in Home and Away in 2007 and then went on to feature in further television shows including It Takes Two, The Strip, Neighbours, and Blinder.

name: Gabriel Medina
about: Gabriel Medina is a Brazilian professional surfer known for his impressive skills and accomplishments in the world of competitive surfing. Bursting onto the scene at a young age, Medina quickly made a name for himself. He was the second person to have executed a maneuver called the "Backflip," and the first to do so in a competition.

name: Gabby Douglas
about:
The first African-American and the first woman of color to win the Olympic individual all-around gold medal. 
 
Douglas was also the first US gymnast to win gold at the same Olympics in both the individual all-around and team competitions .

name: Amy Lee
about: Amy Lee is an American singer-songwriter and musician, best known as the lead vocalist and songwriter for Evanescence. She has also composed the soundtracks to War Story (2014) and, alongside Dave Eggar, Indigo Grey: The Passage (2015).

name: Alexis Sánchez
about: Alexis Sánchez, known also simply as Alexis, is a Chilean football player who is a forward for the Chile national team as well as for the Ligue 1 club Marseille. Since the beginning of his career he was known as "El Niño Maravilla" (The Wonder Child), and he is regarded by many as the best ever Chilean player.

name: Angelique Kerber
