about: Angelique Kerber is a German professional tennis player. She is a former world No. 1 in singles and is currently ranked No. 18 by the Women's Tennis Association (WTA).

name: Hayley Williams
about: Hayley Williams is an American singer-songwriter. She is best known as the lead vocalist and primary songwriter of the rock band Paramore. Williams rose to fame in 2004 after the release of Paramore's debut album All We Know Is Falling, which featured hit singles like "Pressure" and "Emergency."

name: Vanessa Hudgens
about: Vanessa Hudgens is an American actress and singer, best known for playing Gabriella Montez in the   film series (2006-2008). While she had previously starred in the film Thirteen (2003), it was High School Musical which brought her into the limelight.

name: Jared Kushner
about: Jared Kushner is an American investor, real estate developer, and former senior advisor to his father-in-law, President  . His role in the Trump administration covered a broad range of issues, from Middle East policy to criminal justice reform.

name: Derrick Henry
about: Derrick Henry is an American football player, best known as running back for the Tennessee Titans. His size and rushing game have earned him the nickname "King Henry."

name: Jonah Hill
about: A two-time Academy Award nominee ("Moneyball" and "The Wolf of Wall Street"), he is also known for his roles in "Superbad", "Funny People", "21 Jump Street" and "This Is the End".

name: Charlie Heaton
homePlace: Leeds, West Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom
about: Charlie Heaton is best known for his role as Jonathan Byers in the Netflix series "Stranger Things" (2016-present). He has no formal acting training and entered the field through work as an extra and in commercials.

name: Alexander Wang
about:
Alexander Wang is an American fashion designer, best known for his fashion brand which is also called Alexander Wang. He served as creative director at Balenciaga from 2015 after the departure of  Nicolas Ghesquière. 
 
Stylistically, Wang is known for his use of black fabrics and his inspiration by urban designs. He brought this aesthetic to Balenciaga when he was creative director there, and then returned with it to his eponymous brand in 2015.

name: Cynthia Erivo
about: Cynthia Erivo is a critically acclaimed actress, singer and songwriter and has appeared successfully on stage, television and film.

name: Dove Cameron
about:
Best known for playing a dual role as both title characters in the Disney Channel sitcom "Liv and Maddie."  
 
She also starred in the Disney Channel original movie "Cloud 9" as Kayla Morgan.

name: Alison Brie
about: Alison Brie is an American actress who first came to fame with the role of Trudy Campbell in Mad Men (2007-2015), for which she won a Screen Actors Guild Award. She went on to star as Annie Edison in Community (2009-2015) and voice Diane Nguyen in BoJack Horseman (2014-2020).

name: Kevin Systrom
about: Kevin Systrom is an American entrepreneur, computer programmer, and investor. He is the co-founder and former CEO of Instagram, a social media platform he created in 2010 with  .

name: Hailee Steinfeld
about: Steinfeld was the breakout star of the acclaimed 2010 film True Grit, where she starred alongside   and  , and was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress. Since then she has gained recognition for roles in films such as Ender's Game (2013), Begin Again (2013), The Edge of Seventeen (2016).

name: Timothée Chalamet
about: Timothée Chalamet is an American actor who is best known for his breakout role in the 2017 coming of age drama film 'Call Me By Your Name.' He is one of the most acclaimed young actors of his generation with numerous accolades to his name.

name: Labrinth [Timothy Lee McKenzie]
about: Labrinth is an English singer and rapper who started out with a career in music production before moving to pursue his own work as a recording artist. He was then best known for his collaborations with Tinie Tempah, including "Pass Out" (2010) and "Frisky" (2010).

name: Eddie Redmayne
about: Elizabeth: The Golden Age (2007), The Other Boleyn Girl (2008), The Theory of Everything (2014) and The Danish Girl (2015).

name: Tom Hiddleston
about: Tom Hiddleston is an English actor known for his dynamic performances in film, television, and theater. He attended the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art and went on to make his professional acting debut in the West End production of Cymbeline in 2007.

name: Joseph Quinn
about: Joseph Quinn is a British actor whose breakout role came in 2022 when he portrayed Eddie Munson in the fourth season of the Netflix series " ."

name: Jesse Lingard
about: Jesse Lingard is an English football player who plays attacking midfielder and winger for Nottingham Forest, as well as the English national team. He is one of only three players to have scored in all three of the FA Cup, the FA Community Shield, and the EFL Cup.

name: Poppy [Moriah Rose Pereira]
about: Poppy is an American singer-songwriter, musician, and YouTube personality. She first gained notoriety for her surrealist performance art pieces in which she acted the part of an android satirizing modern culture.

name: Michael B. Jordan
about: One of Michael B. Jordan's first significant roles as in the critically acclaimed TV series "The Wire" (2002) as Wallace. Further Tv roles followed, including in "All My Children", "Friday Night Lights".

name: Matthew Stafford
about: Matthew Stafford is an American football player, best known as quarterback for the Los Angeles Rams. He holds a number of rankings and records, including the place for fastest player to reach 40,000 passing yards.

name: Peter Burling
homePlace: Tauranga, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand
about: Peter Burling is one of the best sailers in New Zealand sailing history.

name: Natalia Dyer
about: Natalia Dyer is an American actress, best known for her role as Nancy Wheeler on   (2016-present). She has also appeared in several films since breaking into the limelight, including Velvet Buzzsaw (2019) and Things Heard & Seen (2021).

name: Adam Ondra
about: Adam Ondra is a Czech professional rock climber known for his achievements in lead climbing, bouldering, and competition climbing. He has won World Championship titles in both lead climbing and bouldering in 2014, as well as victories in the World Cup series for both disciplines.

name: Jyoti Amge
about: Jyoti Amge is the world's shortest living woman. She is 62.8 centimeters (2 ft 3⁄4 in) tall due to a genetic disorder called primordial dwarfism.

name: Bethany Hamilton
about:
Bethany Hamilton had her arm bitten off by a shark while surfing aged 13 in Hawaii. She went on establish a profession surfing career, despite her disability. 
 
Hamilton detailed her struggles in her autobiography :Soul Surfer", published in 2004. This was made into a film in 2011.

name: Klay Thompson
about:
Klay Thompson is an American basketball player, best known as one of the all-time greatest three-point shooters in NBA history. He currently plays for the Golden State Warriors, where he has been a four-time NBA champion. 
 
Thompson is the son of NBA player Mychal Thompson, and his brother Mychel Thompson also played professional basketball.  
 
A third brother, Trayce Thompson, is a baseball player currently playing with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

name: Yalitza Aparicio
about:
The actress made her film debut in  's 2018 film "Roma", winning critical acclaim for her performance, including being nominated for an Academy Award for Best Actress.  
 
She was the first indigenous American woman to be nominated and the second Mexican after  .

name: Bryson Tiller
about: Bryson Tiller is an American singer, songwriter, and rapper best known for his debut studio album Trapsoul (2015, which peaked at number 8 on the US Billboard 200. His single "Don't" was certified double platinum in the US and was also a top 10 hit on the US Billboard Hot 100.

name: Yani Tseng
about: Yani Tseng is a Taiwanese professional golfer who has been ranked as the number one female golfer in the world for 109 weeks. She has won five major championships and 15 LPGA Tour events.

name: Ronnie Radke
about: Ronnie Radke is an American musician who is currently the lead singer of rock band Falling in Reverse. He was previously the lead singer of the post-hardcore band Escape the Fate.

name: Calvin Harris
about: Calvin Harris is a Scottish DJ and record producer who came to fame with his debut album I Created Disco in 2007 and his second album Ready for the Weekend in 2009. He had several major singles from these albums that charted highly in the UK and internationally: "Acceptable in the 80s," "The Girls," and "I'm Not Alone."

name: Jade Thirlwall
homePlace: South Shields, Tyne and Wear, England, United Kingdom
about:
Jade Thirlwall is an English singer-songwriter best known as a member of the English girl group Little Mix, which formed on the eighth series of The X Factor in 2011. Thirlwall and the other three members became the first group to win the competition.  
 
Thirlwall has written and produced songs for the group's albums and appeared in films such as Glory Days: The Documentary (2016) and as a guest judge on RuPaul's Drag Race UK.

name: Elizabeth Holmes
about: Founder and CEO of Theranos, a blood test company she founded at the age of 19 while studying at Stanford University.

name: Florence Pugh
about: Florence Pugh is an English actress who came to fame with her performance in the 2014 drama film The Falling alongside  . She also received critical acclaim for her performance in the independent drama Lady   (2016).

name: Avicii
about: Tim Bergling, the Swedish musician, DJ and music producer had adopted the stage name Avicii, a Buddhist term for a realm of hell as a teenager. He rose to fame with the 2011 single "Levels". In 2013 he released his debut album "True"   with its lead single "Wake Me Up", causing controversy by infusing country and folk into electronic dance music. In 2015 he released his second studio album "Stories".

name: Tenley Albright
about:
Tenley Albright was an American figure skater and surgeon, best known for her series of major wins in the sport, including a gold medal at the 1956 Olympics and the World Championship in 1953 and 1955. 
 
Albright also graduated from Harvard Medical School in 1961 at the age of 24, then going on to practice as a surgeon for 23 years. She was inducted into the National Women's Hall of Fame in 2015.

name: Judi Dench
about: Judi Dench is an esteemed English actress, appearing in theatre , television and film throughout her career.

name: John McCain
homePlace: Coco Solo, Panama Canal Zone, US unincorporated territory
about: John McCain served as a United States Senator from Arizona for over 30 years. He was also the Republican nominee for President of the United States in the 2008 election, which brought him to international attention.

name: Bill Russell
about: Widely regarded as one of the greatest basketball players of all time, Bill Russell was five-times NBA Most Valuable Player. He was central to the Celtics winning 11 NBA championships and captained the American team to the an Olympic gold medal in 1956.

name: F. W. de Klerk
about: De Klerk grew up in a political family, his father was a leading senator and de Klerk entered parliament himself in 1972 as part of the conservative National Party.

name: Gordie Howe
about:
Often referred to as Mr. Hockey, and is generally regarded as one of the greatest hockey players of all time. Most famous for his scoring prowess, physical strength, and career longevity. He is the only player to have competed in the NHL in five different decades (1940s through 1980s).  
 
A four-time Stanley Cup champion with the Red Wings, he won six Hart Trophies as the league's most valuable player and six Art Ross Trophies as the leading scorer.

name: Jacob Zuma
about: Jacob Zuma rose from a poor background to become one of South Africa's most prominent freedom fighters in the Apartheid era. He rose further to become President of South Africa 2009-2018 before allegations of corruption forced him from office.

name: Toni Morrison
about: Toni Morrison's work centered on the black experience in America. Her style was both lyrical and unflinching and dealt with topics such as slavery, rape, murder and the supernatural. Her first novel was "The Bluest Eyes" published in 1970 when she was 39.

name: Aretha Franklin
about: Starting out as a gospel singer this "Queen of Soul's" six-decade-long career has made Franklin one of the most influential and important voices in pop history.

name: Mary Tyler Moore
about: Mary Tyler Moore revolutionized the portrayal of women on television. She came to fame for her roles in " " and "The Mary Tyler Moore Show," both of which depicted independent, career-focused women.

name: Tony Roche
homePlace: Wagga Wagga, New South Wales, Australia
about: Won one Grand Slam singles title (1966 French Open) and thirteen Grand Slam doubles titles. He also coached multi-Grand Slam winning World No. 1s, including  , Patrick Rafter, and  .

name: Tony La Russa
about:
Best known for his tenures as manager of the Chicago White Sox, Oakland Athletics, and St. Louis Cardinals.  
 
La Russa guided his teams to three World Series titles, six league championships and twelve division titles in 33 seasons.

name: Vigdís Finnbogadóttir
about:
In 1980 Vigdís Finnbogadóttir became the first woman in the world to be elected as head of state in Iceland. She was re-elected three times before retiring in 1996. Although the position was largely ceremonial, she is credited with raising the profile of Iceland during her time in office.  
 
Prior to her election Finnbogadóttir worked as a theatre director and television presenter of culture and language classes.

name: Barry Levinson
about: Barry Levinson is an American filmmaker, screenwriter, and producer who has made a significant impact on the film industry over the course of his career. He first gained recognition as a screenwriter, with his work on films such as ...And Justice for All (1979) and Inside Moves (1980).

name: Gerhard Schröder
about: Gerhard Schröder is a German politician who served as Chancellor of Germany from 1998 to 2005. His term was marked by economic reforms, foreign policy decisions, and subsequent controversies related to his involvement with Russian companies.

name: Joseph Estrada
about: 13th President of the Philippines from 1998 to 2001. He initially gained popularity as a film actor, which he used to make gains in politics. He was eventually ousted as President, however, after allegations of corruption spawned an impeachment trial.

name: Alex Ferguson
about: Alex Ferguson is a retired Scottish football manager and former player who managed Manchester United from 1986 to 2013. He is the most successful and longest-serving manager in the history of Manchester United, leading them to thirteen Premier League titles, five FA Cups, and two UEFA Champions League titles. Ferguson also before this managed Aberdeen, with whom he won three league titles and four domestic cups.

name: Robert Kraft
about:
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of The Kraft Group, a diversified holding company with assets in paper and packaging, sports and entertainment, real estate development and a private equity portfolio. 
 
He also owns the New England Patriots, an NFL team, and was instrumental in preventing a league lockout in 2012.

name: Silvio Berlusconi
about: Silvio Berlusconi is an Italian media tycoon and politician, best known for serving three times as Prime Minister of Italy: 1994-1995, 2001-2006, and 2008-2011. Since 2019 he has served as a Member of the European Parliament, and since 2022 as a member of the Senate of the Republic.

name: Tina Turner
about: Powerful R&B and rock singer with an energetic stage approach had a 50 year career as the "Queen of Rock and Roll", winning 8 Grammy  Awards.

name: Julie Christie
about: Darling (1965),   (1965), Afterglow (1997) and Away from Her (2006).

name: Warren Beatty
about: Beatty broke onto the scene with 'Splendor in the Grass' (1961). Then at 29, he produced and acted in 'Bonnie and Clyde' (1967)—from there he continued this successful transition from a young actor to a respected producer.

name: Radovan Karadžić
about: Radovan Karadžić is a Bosnian Serb politician, best known for his leadership of the Serbian side during the Bosnian War (1992-1995). He was subsequently charged by the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia with war crimes and crimes against humanity, and found guilty of genocide.

name: Shirley Bassey
homePlace: Tiger Bay, Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom
about:
Bassey is best known for recording the theme songs for three major James Bond films: Goldfinger (1964), Diamonds Are Forever (1971), and Moonraker (1979).  
 
She also recorded a total of 27 Top 40 UK hits, which included two number-ones.

name: Roy DeMeo
about: Roy DeMeo rose to prominence in the Gambino crime family. He is best known for leading the DeMeo crew, a group involved in murder, car theft, drug dealing, and other illegal activities.

name: Ban Ki-moon
homePlace: Injō, Japanese Korea (now Eumseong, South Korea)
about: Ban Ki-moon served as the eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations from 2007 to 2016. He is known for his work on climate change, peacekeeping reform, and humanitarian issues.

name: Bill Cosby
about: Began his career as a stand up comedian before moving into television with "I Spy". Cosby performed in and produced children's TV shows such as "The Electric Company" before creating hugely successful " " (1984-1992), significant for featuring an affluent African American family.

name: Rita Moreno
about:
Known for her roles in films " " (1961), "The King and I" (1956), and in television in the children's show "The Electric Company". 
 
Moreno is one of one a few people to achieve an EGOT, an Emmy, Golden Globe, Oscar and Tony award.   awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2004.

name: Mike Ditka
about: Coached the Chicago Bears for 11 years and New Orleans Saints for three years. He is one of only two people to win an NFL title as a player, an assistant coach, and a head coach, and the only individual in modern NFL history to win a championship with the same team as a player and a head coach.

name: Gary Player
about: Regarded as one of the greatest players in the history of golf.

name: Juan Carlos I
about: Born in Rome during his family's exile, Juan Carlos was named as the successor to Spanish dictator   over his father. He became King on November 22, 1975 after Franco's death two days earlier, and the monarchy was thus restored.

name: Roy Emerson
about: Amateur tennis player who won 12 amateur Grand Slam tournament singles titles and 16 Grand Slam tournament men's doubles titles, the only male player to have completed an amateur Career Grand Slam in both singles and doubles.

name: Rod Laver
about: Laver is regarded as one of the greatest tennis players of all-time and certainly the best left-hander. As the only person to win the coveted Grand Slam twice (1963, 1969), his 200 singles titles are the most in tennis history.

name: Ian Kershaw
about:
One of the most distinguished and pre-eminent historians of German history, Kershaw is particularly noted for his works on the Nazi era, including his momentous biographies of  , published in two parts in 1998 and 2000. 
 
Other books of note include The End, Hitler's Germany 1944–45 (2011) and To Hell and Back: Europe, 1914-1949 (2015). Kershaw has also acted as an historical consultant and interview subject on a number of documentaries.

name: Hale Irwin
about: Won the US Open in 1974, 1979, 1990 and the US Senior Open in 1998 and 2000.

name: Frank Mahovlich
about: Frank Mahovlich, often referred to as the "Big M," is a Canadian ice hockey player and politician. He played NHL during the 1960s and early 1970s, primarily with the Toronto Maple Leafs, and later with the Detroit Red Wings and the Montreal Canadiens.

name: Tom Selleck
about: Best known for his starring role as the private investigator Thomas Magnum in the television series "Magnum, P.I." (1980 to 1988), based in Hawaii. He also plays Police Chief Jesse Stone in a series of made-for-TV movies based on Robert B. Parker novels. Since 2010, he has appeared as NYPD Police Commissioner Frank Reagan in the drama "Blue Bloods" on CBS-TV.

name: Patrick Stewart
about: Most widely known for his roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and as Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men film series, as well as his prolific stage roles with the Royal   Company.

name: Joan Baez
about: The American folk singer was one of the biggest names during the revival of folk music in the 1960s. She released her debut album "Joan Baez" in 1960. Later she worked with  , with whom she had a relationship, recording his songs and helping bring his work to greater prominence.  In 1969 Baez performed at Woodstock, which further raised her profile.

name: Jack Nicklaus
about: Jack Nicklaus, nicknamed "The Golden Bear," amassed a record 18 major championships and 117 professional wins, setting standards that remain benchmarks in the sport.

name: Jackie Stewart
about: Won 27 Grand Prix wins and the World Formula 1 championship in 1969, 1971 and 1973.

name: Alan Kay
about: Alan Kay is an American computer scientist known for his work as a pioneer of object-oriented programming and the use of a graphical user interface. These concepts have served as the basis of modern consumer computing ever since.

name: Pele
about:
Regarded by many football critics, past players, current players and football fans in general to be the best player of all time.  
 
In 1999, Pele was voted World Player of the Century by the International Federation of Football History & Statistics (IFFHS). 
 
After retiring in 1977, he became a worldwide ambassador for football.

name: Peter Ueberroth
about: Orchestrated the organization of the 1984 Summer Olympics, which involved a Soviet-led boycott and was the first Summer Olympics since 1932 to make a profit.

name: Desmond Tutu
about: Desmond Tutu is a South African cleric and theologian known for his work as an anti-apartheid and human rights activist. He rose to international fame during the 1980s as an opponent of apartheid, advocating nonviolent resistance and racial reconciliation.

name: Carl Sagan
about: Carl Sagan was an American astronomer, cosmologist, author, and science communicator. He is best known for his work as a science popularizer, including his 1980 television series Cosmos: A Personal Voyage, which has been watched by more than 500 million people in over 60 countries.

name: Hosni Mubarak
about:
The Fourth President of Egypt, Mubarak ruled in an autocratic manner from 1981 until he was ousted during the Arab Spring in 2011. Before he entered politics, he was a career officer in the Egyptian Air Force. 
 
He stepped down after 18 days of demonstrations during the 2011 Egyptian revolution.

name: Yakubu Gowon
about: Yakubu Gowon was Head of State of Nigeria during the Nigerian Civil War, which he oversaw the end of and delivered a famous speech seeking reconciliation in which he declared that there was "no victor, no vanquished."

name: Geraldine Ferraro
about: Ferraro was the Democratic Party's vice-presidential nominee in 1984; which made history, with her being the first female nominee for a major political party. Prior to this she had been a teacher, then a District Attorney; heading the Special Victims Bureau.

name: Al Michaels
about: Now employed by NBC Sports after nearly three decades (1977–2006) with ABC Sports, he is perhaps best known for his many years of calling play-by-play of National Football League games, including nearly two decades with Monday Night Football.

name: Charles Koch
about: Charles Koch is an American billionaire businessman and philanthropist. He has been the co-owner, chairman, and CEO of Koch Industries, America's second-largest private company, since 1967. The conglomerate, which was originally started by Koch's father,  , has interests in industries such as manufacturing, refining, and distribution of various commodities.

name: Carol Kaye
about: One of the most prolific recorded bass guitarists in rock and pop music, Carol Kaye has played on an estimated 10,000 recordings as a Los Angeles based session musician.

name: Judd Hirsch
about: A stage and screen actor who has had a long and distinguished career in film, television and on the Broadway stage. He is most well known for his role in the TV comedy "Taxi" which ran from 1978-83, opposite Tony Danza and  . He twice won the Emmy for Best Actor for the series in 1981 and 1983. His other successful TV series include "Dear John" and "Numb3rs".

name: Bob Cousy
about: In his first 11 NBA seasons, he led the league in assists eight straight times and introduced a new blend of ball-handling and passing skills that earned him the nicknames "The Houdini of the Hardwood" and "Mr. Basketball".

name: Phil Esposito
about: He played 18 seasons in the NHL for the Chicago Black Hawks, Boston Bruins and New York Rangers, and is considered one of the best to have ever played the game. He won two Stanley Cup Championships.

name: James Bevel
about: James Bevel was one of the most prominent members of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference under the leadership of   that spearheaded non-violent action in the fight for civil rights in the 1960s. Bevel was one of the prime organizational forces behind the 1963 Children's Crusade in Birmingham Alabama protesting against segregation in the city.

name: Akihito
about: Akihito reigned as the Emperor of Japan from 1989 until his abdication in 2019, when he was succeeded by his son,  . Per Japanese imperial tradition, he will be formally known as Emperor Heisei upon his death. He succeeded his father,  , the wartime emperor, in 1989.

name: Tommy John
about:
Tommy John is an American former professional baseball pitcher and four-time MLB All-Star who played for 26 seasons between 1963 and 1989. He is best known for his breakthrough surgical procedure, now known as Tommy John surgery. 
 
John tore his ulnar collateral ligament in a 1974 match against the Montreal Expos, which had previously meant the end of a player's career. John had a successful operation and went on to pitch until 1989.

name: Anne Rice
about:
Anne Rice was a popular modern author of gothic fiction, erotic literature and Christian literature. Her books have sold over 100 million copies.  
 
Rice's most popular series The Vampire Chronicles revolves around a vampire character Lestat and has been adapted both into a film staring   and   as well as comics.

name: Jim Jones
mainType: Founder of the Peoples Temple Cult
about:
Religious leader, community organizer, and leader of the Peoples Temple, best known for the mass suicide of 909 of its members in Jonestown, Guyana.  
 
Five individuals were murdered at the nearby airstrip, including Congressman Leo Ryan.

name: Angela Mortimer
about:
Angela Mortimer is a former world number one tennis player in women's singles.  
 
She won three Grand Slam singles titles during her career, the 1955 French Championship, the 1958 Australian Championship, and the 1961 Wimbledon Championship.

name: Michael Gambon
about: Michael Gambon is an Irish-English actor, best known today for his portrayal of Professor Albus Dumbledore in the   series (2004-2011). While the role was initially played by  , Gambon took over after his death.

name: Maurice Sendak
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Maurice Sendak is best known for his 1963 book "Where the Wild Things Are," which has been credited with revolutionizing children's picture books.

name: Jaclyn Smith
about: Jaclyn Smith is an American actress and businesswoman best known for her role as Kelly Garrett in the television series Charlie's Angels (1976–1981). After acting she transitioning into business, establishing a long-standing partnership with Kmart.

name: John Hopfield
about: John Hopfield is an American physicist and neuroscientist who has made significant contributions to the fields of artificial intelligence (AI), neural networks, and computational neuroscience. He is best known for the development of the Hopfield network, a recurrent neural network model that has been widely used in AI research and has provided valuable insights into the dynamics of associative memory and pattern recognition.

name: Sandra Haynie
about: Won the US Open in 1974, du Maurier Classic in 1982 and the LPGA Women's Championship in 1965 and 1974.

name: Natalie Wood
about: Natalie Wood is an actress who starred in some of the most iconic American films of the 20th century.

name: Ángel Cordero Jr.
about:
Ángel Cordero Jr. is an American thoroughbred horse racing jockey who was the first Puerto Rican to be selected for the United States' Racing Hall of Fame.  
 
He held the record wins at the Saratoga Race Course for thirteen years, rode three Kentucky Derby winners, and won over 6000 races during his career.

name: Robert Mundell
about:
1999 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics - for his pioneering work in monetary dynamics and optimum currency areas. 
 
Called the 'father of the euro' Mundell's work laid much of the groundwork for the establishment of the European currency.

name: Daniel Ortega
about: Ortega first served as the leader of Nicaragua during the latter phase of the country's civil war, from 1985 to 1990, where his term in office was noted for a controversial nationalization and land reform movement. He is a leader of the Sandinista left-wing political party and former guerrilla group.

name: Michael Bloomberg
about: Michael Bloomberg founded Bloomberg L.P., a financial technology and media company, and served as the Mayor of New York City for three terms.

name: Ratko Mladić
about: Nicknamed the "Butcher of Bosnia", Mladić was the chief of staff of the Army of Republika Srpska during the Bosnian War. In this role he commanded the troops that overran Srebrenica in 1995 and committed genocide of 8,300 Muslim men and boys.

name: Eddy Merckx
about:
Won the Tour de France between 1969 and 1972 and again in 74.  
 
Also won the Giro d'Italia in 1968, 1970 and between 1972 and 1974.

name: Barbara Walters
about: One of the best-known American broadcast journalists, Walters began her career in 1953 and began as a television journalist in the early 1960s when she appeared on NBC. Her strong ability to interview guests led to increased popularity and more airtime on the network.

name: Shakuntala Devi
about: Devi was popularly known as the 'Human Calculator' for her feats of  mental calculation. Her father was a magician and performer who discovered his daughters talent while teaching her a card trick when she was three years old.

name: Richard Petty
about: Winner of 7 NASCAR Championships and 7 Daytona 500 races.

name: Woody Allen
about:
American actor, director, screenwriter, comedian, musician and playwright whose career spans more than 50 years.  
 
Allen has been nominated 24 times and won four Academy Awards: three for Best Original Screenplay and one for Best Director ("Annie Hall").  
 
He has more screenwriting Academy Award nominations than any other writer.

name: Herb Alpert
about: Herb Alpert is an American trumpeter, composer, and record producer who became a prominent figure in the music industry as the co-founder of A&M Records. He is best known for his work with the Tijuana Brass, a group he formed in the early 1960s that blended Latin, jazz, and pop music styles.

name: John Searle
about: John Searle was an American philosopher who made significant contributions to the fields of philosophy of mind, language, and artificial intelligence (AI). He is best known for his development of the "Chinese Room" thought experiment, which challenges the idea that computers can truly possess understanding or consciousness in the same way that humans do.

name: Tom Stoppard
about: Tom Stoppard rose to fame with his early play "Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead" (1966), it was his first play on Broadway  and went on to win four Tony Awards. Later plays of significance include "Arcadia", "The Coast of Utopia", and "Every Good Boy Deserves Favour".

name: Edwin Meese
about: Edwin Meese III is best known for his role as U.S. Attorney General under President   from 1985 to 1988. He is a key figure in conservative politics and has been a close advisor to Reagan throughout his political career. Meese continues to be active in conservative policy circles and organizations.

name: Ken Rosewall
about: Won a record 25 tennis Majors including 8 Grand Slam singles titles, and is considered to be one of the top male tennis players of all time.

name: Robert F. Engle
about: Robert F. Engle is best known for developing the ARCH model, which transformed the analysis of financial market volatility. He won the 2003 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for this work, sharing it with  .

name: Ray Floyd
about: Won 22 events on the PGA Tour and four Major Championships: the 1969 PGA Championship, the 1976 Masters, the 1982 PGA Championship, and the 1986 U.S. Open.

name: Lorne Michaels
about:
Created and produced "Saturday Night Live".  
 
Michaels has also been the producer for "Late Night" on NBC since 1993 and "The Tonight Show" on NBC since 2014.

name: Nino Benvenuti
about: Nino Benvenuti was an Italian boxer who competed from 1956 to 1972. He was a two-time Olympic gold medalist and a three-time world champion in the welterweight and junior middleweight divisions.

name: Lenny Wilkens
about:
Played 15 seasons for four NBA teams before becoming a head coach, where he won the 1979 NBA Championship with the Seattle SuperSonics.  
 
As coach he had one most successful records in NBA history.

name: James Brown
about: James Brown was an American musician and songwriter who was one of the most influential figures in 20th century popular music. He is often referred to as the "  of Soul," and his music had a profound impact on the development of funk, soul, and hip hop.

name: James Earl Jones
about: James Earl Jones was an American stage and screen actor with a career spanning decades and fields of entertainment. He earned 3 Tony Awards, 2 primetime Emmy Awards, and a Grammy Award, as well as an honorary 'lifetime achievement Oscar.

name: Ray Davies
about: Primary singer and songwriter for the British rock-pop band The Kinks (1964-96), Ray Davies played rhythm guitar, while his younger brother Dave played lead. He crafted such songs as "You Really Got Me"; "Waterloo Sunset"; "Lola"; "Celluloid Heroes"; "Come Dancing" and "Better Things". His lyrics often unfold in story form, and are filled with varying degrees of nostalgia, distress, and social satire.

name: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis
about: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis was a prominent American figure best known as the wife of the 35th president of the United States,  . She became an international symbol of style, elegance, and grace during her tenure as First Lady from 1961 until her husband's assassination in 1963.

name: Cyril Ramaphosa
about: Before he was President of South Africa in 2018 Cyril Ramaphosa had a long history in politics as an anti-apartheid activist, trade union leader and businessman.

name: Beth Daniel
about: Became a member of the LPGA Tour in 1979 and won 33 LPGA Tour events, including one major championship, during her career, and is a member of the World Golf Hall of Fame.

name: Kathy Bates
about: Kathy Bates is an American actress who has won an Academy Award, two Primetime Emmy Awards, and two Golden Globe Awards. She is best known for her breakthrough role as the obsessive fan Annie Wilkes in the 1990 thriller "Misery," for which she won the Oscar for Best Actress.

name: Robin Williams
about:
Rose to fame with his role as the alien Mork in the TV series "Mork & Mindy", he went on to establish a successful career in both stand-up comedy and as a critically acclaimed actor. 
 
Williams received the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his performance in "Good Will Hunting".  
 
He also received two Primetime Emmy Awards, four Golden Globes, two Screen Actors Guild Awards and five Grammy Awards.

name: Rick James
about: The major popularizer of funk music in the late 1970s and early 1980s thanks to million-selling hits such as 'You and I' (1978), 'Give It to Me Baby' (1981) and 'Super Freak' (1981).

name: Alain Prost
about: Alain Prost is a French racing driver and team owner, best known as having earned the title of Formula One Drivers' Champion four times (1985, 1986, 1989, 1993). Prior to  's win at the 2001 Belgian Grand Prix, Prost held the record for most race wins in Formula One history.

name: Patty Hearst
about: Patty Hearst is the granddaughter of American publisher  , whose life story was the inspiration for the main character in Orson Welle's Citizen Kane (1941). His granddaughter, however, is better known for her kidnapping by and later involvement with the Symbionese Liberation Army.

name: Meryl Streep
about: Widely considered the greatest actress of her generation, if not all time, Streep has won three Academy Awards of 21 nominations, a record for number of nominations. She has also received 31 Golden Globe nominations, with eight wins, both more than any other actor in history.

name: Giuseppe Conte
about: Giuseppe Conte served as Italy's longest-serving independent Prime Minister from June 2018 to February 2021. He became Prime Minister after a career as a lawyer as the leader of a coalition government between the Five Star Movement and the League. Like former Prime Minister  , Conte had no previous political experience before becoming Prime Minister.

name: Kelsey Grammer
homePlace: Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands, USA
about: Frasier Crane in Cheers, Fraiser

name: Alexander Lukashenko
about: Alexander Lukashenko is Europe's longest ruling leader, having been the country's first and only President since 1994. Often called 'Europe's last dictator' Lukashenko heads an authoritarian government with close ties to Russia and the support of  .

name: Stevie Nicks
about: Singer-songwriter Stevie Nicks is the first woman to be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame twice, for the first time in 1998 as part of supergroup Fleetwood Mac and as a solo performer in 2019.

name: Antonio Banderas
about: Banderas began his film career in his native Spain, appearing in a number of films by prominent Spanish director Pedro Almodóvar. These included  "Law of Desire", in which he played a gay man, and the internationally successful "Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown".

name: Clarence Thomas
about: Clarence Thomas is an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States. He is known for his conservative views and originalist approach to interpreting the Constitution.

name: Jon Secada
about: Jon Secada is a Cuban-American singer and songwriter who has sold over 15 million records worldwide, won multiple Grammy Awards, and is known for his hits, Broadway performances, and support for music education.

name: Malcolm Turnbull
about: Turnbull was Leader of the Liberal Party in Australia twice (2008–2009, 2015–2018). During his first stint at the helm, he was Leader of the Opposition; during the second, Prime Minister. Throughout, from 2004 to 2018, he was the Member of Parliament for Wentworth in New South Wales.

name: Forest Whitaker
about: Forest Whitaker is an American actor and director who first gained attention for his part in the critically acclaimed film Bird (1988), in which he portrayed the legendary jazz musician Charlie Parker. Whitaker won several awards for the role, including the Best Actor award at the Cannes Film Festival.

name: Brian Boitano
about:
Boitano originally found acclaim for his jumping ability, winning the US National Championship in 1985 and 1986, and the World Championship in 1986.  
 
He made a concerted effort to improve his artistic presentation in 1987, and successfully defended his national title for two more years, while winning the world title as well as Olympic Gold in 1988. 
 
In 1996 he was inducted into both the World Figure Skating and the United States Figure Skating Halls of Fame.

name: Dennis Rodman
about:
One of the best defensive players in the NBA during the 1990s and arguably the best rebounding forward in NBA history. He won five NBA Championships (three as a member of the Chicago Bulls led by  ) and the NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award twice.  
 
Also well known for his controversial antics, his dyed hair, and his piercings and tattoos.

name: Bill Elliott
about: Won the Winston Cup Championship in 1988 and the Daytona 500 in 1985 and 1987.

name: Frank Bruno
about: Frank Bruno is a British professional boxer who competed from 1982 to 1996. Recognized for his impressive punching power, Bruno was victorious in 40 out of his 45 professional fights, with 38 of his wins coming by knockout.

name: Andrew Dice Clay
about: Andrew "Dice" Clay is an American stand-up comedian, best known for his deliberately provocative persona of "The Diceman" with which he first came to fame in the 1980s. He was a major act in the 1990s, being the first comedian to sell out Madison Square Garden for two nights consecutively.

name: Bernhard Langer
about: Two-time Masters champion and one of the world's leading golfers throughout the 1980s and 1990s. In 1986, he became the sport's first official number one ranked player.

name: Philippe of Belgium
about:
Phillippe has been the reigning King of Belgium since the abdication of his father, Albert II, on 21 July 2013. 
 
Prior to this he served on the Belgian Foreign Trade Board and headed more than 60 economic missions in this capacity.

name: Barry Bonds
about:
Considered to be one of the greatest baseball players of all-time, Bonds has numerous batting records, including the single season home run record and career home run record.  
 
Son of MLB All-Star  , he played for 22 seasons in the MLB; seven seasons with the Pittsburgh Pirates and 15 for the San Francisco Giants.  
 
Bonds was a central figure in baseball's steroids scandal, which has tainted his accomplishments.

name: Paul Kagame
homePlace: Tambwe, Gitarama Province, Ruanda-Urundi, Kingdom of Belgium
about:
Paul Kagame was born in Rwanda in 1957. He was orphaned at a young age and raised in a refugee camp in Uganda.  
 
He joined the rebel group that eventually overthrew the Rwandan government and became the country's president in 2000.  
 
He has been credited with helping to end the Rwandan Genocide, and has been praised for his economic and social reforms in Rwanda.

name: Kate Jackson
about: Kate Jackson's most famous role was as  Sabrina Duncan in the 1970's TV series "Charlie's Angels". Jackson also starred in a number of other TV series including "The Rookies" and "Scarecrow and Mrs. King" which she also produced.

name: Dennis Quaid
about: Big Easy, Dreamscape, Right Stuff

name: Billy Bob Thornton
about: Billy Bob Thornton is an American actor who came to fame internationally with the 1996 film Sling Blade, which he wrote, directed, and starred in as the main character. For this role he was nominated for two Academy Awards, for Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Actor, of which he won the former.

name: Courteney Cox
about: Courteney Cox is best known for her role as Monica Geller in the television series "Friends" (1994-2004) and as Gale Weathers in the "Scream" film franchise.

name: Steven Seagal
about: Steven Seagal began his working life as a martial arts instructor teaching Aikido.

name: Frances McDormand
about: Frances McDormand is an American actress who gained fame for her role in the 1996 film Fargo, directed by her husband Joel Coen, for which she earned an Academy Award for Best Actress. She often collaborates with her husband and his brother Ethan Coen, including films such as Blood Simple (1984) and The Man Who Wasn't There (2001).

name: Holly Hunter
about: Broadcast News (1987), The Piano (1993) and Thirteen (2003).

name: Wesley Snipes
about: One of Wesley Snipes' early roles was the   video "Bad" directed by  . The role got him noticed by filmmaker   and led starring roles in Lee's films "Mo' Better Blues" (1990)  and "Jungle Fever" (1991).

name: Dan Brown
about: Dan Brown is an American author who has gained international acclaim for his bestselling thriller novels, which blend historical facts, cryptography, and conspiracy theories to create gripping and suspenseful narratives. His works have captivated readers worldwide and have been translated into numerous languages.

name: Nicolás Maduro
about: Maduro has been the President of Venezuela since the death of previous leader Hugo Chavez in 2013. His term in office has seen the explosion of the Venezuelan crisis, marked by exceptionally high inflation, shortages of basic goods, the collapse of the country's economy and a political crisis. In early 2019 opposition politician and President of the National Assembly,  , declared himself the President and was recognized by 54 countries.

name: Larry Holmes
about:
Known for his famous left jab, he was the WBC Heavyweight Champion from 1978 to 1983, The Ring Heavyweight Champion from 1980 to 1985, and the IBF Heavyweight Champion from 1983 to 1985.  
 
His 20 successful title defenses are second only to  ' 25.

name: Edward James Olmos
about: Edward James Olmos is an American actor, best known for his roles in television series such as TV crime series Miami Vice (1984-1989) and Battlestar Galactica (2004-2009). He won both an Emmy for Best Supporting Actor and a Golden Globe for Miami Vice.

name: Dan Marino
about:
Held or currently holds dozens of NFL records associated with the quarterback position. Despite never being on a Super Bowl-winning team, he is recognized as one of the greatest quarterbacks in American football history.  
 
Best remembered for his quick release and powerful arm, he led the Dolphins to the playoffs ten times in his seventeen-season career. He was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2005.

name: James Cameron
about: James Cameron is responsible for some of the most popular and technically advanced films ever made including "Terminator 2", "Titanic" (1997) and "Avatar" (2009).

name: Al Green
about: Al Green is an American singer, songwriter, pastor, and record producer known for his hit singles in the early 1970s. He has been honored with the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

name: James Patterson
about: James Patterson is an American author and philanthropist known for his prolific output of popular commercial fiction. He has written countless best-selling books, many of which have become top sellers in the crime, thriller, and young adult genres.

name: Mario Draghi
about: Mario Draghi served as President of the European Central Bank from 2011 to 2019 and Prime Minister of Italy from 2021 to 2022. He is credited with helping to stabilize the euro currency during the Eurozone debt crisis.

name: Chris Christie
about: Chris Christie is an American politician and former governor of New Jersey. Christie's political career highlights include his two-term governorship from 2010 to 2018 where he tackled fiscal issues and the recovery post-Hurricane Sandy. Though his tenure was marred by controversies like the Fort Lee lane closure scandal, he nevertheless had a short-lived candidacy in the 2024 presidential election.

name: Jeffrey Immelt
about: Jeffrey Robert Immelt is an American business executive known for his tenure as the Chairman and CEO of General Electric (GE) between 2001 and 2017. His leadership spanned a challenging period in GE's history, encompassing both the global financial crisis and significant shifts in global business trends.

name: Ashraf Ghani
about: Ashraf Ghani is an Afghan politician who served as the President of Afghanistan until the country fell to the Taliban in 2021.

name: Peter Šťastný
about: Peter Šťastný was an outstanding Slovakian ice hockey center during the 1980's and 90's.

name: Melissa Etheridge
about: Known for the raspy style of her singing, Etheridge's confessional rock n roll pop-influenced style has often been compared to   or  .

name: Dwight Gooden
about: Dwight Gooden, nicknamed "Dr. K" and "Doc", is a former American professional baseball pitcher who played 16 seasons in the Major Leagues.

name: Jordan Mechner
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Jordan Mechner created the popular games "Karateka" and "Prince of Persia," which are known for changing how characters move in video games.

name: Glenn Close
about: Glenn Close began her acting career on stage in the 1970s and has gone on to win 3 Tony awards, the first for "The Real Thing (1983).

name: Scott Hamilton
about: Scott Hamilton was the first American male skater to win Olympic gold since 1960. Known for his athletic performances and shorter stature due to childhood illness, Hamilton won gold in 1984 at the Sarajevo Winter Olympics.

name: Courtney Walsh
about: Courtney Walsh is a former Jamaican cricket who played for the West Indies from 1984 to 2001 and captained the team in 22 Test matches. He is known as one of the all-time greatest fast bowlers, in particular for his partnership with  .

name: Kim Cattrall
about: Kim Cattrall is best known for her role as Samantha Jones in the television series "Sex and the City" (1998-2004). She has worked in film, television, and theater over the course of her career.

name: Wilfred Benítez
about: Became the youngest world champion aged 17 years and 176 days when he won the WBA Light Welterweight title.

name: Kathryn Bigelow
about: Kathryn Bigelow is an American director, best known for The Hurt Locker (2008) and Zero Dark Thirty (2012). She was the first woman to win an Academy Award for Best Director, which she won for her work on The Hurt Locker.

name: David Fincher
about: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button; The Social Network; Gone Girl; Fight Club

name: Victor Pecci
about: Famous for reaching the 1979 French Open final. After beating   in the semi-finals, he lost to Bjorn Borg in the finals.

name: Robyn Erbesfield-Raboutou
about: Robyn Erbesfield-Raboutou is an American rock climber and coach. She is best known for taking the Climbing World Cup title four times, as well as coaching key names in the next generation of climbers. Her achievements led to her being inducted into the Boulder Sports Hall of Fame in 2018.

name: Satoru Iwata
about: Satoru Iwata was a Japanese video game programmer, businessman, and the fourth president and CEO of Nintendo. He led Nintendo from 2002 until his death in 2015, during which time he oversaw several significant developments including the Nintendo DS and Wii game consoles.

name: Jessica Lange
about: Tootsie (1982), Music Box (1989), and Blue Sky (1994).

name: Mark McGwire
about:
Nicknamed "Big Mac", McGwire played first base for the Oakland Athletics and the St. Louis Cardinals between 1986 and 2001.  
 
He averaged a home run once every 10.61 at bats, the best at bats per home run ratio in baseball history, and achieved national fame in 1998 in his pursuit of  ' single-season home run record.

name: Jerry Rice
about:
Played 20 seasons in the National Football league, and is widely considered to be not only the greatest wide receiver in NFL history, but one of the greatest players of all time.  
 
All-time leader in most major statistical categories for wide receivers and the all-time career leader in receptions, touchdown receptions, and receiving yards. He was selected to the Pro Bowl 13 times and won three Super Bowl rings with the San Fransisco 49ers.

name: Greg Chappell
about: Greg Chappell is regarded as one of the most stylish batsmen of 1970s and 1980s cricket, and Australian captain for 48 Tests 1975-83.

name: Mike Schmidt
about: Played 18 seasons in the MLB, all for the Philadelphia Phillies, between 1972 and 1989. Best known for his combination of power hitting and strong defense, he is considered one of the greatest third baseman in baseball history.

name: Arianna Huffington
about:
Best known for her news website "The Huffington Post'.  
 
At one time a liberal Democrat, Huffington later became a popular conservative commentator in the mid-1990s, after which she re-adopted liberal political beliefs in the late 1990s.

name: John Brennan
about: John Brennan served as Director of the America's Central Intelligence Agency from 2013 to 2017 under President  .

name: Evander Holyfield
about: Evander Holyfield is an American boxer who began his career in the sport at the age of 12 and quickly rose through the amateur ranks.

name: Don Mattingly
about: Don Mattingly was an outstanding first baseman who spent his entire major league baseball playing career with the New York Yankees (1982-95).

name: Jeff Bridges
about: Jeff Bridges is an American actor known for his prolific career spanning over seven decades, during which period he has been a Hollywood fixture with enduring roles as both a leading man and supporting actor.

name: David Thewlis
about: David Thewlis's most famous role is that of Remus Lupin in the   films J.K. Rowling has said that Remus Lupin is her favourite series character. The character first appears in the 3rd film in the series "Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban" (2004).

name: Robin Givens
about: Robin Givens is best known for her role in the ABC sitcom "Head of the Class" and her high-profile marriage to boxer  . She has overcome personal challenges to build a successful career in television and film. Givens has appeared in numerous productions and has recently transitioned into directing.

name: Mike Judge
about: Best known as the creator of the cartoon series "Beavis and Butt-Head", and "King of the Hill", Mike Judge is also the filmmaker behind cult favorites "Office Space" (1999) and "Idiocracy" (2006).

name: Kathy Griffin
about: Kathy Griffin is an American comedian, actress, and television host. She is known for her stand-up comedy which often includes candid discussions of celebrities and her personal life. Griffin starred in the reality show "Kathy Griffin: My Life on the D-List" and has released several comedy albums, winning a Grammy Award.

name: Danny Elfman
about: Danny Elfman is a highly celebrated American composer, singer, songwriter, and record producer who has made significant contributions to the film and music industries. Elfman composed the iconic theme music for the television series   and Desperate Housewives.

name: Eric Dickerson
about: Eric Dickerson is an American football player, best known for his time as a running back in the NFL. His career spanned 11 seasons from 1983 to 1993, and his early year in particular were marked by extraordinary performances and records. With a unique upright running style, Dickerson's speed and agility let him to dominate the field.

name: Paul Gross
about: Known for his lead role as Constable Benton Fraser in the television series "Due South" and the Canadian television series "Slings and Arrows". He wrote, produced, directed, and starred in the 2008 war film "Passchendaele".

name: Hugh Laurie
about: Hugh Laurie is a British comedian who rose to fame as one half of the sketch show duo "A Bit of Fry and Laurie" with friend  . Fry went on to appear in " " with  .

name: Alan Jackson
about: Alan Jackson is an American singer-songwriter known for his musical style which has been called "neotraditional" for its combining traditional honky-tonk with contemporary pop country influences. He is one of the all-time best-selling artists, with a total of 75 million records sold worldwide.

name: Jonathan Frakes
about: Commander William T Riker-Star Trek Next Gen

name: Bernard Arnault
about: Bernard Arnault is the richest person in the world as of 2024, with an estimated net worth of $211 billion as of May 2024. This wealth comes from his position as founder, chairman, and CEO of LVMH, the world's largest luxury goods company.

name: António Guterres
about: António Guterres began his professional life as an academic before joining the Socialist Party in 1972 and devoting himself to politics.

name: Michael Flatley
about: Came to fame with the Irish music and dance show "Riverdance", which he choreographed and starred in. After falling out with the producers, Flatley went on to produce his own shows such as "Lord of the Dance" and "Feet of Flames".

name: Pablo Escobar
about: Pablo Escobar founded and led the Medellín Cartel, which dominated the cocaine trade into the United States during the 1980s and early 1990s. Known as "the king of cocaine," Escobar became one of the wealthiest criminals in history.

name: Dmitry Muratov
about: Russian journalist Dmitry Muratov established the newspaper Novaya Gazeta in 1993. It has gone on to investigate and report on corruption and human rights abuses in Russia and elsewhere and on the war in Chechnya.

name: Dale Jarrett
about: Dale Jarrett is an American stock car racing driver and sports commentator best known for winning the NASCAR Winston Cup Series championship in 1999 and for his three Daytona 500 victories in 1993, 1996, and 2000. He was inducted into the NASCAR Hall of Fame in 2014.

name: Carlene Carter
about: Carlene Carter has had a musical career spanning several decades. She is also a part of part of the  : her mother is  , the second wife of  , and her father was Carl Smith, to whom   was married before Cash.

name: Robert Allen Litchfield
about: One of the ten FBI most wanted fugitives during the 1980s.

name: Mary-Louise Parker
about: Mary-Louise Parker is an American actress who made her debut on stage but came to fame with a series of major films. She has since transitioned into a television career and featured on   (2001-2006), Angels in America (2003), and Weeds (2005-2012).

name: Anthony Edwards
about: Anthony Edwards is an American actor, best known for playing Dr. Mark Greene for the first eight seasons of ER. This role brought him many accolades: a Golden Globe Award in 1998, six Screen Actors Guild Awards, including Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Drama Series (1996 and 1998), and four Emmy nominations.

name: Angus Young
about: Angus Young is a Scottish-born Australian guitarist and songwriter best known as the co-founder, lead guitarist, and last remaining original member of the legendary rock band AC/DC. Formed in 1973 with his brother Malcolm Young, AC/DC went on to become one of the most successful rock bands in history, with their 1980 album "Back in Black" being the second best-selling album worldwide.

name: Huey Lewis
about: Huey Lewis is an American singer and songwriter, perhaps best known for the scene in American Psycho where Patrick Bateman, played by  , references his band: Huey Lewis and the News. They are also known by an older generation for their best-selling album Sports (1983) and their work on the Back to the Future (1985) soundtrack.

name: Steve Ballmer
about: Steve Ballmer is an American businessman and former CEO of Microsoft. He is known for significantly increasing the company's revenue and diversifying its product line during his tenure. Ballmer also owns the Los Angeles Clippers NBA team.

name: Ming-Na Wen
about: Ming-Na Wen is an American actress and voice actress. She is well known for her roles as Melinda May in the series Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., as well of the voice of Mulan in the Disney animated film Mulan (1998) and in the video game Kingdom Hearts II (2005).

name: Oliver Stone
about: Oliver Stone is an American screenwriter, director and producer. He first found success for his writing, winning the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay in 1978 for Midnight Express.

name: Hank Williams Jr
about: Williams Jr is a successful American country musician that began his career imitating the sound of his father,   Sr.

name: Laurence Fishburne
about: Laurence Fishburne is best known for his roles as Morpheus in "the Matrix trilogy" with   and as Tyrone Miller in  's "Apocalypse Now" (1979).

name: Viktor Yanukovych
about: Yanukovych served as President of Ukraine from 2010 until his ouster in the 2014 revolution.

name: Harvey Weinstein
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Along with his brother Bob Weinstein, co-founded the Miramax film studio and the Weinstein Company. Together they produced several award-winning films such as  ,   and Gangs of New York.

name: Uta Pippig
about:
Uta Pippig is a German long-distance runner known as the first woman to win the Boston Marathon in three consecutive years: 1994, 1995, 1996. She has also won the Berlin Marathon three times as well (1990, 1992, 1995) and represented Germany at the 1992 and 1996 Olympic Games. 
 
Pippig's win at the 1994 Boston Marathon, her marathon best of 2:21:45, has also earned here the then-record for third-fastest female marathon runner.

name: Ricki Lake
about:
The actress made her film debut in John Waters' cult film "Hairspray" in 1988 as the main character Tracey Turnblad alongside   and Divine.  
 
She went on to host talk show "Rikki Lake" aged just 24. The show ran from 1993-2004. She later hosted another show "The Rikki Lake Show" from 2013-14, which won her a Daytime Emmy award.

name: Maggie Gyllenhaal
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Achieved recognition in a supporting role in the independent cult film, "Donnie Darko" (2001) opposite her brother the actor  , before her breakthrough role in the sadomasochistic romance, "Secretary" (2002), for which she received critical acclaim and a Golden Globe nomination.

name: Michael Strahan
about:
Michael Strahan is an American television personality and former professional football player. Since retiring from the NFL, Strahan has worked as a football analyst for Fox NFL Sunday as well as in various other television roles, including as a co-host of ABC's Good Morning America. 
 
Strahan spent his 15-year NFL career as a defensive end for the New York Giants. During his final season in 2007, he contributed to the Giants win against the New England Patriots at Super Bowl XLII.

name: Heidi Klum
about:
Became internationally known for her appearances on the cover of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue before becoming the first German model to become a Victoria's Secret Angel in 1997. 
 
Following a successful modeling career, she became the host and a judge of the reality show "Project Runway" which earned her an Emmy nomination in 2008 and a win in 2013 for Outstanding Host for a Reality or Reality-Competition Program.

name: Jacinda Ardern
about: Jacinda Ardern is a politician from New Zealand known for her tenure as the Prime Minister of New Zealand, a position she held from October 2017 until February 2023. Her leadership was marked by empathetic and decisive responses to several crises that occurred during her tenure, and she has been compared to a new wave of politicians including   and  .

name: Kelly Macdonald
about:
Kelly Macdonald is a Scottish actress, best known as the voice of Princess Merida in Brave (2012). She made her film debut with Trainspotting (1996) and went on to star in a number of major films such as No Country for Old Men (2007) and Anna Karenina (2012). 
 
Macdonald has also starred in television series, for instance in the Black Mirror episode "Hated in the Nation" as well as her role as Margaret Thompson in Boardwalk Empire (2010-2014).

name: Rachel Maddow
about: Rachel Maddow has been the host of her own show "The Rachel Maddow Show" since 2008 on US cable television network MSNBC, the winner of three Emmy awards.

name: Tom Glavine
about: Played for the Atlanta Braves and won the   Award in 1991.

name: Kanye West
about: Consistently regarded as one of the greatest and most controversial artists of the 21st century, West's musical innovation on albums such as The College Dropout, Graduation, My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy and Yeezus won him plaudits from music critics and commercial success. With a total of 21 Grammy Awards to his name, he is one of the most awarded artists of all time.

name: Calvin Borel
about: Calvin Borel, nicknamed "Bo'rail" for his style of riding close to the rail, is best known for his multiple Kentucky Derby wins. He is one of the most successful and popular jockeys in American horse racing history.

name: Kent Desormeaux
about: Kent Desormeaux is regarded as one of the best-ever American thoroughbred jockeys of all-time.

name: Dan Jansen
about: Dan Jansen is a former American speed skater who is widely recognized as one of the greatest long-track speed skaters in history. He is best known for his incredible determination and resilience, which ultimately led him to Olympic gold after years of heartbreaking setbacks.

name: Peyton Manning
about:
A five-time league MVP, he played for the Indianapolis Colts for 14 seasons from 1998 to 2011 before signing with the Denver Broncos.  
 
Manning won the Super Bowl in 2006, has won 5 AP NFL MVP Awards and has set numerous records at the quarterback position.

name: David Tennant
homePlace: Bathgate, West Lothian, Scotland, United Kingdom
about: David McDonald was born to a Scottish minister, taking the stage name Tennant after Pet Shop Boys singer Neil Tennant to avoid confusion with another actor.

name: Jon Hamm
about:
Best known for playing advertising executive Don Draper in the AMC drama series "Mad Men" (2007-15), for which he won a Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Drama Series in 2008.  
 
His first leading film role was in the 2010 independent thriller "Stolen", and he has also appeared in "The Town", "Sucker Punch", and "Bridesmaids".

name: Samantha Power
about: Samantha Power has served in a variety of high-level positions in the United States government. She is known for her work on genocide prevention and humanitarian intervention.

name: Hilary Swank
about: Boys Don't Cry (1999), Million Dollar Baby (2004) and The Homesman (2014).

name: Matt Biondi
about: Won 8 gold medals in swimming across the 1984, 1988 and 1992 Olympic Games.

name: Greg Maddux
about:
Best known for playing for the Chicago Cubs and the Atlanta Braves. The first pitcher in MLB history to win the   Award for four consecutive years, during which he had a 75–29 record with a 1.98 ERA.  
 
He is the only pitcher in MLB history to win at least 15 games for 17 straight seasons, and he holds the record for most Gold Gloves with eighteen.

name: Idris Elba
about: Came to fame playing the character of Stringer Bell in HBO's critically acclaimed TV series "The Wire" (2002-08). Went on to star in the UK crime series "Luther" for which Elba won a Golden Globe and Screen Actors Guild award.

name: Alicia Silverstone
about: Alicia shot to international fame in the teen classic film comedy "Clueless" (1995), partly based on the novel "Emma" by  . The film also starred Stacey Dash, Brittany Murphy and   in his debut film role.

name: Catriona Matthew
about: Catriona Matthew is best known for her success on the LPGA Tour and Ladies European Tour. She was the first Scottish woman to win a major golf tournament.

name: Shinji Mikami
about: Shinji Mikami is best known for creating the Resident Evil series, as well as his influence more broadly in the survival horror genre and third-person shooter gameplay.

name: Trent Reznor
about: Known as the member of industrial rock band "Nine Inch Nails"

name: John C. Reilly
about: John C. Reilly is a frequently nominated actor who has worked with some of the best directors in Hollywood. He first appeared in Brian De Palma's "Casualties of War" (1989). Reilly has worked on three of Paul Thomas Anderson's films Hard Eight (1996), Boogie Nights (1997) and Magnolia (1999).

name: Nelly
about: Nelly is an American rapper best known for his major chart-topping singles, including "Hot in Herre" (2002) and "Dilemma" (2002). His career began in earnest with his debut album Country Grammar, which gave birth to two top-10 singles including "Ride wit Me."

name: Aamir Khan
about: Aamir Khan is an Indian actor, director, and producer who became a key figure in Indian cinema over a 30-year career. He has been honored with multiple awards for his work, including nine Filmfare Awards and four National Film Awards, as well as India's Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.

name: Ray Lewis
about: Considered one of the greatest ever to play middle linebacker, playing his entire 17-year career with the Baltimore Ravens and winning two Super Bowls (2000 and 2013).

name: Diane Kruger
about: Her fluency in German, French and English has enabled Diane Kruger to become an international star.

name: Danai Gurira
about: Danai Gurira is best known for her roles in television, film, and theater—including "The Walking Dead" and " "—as well her writing for Broadway. She is also recognized for her work in raising awareness about women's issues and HIV/AIDS.

name: River Phoenix
about: River Phoenix was acclaimed as one of the most influential actors of his generation before he died of a drug overdose on a West Hollywood sidewalk at the age of 23.

name: Jason Statham
about: Statham came to initial prominence in the films Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels (1998) and Snatch (2000). These films and other roles led him to being typecast in the role of the antihero, typically playing tough guy and Machiavellian characters in films.

name: Kristen Bell
about: Kristen Bell started her career on stage in New York before appearing as the lead in the cult teen noir TV series "Veronica Mars" (2004-7) for which she earned critical acclaim. The series later produced a film and was revived on TV in 2019.

name: Christian Slater
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Christian Slater is an American actor and producer who has been active in the entertainment industry since the 1980s. He made his film debut with The Legend of Billie Jean (1985) and has continued to star through to films such as He Was a Quiet Man (2007) and Nymphomaniac (2013).

name: Alex Jones
about: Alex Jones is an American radio host known as a prominent advocate of various conspiracy theories, both through The Alex Jones Show and his website, InfoWars.

name: Michael Bay
about: Michael Bay is an American film director and producer best known for his action films characterized by special effects and explosions. His notable works include Bad Boys (1995), The Rock (1996), Armageddon (1998), Pearl Harbor (2001), and the Transformers series.

name: Eric Lindros
about: Eric Lindros is a Canadian ice hockey player known for his physical power combined with scoring ability and playmaking. Drafted as the first overall pick by the Quebec Nordiques in 1991, he famously refused to play for the team, leading to his trade to the Philadelphia Flyers. His time with the Flyers was marked by both outstanding performances and recurring injuries.

name: Olivia Munn
about: Olivia Munn is an American actress and former television host who went from co-hosting on Attack of the Show! to acting in The Newsroom and"X-Men: Apocalypse.

name: Jessica Chastain
about: Jessica Chastain is an American actress and producer. She is known for her roles in films such as Zero Dark Thirty, The Help, and Miss Sloane. In 2012, she was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Actress for her performance in Zero Dark Thirty.

name: Sanath Jayasuriya
about:
Widely regarded as one of the greatest One-Day International players of all time; his style of play is considered to have revolutionized ODI cricket by introducing the hard-hitting strategy now adopted by all competing nations. 
 
He played as captain for the Sri Lankan national team for many years. He is the only player to score over 12,000 runs and capture more than 300 wickets in ODI cricket.

name: Sam Worthington
about: Sam Worthington is an Australian actor, best known for his role as Jake Sully in Avatar (2009). He reprised this role in the 2022 sequel, Way of Water. Alongside this, Worthington has also played major roles in Terminator Salvation (2009), Clash of the Titans (2010), and Wrath of the Titans (2012).

name: Ralf Schumacher
about: Formula One career spanned 11 seasons from 1997 to 2007, during which time he won six races from 180 starts and achieved 27 podium finishes, before retiring from Grand Prix racing after failing to secure a drive for 2008.

name: Roberto Carlos
about: Roberto Carlos is Brazilian footballer who is widely considered one of the greatest left-backs in the history of the sport. He rose to prominence in the 1990s, playing for prestigious clubs such as Palmeiras, Inter Milan, and Real Madrid.

name: John Krasinski
about:
Best known for playing Jim Harper on the NBC version of "The Office".  
 
He has been nominated for an Emmy Award four times, as well as two Screen Actors Guild Awards. 
 
Aside from his work on The Office, which he also produced and occasionally directed, Krasinski has also starred in a number of films and further television shows. Most notably in the Amazon series "Jack Ryan", in which he plays the title character.

name: Conchita Martínez
about: Conchita Martínez is a Spanish former professional tennis player and current coach.

name: Simon Pegg
about:
Pegg has had numerous successes in the comedy genre, particularly known for his roles in Shaun of the Dead (2004), Hot Fuzz (2007) and The World's End (2013). 
 
In addition to these roles, which he often co-writes, Pegg is known for starring in the Mission: Impossible franchise and the Star Trek reboots.

name: Jeff Gordon
about: Jeff Gordon is an American professional stock car racing driver. He was renowned for his dominating presence in NASCAR, securing four Cup Series championships and winning the prestigious Daytona 500 three times.

name: Martin Brodeur
about: Played his entire career with the New Jersey Devils, and is highly regarded as the greatest goaltender of all time. In his 21-year tenure with the Devils, he has won three Stanley Cup championships. He also won two Olympic gold medals with Team Canada in the 2002 and 2010 Winter Olympic Games.

name: Joe Sakic
about:
Played his entire 21-year NHL career with the Quebec Nordiques/Colorado Avalanche franchise where he won two Stanley Cups.  
 
Regarded as one of the most able team leaders in league history, and his wrist shot is considered one of the best in NHL history.

name: Juan Carlos Ferrero
about: Juan Carlos Ferrero is a Spanish tennis player who was ranked number one in 2003, the same year as he won the men's singles title at the French Open. He won a title of 16 ATP titles, as well as being runner-up for the 2002 French Open and the 2003 US Open.

name: Brett Favre
about: Brett Favre is an American professional football quarterback. He is best known for his 20-year stint in the National Football League (NFL), where he accomplished a record-breaking streak of 321 consecutive starts.

name: Natasha Lyonne
about: Most well known for her roles in the Netflix productions "Orange is the New Black" (2013-19) for which she was nominated for an Emmy award and for "Russian Doll" (2019), which Lyonne also co-created along with   and Leslye Headland. Lyonne also wrote, produced and directed "Russian Doll" which was subsequently nominated for 15 Emmy awards.

name: Tom Ellis
about: The British actor has starred in a number of popular TV series including the lead in US fantasy series "Lucifer" (2016-2021) and opposite   in the comedy "Miranda" (2009-2015).

name: Josh Brolin
about: Josh Brolin is an American actor, best known recently for his roles in Oldboy (2013), Sicario (2015) and as Thanos in   (2014) and the   series. More recently he played Gurney Halleck in Dune (2021) and will return to this role in its upcoming sequel.

name: Jeezy
about:
Jay Wayne Jenkins, also known as Jeezy, is an American rapper signed to Def Jam Recordings.  
 
He is best known for popularizing trap music, along with T.I. and  , which has since firmly seized mainstream appeal.

name: Julie Bowen
about: Julie Bowen is an American actress, best known for her role as Claire Dunphy in Modern Family (2009-2020) alongside an ensemble cast including Ed O'Neill,   and Ty Burrell. She was nominated for an Emmy six times for her performance on this show, of which she won two.

name: Dan O'Toole
about: Dan O'Toole is a Canadian sports broadcaster best known for co-hosting SportsCentre with  . He has since successfully transitioned to a career in podcasting.

name: Rishi Sunak
about: Rishi Sunak is a British politician who is currently serving as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, as well as Leader of the Conservative Party, since 2022. Prior to this role he served as Chancellor of the Exchequer under  , and he has been MP for Richmond (Yorks) since 2015.

name: Sebastian Thrun
about: Sebastian Thrun is best known for his work on self-driving cars and online education. He currently serves as the CEO of Kitty Hawk Corporation and chairman and co-founder of Udacity, an online learning platform.

name: 50 Cent
about: Curtis James Jackson III, better known as 50 Cent, is an American rapper, actor, and entrepreneur who came to fame with his 2003 album Get Rich or Die Tryin' and further established his presence in the industry by founding G-Unit Records the same year.

name: Scott Foley
about:
Scott Foley is an American actor best known for his television work. He first came to fame playing Noel Crane on Felicity (1998-2002). He had recurring roles in Scrubs and Dawson's Creek, as well as a starring in Scream 3 (2000), for which he was nominated for a Teen Choice Award. 
 
Foley was married to Jessica Garner from 2000 to 2003, and then to Marika Dominczyk in 2007. The couple have three children together, a daughter and two sons.

name: Andrea Jaeger
about:
Andrea Jaeger is an American tennis player, known for her brief but highly successful career which came to an early end with a major shoulder injury. She went professional at 14 and reached world number two by the time she was 16. 
 
Jaeger won ten singles titles, as well as reaching the singles final at Wimbledon in 1983 and at the French Open in 1982. Her career came to the end at 19, however, and she went on to obtain a degree in theology.

name: Shah Rukh Khan
about: Often referred to as the "King of Bollywood", Khan is one of the most successful actors in the world, and one of the most popular actors in Bollywood history.

name: Gerard Way
about:
The lead singer of My Chemical Romance, Way co-founded the band in September 2001 and led it until its dissolution in March 2013. 
 
Since then he has embarked on a solo career, including the album Hesitant Alien, released in 2014. 
 
In addition to music he has pursued comic book writing, authoring the series The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys and the comic book The Umbrella Academy.

name: Laverne Cox
about:
Best known for her role as Sophia Burset on the Netflix show " ", she is also the first openly transgender person to be nominated for an acting Emmy.  
 
Cox is now considered a prominent LGBT advocate.

name: Lisa Bonet
about: Most well known professionally for her role in the phenomenally successful sitcom "The Cosby Show" alongside   and Phylicia Rashad which ran from 1984-1992. She also appeared in its spin-off "A Different World".

name: Vin Diesel
