about: Vin Diesel is most famous for his starring role in the very successful film franchise "The Fast and the Furious" playing  Dominic Toretto alongside   and The Rock. His other high profile role is as the voice of Groot in the " " films and the Marvel film universe.

name: Joseph Fiennes
about: Joseph Fiennes is the youngest of six children. His siblings include the actor   and the director Martha Fiennes.

name: Katie Price
about: Katie Price, also known as Jordan, is a British media personality, author, former glamour model, occasional singer, and businesswoman. She initially gained recognition as a topless female glamour model in a pictorial Page 3 in British tabloid newspaper The Sun, at the age of 18, under her pseudonym, Jordan.

name: Steve Yzerman
about:
Played his entire NHL career with the Detroit Red Wings. He served as captain for over 1300 games, making him the longest-serving captain of any team in North American major league sports history.  
 
He led the Red Wings to three Stanley Cup Championships. He was also executive director of Team Canada for the 2010 and 2014 Winter Olympics, winning two consecutive gold medals.

name: Robert Rodriguez
about:
Rodriguez shoots, edits, produces, and scores many of his films in Mexico and his home state, Texas. 
 
His first film was El Mariachi (1992), and others include From Dust 'til Dawn (1996) which started a long association with  , Sin City (2005), the Spy Kids films and co-directing the 2007 double-feature film Grindhouse with Tarantino.

name: Russell Brand
about:
Achieved notoriety as the host of "Big Brother's Big Mouth", a "Big Brother" spin-off. In 2008, he had a major role in "Forgetting Sarah Marshall", which led to a starring role in "Get Him to the Greek" in 2010. 
 
Received significant media coverage for controversies such as his dismissal from MTV, his behaviour as a presenter at various award ceremonies, and his drug use.

name: Benedict Cumberbatch
about: The English actor initially came to notice for his portrayal of the scientist   in the 2004 television film "Hawking". He went on to greater acclaim when he took on the role of Sherlock Holmes in the British series "Sherlock" (2010-17) created by Steven Moffat and Mark Gatiss and playing opposite   as Dr. Watson. Cumberbatch won an Emmy for the role.

name: Too Short
homePlace: South Central Los Angeles, California, USA
about:
Too $hort, born Todd Shaw, is an American rapper and record producer known for his involvement in the West Coast hip hop scene; starting with his debut album: Don't Stop Rappin' (1985). 
 
In 1985, Too Short started a label (Dangerous Music) with Freddie B. This label later became Up All Nite Records, which he runs to this day.

name: Sarah Michelle Gellar
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Came to prominence in the late 1990s, landing roles in 1997's horror films "I Know What You Did Last Summer" and "Scream 2". 
 
Gellar also portrayed Buffy Summers on the WB/UPN TV series "Buffy the Vampire Slayer" (1997–2003).

name: Wasim Akram
about: Wasim Akram is a former Pakistani cricketer who is widely regarded as one of the greatest bowlers of all time. He played in Test cricket for Pakistan from 1984 to 2001, and in One Day International cricket from 1984 to 2003. He is one of only two bowlers to have achieved the distinction of becoming a Wisden Cricketer of the Year twice.

name: Richard Ayoade
about: Richard Ayoade is a British comedian and actor who gained widespread recognition for his role as Maurice Moss in the British sitcom The IT Crowd (2006–2013), which earned him a BAFTA for Best Male Comedy Performance in 2014.

name: Sundar Pichai
about: The Indian-born American computer scientist moved to America to study at Stanford University earning a degree in engineering and materials science.

name: Shannen Doherty
about: Shannen Doherty is a TV and film actress known for her roles as Brenda Walsh in " ", and as Prue Halliwell in "Charmed".

name: Rob Thomas
about: Primary songwriter and lead singer of the band Matchbox Twenty. Also records and performs as a solo artist. He earned three Grammy awards for co-writing and singing on the   triple-platinum hit "Smooth", on the album Supernatural in 1999.

name: David Ortiz
about: David Ortiz is regarded as one of the most effective designated hitters in baseball history.

name: Sean Astin
about:
Sean Astin is an American actor, best known for playing Samwise Gamgee in The   trilogy (2001-2003). He has also featured in The Goonies (1985), Toy Soldiers (1991), and 50 First Dates (2004).  
 
More recently Astin has acted in a number of television series, including Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012-2017) and the third season of Strange Things (2017).

name: Michael Cohen
about: Michael Cohen came to fame as  's personal attorney and self-described "fixer." He played a significant role in various controversies surrounding Trump's business and political career.

name: David Robinson
about: A 10-time NBA All-Star, the 1995 NBA MVP, a two-time NBA Champion (1999 and 2003), and a two-time Olympic Gold Medal winner (1992, 1996), he is widely considered to be one of the greatest centers in both college and NBA history.

name: Jodhi May
about: Jodhi May is an English actress who began her career as a child actress. She made history as the youngest recipient of the Best Actress Award at the Cannes Film Festival for her performance in "A World Apart" (1988) at the age of 12, which she shared with co-stars Barbara Hershey and Linda Mvusi.

name: Cynthia Nixon
about: Cynthia Nixon is best known for her role as Miranda Hobbes in the television series "Sex and the City" (1998-2004) and its subsequent films and revival.

name: Lucy Lawless
about: New Zealand actress, activist and musician best known for playing the title character of the internationally successful television series " ".

name: Ernie Els
about: Ernie Els, known as "The Big Easy" due to his imposing stature and seemingly effortless golf swing, is a South African professional golfer. He has won more than 70 professional career victories, including four major championships: the U.S. Open in 1994 and 1997, and The Open Championship in 2002 and 2012.

name: Petteri Orpo
about: Petteri Orpo is a Finnish politician who has served as the Prime Minister of Finland since 2023. He is also the leader of the National Coalition Party, a position he has held since 2016.

name: Trey Parker
about:
Co-created the hit animated TV sitcom "South Park" with Matt Stone. 
 
The pair also co-developed the musical comedy "The Book of Mormon" and the feature-length musical "Cannibal! The Musical".

name: Nancy Kerrigan
about: Nancy Kerrigan was an outstanding American figure skater who unfortunately is best known for being the victim of one of the most infamous assaults in sporting history.

name: Rodney King
about: Rodney King, an African American construction worker was on parole for robbery when after a car chase in Los Angeles he was stopped and beaten by LA police officers in 1991. The beating was filmed and shown around the world.

name: Scott Morrison
homePlace: Waverley, Syndey, New South Wales, Australia
about: Morrison became leader of the Liberal Party in 2018 after Prime Minister   fell to a leadership challenge, at which point Morrison was sworn in as Prime Minister, then leading the Liberal Party to another victory in the 2019 election. Prior to politics he had worked in the New Zealand Office of Tourism and Sport, then as managing director of Tourism Australia.

name: José Andrés
about: José Andrés is a chef and restaurateur most known for founding the World Central Kitchen, a non-profit organization that provides food relief after natural disasters. Andrés has won multiple awards for his culinary skills and humanitarian efforts.

name: Dmitry Medvedev
about: Dmitry Medvedev served as the President of the Russian Federation from 2008 to 2012. Before his presidency, he held various government positions, including First Deputy Prime Minister under  . Medvedev's term as president was marked by modernization efforts in Russia's economy and political system, although these were often overshadowed by criticisms regarding a perceived lack of progress and concerns over the continued influence of his predecessor, Putin.

name: Zach Braff
about: Zach Braff is best known for his leading role as J.D. on the TV series "Scrubs" (2001-2010) and for writing, directing, and starring in the movie "Garden State" (2004).

name: Mario Lopez
about: A C Slater-Saved by the Bell

name: Jay Onrait
about:
Best known for co-anchoring the daily 1:00 AM (ET) edition of Sportscentre on TSN in Canada with  . 
 
Onrait also anchored Fox Sports Live on the American Fox Sports 1 network between 2013-17.  
 
He is now hosting his own show, "SC with Jay Onrait" on TSN.

name: Kelly Hu
about:
Kelly Hu is an American actress and model who has starred in a number of recurring television roles. She has been Pearl in The Vampire Diaries (2009-2017) and China White in Arrow (2012-2020). 
 
Hu began her career as a model and beauty queen, winning Miss Teen USA 1985 and Miss Hawaii USA 1993. She then went on to star in a variety of television roles before moving on to also feature in films such as The Scorpion King (2002) and X2 (2003).

name: Nick Foles
about: Nick Foles is an American football player, best known as quarterback for the Indianapolis Colts. During Foles second term with the Philadelphia Eagles, he led the team to their first Super Bowl title in Super Bowl LII, for which game Foles also earned the MVP award.

name: Poonam Pandey
about: Poonam Pandey is an Indian model and actress renowned for her roles in Bollywood and for stirring up controversy with her provocative persona. Her career was marked by bold choices and a series of public stunts.

name: Louis Tomlinson
homePlace: Doncaster, South Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom
about: Louis Tomlinson is a singer and songwriter best known as a member of the boy band  . He was born in 1991 in the English town of Doncaster and grew up in a working-class family.

name: Eli Manning
about:
Manning is an American NFL quarterback, best known for his sixteen seasons with the New York Giants. He is also known via his family—including his father, Archie Manning and his younger brother,  .  
 
While Manning has been criticised by some as inconsistent, his career has also been marked by several incredible highlights—including two Super Bowl MVP awards.

name: Kim Tae-hyung
about: Kim Tae-hyung is a South Korean singer, songwriter, record producer, and actor. He is a member of the South Korean boy band BTS and is also known by his stage name V. Tae-hyung showed early interest in music and dance and was part of several dance teams before joining BTS in 2013.

name: Justin Gatlin
about: Justin Gatlin is an American track and field sprinter who specializes in the 100 and 200 meters. He is the 2004 Olympic champion in the 100 meters, a two-time World Champion in the 100m and a one-time World Champion in the 200m. He is also a two-time Olympic silver medalist in the 100m, and a two-time World indoor gold medalist in the 60m.

name: Theo James
homePlace: High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire, England, United Kingdom
about: Theo James is an English actor and producer, best known for his roles in the Divergent film series and Underworld: Awakening (2012). He has also starred in the television series Golden Boy (2012), The Time Traveler's Wife (2022) and The White Lotus (2022).

name: Zayn Malik
about: Zayn Malik gained international fame as one member of the Irish-British boy band  . The band was formed during the British talent show "The X Factor", with five members,  , Niall Horan,   and  , including Malik.

name: Dolly the Sheep
about: Dolly was a Scottish sheep who was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell, using the process of nuclear transfer, marking a significant breakthrough in the field of genetics. Created by scientists Ian Wilmut and Keith Campbell at the Roslin Institute in Scotland, Dolly's birth in 1996 challenged previous assumptions about the reproductive capacity of adult cells.

name: Emma Roberts
about: Emma Roberts is an American actress and singer who comes from a family of actors, with her aunt being the renowned actress  . She has starred in several seasons of the American Horror Story anthology, as well as the controversial political thriller The Hunt (2020).

name: Harry Styles
about: Harry Styles gained international fame as one member of the Irish-British boy band  . The band was formed during the British talent show "The X Factor", with five members, Niall Horan,  ,   and  , including Styles.

name: Richard Sherman
about:
NFL cornerback and a star player for the Seattle Seahawks 2011-2017. In 2013 he helped them win Super Bowl XLVIII.  
 
Many analysts consider him to be the best corner in the NFL. Sherman has more interceptions than any other player since he entered the league in 2011.

name: Sergio Ramos
about: Sergio Ramos is a Spanish professional footballer, renowned for his skill as a defender, who currently plays for Sevilla. Prior to this he spent sixteen years at Real Madrid, where he became one of the most decorated players in the club's history—including five La Liga and four Champions League titles.

name: Alicia Keys
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Alicia Keys is an American singer-songwriter, best known for her debut album Songs in A Minor (2001) which was a worldwide success selling over 12 million copies. For this album alone, Keys won five Grammy Awards in 2002.

name: Stacy Lewis
about: Stacy Lewis is an American professional golfer best known for her accomplishments on the LPGA Tour, including two major championships. Despite early challenges with scoliosis, Lewis's amateur career and transition into professional success established her as a top contender in women's golf.

name: J. J. Watt
about:
Watt is an American football defensive end for the Houston Texans who in 2014 became the first player in NFL history to record two 20+ sack seasons in a career.  
 
In 2017 Watt was one of Sports Illustrated's Sportsperson of the year, alongside   for raising more than $37 million in relief aid for the city of Houston, Texas, to recover from the impact of Hurricane Harvey.

name: Shohei Ohtani
about: Shohei Ohtani is a baseball player known for his spectacular success as both a pitcher and a hitter, a rare combination in modern baseball. He began his career in Mizusawa, Japan, where he developed as a two-way player under coaches who supported his dual ambitions.

name: Inbee Park
about: Won 7 major titles including the US Open in 2008 and 2013 and the inaugural Olympic women's individual gold in 2016.

name: Timnit Gebru
about: Timnit Gebru is a prominent Ethiopian-American computer scientist and AI researcher, known for her work in the areas of computer vision, AI ethics, and fairness in machine learning. She has made significant contributions to understanding and addressing the potential biases and ethical issues in AI, particularly in facial recognition technology and natural language processing.

name: Amy Schumer
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Amy Schumer is an American stand-up comedian and actress, whose career began with the fifth season of Last Comic Standing in 2007. She went on to have her own shown on Comedy Central, called Inside Amy Schumer (2013-2016).

name: Yuzuru Hanyu
about: Yuzuru Hanyu is a Japanese figure skater and two-time Olympic champion. He is the first male skater to win consecutive Olympic gold medals, and the first to break the 100-point barrier in the men's single event. He is also the first to land the quadruple Lutz jump.

name: Swann Arlaud
about: Swann Arlaud is a French actor who has received multiple César Awards. His work in Bloody Milk (2017) and the film By the Grace of God (2019) has been particularly acclaimed.

name: Juan Guaidó
about: Guaidó is one of the leading opposition figures in Venezuela opposing the government of  . In January 2019, as the President of the National Assembly of Venezuela, he declared himself the rightful President of Venezuela over Maduro. Venezuela has been experiencing an intense political and economic crisis since 2010, marked by increasing authoritarian power, severe inflation and shortages of basic goods.

name: Ben Roethlisberger
about: Ben Roethlisberger is an American football player, best known for his 18 seasons as quarterback for the Pittsburgh Steelers (2004-2021). He was selected for the Steelers in 2004 and played with them until his retirement in 2021.

name: Paul Pogba
about: Paul Pogba is a French professional footballer who currently plays as a central midfielder for Juventus and the French national team. He began his senior professional career at Manchester United, but in 2012, he moved to Juventus, where he won four consecutive Serie A titles and reached the UEFA Champions League final in 2015.

name: Taran Killam
about: Taran Killam is an American actor, comedian, and writer best known for his work on the long-running sketch comedy show Saturday Night Live (SNL) from 2010 to 2016.

name: Mohamed Salah
about: Mohamed Salah is an Egyptian professional soccer player who plays for Premier League club Liverpool and the Egyptian national team. He is considered one of the best players in the world and has won several individual awards, including the Premier League Player of the Season in 2018–19.

name: Justine Henin
about:
Won 43 WTA singles titles including 7 Grand Slam singles titles.  
 
Also won an Olympic gold medal in 2004 and the WTA Tour Championship in 2006 and 2007;.

name: Charlie Kirk
about: Charlie Kirk was a controversial right-wing political activist, entrepreneur, and media personality. He co-founded Turning Point USA with Bill Montgomery in 2012, serving as its director until his assassination.

name: Justin Thomas
about: Justin Thomas is an American golfer known for his achievements on the PGA Tour and for being one of the leading golfers in the world. His career is marked by multiple PGA Tour wins, major championships, and being a former world number one. Thomas' father, Mike Thomas, was also a professional golfer.

name: Louis Oosthuizen
about: British Open 2010; runner-up in all 4 major events

name: Anna Stöhr
about: Anna Stöhr is an Austrian rock climber whose record includes four Bouldering World Cups in the years 2008, 2011, 2012, and 2013, as well as securing victory in two World Championships in 2007 and 2011. At the 2013 Bouldering World Cup series she took gold in seven of the eight events.

name: HolaSoyGerman
about: Germán Alejandro Garmendia Aranis, better known as HolaSoyGerman, is a Chilean YouTuber, singer-songwriter, comedian, and writer. He is the most-subscribed YouTuber in Chile and one of the most influential and popular YouTubers in the Spanish-speaking world.

name: Hayden Christensen
about: Life as a House,  : Episode III - Revenge of the Sith

name: Olivia Wilde
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Olivia Wilde is an American actress and filmmaker who began her acting career in the early 2000s and gained recognition for her role as Dr. Remy "Thirteen" Hadley on the medical drama series House (2007-2012).

name: Kesha
about: Kesha's first success came after being featured on the song Right Round by Flo Rida in 2009. Her debut album Animal topped several charts in 2009 and 2010. Her song "Tik Tok" sold more than 16.5 million digital units.

name: Joe Burrow
about: Joe Burrow is an American football quarterback, best known for his time playing in the NFL for the Cincinnati Bengals. He was selected for the Bengals straight out of college football after winning the Heisman Trophy in 2020.

name: Josh Gad
about:
Josh Gad is an American actor, best known as the voice of Olaf in Frozen (2013) and Frozen II (2019). He has also had a successful stage career, starring on Broadway as Elder Arnold Cunningham in The Book of Mormon (2011). 
 
Gad has received a Grammy Award for Best Musical Album for his part in The Book of Mormon, and also shared a Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical with Andrew Rannells.

name: Sadio Mane
about: Sadio Mane is a Senegalese football player who plays in the Saudi Pro League for Al Nassr, as well as for the Senegalese national team. He is widely regarded as one of the all-time greatest African players, particular renowned for his dribbling and speed.

name: Justin Timberlake
about: Rose to prominence as a singer as one of the two lead vocalists and youngest member of the boy band "'N Sync". Also held starring roles in the films "The Social Network", "Bad Teacher", "In Time", and "Friends with Benefits".

name: Emily Blunt
about: Emily Blunt is a British actress whose film debut came with My Summer of Love (2004), but it was her role in   (2006) that brought her widespread acclaim.

name: G-Eazy
about: G-Eazy is an American rapper who came to fame in 2014 with the release of his debut studio album, These Things Happen, which reached number 3 on the Billboard 200. He continued with When It's Dark Out in 2015, peaking at number 5, and The Beautiful & Damned in 2017, which reached number 3.

name: Brooks Koepka
about: Brooks Koepka is an American professional golfer who first gained recognition with back-to-back U.S. Open wins in 2017 and 2018. He replicated this achievement in the PGA Championship in 2018 and 2019, and has since spent time as world number one.

name: Magnus Carlsen
about: Magnus Carlsen became World Chess Champion in 2013 and has dominated the game for over a decade.

name: Kim Clijsters
about:
Kim Clijsters is a Belgian tennis player best known for having reached the world number one ranking in both singles and doubles, a feat which she achieved in 2003.  
 
She has also won six major titles, with four in singles (Australian Open 2011; US Open 2005, 2009, 2010) and two in doubles, the French Open in 2003 with Ai Sugiyama and Wimbledon in 2003 again with Sugiyama.

name: Claire Foy
about: Claire Foy is best known for her portrayal of   in the Netflix series "The Crown" (2016-2017, 2020, 2022-2023). Her performance in this role earned her multiple awards, including a Golden Globe and two Primetime Emmy Awards.

name: Bonnie Wright
about: Bonnie Wright is a British actress known for her role as Ginny Weasley in the   film series from 2001 to 2011. Beyond acting, Wright has directed several short films and has become an outspoken advocate for environmental issues, engaging in activities with organizations such as Greenpeace and Lumos.

name: Selena Gomez
about: Selena Gomez first appeared on children's TV program "Barney and Friends" before finding fame in the Disney Channel series "Wizards of Waverly Place", which ran from 2007-2012.

name: Jamie Lynn Spears
about: Jamie Lynn Spears is an American actress and singer. She is best known for playing Zoey Brooks on the Nickelodeon sitcom "Zoey 101" (2005-2008) and its 2023 sequel film "Zoey 102."

name: Chloé Zhao
about: Chloé Zhao is a Chinese filmmaker, best known for her Nomadland (2020) which received four Academy Award nominations and won Best Picture and Best Director. This made her the second woman ever to win Best Director, after   who won in 2010 with The Hurt Locker (2008).

name: Michael Cera
about: Michael Cera is a Canadian actor and musician best known for his charmingly awkward characters in films such as "Superbad" (2007), "Juno" (2007), and "Scott Pilgrim vs. the World" (2010).

name: Elaine Thompson-Herah
about: Elaine Thompson-Herah is an Jamaican sprinter who is the fastest woman alive in the 100-meter dash. She is a five-time Olympic champion and was the first female sprinter, and otherwise only overtaken by  , to win the "sprint double" two times consecutively with gold in the 100m and the 200m at the 2016 Rio and 2020 Tokyo Olympics.

name: Jacob Blake
about: Jacob Blake was shot and paralyzed by police in front of three of his children in Kenosha, Wisconsin in August 2020. The incident was captured on video and circulated in the media causing widespread outrage.

name: Saoirse Ronan
about: Critically acclaimed actress who came to notice for her role in Joe Wright's film " " (2007) starring   and  .

name: Jesy Nelson
about: Jesy Nelson is an English singer known for her success with the girl group Little Mix and her solo career. She became notable as a member of the first group to win on the British version of The X Factor. Following her departure from the group, Nelson has been candid about her struggles with mental health and cyberbullying, which she highlighted in her documentary Jesy Nelson: Odd One Out (2019).

name: Aaron Judge
about: Aaron Judge is an American professional baseball outfielder for the New York Yankees. Widely renowned for his power hitting and physical stature, Judge has set several records and played a central role for the Yankees since his debut.

name: Brittany Snow
about:
Brittany Snow is an American actress who first came to fame with her performance on the television series Guiding Light (1998-2001). She subsequently went on to star in American Dreams (2002-2005), as well as starring more recently in many films. 
 
She has starred in films such as The Pacifier (2005) and John Tucker Must Die (2006), as well as more recently Someone Great (2019) and X (2022). Snow also directed Parachute, which debuted in 2023.

name: Paulo Dybala
about: Paulo Dybala is an Argentine professional footballer who played for Italian club Juventus from 2015 to 2022. He currently plays for Roma after signing a three-year contract.

name: Sultan Kösen
about: Sultan Kösen is a Turkish farmer who holds the record for being the tallest living man in the world at 251 cm (8 ft 2.82 in) tall. Kösen's height is caused by a tumor affecting his pituitary gland, which led to the conditions gigantism and acromegaly.

name: Canelo Álvarez
about: Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez is one of boxing’s biggest stars. He has won world titles in four weight classes, and is one of only four boxers to win titles at both 154lbs and 175lbs, joining the likes of  ,  , and Mike McCallum.

name: Brian Ortega
about: Brian Ortega is an American mixed martial artist known for competing in the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). He has gained recognition for his Brazilian jiu-jitsu expertise and has contended for the UFC Featherweight Championship. Ortega's career has won multiple Fight of the Night and Performance of the Night awards.

name: Brendon McCullum
about: Brendon McCullum is known for his record-setting performances as a batsman and significant influence as a captain and coach. As a former New Zealand cricketer and current English men's cricket coach, McCullum is noted for his aggressive playing style and leadership in both domestic and international cricket.

name: Rose Leslie
about: Rose Leslie is a Scottish actress, best known for her roles in "Downton Abbey" (2010-15), " " (2011-19), and "Utopia" (2013-14).

name: Rory McIlroy
about: A former world number one and four time major champion.

name: Liam Hemsworth
about: Actor Liam Hemsworth is the younger brother of fellow actors Luke and  . After moving to Hollywood from his native Australia Liam lost the role of superhero Thor to his brother Chris in 2009.

name: Raven-Symoné
about: Raven-Symoné is an American actress and singer. She first rose to fame as a child star in the early 2000s for her role as Olivia Kendall on the sitcom   (1984-1992), and later as the titular character of the Disney Channel series That's So Raven (2003-2007).

name: Scottie Scheffler
about: Scottie Scheffler is an American golfer who plays on the PGA Tour and, since March 2022, has been world number one. He has won the 2022 Masters Tournament and the 2023 Players Championship, as well as various PGA Tour titles for a total professional wins of eight.

name: John Boyega
about:
Boyega is best known for his portrayal of Finn in the   films The Force Awakens (2015) and The Last Jedi (2017). 
 
He reached a wide audience in the United Kingdom in the 2011 sci-fi comedy film Attack the Block.

name: Constance Wu
about: Constance Wu came to fame with her portrayal of Jessica Huang in the TV series "Fresh Off the Boat" (2015-2020). She was named by Time magazine as one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2017.

name: Trevor Noah
about: Born in South Africa, Noah took over   as host of American cable TV's late-night talk and satirical news program "The Daily Show" in 2015, after serving as a correspondent for the program the year before. Prior to this he had a comedy career that gained traction on late-night talk shows and hosted "Tonight with Trevor Noah" on M-Net and DStv in South Africa.

name: Dev Patel
about: Dev Patel is a British actor who came to fame with his debut role in Slumdog Millionaire (2008), for which he received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor. He portrayed Jamal Malik, a young man reliving his childhood experiences while being a contestant on the Indian version of "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?"

name: Cristiano Ronaldo
about: Cristiano   is regarded by some as currently the best football player in the world and one of the greatest of all time.

name: Elizabeth Olsen
about: Elizabeth Olsen is an American actress, known for her roles in independent films and television. She is the younger sister of actresses   and  .

name: Lorena Ochoa
about: Lorena Ochoa is a Mexican professional golfer. She was the number one ranked female golfer in the world from April 2007 to May 2010. Ochoa is one of the most successful female golfers of all time, having won 27 international tournaments throughout her career.

name: Duffy
about: Duffy is a Welsh singer, songwriter and actress who came to fame with her debut album "Rockferry" (2008), which won a Grammy and three Brit Awards. She later suffered a traumatic personal experience, however, which led to a many year hiatus.

name: The Weeknd
about: Canadian R&B and pop singer-songwriter and record producer known as "The Weeknd" has sold/streamed over 12 million albums, and 83 million singles since 2012. His work has earned him 19 Billboard Music Awards, 15 Juno, and 3 Grammy awards.

name: Ryan Lochte
about:
Lochte has won seven individual Olympic medals as well as winning the World Swimmer of the Year Award. In addition to this he has won 90 medals in major international competitions. 
 
Lochte is perhaps best known for the global controversy he caused by falsely claiming to have been robbed - along with some of his teammates - at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

name: John Isner
about: John Isner is an American professional tennis player famous for defeating Nicolas Mahut in the longest match in history. The match took 11 hours and 5 minutes and was played over three separate days.

name: Xander Schauffele
about: Won the British Open in 2018 and came runner-up in the US Masters in 2019.

name: Emma McKeon
about: Emma McKeon is an Australian swimmer known for competing primarily in freestyle and butterfly events, she has established herself as one of Australia's most successful swimmers, earning numerous medals at major international competitions.

name: Manuel Neuer
about: Manuel Neuer is a German professional footballer who is widely regarded as one of the best goalkeepers of his generation. He has spent the majority of his career playing for FC Bayern Munich, where he has consistently showcased his exceptional shot-stopping abilities and precise distribution.

name: LeBron James
about: James won four NBA championships (with the Miami Heat in 2012 and 2013; with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2016; and with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020), four NBA Most Valuable Player Awards, four NBA Finals MVP Awards, and three Olympic gold medals (2008, 2012, and 2024).

name: Rachel Brosnahan
about: The actress came to fame starring in the TV period comedy "The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel" in 2017. She won a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series in 2018 and two Golden Globes for the part of a housewife aspiring to be a comedienne.

name: Kit Harington
about: Educated at a drama school in London, Harington scored his first notable role in the West End play War Horse in 2009. Shortly afterward he was cast in his most famous role, as Jon Snow in the acclaimed HBO series   (2011-2019).

name: Aziz Ansari
about: Aziz Ansari is an American actor and comedian, best known for his role in   (2009-2015). He has also created and starred in Master of None (2015-2021), for which he won two Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe.

name: Bethany Joy Lenz
about: Bethany Joy Lenz is an American actress, singer-songwriter, and filmmaker best known for her role as Haley   on the television series One Tree Hill (2003–2012). In addition to her acting career, Lenz has also released several albums and singles as a solo singer-songwriter and with the band Everly.

name: Chris Sharma
about: Chris Sharma is an American rock climber known as a pioneer of the sport, as well as one of the most commercially successful climbers. He was the first to prove the possibility of being a "professional climber"—where previously this had been an oxymoron.

name: Elijah Wood
about: Best known for playing the hobbit Frodo Baggins in The   film trilogy.

name: Lindsey Vonn
about: Lindsey Vonn is an American alpine ski racer, known for winning four World Cup championships (2008, 2009, 2010, 2012); a feat which places her second only to Annemarie Moser-Pröll. She is a gold medal Olympian, winning the women's downhill at the 2010 Winter Olympics.

name: Young M.A
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Young M.A is an American rapper that first came to fame in 2016 with her hit single "Ooouuu," which charted in the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100 and has reached over 400 million views on YouTube. She was nominated for BET and MET awards that year, and this was followed by a series of television appearances.

name: Dylan Sprouse
about:
Sprouse rose to fame with his identical twin brother Cole as child actors. Their first major role came alongside   in Big Daddy (1999). 
 
After roles in several films they shot to stardom with the Disney Channel series The Suite Life of Zack and Cody (2005-8), in which Dylan played Zack, and its spin-off, The Suite Life on Deck (2008-11).

name: Aaron Peirsol
about: Aaron Peirsol is an American swimmer known for his backstroke. As a three-time Olympian, Peirsol captured seven Olympic medals which included five golds and two silvers. He notably set world records in the 200-meter backstroke and accrued thirty-six medals in major international competitions before retiring from the sport in 2011.

name: Adam Young
about: Adam Young is an American musician who founded Owl City, a project that he started while suffering from insomnia. His musical presence started out online, particularly with posting songs to MySpace and culminated in the hit single "Fireflies" in 2009.

name: Mia Wasikowska
about: The Australian actress rose to fame after she was cast as the lead in Tim Button's film "Alice in Wonderland" (2010). She later revisited the role, starring in its follow-up "Alice Through the Looking Glass" (2016).

name: Alex Puccio
about: Alex Puccio an American rock climber best known as one of America's most accomplished female bouldering competitors. She has competed in bouldering at the World Cup, the Climbing World Championship, and the American Bouldering Series—the latter of which she has won 11 times.

name: Laurent Duvernay-Tardif
about: Laurent Duvernay-Tardif is a Canadian gridiron football guard and medical doctor. He attended McGill University in Montreal, where he played university football and simultaneously pursued a medical degree, graduating with an M.D. in 2018. This made him one of the few NFL players to have graduated from medical school.

name: Tom Holland
about: Holland is best known for his role as Spider-Man in several Marvel films including  : Civil War (2016), Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017), and  : Infinity War (2018).

name: Taylor Swift
about: A leading contemporary artist in American popular culture, Swift is known for her worldwide hit singles "Love Story", "You Belong with Me," "Blank Space" and "Shake It Off" among others.

name: Ava Max
about: Ava Max is best known for her hit song "Sweet but Psycho" (2018).

name: Stefanie Powers
about: Stefanie Powers is an American actress best known for her television work, particularly her role in   (1979–1984). Powers began her acting career at 16 and rose to prominence in the 1960s. Her performances span film, television, and stage, and she has been recognized with Emmy and Golden Globe nominations.

name: Luciano Pavarotti
about:
Operatic tenor who also crossed over into popular music, eventually becoming one of the most commercially successful tenors of all time.  
 
Pavarotti made numerous recordings of complete operas and individual arias, gaining worldwide fame for the brilliance and beauty of his tone—especially into the upper register—and eventually established himself as one of the finest tenors of the 20th century.

name: Steve Miller
about: Steve Miller is an American musician, singer, songwriter, and guitarist who rose to fame in the late 1960s and 1970s as the leader of the Steve Miller Band. Known for his distinctive voice and guitar skills, Miller has produced a string of successful albums and hit songs, making him an enduring figure in the world of classic rock.

name: Garfield Sobers
about: Sir Garfield Sobers, commonly known as Gary Sobers, is a West Indian cricketer widely regarded as one of the greatest all-rounders in the history of the sport. He was skilled as a bowler, batsman, and fielder in his day and is still esteemed among the greats.

name: Madeleine Albright
about: Madeleine Albright is an American diplomat and politician who served as the first female Secretary of State from 1997 to 2001. She was born in 1937 in Prague, Czechoslovakia, and fled the country with her family in 1948 after the Communist takeover.

name: Rick Barry
about:
NBA observers consider him to be one of the greatest small forward's of all time as a result of his uncanny ability to score, acute court vision, knowledge and execution of team defense principles, and his tenacious (and ofttimes demanding) will to win.  
 
He won the NBA Championship in 1975 with the Golden State Warriors.

name: Wilt Chamberlain
about: Wilt Chamberlain dominated the sport of basketball throughout his career, setting numerous NBA records, many of which still stand today, and changing the way the game was played.

name: Jim Henson
about: Jim Henson was a puppeteer and filmmaker whose work proved to be not only extremely popular but hugely influential. He is the creator of not only The Muppets but also many of the puppet characters on Sesame Street as well as a number of other films and television specials.

name: Muammar Gaddafi
about: Authoritarian leader of Libya for 42 years who began as a revolutionary hero before establishing a regime where his supporters and family dominated Libyan politics and society till they and Gaddafi were overthrown in 2011 during the Arab Spring.

name: Barbara Eden
about: Barbara Eden is best known for her starring role in the television series " " (1965-1970). She has had a long career in entertainment spanning several decades.

name: Chico Mendes
about: Chico Mendes, originally a rubber tapper became an environmental and social activist to stop the slashing and burning of the Amazon rainforest. He believed the best protectors of the forest were the people whose lives depended on its continuing existence.

name: John Lithgow
about: John Lithgow is an American actor who has won two Golden Globe Awards, six Emmy Awards, and two Tony Awards. He has been nominated for two Academy Awards and four Grammy Awards over his lengthy career in stage, film, and television.

name: Herb Brooks
about:
Most notable achievement came in 1980 as head coach of the gold medal-winning USA Olympic hockey team at Lake Placid. At the games, his USA team upset the heavily favoured Soviet team in a match that came to be known as the 'Miracle on Ice'.  
 
He would go on to coach multiple NHL teams, and ultimately returned to coach the USA men's team to a silver medal at the 2002 games in Salt Lake City.

name: Thabo Mbeki
about: Thabo Mbeki served as South Africa's second president from 1999-2008. The son of a prominent jailed ANC leader Govan Mbeki, Mbeki was educated in the United Kingdom and for a year in the Soviet Union before returning to Africa in 1971 to serve in ANC roles.

name: Gloria Steinem
about: Gloria Steinem is an American journalist and activist who became nationally recognized as a leader and a spokeswoman for the American feminist movement in the late 1960s and early 1970s. Steinem was a prominent figure in the fight for women's rights and played a pivotal role in shaping feminist discourse and activism in the United States.

name: Michael Spence
about: 2001 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences - for dynamics of information flows and market development

name: Bill Parcells
about: Known as "The Big Tuna", he won two Super Bowl rings as head coach of the New York Giants. He is the only coach in NFL history ever to lead four different teams to the playoffs and three different teams to a conference championship game.

name: Geraldo Rivera
about: Geraldo Rivera is an American television journalist and author. He was born in New York City and raised in West Babylon, New York. Rivera began his journalistic career as a reporter for WABC-TV in New York City. He later worked as a correspondent for ABC News.

name: Jimmy Johnson
about:
One of only three football coaches to lead teams to both a major college football championship and a Super Bowl, winning back-to-back Super Bowls with the Dallas Cowboys. 
 
Served as the head football coach at Oklahoma State University–Stillwater from 1979 to 1983 and the University of Miami from 1984 to 1988.  
 
Before moving to the NFL where he coached the Dallas Cowboys from 1989 to 1993 and the Miami Dolphins from 1996 to 1999.

name: Larisa Latynina
about: Larisa Latynina made her Olympic debut at the 1956 Melbourne Games, winning 4 gold medals, 1 silver, and 1 bronze.  in a career that included the 1956, 1960, and 1964 games, she collected a total of 18 Olympic medals (9 gold). She held the  record for most individual Olympic medals until American swimmer Mike Phelps passed her in 2012  She remains the most decorated female Olympian.

name: Oliver North
about: North is a decorated American service member who has held numerous political and public appointments, including as a member of the National Security Council and as President of the National Rifle Association. He also ran for the United States Senate in 1994, challenging the incumbent, Chuck Robb, in Virginia.

name: Chuck Norris
about: Chuck Norris first gained fame as a karate champion and later became a popular action movie star.

name: Wole Soyinka
about: In 1986 Wole Soyinka was the first person from the African continent to be awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature. Soyinka is primarily a playwright, but has also written poetry, novels and essays.

name: Billie Jean King
about:
Won 39 Grand Slam titles, including 12 singles, 16 women's doubles, and 11 mixed doubles titles.  
 
King is a strong advocate for sexual equality, famously winning the "Battle of the Sexes" match against the 55-year-old   in 1973.  
 
She also founded the Women's Tennis Association, World TeamTennis, and the Women's Sports Foundation.

name: Ritchie Blackmore
about:
Ritchie Blackmore is an English guitarist and songwriter, known as a founding member of the band Deep Purple.  
 
He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the band in 2016, and is commonly regarded as one of the most influential guitarists in the history of rock music.

name: Eduard Shevardnadze
about: Shevardnadze was the de factor leader of Soviet Georgia from 1972 to 1985, as First Secretary of the Georgian Communist Party, and then Minister of Foreign Affairs for the Soviet Union from 1985 to 1991. This made him responsible for a number of key foreign policy decisions under  .

name: Linda Hunt
about: Linda Hunt is an American actress known for her powerful acting skills and distinctive voice. She rose to prominence after her Academy Award-winning performance as Billy Kwan in The Year of Living Dangerously (1982). This role made her the first person to win an Oscar for playing a character of the opposite sex.

name: Aldrich Ames
about: Aldrich Ames is a former Central Intelligence Agency officer, best known as a KGB double agent. He was convicted of espionage in 1994 and is currently serving a life sentence.

name: John Newcombe
about: Won 7 Grand Slam singles titles and 17 Grand Slam doubles titles.

name: Rodrigo Duterte
about: Duterte took office as President of the Philippines in 2016, having most recently served as vice mayor (2010-2013) and then mayor (2013-2016) of Davao City.

name: Billy Dee Williams
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Known most for playing the character Lando Calrissian in the movies "  Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back" and "Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi", Billy Dee Williams' first love was visual arts.

name: Lance Gibbs
about: Lance Gibbs was an outstanding spin bowler representing the West Indian cricket team over a period of 18 years.

name: John Carlos
about: After taking the bronze medal in the 200 meters at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, Carlos along with gold medal winner and fellow African-American   caused huge controversy when they gave the Black Power salute on the medal podium.

name: Marina Popovich
about: Marina Popovich, known as "Madame MiG" for her mastery of the Soviet MiG fighter jet, was the first Soviet woman to break the sound barrier. She would set over 100 aviation world records in the course of her career.

name: John Nash
about: Nash's work provided insight into the factors that govern chance and decision making in daily life. His insights made fundamental contributions to game theory, differential geometry, and partial differential equations.

name: Jim Croce
about: Jim Croce was an American folk and rock singer-songwriter, who died in a plane crash at the very peak of his popularity. Despite his early death, Croce's music remained listed on top charts for years after. His legacy was continued by his wife, Ingrid Croce, and their son, A. J. Croce.

name: Ridley Scott
about: Ridley Scott is a British film director and producer most renowned for his work in the science fiction, action and horror genres. He is best known for his iconic films Alien,   and Gladiator.

name: Boris Yeltsin
about: Yeltsin served as the first President of Russia from 1991-1998. During the Soviet era Yeltsin served as the head of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic, before coming to national prominence by opposing the communist coup attempt in August 1991, during the collapse of the Soviet Union.

name: Masanori Murakami
about:
Masanori Murakami is a Japanese baseball player, renowned for being the first Japanese player in Major League Baseball. He made his debut at 20 years old with the San Francisco Giants.  
 
After two seasons with the Giants, however, Murakami returned to Japan to play with his original club: the Nankai Hawks.

name: Warren Buffett
about: Warren Buffett is known for his success in value investing, being regarded by many as the best investor of the 20th century, and for his role as the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway.

name: John Lewis
about: On his death, John Lewis was the last surviving speaker from the 1963 March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom which he also helped organize and where   delivered his iconic "I have a Dream" speech.

name: Otis Redding
about: Although his life and career were tragically cut short by his death in a plane crash in 1967, aged 26, Otis Redding is still regarded today as one of the most influential soul singers and songwriters.

name: Frank Zappa
about: Frank Zappa had a varied and multi-faceted career as an experimental  musician, guitarist, singer-songwriter, composer, bandleader, and filmmaker.

name: Tom Jones
about: One of the most popular vocalists and hit makers of the last five decades, Jones rose from a pub singer to a Las Vegas headliner, winning the Grammy Award for Best New Artist in 1966.

name: June Carter Cash
about: Born into the famous Carter country music family June Carter started performing aged 10 with her mother and sisters as  "Mother Maybelle and the Carter Sisters".

name: Robert Crumb
about: Robert Crumb is an American cartoonist and illustrator who is widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in the world of underground comics. His distinctive drawing style and often controversial subject matter have made him both a celebrated and polarizing figure in the art and comics community.

name: Michael Graves
about: Michael Graves was a prolific American architect and designer and one of the leading proponents of the postmodernist style.

name: Paul Anka
about: Paul Anka is a Canadian-American singer, songwriter, and actor who achieved significant success as a teen idol in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

name: Paul Martin
about: The 21st Prime Minister of Canada (2003-2006), he succeeded Jean Chrétien as leader of the Liberal Party.

name: Daniel Kahneman
about: Daniel Kahneman is an Israeli-American psychologist and economist, renowned for his work on the psychology of judgment and decision-making. In 2002, he received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his pioneering work with Amos Tversky on prospect theory, which became a seminal framework in behavioral economics. Their research challenged traditional economic theory, which posits that humans behave rationally when making decisions. Instead, they demonstrated that human decision-making often involves cognitive biases.

name: Lee Trevino
about: Lee Trevino is best known for winning six major championships and 29 PGA Tour events. He is celebrated for his unique swing style, humor, and overcoming a challenging childhood to become a golfing legend. Trevino's most significant achievement was winning the U.S. Open, Canadian Open, and The Open Championship in a 20-day span in 1971.

name: David McKee
about: David McKee is best known for his popular children's books and animations, including the character of Elmer the Patchwork Elephant. Throughout his career, McKee created numerous memorable characters that have entertained generations of young readers.

name: Ard Schenk
about: Won 3 Olympic gold medals at the 1972 Winter Olympic Games in Sapporo, Japan.

name: Ted Turner
about:
Media mogul who most notably was the founder of the Cable News Network (CNN), the world's first 24-hour cable news channel. 
 
Turner owned the Atlanta Braves baseball team from 1976 to 1996 and in 1977 successfully defended sailing's America's Cup for the USA. 
 
Donated US$1 billion in 1997 to support the United Nations, creating the public charity, the United Nations Foundation.

name: Walter Mondale
mainType: Vice President of the United States
about: Walter "Fritz" Mondale began his political career as a Senator from Minnesota in 1964, serving two terms, then as Vice President to   from 1977 to 1981. He was the Democratic Party's 1984 Presidential nominee, and notably selected   as his running mate, the first woman in that role for a major party in the US. He later served as US Ambassador to Japan.

name: Linda Evans
about: Linda Evans is most famous for her role in the US primetime soap opera "Dynasty" (1981-89), in which she played the role of Crystal Carrington opposite   and  .

name: Tom Dreesen
about: Tom Dreesen is an American stand-up comedian and actor best known for his work with Tim Reid. Together they were the first biracial comedy duo in the United States in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

name: Rajiv Gandhi
about: A member of the India's great political dynasty, Rajiv Gandhi was Prime Minister of India for five years until his resignation in 1989.

name: Mitch McConnell
about: Mitch McConnell is an American politician who has served as a U.S. senator from Kentucky since 1985. He is the Senate Minority Leader and the longest-serving U.S. senator from Kentucky in history.

name: Debbie Harry
about:
Lead singer of the new wave rock band Blondie, who rose to international success with their third album "Parallel Lines", which included the hit single "Heart of Glass".  
 
The band later broke up and Harry released solo albums but reunited in the 1990s. 
 
As an actress, Harry has worked mostly with independent directors including on John Waters' "Hairspray" (1988) and in John Cronenberg's horror "Videodrome" (1983).

name: Doris Kearns Goodwin
about: Doris Kearns Goodwin is known for her detailed biographies of United States presidents. She has won numerous awards, including the Pulitzer Prize, for her historical works.

name: Shirley Jones
about: Shirley Jones is an American actress and singer best known for her roles in musical films and television during the 1950s and 1960s. She made her film debut in the 1955 movie adaptation of the Broadway musical Oklahoma! as Laurey Williams, which launched her career as a leading lady in Hollywood.

name: Richard M. Daley
about: Richard M. Daley is an American politician who served as the mayor of Chicago from 1989 to 2011. He was the longest-serving Chicago mayor, and also the third longest-serving mayor in United States history. Daley was first elected in 1989 and was re-elected five times, becoming the longest-serving mayor of the city.

name: Tuesday Weld
about:
Tuesday Weld is an American actress who won the Golden Globe Award for Most Promising Female Newcomer in 1960. She performed from the 1950s to the 1980s. 
 
She started out as a child actress and then progress to mature roles, including being nominated for a Golden Globe after her performance in Play It as It Lays (1972). She was also nominated for an Academy Award for her performance in Looking for Mr. Goodbar (1977).

name: Robert Evans
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Robert Evans was a successful businessman before beginning a short-lived acting career at the request of actress  . Preferring producing, he switched again and worked for Paramount Pictures, becoming its Head of Production and making it the most successful studio in Hollywood.

name: Jim Palmer
about: Played for the Baltimore Orioles between 1965 and 1984.

name: Neale Fraser
about: Three-time Grand Slam winner and Australian Davis Cup captain.

name: Dawn Fraser
about:
Won four Olympic gold medals in the 100m freestyle across the  
1956, 1960 and 1964 games.  
 
Making her one of only three swimmers to have won the same Olympic individual event three times.

name: A. J. Foyt
about: Foyt is one of the great all-round motor racing drivers of all-time. He is the only driver to win the Indianapolis 500 (1961, 64, 67, 77), Daytona 500, 24 Hours of Daytona, 24 Hours of Le Mans as well as the 12 Hours of Sebring.

name: Harvey Milk
about: The first openly gay person to be elected to public office in California when he won a seat on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors.

name: Joel Grey
about: Joel Grey is an American actor known for his performances on stage, screen, and television. His breakthrough role came in the Broadway production of Cabaret (1966), where he portrayed the enigmatic Master of Ceremonies, a role that earned him a Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical.

name: Dudley Herschbach
about: Dudley Herschbach is an American chemist known for his research in chemical kinetics and molecular dynamics. His work in these areas of chemistry has been instrumental in understanding the mechanisms of chemical reactions. Together with   and  , he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1986 for their investigations of the dynamics of chemical elementary processes.

name: Ann Haydon-Jones
about: Ann Haydon-Jones is a British table tennis and lawn tennis champion, best known for winning eight Grand Slam titles: French Open singles (1961, 1966) and doubles (1963, 1968, 1969), Wimbledon singles (1969) and mixed doubles (1969), Australian Open mixed doubles (1969).

name: Imelda Marcos
about: Imelda Marcos was the wife of President  , a politician in her own right and notorious for her lavish lifestyle.

name: Michel Temer
about: Michel Temer is a Brazilian lawyer and politician who served as the 37th President of Brazil from August 2016 to December 2018. Formerly the vice president, he assumed the presidency after the impeachment of his predecessor,  , in relation to a scandal at the Brazilian national petroleum company, Petrobras.

name: Rod Stewart
about: One of the best-selling music artists of all time, having sold over 100 million records worldwide. He is known for his distinctive raspy singing voice.

name: Ralph Lauren
about: Famous for his American clothing brand, Polo Ralph Lauren which he turned into a globally successful lifestyle brand.

name: JoAnne Carner
about: JoAnne Carner is an American professional golfer who is widely regarded as one of the greatest players in the history of women's golf. Her outstanding skill, tenacity, and longevity in the sport earned her the nickname "Big Mama" and solidified her place among the all-time greats.

name: Brian Wilson
about: Widely regarded as one of the most innovative and influential songwriters and record producers in music history, Wilson co-founded the 1960s rock band The Beach Boys, with his brothers Dennis and Carl. their cousin Mike Love, and friend Al Jardine. In this group, he co-wrote two dozen Top 40 hits for them.

name: Ada E. Yonath
about: Ada E. Yonath is best known for her pioneering work on determining the structure of ribosomes. For this work, she was awarded the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, making her the first Israeli woman to win a Nobel Prize.

name: Amitabh Bachchan
about: Amitabh Bachchan is an Indian actor, known for his work in Hindi cinema. He is one of the most successful and influential actors in the history of Indian cinema, having been dominant during the 1970s and 1980s.

name: F. Murray Abraham
about: F. Murray Abraham is an American actor who achieved international acclaim for his performance as   in the 1984 film Amadeus, for which he won the Academy Award for Best Actor.

name: Bill Bradley
about: Bill Bradley is a Basketball and College Basketball Hall of Fame shooting guard and American politician.

name: Francis Ford Coppola
about: Francis Ford Coppola is a hugely influential film director, producer and scriptwriter responsible for such films as   trilogy and " ".

name: Vera Miles
about: She's best known for her role as Lila Crane in the classic masterpiece "Psycho."

name: Joe Clark
about: Served as the 16th Prime Minister of Canada from June 1979 to March 1980. He is the youngest person to become Prime Minister, taking office the day before his 40th birthday. As he had only won a minority government, his tenure was brief and eventually defeated on a motion of non-confidence.

name: Elliott Gould
about: Elliott Gould is an American actor known for his work in film and theater. He began his career on Broadway before achieving fame with Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice (1969) and M*A*S*H (1970). Gould has received Academy Award, BAFTA, and Golden Globe nominations and is recognized for his performances in a range of genres, including drama, comedy, and action.

name: Reggie Jackson
about:
Played 21 seasons in the MLB for five different teams (1967–1987).  
 
He was nicknamed "Mr. October" for his clutch hitting in the postseason with the Oakland A's and the New York Yankees.  
 
He is perhaps best remembered for hitting three consecutive home runs in the clinching game of the 1977 World Series.

name: Jimmy Connors
about:
Won eight Grand Slam singles titles and played in 15 total.  
 
He also won 109 ATP-listed singles titles, more than any other male player in the open era, and is widely considered to be one of the greatest players of all time.

name: Michael Moore
about: Michael Moore began his career as a journalist before a redundancy package provided the capital for his first documentary film "Roger and Me" about the effects of a company downsizing on his native town Flint, in 1989.

name: Tommy Lee Jones
about: Jones is an American multi-award winning actor. Born and raised in Texas, he is often seen playing gruff, no-nonsense characters.

name: Freddie Mercury
homePlace: Stone Town, Sultanate of Zanzibar (now Tanzania)
about:
Freddie Mercury was the frontman for the British rock band Queen, and one of their principal songwriters for such hits as "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "We are the Champions". 
 
Born of Parsi descent, Mercury was famously flamboyant on stage and known for his vocal range.  
 
Mercury died of complications from AIDS, at a time when much stigma was attached to the disease and only confirmed he had contracted the disease a day before his death.

name: Bobby Orr
about: Played in the NHL for 10 seasons with the Boston Bruins. Widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest hockey players of all time. As a defenceman, he used his ice skating speed and scoring and play-making abilities to revolutionize the position.

name: Steve Howe
about:
British musician Steve Howe joined the band Yes in 1970 and helped lead them to critical and commercial success with his experimental guitar playing and songwriting abilities. After leaving in 1981, he rejoined the group in the 1990s. In 2017 was inducted into the Rock and Roll hall of Fame as a member of the band. 
 
Howe has also had success performing with other bands including GTR, and Asia and has released regular solo albums throughout his career.

name: Sugar Ray Leonard
about: Winner of an Olympic gold medal in 1976 and 5-division world boxing champion.

name: Roscoe Tanner
about: Famous for his big left-handed serve and for winning the men's singles title at the first of two Australian Open tournaments held in 1977.

name: Carles Puigdemont
about: Puigdemont was President of the Spanish region of Catalonia from 12 January 2016 until his dismissal by the central government on 28 October 2017.

name: Jim Steinman
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Known as the "Father of the Power Ballad," Steinman is responsible for such hit songs as Bonnie Tyler's “Total Eclipse Of The Heart,”  's "I'd Do Anything for Love (But I Won't Do That)",  's "It's All Coming Back to Me Now" and Boyzone's "No Matter What"

name: John Grisham
about: Best known for his popular legal thrillers. One of only three authors to sell 2 million copies on a first printing, the others being Tom Clancy and J.K. Rowling.

name: Boy George
about: Boy George is a British singer-songwriter and fashion designer, who rose to fame in the 1980s as the lead singer of the band Culture Club. Known for his voice and androgynous appearance, he became a cultural icon for his unique style and music.

name: Emmylou Harris
about: Emmylou Harris is an American singer, songwriter, and musician who has made substantial contributions to country, folk, and Americana music. Over her decades-long career, she has collaborated with numerous notable artists such as Gram Parsons,  , and  .

name: Woody Harrelson
about: Woody Harrelson's breakout role came in the television sitcom "Cheers" as bartender Woody Boyd in 1985.

name: Flavor Flav
about: Flavor Flav is an American musician, rapper, and television personality best known for his work with the rap group Public Enemy. The group—featuring Flav and Chuck D as its core, alongside Professor Griff, Terminator X, DJ Lord, and Sammy Sam—earned six Grammy nominations and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2013.

name: John Goodman
about: John Goodman is best known for his role as Dan Conner on the sitcom "Roseanne" from 1988 to 1997 and again in 2018. He has also had a successful film career, often collaborating with the Coen brothers in movies such as "Raising Arizona" (1987), "The Big Lebowski" (1998), and "O Brother, Where Art Thou?" (2000).

name: Mats Wilander
about: From 1982 to 1988, he won seven Grand Slam singles titles (three at the French Open, three at the Australian Open, and one at the US Open). In 1988, he won three of the four Grand Slam events, and finished the season ranked number one in the world.

name: Hironobu Sakaguchi
about: Hironobu Sakaguchi is best known for creating the Final Fantasy series.

name: Joko Widodo
about:
Previously the Mayor of Surakarta from 2005 to 2012 and Governor of Jakarta from 2012 to 2014, he is the first Indonesian president not to have emerged from the country’s political elite or as an army general.  
 
His win was seen as reflecting Indonesian voters' desire for new and less corrupt leaders.

name: Stanley Tucci
about: The actor and filmmaker has a long and acclaimed career in film, on TV and the stage. He is the winner of five Emmys, and has been nominated for an Academy Award, a Tony and a Grammy throughout his career.

name: Tim Cook
about:
Replaced   as CEO of Apple in 2011 and transformed the company into one of the most valuable and influential companies that ever existed. 
 
Cook joined Apple in 1998 as senior vice president of worldwide operations and used his skill in supply chain management to rise to Chief Operating Officer, second in command at Apple.  
 
He is also the first CEO of a Fortune 500 company to admit publicly that he is gay.

name: Geddy Lee
about:
Geddy Lee is a Canadian musician best known as lead vocalist, bassist, and keyboard player for the rock group Rush. He replaced their original bassist and frontman Jeff Jones in 1968, joining at the request of his childhood friend Alex Lifeson who was the band's guitarist and backing vocalist. 
 
Lee was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2013 along with the remainder of Rush: Alex Lifeson and Neil Peart

name: Hillary Clinton
about: Born in Chicago, Hillary Rodham trained as a lawyer at Yale before meeting   in Arkansas and marrying him. As Hillary Clinton she served as first lady through her husband's presidency (1993-2001) and supported him throughout the Monica  .

name: Tim Robbins
about: Tim Robbins is an American actor, director, and musician. He is known for his roles in The Shawshank Redemption (1994) and Mystic River (2003), the latter of which earned him an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. Also recognized for his directorial work in Dead Man Walking (1995), Robbins has contributed significantly to both film and theater.

name: Theresa May
about: May served as Home Secretary in the government of  , becoming the longest serving person in that position for over 60 years. In this position she implemented several key policies, including the deportation of Abu Qatada, police reform and the creation of the National Crime Agency.

name: Nadia Comăneci
about: Nadia first became internationally known winning the European Championship in 1975. She became a world-wide sensation at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, at 14 years old - becoming the first gymnast to score a perfect 10 - then doing it 6 more times.  She won 3 individual gold medals in Montreal, and inspired global popularity in the sport.

name: Steven Tyler
about: Steven Tyler is an American singer, songwriter, and musician best known as the lead vocalist and frontman for the rock band Aerosmith. Formed in 1970, Aerosmith went on to become one of the most successful and enduring rock bands in history, with numerous hit albums and singles, such as "Dream On" (1973), "Sweet Emotion" (1975), and "Walk This Way" (1975).

name: Jay Leno
about: Leno became host of The Tonight Show with Jay Leno on NBC in 1992 and served until 2009 and again from 2010 to 2014. His transition to host was controversial as he replaced   as host; Carson and others had expected   to replace him, this led to a longtime feud between the rival late-night hosts.

name: Tom Watson
about: One of the leading players in the world in the 1970s and 1980s.

name: Susan Sarandon
about: Susan Sarandon’s acting career has spanned five decades in film, television, and theater. She is known for her Oscar-winning performances and political engagement.

name: Jeremy Irons
about: Jeremy Irons is a highly regarded British actor whose work spans film, television and the theatre. He is one of the few actors to have won the Triple Crown of Acting.

name: Anna Wintour
about: Dame Anna Wintour is an iconic fashion magazine editor who served as the editor-in-chief of American Vogue from 1988 to 2025. During this period, she has been credited with reviving the magazine, making it and herself one of the most influential voices in fashion.

name: Peter Gabriel
about: The lead vocalist for progressive rock band Genesis, which first formed when he was 15 years old and included Mike Rutherford and later  .

name: Guillermo del Toro
about: Guillermo del Toro is a Mexican filmmaker, screenwriter, producer, and author who came to prominence in the late 1990s with his Spanish-language films like Cronos (1993) and The Devil's Backbone (2001), but it was his dark fantasy film Pan's Labyrinth (2006) that cemented his reputation as a master storyteller. The film received critical acclaim and won three Academy Awards, including Best Cinematography and Best Art Direction.

name: Anjelica Huston
about:
Anjelica Huston is an American actress who initially worked as a model in the 1970s and then had a breakthrough performance in Prizzi's Honor (1985).  
 
She is the daughter of director John Huston and granddaughter of actor Walter Huston. Three generations of her family, her alongside both Walter and John, have won an Academy Award.

name: Orel Hershiser
about: Hershiser is a former three-time All-Star baseball pitcher who, during his tenure at the Los Angeles Dodgers, was given the nickname 'Bulldog' by manager  . At age eight, Hershiser finished third in the national youth hit, run, and throw competition.

name: George Brett
about:
George Brett played 21 years for the Kansas City Royals in the MLB.  
 
His 3,154 career hits are the most by any third baseman in MLB history, and he is one of four players in MLB history to accumulate 3,000 hits, 300 home runs, and a career .300 batting average.

name: Jane Lynch
about: Jane Lynch's most famous role is that of cheerleading coach Sue Sylvester in the musical TV series "Glee" (2009-15). Lynch won both an Emmy and a Golden Globe award for best supporting actress for the role.

name: Angela Merkel
about: Angela Merkel served as Chancellor of Germany from 2005 to 2021. She was the first woman to hold this position and is widely regarded as one of the most influential leaders in modern European history.

name: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad
about:
Iranian politician who was the sixth President of Iran from 2005 to 2013.  
 
During his presidency, Ahmadinejad was viewed as a controversial figure within Iran, as well as internationally. He has been criticized domestically for his economic policies and alleged disregard for human rights. 
 
Internationally he is criticized for his hostility towards some countries, most notably Israel, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

name: Marisa Tomei
about: Marisa Tomei is an Academy Award-winning American actress. She is best known for her roles in the films "My Cousin Vinny" (1992), "In The Bedroom" (2001) and "The Wrestler" (2008). She has also appeared in television shows such as "A Different World" (1988-93) and "Rescue Me" (2004-11).

name: David Ho
about: David Ho played a key role in developing effective treatments for HIV. He is known for his work on combination antiretroviral therapy, which transformed HIV from a fatal disease to a manageable chronic condition.

name: Warren Spector
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Warren Spector is best known for creating “Deus Ex" (2000).

name: Calista Flockhart
about: Calista Flockhart is most famous for her role as the title character in the legal comedy-drama series "Ally McBeal" (1997-2002).

name: Bernadette Peters
about:
Bernadette Peters is an American actress renowned for her Broadway performances, having been nominated for a Tony Award seven times of which she has won two.  
 
Peters is particularly known for her roles in musicals over several decades, from Mack and Mabel (1974) and Into the Woods (1987) to Gypsy (2003) and Follies (2011).

name: John James
about:
John James played the role of Jeff Colby in the 1980s hit soap Dynasty (1981-89) alongside  ,   and  . 
 
He also played the same role in the Dynasty spin-off "The Colbys" (1985-87).

name: Janusz Kamiński
about: Janusz Kamiński is a Polish cinematographer and film director who is known for his long-standing collaboration with famed director  . His visually evocative and distinct cinematic style has brought a certain depth to many films, and his work has earned him significant recognition in the film industry.

name: Roseanne Barr
about:
Began her career in stand-up comedy at clubs before gaining fame for her role in the sitcom "Roseanne". The show was a hit and lasted nine seasons, from 1988 to 1997. She won both an Emmy and a Golden Globe Award for Best Actress for her work on the show. 
 
"Roseanne" with its original cast was revived in 2018.

name: Matthew Broderick
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Among other roles, Broderick played the title character in "Ferris Bueller's Day Off", voiced Simba in "The  ", and portrayed Leo Bloom in the Hollywood and Broadway productions of "The Producers".

name: Juliane Koepcke
about: Juliane Koepcke is a German-Peruvian mammalogist whose specialty is bats, but she is best known as the sole survivor of the LANSA Flight 508 crash in 1971. The plane was struck by lightning and Koepcke, still strapped to her seat, fell into the Amazon rainforest from 3,000m. She spent 11 days in the rainforest but was rescued after being found by local fisherman.

name: Richie Sambora
about:
Richie Sambora was the lead guitarist for rock band Bon Jovi. He and frontman   formed the primary songwriting unit of the band. Sambora left the band in 2013. 
 
Sambora has also released 3 successful solo albums as a solo artist. He was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2009.

name: Evonne Goolagong Cawley
about: Evonne Goolagong Cawley is an Australian tennis player, formerly the world number one. She won 14 Grand Slam tournament titles, seven of which were in the women's singles: the Australian Open four times, Wimbledon twice, and the French Open.

name: Bryan Cranston
about: Best known for portraying Walter White in the AMC crime drama series " ", Hal in the Fox comedy series "Malcolm in the Middle", and Dr. Tim Whatley in the NBC series " ".

name: Hana Mandlikova
about: Hana Mandlíková is a professional tennis player from Czechoslovakia who later became an Australian citizen. She achieved notable success in her career, winning four Grand Slam singles titles: the Australian Open in 1980 and 1987, the French Open in 1981, and the US Open in 1985.

name: Jackson Browne
about: Jackson Browne is an American singer-songwriter who came to fame in the early 1970s with a series of critically-acclaimed albums that included hits like "Doctor, My Eyes" (1972), "Running on Empty" (1977) and "The Pretender" (1976).

name: Fran Drescher
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
A native of Queens, New York, Fran Drescher used her background and her Jewish heritage to create her most famous role - that of Fran Fine in the sitcom "The Nanny" (1993-98). Drescher also created and produced the show alongside her then husband Peter Marc Jacobson. She was nominated for two Golden Globes and two Emmys for her performance. 
 
In 2021 Drescher was voted president of the screen actors union SAG-AFTRA and led it through a five month strike in 2023.

name: Gianni Versace
about: Gianni Versace was an Italian fashion designer and founder of the luxury fashion house Versace. He is best known for his bold designs that helped define the look of the 1980s and 1990s, as well his close relationships with celebrities.

name: Merrick Garland
about: Merrick Garland served as United States Attorney General during the Biden administration. He has had a long career in law, including roles as a federal judge and prosecutor.

name: Daniel Day-Lewis
about: Regarded by many as the greatest actor of all time, Day-Lewis holds the record for being only male actor in history to have three wins in the lead actor category and one of only three male actors to win three Oscars.

name: Pope Leo XIV
about: Pope Leo XIV is the current Pope of the Roman Catholic Church, making him the 267th Pope. He was elected in 2025 as the successor to   and is the first American Pope.

name: Patrick Warburton
about: Patrick Warburton is an American actor and voice artist known for his roles in shows such as   and  .

name: Stephen King
about:
American author of contemporary horror, suspense, science fiction, and fantasy.  
 
His books have sold more than 350 million copies and many of them have been adapted into feature films, television movies and comic books.  
 
Many of his stories are set in his home state of Maine.

name: Sally Field
about: Sally Field has won two Academy Awards and three Emmy Awards over an acting career spanning six decades.

name: Sarah Brightman
about: Sarah Brightman is the world's best-selling soprano and has a long and hugely successful career on stage and as a solo artist, singer, actress and dancer.

name: Nick Cave
about: Known as the leader of rock band Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds.

name: Reba McEntire
about: Reba McEntire is an American country music singer, songwriter, and record producer. She began her career in the music industry as a high school student singing in local talent contests and performing at rodeos.

name: Vanessa Williams
about: Vanessa Williams came to fame when she became the first person  of African American descent to win the Miss America contest in 1983. She was forced to give up the title after a scandal erupted when Penthouse published unauthorized nude photographs of her.

name: John Bonham
about:
The drummer of Led Zeppelin, one of the most successful and influential rock groups in music history.  
 
Bonham's distinctive sound, power, speed and feel for the groove helped establish him as one of the greatest drummers of all time.

name: Bill Murray
about:
First gained exposure on "Saturday Night Live" for which he earned an Emmy Award and later went on to star in numerous comedy films, including " ", "Caddyshack", and "Groundhog Day".  
 
Murray also starred in the critically acclaimed "Lost in Translation" earning him a Golden Globe, a BAFTA and an Oscar nomination for Best Actor.

name: Rowan Atkinson
about: Rowan Atkinson first rose to prominence in the sketch TV show "Not the Nine O'Clock News" and was named "BBC Personality of the Year" in 1979.

name: O.J. Simpson
about: Nicknamed the 'Juice' during his professional football career O.J. Simpson became the first player to rush for over 2,000 yards in a 14 game season.

name: Alec Baldwin
about: Alec Baldwin is an American actor, comedian, and producer who has won three Primetime Emmy Awards and three Golden Globe Awards, among other honors. He has worked in film, television, and theater, with iconic roles ranging from 30 Rock (2006-2013) to his impersonation of   on Saturday Night Live (2016-2021).

name: Greg Norman
about:
