Professional golfer and entrepreneur who spent 331 weeks as the world's Number 1 ranked golfer in the 1980s and 1990s. Won over 85 international tournaments in his career, including two majors: The Open Championship in 1986 and 1993. 
 
Nicknamed The Great White Shark or sometimes simply The Shark – a reference to his blond hair, size, aggressive golf style and in reflection to the native coastal animal of his birthplace.

name: Ricky Gervais
about: Gervais achieved mainstream fame with his television series "The Office" and the subsequent series "Extras".

name: Mike Pence
mainType: Vice President of the United States
about:
Vice President of the United States under  . 
 
Pence was also the Governor of Indiana from 2013 to 2017 and represented Indiana's 2nd congressional district from 2001 to 2013. 
 
Before his career in public office, Pence was a conservative radio and television talk show host.

name: Christopher Hitchens
about: One of the most prolific polemicists and social critics in modern public discourse, Hitchens' eloquent and confrontational style of debate and public speaking made him an immensely popular intellectual, as well as a controversial public figure.

name: Sandra Bullock
about: Sandra Bullock is a prominent figure and one of Hollywood's most successful actresses.

name: Chris Isaak
about: Chris Isaak is an American singer and songwriter best known for his hit single "Wicked Game." He has released 13 albums, as well as appearing in various films and television shows.

name: Julia Louis-Dreyfus
about: Julia Louis-Dreyfus is an American actress and comedian best known for playing Elaine Benes on   (1989-1998) alongside  , Jason Alexander, and Michael Richards. She has also worked on Saturday Night Live, The New Adventures of Old Christine, and Veep.

name: Meat Loaf
about:
Meat Loaf, born Marvin Lee Aday, was an American singer and best-selling artist known for his Bat Out of Hell trilogy. Over his career he sold more than 65 million albums, including "I'd Do Anything for Love."  
 
He also had an acting career, appearing in Spice World (1997).

name: Bob Geldof
about: Bob Geldof rose to fame as the singer for the Irish punk-rock band the Boomtown Rats in the late 1970s, with such hits as " Don't like Mondays"

name: Gary Larson
about:
Gary Larson drew the phenomenally popular "The Far Side" comic strip from 1980 to 1995, when he retired. His style was surreal, subversive and a big departure from the most cute comic strips of time. 
 
From 2020 he began publishing again uploading new material on his website.

name: Maureen McCormick
about: Widely known for her career as a child actress, during which she portrayed Marcia Brady on ABC's The Brady Bunch from 1969 to 1974.

name: Larry David
about: Larry David is an American comedian best known for creating the sitcom   with  . David's own personality was the primary inspiration for the character of George Costanza played by Jason Alexander.

name: Johnny Depp
about: Johnny Depp is best known for his role as Captain Jack Sparrow in the "Pirates of the Caribbean" franchise and for his collaborations with director  .

name: Kim Alexis
about:
Kim Alexis is an American supermodel and actress best known for her work in the 1970s and 1980s. During this period she was a mainstay in Sports Illustrated, Vogue, Harper's Bazaar, and many more publications.  
 
Alexis was one of the top models of her generation, alongside Gia Carangi, Carol Alt, Patti Hansen, Christie Brinkley, Kelly Emberg, Iman, Janice Dickinson, and Paulina Porizkova. After this she went on to a sporadic career in television, hosting health and other shows.

name: Park Geun-hye
about: Park was the first female President of South Korea, and also the first women to be popularly-elected head of state in East Asia. Notably, her father, Park Chung-hee, had also been President of South Korea (1963–1979)—though his presidency began with the 1961 military coup d'état.

name: Lisa Kudrow
about: Best known for her portrayal of the eccentric Phoebe Buffay on the sitcom Friends (1994-2004), which made her a household name and became one of the most popular television programs of all time.

name: Allison Janney
about: The critically acclaimed actress rose to fame playing C. J Cregg in Aaron Sorkin's "West Wing" (1999-2006), as part of an ensemble cast that included  , Rob Lowe and Bradley Whitford. Janney won four Emmy awards for the role.

name: Sam Neill
about: Sam Neill is known for his roles in blockbuster films and critically acclaimed dramas over five decades, particularly his lead role in " " (1993).

name: Jackie Chan
about: Jackie Chan is a Chinese martial arts actor, producer, stuntman and singer known for Hong Kong produced martial arts films and Hollywood's "Rush Hour: and its sequels.

name: Penn Jillette
about: Jillette is a magician best known as one half of Penn & Teller, who as a pair have featured across numerous television and stage shows: 'Penn & Teller: Fool Us', 'Penn & Teller: Bullshit!', etc. They are currently headlining together for The Rio in Las Vegas.

name: Demi Moore
about:
Famous for her role in "Ghost", which was the highest-grossing film of 1990 and brought her a Golden Globe nomination.  
 
Moore had a string of additional box-office successes over the early 1990s with "A Few Good Men", "Indecent Proposal", and "Disclosure".

name: Martina Navratilova
about: Martina Navratilova is widely regarded as one of the greatest in the history of tennis. She has won 59 major titles, including 18 Grand Slam singles championships, and held the world number one ranking for 332 weeks in singles and 237 weeks in doubles.

name: Fatboy Slim
about: Fatboy Slim is a British musician, DJ, and record producer known for popularizing the "big beat" genre. He gained international fame in the 1990s with hits like "Praise You" and "The Rockafeller Skank." Prior to his success as Fatboy Slim, Cook was a member of the indie rock band The Housemartins, as well as the electronic dance music acts Beats International and Freak Power.

name: Jodie Foster
about: Jodie Foster has two Academy Award wins for Best Actress. She began her career as a child actor in the 1960s and has since become one of Hollywood's most respected figures, with a career spanning over five decades.

name: Danielle Steel
about: Danielle Steel is one of the most popular authors in the United States, specializing in romance novels. She has written more than 190 books, many of which have been bestsellers.

name: James Taylor
about: James Taylor was born to a medical doctor and a classically trained soprano in Boston, and raised in North Carolina.  He began his career in Martha's Vineyard, where he spent summers, performing folk music with Danny Kortchmar.

name: Thomas Huber
about: Thomas Huber is a German rock climber and mountaineer famous for his big wall climbing and alpine expeditions, often carried out with his brother  . As the Huberbuam ("Huberboys"), they are together known for their climbing achievements and were showcased in To the Limit (2007).

name: Sam Mendes
about: The prominent British director, producer and screenwriter began his career directing   aged 24 in Chekhov's "The Cherry Orchard in London's West End. Since then he has gone on to major success, including his 1999 film " " for which he won an Academy award and a Golden Globe.

name: Helena Bonham Carter
about:
Famous for her roles in films such as "Fight Club" and "The King's Speech", and for playing Bellatrix Lestrange in the   series.  
 
Carter also frequently collaborates with her domestic partner, director  .

name: Cindy Crawford
about: Cindy Crawford is one of the most successful models of her generation. She originally began modelling as a scholarship student studying engineering at Northwestern University, before quitting to focus on modelling full time.

name: Aishwarya Rai
about: Aishwarya Rai Bachchan is an Indian actress known for her performances in both Hindi and Tamil cinema. After winning the Miss World 1994 pageant, she transitioned into an acting career and has since become a cultural icon in India. Her accomplishments have garnered her prestigious recognitions, including the Padma Shri from the Indian government in 2009 and the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres from the French government in 2012.

name: Bill Burr
about:
Burr has released six stand-up comedy specials. In addition to this he hosts the Monday Morning Podcast, appeared in   and created the Netflix comedy series F Is for Family. 
 
In 2017, Rolling Stone ranked him 17th on its list of the 50 best stand-up comics of all time.

name: Kevin Connolly
about: Kevin Connolly is an American actor and director. He began his career at age six, appearing in television commercials, and made his film debut in Rocky V (1990). Connolly subsequently gained recognition for roles in the sitcoms Great Scott! (1992) and Unhappily Ever After (1995-1996), with the latter also marking his directorial debut.

name: Alan Davies
about: Alan Davies is an English stand-up comedian, actor, writer, and television presenter known for his role in the mystery crime series Jonathan Creek (1997–2016) and as a regular panelist on the quiz show QI since 2003.

name: James Van Der Beek
about: James Van Der Beek  is an American actor best known for his portrayal of Dawson Leery in the television drama Dawson's Creek, which aired from 1998 to 2003. This role catapulted him to fame among teenage and young adult audiences during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

name: Marion Jones
about: Former world champion track and field athlete who won 3 gold medals at the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney, Australia, but was later stripped of the titles after admitting doping.

name: Martin Lawrence
about: He came to fame during the 1990s, establishing a Hollywood career as a leading actor, most notably in the films "House Party", "Bad Boys", "Blue Streak", "Big Momma's House" and "A Thin Line Between Love & Hate".

name: Tobey Maguire
about: He is known for his role as Peter Parker in Spider-Man film trilogy.

name: Todd Eldredge
about: World champion in 1996 and a six-time U.S. national champion.

name: Sarah Silverman
about: Sarah Silverman is an American stand-up comedian, actress, producer and writer. She is known for her satirical comedy addressing social issues such as racism, sexism and religion. She has also starred in numerous films and television shows.

name: The Undertaker
about: The Undertaker is an American professional wrestler who spent the majority of his career with World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE). Known for his dark, supernatural persona, he became one of the most iconic figures in professional wrestling history; especially alongside his character's half-brother Kane.

name: Cory Barlog
about: Cory Barlog is best known for his work on the "God of War" series. He has played a key role in shaping the franchise's narrative and gameplay, with his father also being involved in the project.

name: Brian Lara
homePlace: Cantaro, Santa Cruz, Trinidad and Tobago
about: Lara is considered one of the greatest cricket batsmen of all-time.

name: Jeremy Sisto
about: Jeremy Sisto is an American actor who came to fame with performances in Clueless (1995),   (2001-2005), and Law & Order (2008-2010). Besides acting, Sisto has ventured into screenwriting and producing, as with his work on Break Point (2014).

name: Uma Thurman
about:
Uma Thurman has starred in leading roles in a variety of films, ranging from romantic comedies and dramas to science fiction and action movies.  
 
She rose to international prominence in 1994 following her role in  's " " for which she was nominated for an Academy Award.

name: Tupac Shakur
about: Tupac Shakur's mother and many of his family were members of   revolutionary party and their beliefs informed Shakur's music. Shakur was particularly concerned the struggles and violence of inner city life.

name: Patricia Arquette
about: Patricia Arquette is an accomplished American actress who has been captivating audiences with her performance over three decades. She first gained widespread attention for her role as Alabama Whitman in the  -written film, True Romance (1993).

name: Didier Drogba
about:
Didier Drogba is an Ivorian football player, best known as a striker for Chelsea. He holds the record for highest scorer on the Ivory Coast national team, as well as highest scorer among foreign players at Chelsea.  
 
In 2012 Drogba was named Chelsea's greatest ever player by a poll of fans, and he is regarded as one of the greatest African players. He was named African Footballer of the Year in 2006 and then again in 2009.

name: Akon
about: Akon is an American-Senegalese singer, songwriter, producer, and entrepreneur who rose to fame in the mid-2000s with his unique blend of R&B, hip hop, and world music. Known for his smooth vocals and catchy hooks, Akon has released numerous hit singles and albums, collaborating with a wide range of artists across different genres.

name: Hidetaka Miyazaki
about: Hidetaka Miyazaki created the Dark Souls series, which established a new subgenre of action role-playing games known for their high difficulty, and serves as president of FromSoftware.

name: Nathan Fillion
about: Nathan Fillion is a Canadian-American actor who gained widespread recognition for his role as Captain Malcolm "Mal" Reynolds in the science fiction television series Firefly (2002) and the subsequent film Serenity (2005). Although Firefly was short-lived, it developed a cult following and remains a beloved series among fans.

name: Jason Momoa
about: Of part Hawaiian decent Jason Momoa was actually brought up in Iowa before later moving to Hawaii and landing a role in the TV series Baywatch at 19.

name: Missy Elliott
about:
Beginning her rapping career in the 1990s with the all-female R&B group Sista, Elliot later joined the Swing Mob collective before launching her solo career in 1997.  
 
To date, Elliot is the bestselling female rap album artist in Nielson Music History.

name: David Krumholtz
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Known for playing Charlie Eppes in the CBS drama series "Numbers". Also appeared as Seth Goldstein in the "Harold & Kumar" film series.

name: Wladimir Klitschko
about: Klitschko came to fame as a professional boxer, having been world heavyweight champion twice and first winning gold at the 1996 Olympics. He was known as an impressively agile and intelligent boxer for his size and class.

name: Gisele Bündchen
homePlace: Horizontina, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
about: A Brazilian supermodel, Bündchen rose to fame in the 1990s becoming well known as a model for American lingerie brand Victoria's Secret.

name: David Muir
about: David Muir is an American journalist and news anchor, best known for his current role as anchor for ABC World News Tonight. He had previously worked as a weekend and substitute anchor for ABC World News Tonight with Diane Sawyer.

name: Ken Jennings
about:
Holds the record for the longest winning streak on the US syndicated game show Jeopardy!  
 
Jennings is also the all-time leading money winner on American game shows.

name: Ichiro Suzuki
about:
Has the most career base hits with 4,367 in a professional career stretching across Japan and the United States. 
 
Also holds MLB's single-season record for hits with 262.  
 
Suzuki was a MLB All-Star between 2001 and 2010.

name: Brandy Norwood
about: Brandy Norwood is an American singer who has sold over 40 million records worldwide and earned numerous accolades, including a Grammy Award and an American Music Award.

name: Gabriela Sabatini
about: Gabriela Sabatini is an Argentine former professional tennis player. She was one of the leading players on the women's circuit in the late-1980s and early-1990s.

name: Mary Joe Fernández
about: Mary Joe Fernández was an American tennis player best known for reaching the finals of three Grand Slam singles tournaments and winning two Grand Slam doubles titles, as well as her Olympic performances, coaching career, and role as a tennis commentator.

name: Jason Mraz
about: Jason Mraz is an American singer-songwriter and guitarist best known for his hit singles like "The Remedy (I Won't Worry)" (2002) and "I'm Yours" (2008).

name: Tricia Helfer
about: Tricia Helfer is a Canadian actress and former model, best known for her role as Number Six, a humanoid Cylon, in the reimagined Battlestar Galactica television series (2004-2009). Her captivating performance in the series garnered her significant acclaim and a strong fan following.

name: Chris Stapleton
about: Chris Stapleton has won numerous awards, including ACM’s Artist-Songwriter of the Decade, and is recognized as one of the most influential artists in modern country music.

name: Ice Cube
about: The pioneering rap artist helped establish the American west coast gangsta rap sound as part of N.W.A. and later as a solo artist. He then went on to become a successful actor in film and on TV.

name: Yuji Naka
about: Yuji Naka is best known for co-creating Sonic the Hedgehog.

name: Dave Chappelle
about: Dave Chappelle is an American stand-up comedian and actor. He came to fame with his comedy sketch series Chapelle's Show (2003-2006), which he quit in the middle of the third season. He has since become a major stand-up comic in the United States, being ranked No. 9 in Rolling Stone's list of the "50 Best Stand Up Comics of All Time."

name: Kelly Jones
about: Lead singer of the Welsh rock band Stereophonics. The band released their debut studio album in 1997 and have gone on to produce regular album ever since including five no. 1 UK albums.

name: Christopher Nolan
about: Christopher Nolan is known for the complex narratives and innovative storytelling techniques used in his blockbuster films. He is one of the most successful and influential directors in modern cinema, with his films earning both critical acclaim and commercial success.

name: Renée Zellweger
about: Renée Zellweger made her film breakthrough in the 1996 film  "Jerry Maguire" opposite  . Her next major success was "Me, Myself and Irene" (2000) with  , with whom she became briefly engaged. She then won a Golden Globe award for the lead role in the dark comedy "Nurse Betty" (2000).

name: Eva Mendes
about: Eva Mendes is an American actress and model. She began acting in the late 1990s and rose to prominence with a series of roles in major Hollywood films. Her breakthrough came with the 2001 film Training Day, where she starred opposite  .

name: Aaron Eckhart
about: Aaron Edward Eckhart is an American actor known for his performances in a range of films, including Erin Brockovich (2000) and   (2008).

name: Ioan Gruffudd
about: Ioan Gruffudd is a Welsh actor who came to fame through the Hornblower series and mainstream success with roles in Titanic, Fantastic Four, and as   in Amazing Grace. His career spans stage, screen, and voice work, and he is also known for his cultural contributions as a native Welsh speaker.

name: Ken Griffey Jr.
about: Ken Griffey Jr. hit 630 home runs in his career, ranking 7th all-time, and was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2016 with 99.32% of the vote, the highest percentage at that time.

name: MacKenzie Scott
about: MacKenzie Scott is best known as the ex-wife of Amazon founder  .

name: Halle Berry
about: Monster's Ball (2001), Their Eyes Were Watching God (2005) and X-Men: Days of Future Past (2015).

name: Floyd Mayweather Jr.
about: Floyd Mayweather Jr. is an American former professional boxer who achieved an undefeated record during his career with a record of 49–0, with 26 knockouts. Known for his technical skill, defensive prowess, and strategic approach to fighting, Mayweather is often cited as one of the greatest boxers in the history of the sport.

name: Slash
about: Born in England to a Black American mother and an English father, Slash moved to Los Angeles as a child. He began playing bands before joining Guns N' Roses in 1985 alongside  , Izzy Stradlin, Duff McKagan and Steven Adler, replacing some of the band's earlier members.

name: Chai Jing
about: Chai Jing is known for her investigative reporting and environmental activism.

name: Paul Walker
about:
Paul Walker was the star of The Fast and the Furious film franchise. He was filming the 7th film "Furious 7"  when he died in a car accident in 2013. 
 
The single "See You Again" by Wiz Khalifa off the "Furious 7" soundtrack is a tribute to Walker. In July 2017 it became YouTube's most watched video and has recorded over 5.9 billion views.

name: Keith Urban
about: Born in New Zealand, Keith Urban grew up in Australia where he released his first solo album in 1991. A move to America followed a year later where Urban has built a hugely successful career as a singer-songwriter and music producer. Primarily known as a country music artist, Urban is also recognized for the strong pop and rock elements to his music.

name: Gucci Mane
about: Gucci Mane is an American rapper and record executive best known as an early pioneer of trap music. He was an early influence alongside other rappers from Atlanta, including T.I. and Young Jeezy, during the rise of trap music in the 2000s and 2010s.

name: Jim Parsons
about: Jim Parsons big breakthrough role was as Sheldon Cooper, the socially challenged physicist in the TV sitcom "The Big Bang Theory." The series ran for 12 seasons from 2007 to 2019.

name: Gwyneth Paltrow
about:
She garnered worldwide recognition through her performance in " ", for which she won an Academy Award for Best Actress and a Golden Globe Award.  
 
She is also the face of American fashion brand Coach, owner of the lifestyle company Goop.com and author of two cookbooks: My Father's Daughter: Delicious, Easy Recipes Celebrating Family & Togetherness, and It's All Good.

name: Tony Hawk
about: Former professional skateboarder. Well known for completing the first documented 900 and for his licensed video game titles, distributed by Activision. He is widely considered to be one of the most successful and influential pioneers of modern vertical skateboarding.

name: Derek Jeter
about: He is known as the key factor during the success of New York Yankees in the late 1990s.

name: Jewel Kilcher
about:
Jewel Kilcher is an American singer-songwriter, known for having received four Grammy nominations and having sold over 30 million albums worldwide.  
 
Her top singles are "You Were Meant for Me" (1995) and "Foolish Games" (1995), which both charted at number two.

name: Venus Williams
about: A former World No. 1 who won four Olympic gold medals and 7 grand slam singles titles.

name: Petro Poroshenko
about: Poroshenko is a Ukrainian businessman who served as President of Ukraine from 2014 to 2019, when he was ousted by  .

name: Tom Brady
about:
Widely considered the greatest quarterback of all time, Brady is a seven-time Super Bowl winning quarterback. Five of which he was named most valuable player. 
 
In a long career, Brady has played for just two NFL franchises, the New England Patriots from 2000 to 2019 and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers from 2019 to 2023.  
 
He has set and continues to hold numerous quarterback records.

name: Pedro Pascal
about: Pedro Pascal is a Chilean-born American actor who gained recognition for his roles in the fourth season of the HBO series   (2014) as Oberyn Martell, and the Netflix crime series Narcos (2015-2017) as Javier Peña.

name: Sam Houser
about: Sam Houser is best as known co-founder and president of Rockstar Games, which creates the Grand Theft Auto series.

name: Dan Houser
about: Dan Houser is best known for co-founding Rockstar Games, having played a key role in creating some of the most popular video game franchises such as Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption.

name: Luke Bryan
about: Luke Bryan achieved success as a songwriter before releasing his own debut album in 2007 "I'll Stay Me". His second album "Doing My Thing" (2009) included two No. 1 singles and went to No. 2 on the country chart. His third album "Tailgates and Tanlines" (2011) was equally successful.

name: James McAvoy
about: The Scottish actor came to fame in the UK in TV series such as "Shameless", "State of Play" and the adaption of Zadie Smiths book "White Teeth"'.

name: Peter Andre
about: Peter Andre is an Australian singer, songwriter, businessman and television personality. He gained popularity as a singer in the early 1990s with his debut album, "Peter Andre."

name: David Schwimmer
about: Schwimmer gained worldwide fame for his starring role as Ross Geller on the sitcom Friends (1994-2004), which became one of the most popular television programs of all time.

name: Sammy Sosa
homePlace: San Pedro de Macoris, Dominican Republic
about:
Played with four Major League Baseball teams over his career, which spanned from 1989 to 2007, but is best known for playing with the Chicago Cubs.  
 
As a Cub, he became one of the league's best hitters, and in 1998 he and   achieved national fame for their home run-hitting prowess in pursuit of  ' home run record.

name: Larry Page
about: One of the co-founders of Google, he also invented Google's best-known search ranking algorithm "PageRank."

name: Steve Zahn
about: Steve Zahn is an American actor best known for his performances in Sahara (2005) and Dallas Buyers Club (2013). He also starred in all three of the Diary of a Wimpy Kid trilogy (2010-2012).

name: Jessica Simpson
about:
American recording artist, actress, television personality and fashion designer.  
 
Simpson has many popular recordings to her name and has starred in several television shows, movies and commercials.  
 
She also launched a line of hair and beauty products and designed fragrances, shoes and handbags for women.

name: Annika Sörenstam
about: Won 10 LPGA major titles and an 8-time LPGA Tour Player of the Year.

name: Alexis Denisof
about: Alexis Denisof is an American actor known for his roles as Wesley Wyndam-Pryce in the television series Buffy the Vampire Slayer (1999) and its spin-off Angel (1999–2004). He also appeared as Sandy Rivers in the popular sitcom How I Met Your Mother (2006–2014), working alongside his wife, actress  .

name: Penélope Cruz
about: Penélope Cruz is a Spanish actress known for her work in both Spanish and English-language films.

name: Chris O'Donnell
about: Chris O'Donnell first gained fame for his performance in "Scent of a Woman" (1992) and later became a household name as Robin in the Batman film series.

name: Amy Fisher
about: Amy Fisher was just 16 years old when she shot Mary Jo Buttafuoco, the wife of Joey Buttafuoco (35), with whom she was having an affair. Mary Jo survived and Fischer pleaded guilty to  first-degree aggravated assault and served seven years in jail.

name: Marine Le Pen
about: Marine Le Pen is a prominent figure in the French far-right political movement. She is best known for her leadership of the National Rally party and her multiple campaigns for the French presidency.

name: Jill Soloway
about:
Soloway is an Emmy award-winning television writer.  
 
She won the Best Director award at the Sundance Film Festival for the film "Afternoon Delight".  
 
She has also worked on the show "Six Feet Under".

name: Louise Woodward
about: Convicted of the involuntary manslaughter for the death of eight-month-old Matthew Eappen In 1997.

name: Casey Affleck
about: Casey Affleck is best known for his roles in independent films and his Academy Award-winning performance, as well as for being the younger brother of actor  .

name: Daniel Johns
about: Former front man of Australian rock band "Silverchair", he is also one half of "The Dissociatives" with Paul Mac.

name: Sergey Brin
about: Sergey Brin co-founded Google, one of the world's most influential companies. He is known for his innovative work in search engine technology and his philanthropic efforts.

name: Chris Tucker
about: Chris Tucker is an American comedian and actor. He is known for his stand-up comedy and roles in films such as Friday (1995), The Fifth Element (1997), and the Rush Hour series.

name: Seth MacFarlane
about:
Creator and star of "Family Guy", one of the most successful adult animated television series in history.  
 
MacFarlane also co-created the highly successful follow on TV series "American Dad" which also achieved widespread success and the spinoff series "The Cleveland Show".  
 
He also wrote, directed and starred in the films "Ted", "Ted 2" and "A Million Ways to Die in the West".

name: Wes Bentley
about: Wes Bentley is an American actor best known for his roles in American Beauty (1999) and   (2012). He gained early acclaim for his performance in American Beauty which led to a BAFTA Award nomination but struggled with substance abuse, causing a temporary decline in his career.

name: Daniel Craig
about: Daniel Craig was an English stage and screen actor before landing the role of James Bond in 2005. He initially trained at London's Guildhall School of Arts, graduating in 1991. He then worked consistently, appearing in the TV series "Our Friends in the North" alongside Christopher Eccleston, and in the film "Elizabeth" (1998) starring  . His international breakthrough came playing  's love interest in "Lara Croft: Tomb Raider" (2001) before going on to appear in   "Road to Perdition" (2002) as an Irish gangster. A role in  's "Munich" (2005) followed.

name: Sacha Baron Cohen
about: Sacha Baron Cohen is best known for creating controversial characters that expose societal prejudices. He first gained fame through his character Ali G on British television in the late 1990s.

name: Zinedine Zidane
about: Zidane is regarded as one of football’s greatest attacking midfielders of all-time

name: Enrique Peña Nieto
about: Enrique Peña Nieto was a Mexican politician who served as the President of Mexico from 2012 to 2018, representing the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). His term was marked by significant policy changes, encompassing reforms in sectors such as energy, education, telecommunications, and the financial system. Despite these ambitious efforts, his administration also faced criticism and controversy, particularly in areas such as human rights and corruption.

name: Blake Shelton
about: Blake Shelton is an American country music singer and television personality who made his debut in 2001 with the single "Austin."

name: Pamela Anderson
about: Pamela Anderson had her first Playboy cover in October 1989 and has since appeared on more Playboy covers than any other model.

name: Marshawn Lynch
about: Marshawn Lynch is an American football running back who was nicknamed "Beast Mode" for his style of play. He is best known for his time with the Seattle Seahawks, where he spent the majority of his football career.

name: Joseph Mazzello
about:
Mazzello began his career as a child actor, gaining fame for his role as Tim Murphy in  's   (1993). 
 
He has since become known for his roles as Eugene Sledge in the acclaimed HBO miniseries The Pacific (2010), also executive produced by  , and as Dustin Moskovitz in The Social Network (2010).

name: Josh Hutcherson
about: Josh Hutcherson is an American actor. His career spans from early childhood roles to the international recognition as Peeta Mellark in   film series (2012-2015). Hutcherson has also been involved in independent cinema and production while actively supporting the LGBT community and engaging in political activism.

name: Rupert Grint
about: Best known for his role as  's best friend Ron Weasley in the Harry Potter film series.

name: Pete Davidson
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Pete Davidson is an American stand-up comedian, actor and writer. He was a cast member on Saturday Night Live from 2014 to 2022. Davidson first achieved recognition after guest roles on comedy shows such as Brooklyn Nine-Nine and Guy Code.

name: Diana Taurasi
about: Diana Taurasi is a professional basketball player who has played for the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury since 2004. She is a nine-time WNBA All-Star and was the league's MVP in 2009. Taurasi has also played professionally in Russia and Turkey.

name: Suzann Pettersen
about: Suzann Pettersen is known for her success on the LPGA Tour and her dramatic performances in the Solheim Cup. She has won two major championships and has been ranked as high as second in the world.

name: El Rubius
about: El Rubius is a Spanish YouTuber, streamer, and internet personality best known for his gaming content, humor, and ability to connect with his audience. This has made him one of the most popular and influential online figures in the world.

name: Kenenisa Bekele
about: Kenenisa Bekele is an Ethiopian long-distance runner who held the records in 5,000-metre from 2004 and 10,000-metre from 2005 until 2020. He won gold in the 10,000m and silver in the 5,000m at the 2004 Olympics in Athens.

name: Kyrie Irving
about:
Named NBA Rookie of the Year for the 2011-2012 season, Irving played for the Cleveland Cavaliers from 2011 to 2017, when he signed up with the Boston Celtics. 
 
He was named NBA All-Star Game Most Valuable Player in 2014. In 2016 he was part of the US national team that won gold at the Rio Olympics.

name: Chance the Rapper
about: Chance the Rapper is best known for his independent music career, as well as his philanthropic work in Chicago. He gained fame through his mixtapes and became the first artist to win a Grammy Award for a streaming-only album.

name: Henry Cavill
about: Henry Cavill is the 1st non-American actor to play the DC hero Superman. His 2013 "Man of Steel" was the highest-grossing Superman film ever, Cavill again played the superhero in the follow-up film " : Dawn of Justice" (2016) opposite   and   and in "Justice League" (2017).

name: David Lee
about: David Lee is an American former professional basketball player who is perhaps best known as the husband of Danish former world #1 tennis player  .

name: MS Dhoni
about: Indian cricketer MS Dhoni is his country's the most successful captain of the national side. Under his captaincy 2007-2016 India won every ICC trophy, including the 2007 ICC World Twenty20, the  2011 ICC Cricket World Cup and the 2013 Champions Trophy.

name: Kaley Cuoco
about: Kaley Cuoco achieved worldwide fame playing Penny in the phenomenally successful TV sitcom "The  " which ran from 2007 -2019 and for 12 seasons. Cuoco was one of the original three main actors along with Jim Parson's Sheldon and  's Leonard.

name: Barbara Pierce Bush
about: is an American activist and health care advocate who is the daughter of former President   and former First Lady Laura Bush. She is also the granddaughter of former President   and former First Lady Barbara Bush, after whom she is named, as well as the co-founder and chair of nonprofit organization Global Health Corps

name: Conor McGregor
about: Conor McGregor is an Irish professional mixed martial artist and boxer. He is the former Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) featherweight and lightweight champion. He has also competed as a welterweight in mixed martial arts (MMA), and light middleweight in boxing.

name: Gunna
about: Gunna is an American rapper who first came to fame with his 2018 mixtape, Drip Season 3. He followed this with a mixtape collaboration with  , Drip Harder (2018), from which the single "Drip Too Hard" reached number four on the Billboard Hot 100.

name: Michelle Wie
about:
Michelle Wie is an American professional golfer who plays on the LPGA Tour. Wie began playing golf at the age of four, and by age ten she was the youngest player to qualify for the U.S. Women's Amateur Public Links Championship.  
 
She turned professional at the age of sixteen after a successful amateur career, winning several tournaments. Since then she has had some success with her highest achievement thus far winning the 2014 U.S. Women's Open.

name: Evan Rachel Wood
about: Evan Rachel Wood is an American actress best known for her roles in Thirteen (2003), The Wrestler (2008), and Westworld (2016–2022), as well as her advocacy for survivors of sexual assault. She has won a Critics' Choice Television Award and has been nominated for Primetime Emmy and Golden Globe awards.

name: Lena Dunham
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Lena Dunham came to fame as the creator and star of the HBO series "Girls", based in part on her own life. Durham was nominated for seven Emmy award and has won two Golden Globe awards for "Girls".  
 
Dunham has also published a successful biography "Not That Kind of Girl: A Young Woman Tells You What She's "Learned" and is a prominent voice on social media.

name: Nicholas Hoult
about: Nicholas Hoult is an English actor and producer. He began his career in the UK, appearing in films and television shows as a child. He is best known for his roles in the films "About a Boy" opposite   and in the "X-Men" film franchise.

name: Kyle Busch
about: Was the NASCAR Cup Series Champion in 2015 and at 20 years-old became the youngest driver to win a NASCAR Cup Series race

name: Alex Morgan
about: Professional US soccer player Alexa Morgan graduated from the University of California, Berkeley before joining her first team the Western New York Flash in 2011. Since then, playing as a forward, she has played for a series of US and international clubs, joining English club Tottenham Hotspur in 2020.

name: Calum Scott
homePlace: Beverly, East Riding of Yorkshire, England
about: Calum Scott is a British singer and songwriter. He is best known for his breakthrough performance on Britain's Got Talent and his hit single "Dancing on My Own." Following his appearance on the talent show, Scott embarked on a successful music career.

name: Joel Embiid
about: Joel Embiid is a Cameroonian professional basketball player known for his career with the Philadelphia 76ers. He has achieved recognition as an NBA MVP, respected for his scoring prowess and defensive skills. Embiid overcame early injuries to become an accomplished player, earning multiple All-Star selections and All-NBA Team honors.

name: N'Golo Kante
about: N'Golo Kanté is a French footballer known for his skill as a defensive midfielder. He currently play for Al-Ittihad in the Saudi Pro League, having moved there in 2023 from Chelsea, as well as the French national team.

name: Anna Kournikova
about: Anna Kournikova is a Russian former professional tennis player who achieved worldwide celebrity status, despite never winning a WTA singles title.

name: Brittany Lincicome
about:
Brittany Lincicome turned professional in 2008 and has since won eight professional golf tournaments, including two major championships.  
 
She is married to fellow professional golfer Dewald Gouws.

name: Lucy Hale
about:
Lucy Hale starred in the teen drama "Pretty Little Liars (2010-2017), alongside an ensemble cast that included Ashley Benson, Shay Mitchell, Sasha Pieterse and Janel Parrish. Hale won a number of Teen Choice and People's Choice awards for the role. 
 
In 2019 she appeared in "Katy Keene", the spin-off to "Riversdale" as the titular character. This has been followed by the thriller series "Ragdoll"

name: Candice Swanepoel
about: Candice Swanepoel is known for her work with Victoria's Secret and her swimwear line. She began her career at a young age and has since become one of the world's top-earning models.

name: John Tavares
about:
John Tavers was selected first overall by the New York Islanders in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft and went on to serve as their captain. After playing for the New York Islanders from 2009-2018 Tavers signed for the Toronto Maple Leafs.  
 
Tavers has represented Canada at the World Championships and was part of a gold medal winning team at the 2014 Olympic Games despite injuring his knee.

name: Dave Franco
about:
Dave Franco is an American actor who first came to fame with a supporting role in 21 Jump Street (2012), featuring   and Channing Tatum. He has since gone on to start in a number of films, such as Now You See Me (2013) and The Disaster Artist (2017).  
 
Franco is the brother of James Franco, and he is married to  .

name: Edward Snowden
about:
Came to international attention after leaking thousands of classified documents from the National Security Agency to several media outlets. 
 
He acquired the documents while working as an NSA contractor. The leaked documents revealed publicly numerous global surveillance programs for the first time.

name: Li Na
about: Li Na is a pioneering Chinese tennis player and the first Asian player to win a Grand Slam title. In 2011 she won the French Open, followed by the 2014 Australian Tennis Open.

name: Bad Bunny
homePlace: Almirante Sur, Vega Baja, Puerto Rico
about: Bad Bunny is a Puerto Rican rapper best known for his 2016 song "Diles." He has since released further hit singles such as "Soy Peor" (2016) and featured on  's "I Like It" with J Balvin. Bunny had a top-10 single in the form of "Mia" (2018) featuring Drake.

name: Daniil Medvedev
about: Daniil Medvedev is a Russian professional tennis player best known for winning the 2021 US Open, becoming the world No. 1 in 2022, and winning 20 ATP Tour singles titles, including six Masters titles. He was recognized for defeating the top three players in the world at the 2020 ATP Finals and for his rivalries with Stefanos Tsitsipas and  .

name: José Altuve
about:
Altuve is the second baseman for the Houston Astros of Major League Baseball, who made his major league debut on July 20, 2011. 
 
Having won the American League batting title and its MVP Award, Altuve was declared Sports Illustrated's Sportsperson of the Year in 2017.

name: Phoebe Waller-Bridge
about: Phoebe Waller-Bridge is known for the comedic yet tragic TV series "Fleabag" (2016-19) and the assassin drama " " (2018-22)

name: Shia LaBeouf
about: Known as Sam Witwicky in the science fiction film Transformers.

name: Elisabeth Moss
about: Elisabeth Moss has been acting since she was a child. her most well known early role is as Zoey Bartlet in the Alan Sorkin drama "West Wing".

name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
about: Giannis Antetokounmpo is a professional basketball player for the Milwaukee Bucks. He was born in Athens, Greece in 1994 and grew up in Sepolia, a neighborhood of Athens. He is the son of Nigerian immigrants and the second-youngest of four brothers.

name: Lil Durk
about: Lil Durk, born Durk Derrick Banks, is an American rapper and singer. He first came to fame with his mixtape series called "Signed to the Streets" (2013-2014), which led to him receiving a label deal with Def Jam Recordings.

name: Alessia Cara
about: Alessia Cara is a Canadian singer-songwriter who started out uploading covers to YouTube. She came to mainstream fame with her debut single "Here" in 2015, and released her debut studio album Know-It-All in that same year.

name: Sebastian Kurz
about: Sebastian Kurz is an Austrian politician who has served as Chancellor of Austria since January 2020. He is the youngest person to hold the office, at the age of 33. Kurz is leader of the conservative Austrian People's Party (ÖVP) and has been a Member of the Austrian Parliament since 2013.

name: Lily James
about: Lily James is an English actress who has gained recognition for her roles in both television and film. She is best known for her portrayal of Lady Rose MacClare in the acclaimed TV series,   (2012-2015).

name: Kawhi Leonard
about: Kawhi Leonard is an American basketball player best known as one of the greatest two-way players in NBA history. He has achieved two NBA championships and two Finals MVP awards, leading both the San Antonio Spurs and Toronto Raptors to titles.

name: Ozuna
about:
Known as the 'New King of Reggaeton,' Ozuna's music mixes reggaeton and trap—though this hasn't limited his collaborations, which have ranged several further genres.  
 
Ozuna has been particularly prominent in Latin music, with all his albums charting on the Billboard Top Latin Albums, including 'Aura' which made it to number seven on the Billboard 200.  
 
As one of the all-time best-selling Latin music artists, Ozuna has sold over 15 million records.

name: Mohammed bin Salman
about: Salman, Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia since 2017, is widely considered the de facto ruler of Saudi Arabia in place of his father King Salman. Early in his tenure he was praised for several reforms including liberalizing the country's strict laws against women driving and working and an effort to diversify the Saudi economy.

name: Petra Kvitová
about: Petra Kvitová best known for winning the Wimbledon Championship in 2011 and 2014, as well as 28 career singles titles. She also won bronze for the Czech Republic at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

name: Maria Sharapova
about: The No. 1 ranked women's tennis player in 2005, Maria Sharapova won five Grand Slam singles titles including a career grand slam and 36 WTA singles titles.

name: Emile Hirsch
about: Emile Hirsch is an American actor who gained significant attention for his lead role in the biographical adventure drama Into the Wild (2007). In this film, directed by  , Hirsch portrayed Christopher McCandless, a young man who abandons his possessions and savings to travel across America.

name: Anita Sarkeesian
about: Anita Sarkeesian is a Canadian-American feminist media critic and public speaker, best known as the founder of Feminist Frequency and for her analysis of the tropes in the depiction of women in video games.

name: Daniel Logan
about: Daniel Logan is a New Zealand-born American actor, known for his role as Boba Fett in  : Episode II – Attack of the Clones (2002). He was discovered at a rugby match and began acting in commercials and television in New Zealand. His portrayal of Boba Fett brought him international recognition.

name: Casey Neistat
about: Casey Neistat first gained attention with his 2003 video "iPod's Dirty Secret," which criticized Apple's battery replacement policy. He has since become known for his innovative video content and business ventures.

name: Julia Stiles
about: Julia Stiles is an American actress who came to fame as a teen icon with leading roles in films like "10 Things I Hate About You" (1999), "Down to You" (2000), and "Save the Last Dance" (2001), winning several MTV Movie Awards. She has also received critical acclaim for her performances in Shakespearean adaptations like "Hamlet" (2000) and "O" (2001).

name: Anthony Ramos
about: Anthony Ramos is an American actor and singer, best known for playing   and Philip Hamilton in the Broadway musical Hamilton created by  . Since then he has also appeared in A Star Is Born (2018) and In the Heights (2021).

name: Cole Sprouse
about: Cole Sprouse first gained fame as a child actor alongside his twin brother,  , and has since transitioned to adult roles in television and film.

name: Emily Osment
about: Emily Osment is an American actress whose career began as a child star in such movies as Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams (2002) and Spy Kids 3-D: Game Over (2003). She is perhaps best known for starring alongside   as Lilly Truscott on Hannah Montana (2006-2011) as well as Hannah Montana: The Movie (2009).

name: Robbie Amell
about: Robbie Amell is a Canadian-American actor best known for playing Stephen Jameson in The Tomorrow People (2013-2014), Ronnie Raymond / Firestorm in The Flash (2014-2023), and Nathan Brown in Upload (2020-present).

name: Jessie J
about: Jessie J is a British singer and songwriter who first came to fame with her debut single, "Do It Like a Dude" (2010). This was followed up by the hit single "Price Tag," which was chart-topper in the UK and eighteen other countries. After this she released her debut album, Who You Are (2011)

name: Cobie Smulders
about: Cobie Smulders is a Canadian actress who gained fame for her role as Robin Scherbatsky on the popular television series How I Met Your Mother, which aired from 2005 to 2014.

name: Xie Na
about:
Xie is one of the most followed Chinese celebrities on Weibo, with more than 100 million followers on the social media website. 
 
She became famous hosting the variety television show Happy Camp, which is one of China's most popular television shows, regularly achieving an active viewership of tens of millions. 
 
Xie founded her own personal clothing line "HUANXING" in 2010.

name: Josh Allen
about: Josh Allen is a quarterback for the Buffalo Bills in the National Football League (NFL). He is considered one of the most talented and successful quarterbacks in the league today.

name: Paris Hilton
about:
The socialite Paris Hilton, a member of the Hilton hotel dynasty, rose to fame as a reality star on the TV series “The Simple Life” with Nicole Richie. Numerous reality show appearances have followed. 
 
The leak of a sex tape with her then-boyfriend Rick Salomon in 2003 seemed to only add to her public profile and fame.

name: Soulja Boy
about:
Soulja Boy is an American rapper, best known for his debut single "Crank That (Soulja Boy)" which was a number 1 hit on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2007, a position it held for a total of seven weeks. He followed this with his debut album, Souljaboytellem.com (2007). 
 
These albums were followed by iSouljaBoyTellem (2008) and The DeAndre Way (2010). The former featured two hit singles, "Turn My Swag On" and "Kiss Me thru the Phone."

name: Jaimie Alexander
about:
Jaimie Alexander is best known for playing Lady Sif in the Marvel Cinema Universe films such as Thor (2011), Thor: The Dark World (2013), and Thor: Love and Thunder (2022).  
 
Alexander has also starred in the television series Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (2013-20) and Loki (2021).

name: Megan Thee Stallion
about: Now a globally famous American rapper, Megan Thee Stallion first came to fame when videos of her freestyle rapping went viral on social media.

name: JD Vance
about: JD Vance is a United States Senator and author known for his bestselling memoir and rapid rise in politics. He is currently a vice presidential nominee for the 2024 election.

name: Dakota Fanning
about: Dakota Fanning is an American actress who started out as a child actress before successfully transitioning to adult roles. She became the youngest SAG Award nominee for her performance in I Am Sam (2001), and is also known for her role alongside   in Man on Fire (2004).

name: Carol E. Reiley
homePlace: Flint, Michigan, United States of America
about: Best known for her work in teleoperated and autonomous robotics, having worked on surgical, rescue, and space exploration systems for companies such as Lockheed Martin and General Electric.

name: Léa Seydoux
about: Léa Seydoux is a French actress known for her work in both French cinema and Hollywood films. Coming from a prominent family with entertainment industry ties, Seydoux's upbringing in Paris included aspirations of becoming an opera singer before she pivoted to acting.

name: Patrick Stump
about: Best known as the lead singer, guitarist and songwriter for Fall Out Boy, an American rock band from Wilmette, Illinois.

name: Raheem Sterling
about: Raheem Sterling is an English professional footballer who plays as a winger and attacking midfielder for Manchester City and the England national team. He began his career at Queens Park Rangers before signing with Liverpool in 2010 and making his professional debut in 2012.

name: Shailene Woodley
about: Shailene Woodley is an American actress, best known for her roles in films such as The Fault in Our Stars (2014) and Divergent (2014).

name: Gareth Bale
about: Gareth Bale is a Welsh professional footballer considered one of the best of his generation, and one of the all-time best Welsh players. He rose to prominence during his time with Tottenham Hotspur (2007-2013), where he transitioned from a left-back to a winger and established himself as one of the Premier League’s standout players.

name: Diana DeGarmo
about: Rose to fame in 2004 as the runner-up of the third season of American Idol. Also appeared on "The Young and the Restless" as "jersey girl" Angelina Veneziano.

name: Jamie Dornan
about: Jamie Dornan is a Northern Irish actor who started out as a model and then went on to play a number of major television roles. He played Sheriff Graham Humbert in Once Upon a Time (2011-2013) and then Paul Spector in The Fall (2013-2016). These led him to a variety of film and television roles.

name: Joshua Wong
about:
Joshua Wong is a student activist influential during Hong Kong's Umbrella Revolution in 2014.  
 
He is the founder of student protest group Scholarism and in 2016 helped establish the pro-democracy political party Demosistō.

name: SZA
about: SZA is an American R&B Singer who came to fame with her debut album Ctrl in 2017, which debuted at number three and was acclaimed by critics. She was nominated for four Grammy Awards, including Best New Artist.

name: Benny Blanco
about: Benny Blanco has shaped modern pop music through his writing and production collaborations with major artists such as  ,  ,  ,  ,  , Maroon 5, and more.

name: Patrick Kane
about: Patrick Kane is an American professional ice hockey player best known for his time with the Chicago Blackhawks. He won three Stanley Cup championships and earned recognition as one of the best American-born players.

name: Bobi Wine
about: Bobi Wine is a pop star turned politician in his native Uganda.  He turned to politics in 2017 and led the opposition National Unity Platform (NUP) in an effort to oust long-serving Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni from power.

name: Ben Stokes
about: Ben Stokes is an English cricketer known for his all-round abilities and significant impact in high-profile matches, most notably the 2019 World Cup final and the Ashes. Born in New Zealand and raised in England, Stokes has held key roles for the national team, including Test captain, and has contributed to both England’s on-field successes and changes in team approach.

name: Rob Gronkowski
about: Rob "Gronk" Gronkowski is known as one of the greatest tight ends in NFL history. He played 11 seasons, winning four Super Bowls and setting several records at his position.

name: Gugu Mbatha-Raw
about: The stage and screen actress rose to fame in the 2013 period film "Belle" portraying historical figure Dido Elizabeth Belle, the mixed race woman brought up in an aristocratic English household in the sixteenth century.

name: Russell Wilson
about: Russell Wilson is an American football quarterback who has played for more than 12 years with the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and the Pittsburgh Steelers. He has earned seven Pro Bowl selections, led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory in 2014, during which he was named Super Bowl XLVIII MVP.

name: Adriana Lima
about: Adriana Lima is a Brazilian model and actress best known for her work as a Victoria's Secret Angel. She gained international fame after placing second in the Ford Supermodel of the World contest.

name: Anthony Davis
about: Anthony Davis is an American basketball player who plays power forward and center for the Los Angeles Lakers. He has been selected for four All-NBA First Teams and four NBA All-Defensive Teams.

name: Thomas Müller
about:
Müller is a German professional footballer, currently playing for Bayern Munich and the German team. His positional awareness has earned him a reputation as one of the all-time greatest off-the-ball players. 
 
Müller usually plays midfielder or forward, though he is a flexible player and has been placed in a wide variety of positions. This has led some to regard him as one of the best all-round attacking players currently in the game.

name: Lindsay Lohan
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: A model since she was three years old, Lindsay Lohan became a successful teen actress starring in "The Parent Trap", "Freaky Friday" (2003) opposite  , and in  's teen comedy " " (2004).

name: Davido
about:
Davido is a Nigerian-American singer-songwriter known for his style which blends traditional Africa music with mainstream pop.  
 
He came to fame in 2012 with his debut album Omo Baba Olowo (2012), eventually signing with Sony Music in 2016.

name: Bebe Rexha
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Bebe Rexha is an American singer, songwriter, and record producer. She is of Albanian descent and gained fame for her songwriting skills and successful solo career. Her accomplishments include penning songs for eminent artists and her works earning Grammy recognition. She has been a strong advocate for mental health awareness and the LGBTQ+ community.

name: Rami Malek
about: Malek's breakthrough role as an actor was the television series Mr. Robot (2015-19), for which he received critical acclaim.

name: Victoria Azarenka
about: Victoria Azarenka is the first Belarusian tennis player, male or female, to win a Grand Slam tournament singles title.

name: Stefanie Scott
about:
Best known for her role in Insidious: Chapter 3 (2015), Scott has also appeared in Flipped (2010) and Jem and the Holograms (2015) as well as other movies and television shows. 
 
She is also a recording artist, having released the pop EP New Girl in Town in 2009 and has released several singles since then. She has also contributed to the soundtracks of some of her films and has appeared in other artists' music videos.

name: Prince William
about:
The eldest son of King   of Great Britain and his first wifr  .  He is first in line to the  throne.  
 
He is the husband of Catherine "Kate" Middleton.

name: A Boogie wit da Hoodie
about:
A Boogie wit da Hoodie, born Artist Julius Dubose, is an American rapper and musician. He has had two significant charting singles with "Look Back at It" (2018) and "Drowning" (2017). 
 
Since signing with Atlantic Records he has released a series of albums, starting with his debut The Bigger Artist (2017) and followed by Hoodie SZN (2018), which reached number one on the Billboard 200, Artist 2.0 (2020) and Me vs. Myself (2022).

name: Rod Carew
about: 18-time MLB All Star and American League MVP in 1977 Minnesota Twins

name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
about: Emmerson Mnangagwa is a Zimbabwean politician who has served as the President of Zimbabwe since November 2017. He succeeded  , following Mugabe's resignation. Long a fixture of Zimbabwean politics, Mnangagwa was a leader of the rebel forces in the Rhodesian Bush War, alongside future president Robert Mugabe.

name: Harrison Ford
about: Regarded as a cinematic cultural icon, Harrison Ford has starred in many notable films since the 1960s. He reached global stardom as Han Solo in  's original " " trilogy (1977-83). He received further recognition for his role as Indiana Jones in the hit franchise from 1981 to 2023.

name: Roman Polanski
about: Roman Polanski is a Polish-French director known for his critically acclaimed films, including The Pianist (2003) for which he won the Oscar for Best Director.

name: Yasser Arafat
about: Yasser Arafat served as Chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) from 1969 until his death in 2004, and as President of the Palestinian National Authority (PNA) from 1994 also to 2004.

name: Berry Gordy
about: Founder of the Motown record label which was the highest-earning African-American business for decades.

name: Bobby Fischer
about:
Youngest grandmaster and the youngest candidate ever for the World Championship.  
 
At the age of 20 he won the 1963–64 U.S. Championship with 11/11, the only perfect score in the history of the tournament.

name: Pete Townshend
about: Best known as the guitarist and songwriter for rock group The Who, which was considered one of the most influential bands of the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Jorge Paulo Lemann
about:
The richest man in Brazil and second richest in Switzerland thanks to his stake in Anheuser-Busch InBev, the world's largest brewer. 
 
Lemann runs the private equity firm 3G Capital together with fellow billionaires and longtime partners Carlos Sicupira and Marcel Herrmann Telles. 
 
The trio also have stakes in Burger King and H.J. Heinz & Company. 
 
Lemann is also a former Brazilian tennis champion who played at Wimbledon.

name: Henry Winkler
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Henry Winkler is an American actor, producer, director, and author. He first rose to fame for his role as Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on the popular 1970s American sitcom Happy Days. The leather-jacket-wearing, motorcycle-riding "Fonz" was immensely popular and became a cultural icon, significantly defining Winkler's early career.

name: Carl Yastrzemski
about: Carl Yastrzemski is best for his 23-year career with the Boston Red Sox. He is regarded as one of the greatest players in Red Sox history and is a member of the Baseball Hall of Fame.

name: Stephen Jay Gould
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Gould formulated the evolutionary theory of punctuated equilibrium in 1972 with Niles Eldredge, and is one of the best known and most widely read scientists of the late 20th century. 
 
His theory of punctuated equilibrium states that evolutionary change is not a slow, steady process but rather occurs in a series of fits and starts.

name: Larry Ellison
about: Larry Ellison co-founded the Oracle Corporation. He is known for building one of the world's largest software companies and becoming one of the wealthiest individuals globally.

name: Andrew Grove
about: Andrew Grove was a Hungarian-American businessman and engineer who served as the third Chief Executive Officer of Intel Corporation. During his tenure, Intel would become the largest semiconductor company in the world.

name: John Major
about: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and the Leader of the Conservative Party from 1990 to 1997. Prior to holding these positions, Major worked in the cabinet of  , briefly holding the position of Chancellor of the Exchequer.

name: Oscar Robertson
about:
Hall of Fame basketball guard who played 14 NBA seasons and one-time winner of the MVP award.  
 
Robertson is the only player in NBA history to average a triple-double for a season and retired as the league’s all-time assist leader.

name: Newt Gingrich
about: Leader of the "Republican Revolution" of 1994 which led to a Republican party election landslide and to Gingrich being elected Speaker of the House in 1995.

name: R. L. Stine
about: R.L. Stine is best known for creating the Goosebumps and Fear Street series, which have sold hundreds of millions of copies worldwide. Goosebumps is the world's best-selling children's series and has sold over 400 million copies in 24 languages.

name: Brian Mulroney
about: Brian Mulroney was the 18th Prime Minister of Canada, serving from 1984 to 1993. He led the Progressive Conservative Party and is known for implementing major economic reforms and promoting free trade.

name: Herbie Hancock
about: Herbie Hancock is a jazz and jazz-funk fusion, and world music keyboard player and composer. After a childhood schooling in classical piano, he switched to jazz and at age 23, was tapped by   to join his second famous Quintet. In this role, from 1963 to 1968, he served as one of the primary founders of the post-bop jazz sound. Davis also encouraged him to explore electric instruments.

name: Little Eva
about:
Eva Narcissus Boyd, better known as Little Eva, was an American singer best known for her 1962 hit song "The Loco-Motion."  
 
Her career started with working as a babysitter for songwriters   and Gerry Goffin; and it was this pair that would write her hit song.

name: Jim Morrison
about: Poet and singer-songwriter best known as the lead singer of the Los Angeles rock band "The Doors".

name: Bill Wyman
about: Bill Wyman is a British musician best known as the former bass guitarist of  . He also formed Bill Wyman's Rhythm Kings and has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

name: Jean Shrimpton
homePlace: High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire, England, United Kingdom
about: Often called the world's first supermodel, Jean Shrimpton was alongside Twiggy one of the most prominent faces of 1960s swinging Britain. She marked a change from more aristocratic voluptuous models to a younger, hipper look.

name: Christopher Lloyd
about: Christopher Lloyd is an American actor who came to fame with his portrayal of Dr. Emmett "Doc" Brown in the Back to the Future trilogy and his Emmy-winning role as Jim Ignatowski in the television series Taxi.

name: Amartya Sen
about: Amartya Sen is an Indian economist known for his work on humanitarian topics including welfare economics, the causes of famine and poverty, social justice, and measures of well-being.

name: Colin Powell
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Colin Powell was a United States Army general who went on to become the first African American Secretary of State. He held this office under President   from 2001 to 2005. Powell was known for his moderate stance on foreign policy, his emphasis on the diplomatic model he dubbed "Powell Doctrine," and his compelling personal story.

name: Charles Schwab
about: Charles R. Schwab is known for having founded the Charles Schwab Corporation, a major financial services company. He changed how many Americans invest by making stock trading more accessible to the general public.

name: Dustin Hoffman
about: Dustin Hoffman rose to prominence in the late 1960s and has since become one of the most acclaimed actors of his generation, winning two Academy Awards for Best Actor.

name: Tom Fogerty
about: Tom Fogerty is best known as the rhythm guitarist in the popular rock band   Revival. The rock band achieved wide success 1968-72, releasing such singles as "Proud Mary", "Good Golly Miss Molly" and "Bad Moon Rising".

name: Paul Simon
about: Paul Simon is an American musician, best known for his partnership with Art Garfunkel under the name of Simon & Garfunkel. The pair released several hit album, with a number of massive singles including "The Sound of Silence" (1964) and "Mrs. Robinson" (1968).

name: Shirley MacLaine
about: American film, television and theater actress, singer, dancer, activist and author. Nominated for an Academy Award five times before winning the Academy Award for Best Actress in 1983 for her role as Aurora Greenway in "Terms of Endearment".

name: Jimi Hendrix
about:
Influential electric rock guitarist, Hendrix moved to England in 1966 and formed The Jimi Hendrix Experience releasing tracks 'Hey Joe' and Purple Haze'.  
 
His performance at the  Monterey Pop Festival established him in the US and he is especially known for playing at Woodstock where he played the 'Star Spangled Banner'.

name: Manuel Noriega
about: Manuel Noriega came to prominence in the Panama National Guard under Omar Torrijos. When Torrijos died in a plane crash Noriega emerged as head of the National Guard, appointing himself General.

name: Bob Woodward
about: Bob Woodward rose to prominence as an investigative journalist working alongside  , on the Watergate Scandal that would lead to President  's resignation. Working for "The Washington Post" under editor   Woodward was famous for his use of anonymous sources, the most famous of all he called "Deep Throat".

name: Robert Redford
about: American actor, film director, and founder of the Sundance Film Festival. He received two Academy Awards: one in 1981 for directing "Ordinary People", and one for Lifetime Achievement in 2002.

name: Jesse Jackson
about: Jesse Jackson is an American civil rights activist, politician, ordained Baptist minister, and protégé of   Jackson is regarded as one of the most influential African-American activists of the 20th and 21st centuries.

name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
about: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, better known simply as Lula, is a Brazilian politician who returned to office for a second term as President of Brazil after defeating  . Lula is renowned as a staunch left-wing politician and member of the Workers' Party, of which he was president from 2003 to 2010.

name: Che Guevara
about: Argentine born revolutionary who became a prominent figure in the Cuban revolution and later a guerilla leader in South America. Lives on as a symbol of left-wing revolution, capsulated in the 1960 photo of his by Alberto Korda that have been called the most reproduced photographic image ever.

name: Muhammad Yunus
about: Muhammad Yunus is best known for pioneering the practice of microfinance and the concept of social business. He founded Grameen Bank, which provides small loans to poor people without collateral, and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

name: Aung San Suu Kyi
about: Burmese opposition politician and chairperson of the National League for Democracy (NLD) in Burma.

name: Judith Sheindlin
about: Judith Sheindlin, better known as Judge Judy, is an American television personality, former New York family court judge, and author. She is famous for her long-running courtroom television series "Judge Judy" (1996-2021), which made her a pop culture icon and the longest-serving television arbitrator in courtroom programming history.

name: Andreas Baader
about: Baader was a leader of the Red Army Faction, also known as the Baader-Meinhof Group, a West German left-wing militia.

name: Amancio Ortega
about: Amancio Ortega is a Spanish billionaire businessman who is best known as the founder of the Inditex fashion group, which includes the wildly popular Zara clothing and accessories chain. He began his career as a delivery boy for a local shirtmaker, eventually working his way up in the textile industry.

name: Dudley Moore
about: Most famous for his partnership with Peter Cook - Pete & Dud.

name: William Shatner
about: A cultural icon for his portrayal of Captain James   Kirk, captain of the Federation Starship USS Enterprise in the 1960s TV series 'Star Trek' and subsequent movies.

name: Janis Joplin
about:
Rose to fame in the late 1960s as the lead singer of the psychedelic-acid rock band Big Brother and the Holding Company. 
 
Later Joplin performed as a solo artist with her own backing groups, The Kozmic Blues Band and The Full Tilt Boogie Band.  
 
She was also one of the major attractions at the Woodstock festival.

name: Li Ka-shing
about: Li Ka-shing is a Hong Kong business magnate, investor, and philanthropist. Born in Chaozhou, Guangdong, China in 1928, he moved to Hong Kong in 1940. He had to leave school after his father's death at age 15 and went to work at a plastics company, and the manufacturing of plastic flowers would be his breakthrough into business.

name: Ali Hosseini Khamenei
about: Ali Hosseini Khamenei is the current Supreme Leader of Iran, holding the position since 1989 following the death of his predecessor,  . Khamenei's role as Supreme Leader, a position of paramount importance in Iran's mixed theocratic and republican order, has seen him exert influence over every major area of Iranian politics and society.

name: Alice Walker
about: Alice walker is a best-selling American poet and novelist. Her most famous work is the critically acclaimed novel "The Color Purple", which won the National Book Award and the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. It was later turned into an Oscar nominated film directed by   starring  .

name: Giorgio Armani
about:
Italian fashion designer, famous for his menswear and known for his clean, tailored lines.  
 
Giorgio Armani formed his namesake company, Armani, in 1975, and by 2001 was acclaimed as the most successful designer to come out of Italy.

name: Ernő Rubik
about: Ernő Rubik is a Hungarian professor of architecture and inventor, best known for creating the Rubik's Cube. This three-dimensional combination puzzle was invented in 1974 and has since become one of the best-selling puzzles in the world. Rubik initially designed the Cube as a teaching tool to help explain three-dimensional geometry, but the challenge quickly captivated a much broader audience.

name: Anthony Kennedy
about: Anthony Kennedy is a retired Associate Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court who served from 1988 to 2018. He was nominated to the court by President   and was thereafter often considered the swing vote on many important 5-4 decisions during his tenure.

name: Michael Douglas
about: The eldest of actor  ' four sons. Has won four Golden Globes, including the   Award, and two Academy Awards, including Best Actor in 1987 for his role as Gordon Gekko in "Wall Street".

name: Elie Wiesel
about: Elie Wiesel was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1986 as the world's leading spokesperson on the Holocaust. As a teenager Wiesel was a survivor of the   and Buchenwald Nazi concentration camps during WWII.

name: Johnny Cash
about: During Johnny Cash's long and influential music career he was mainly known as a country music artist but his work also encompassed other styles including gospel, rockabilly and blues.  Raised by poor cotton farmers during the depression, themes of their struggles were often incorporated into his work.

name: Gladys Knight
about: Gladys Knight is an American singer-songwriter and actress, often referred to as the "Empress of Soul." She gained fame as the lead vocalist of Gladys Knight & the Pips, a soul and R&B group.

name: Brigitte Bardot
about:
Known simply as "B.B.", Bardot was one of the best-known sex symbols of the 1950s and 1960s. She first achieved fame in the 1957 film And God Created Woman.  
 
Before she retired in 1973, Bardot appeared in the 1963 film Le Mépris and in the 1965 film Viva Maria!.

name: Calvin Klein
about: Calvin Klein revolutionized the clothing industry with his minimalist designs and provocative marketing. He founded his company in 1968 and quickly rose to prominence in the fashion world.

name: Muhammad Ali
about: Muhammad Ali was a legendary boxer and civil rights activist, known as "The Greatest," who famously described his boxing style as "float like a butterfly, sting like a bee." He became the world heavyweight champion three times and was known for his quick wit and charismatic personality.

name: John Lennon
about: Founding member of The Beatles, Lennon formed a songwriting partnership with   that became one of the most successful and famous in the history of music. Born in Liverpool, Lennon was in the group the Quarrymen which eventually developed into the Beatles in 1960.

name: Pete Best
about: Best was the drummer for the Beatles from 1960 to 1962, when he was hired immediately prior to the group's two-year residency in Hamburg, Germany. When the band returned to Liverpool, the band's manager   fired him under orders from  ,   and  , and   was eventually asked to join the group.

name: Michael Caine
about: Michael Caine is known for his distinctive Cockney accent and long-standing career in film. He has won two Academy Awards and starred in over 160 films.

name: Martha Stewart
about: The founder of Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia, Stewart has become one of America's best-known television personalities and businesswomen with a focus on domestic arts and cooking.

name: Barry Manilow
about: Barry Manilow is a renowned American singer and songwriter that has had 51 Top 40 singles, including 13 number ones. Some of his hit songs include 'Could It Be Magic' (1973), 'Can't Smile Without You' (1978), and 'Copacabana' (1978).

name: Martin Scorsese
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Martin Scorsese is an influential film director, screenwriter and producer, part of the "new Hollywood" group of filmmakers that include  ,   and  .

name: Ira Levin
about: Ira Levin was an American novelist, playwright, and songwriter whose most notable works include the novels Rosemary's Baby (1967), The Stepford Wives (1972), and The Boys from Brazil (1976), as well as the record-breaking play Deathtrap (1978).

name: Bernie Sanders
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: The longest-serving independent Senator in Congressional history and a Democratic candidate for President of the United States in the 2016 Democratic primary.

name: James Meredith
about: James Meredith is an American civil rights activist, writer, and Air Force veteran. He is most notably recognized for his role in the desegregation of the University of Mississippi, also known as "Ole Miss," in 1962, a pivotal moment in the American civil rights movement.

name: Micky Dolenz
about: Micky Dolenz is an American actor and musician, best known as drummer and vocalist for the Monkees. He also starred in the television series The Monkees (1966-1968) which was the original inspiration for the band.

name: Joan Collins
about: Joan Collins' long career as an actress began at 17 after training at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in the UK. Hollywood Studio 20th Century Fox put her under contract in 1953 and she appeared in films that included "Virgin Queen" (1955) with   and the historical epic "Land of the Pharaohs" directed by Howard Hawks.

name: Van Morrison
about: Van Morrison is a Northern Irish singer-songwriter and musician, widely recognized as an iconic figure in rock and folk music, particularly for his solo career. He first gained international fame as the lead singer of the rock band Them, with hits like "Gloria" (1964) and "Here Comes the Night" (1965).

name: Isabel Allende
about: Dubbed "the world's most widely read Spanish-language author," Allende is best known for such commercially successful novels as "The House of the Spirits" (La casa de los espíritus, 1982) and "City of the Beasts" (La ciudad de las bestias, 2002).

name: Steve Martin
about:
In the 1970s, Martin became a hit stand-up comic, performing his offbeat, absurdist comedy routines before packed houses on national tours.  
 
Since the 1980s, he has had a successful acting career, starring in the box office hits "Roxanne", "Father of the Bride" and "The Pink Panther".

name: Gary Glitter
about:
The English glam rocker came to fame in the 1970s releasing such tracks as "Rock and Roll".  
 
In 1999 he was convicted on child pornography charges. In 2015 he was further convicted of rape and indecent assault and sentenced to 16 years in prison.

name: Bobby Seale
about: A political and civil rights activist best known for founding   Party with Huey Newton. The party was initially tasked with monitoring and responding to police brutality in Black communities within California before spreading to cities across the United States.

name: Stephen E. Ambrose
about:
The author of many popular books about American history and the writer of several notable biographies, Ambrose published Band of Brothers, which was adapted into the immensely popular 2001 miniseries created by   and  . 
 
Later in his life he was accused of plagiarism in several of his works, but he remains a highly regarded historian.

name: Joseph Stiglitz
about: Joseph Steiglitz won the 2001 Nobel Prize in Economics. He and few economists George A. Akerlof and A.   showed that asymmetric information can provide the key to understanding many observed market phenomena, including unemployment and credit rationing.

name: Pete Rose
about: Nicknamed "Charlie Hustle", he was the all-time Major League leader in hits (4,256), games played (3,562), at-bats (14,053), singles (3,215), and outs (10,328). He appeared in 17 All-Star games, won three World Series rings, three batting titles, and one Most Valuable Player Award, His playing career lasted from 1963-86, and he was a team manager from 1984-89.

name: Richard Chamberlain
about: Richard Chamberlain was an American actor who first gained fame for his role as Dr. Kildare in the eponymous 1960s television series. He was also the first actor to play the character of Jason Bourne, the role later played to great acclaim by  , in the 1988 television film "The Bourne Identity".
