name: Tenzin Gyatso
about:
Spiritual leader of Tibetans. 
 
During the 1959 Tibetan uprising, the Dalai Lama fled Tibet for India, where he currently lives as a refugee.  
 
He has since traveled the world, advocating for the welfare of Tibetans and teaching Tibetan Buddhism. 
 
He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989.

name: Margaret Atwood
about: Margaret Atwood is best known for her work as a novelist and her fifteen books of poetry. She has won both the   Award and Prince of Asturias Award for Literature, and has been shortlisted for the Booker Prize five times, winning in 2000 for "The Blind Assassin".

name: John Cleese
about: John Cleese is a British comedian and one of the 6 member of the influential comedy group Monty Python. As part of Monty Python he appeared in TV sketch shows and such movies as "Life of Brian".

name: Cliff Richard
about: Cliff Richard has sold over 250 million records worldwide and achieved 14 UK No. 1 singles across five consecutive decades.

name: Nicolas Hayek
about: Nicolas Hayek co-founded and leading The Swatch Group, which makes watches. Hayek helped save the Swiss watch industry in the 1980s.

name: Fats Domino
about: Fats Domino was an American pianist and singer-songwriter, known for pioneering rhythm and blues and rock and roll music. He achieved widespread fame with hits like Ain't That a Shame, Blueberry Hill, and I'm Walkin'.

name: Goldie Hawn
about: The American actress is famous for her effervescent portrayal of often kooky characters on film. Her most famous role is as Judy Benjamin in 1980s "Private Benjamin, which she also produced and for which she received an Oscar nomination for Best Actress.

name: Elvis Costello
about: The son of jazz trumpeter and pop singer Ross McManus, Elvis   burst onto the music scene in 1977 with his album "My Aim Is True". Since then he has proven to be a prolific and versatile songwriter and performer. Among the more than thirty albums he has released, there are collaborations with his bands The Attractions, and The Imposters; New Orleans icon  ; pop legends  ,  , and  ; country artists George Jones, and Lucinda Williams; hip-hop group The Roots; operatic soprano Anne Sofie von Otter, classical ensemble The Brodsky Quartet; and jazz figures  ,  , and Bill Frisell.

name: Melinda Gates
about: Gates is a computer scientist, philanthropist and co-chair of the   Foundation, which she co-founded with her then husband  .

name: David Gilmour
about:
David Gilmour has been a member of the British progressive rock band   since 1968, one of the world's most successful bands. 
 
The band has sold over 250 million records worldwide, including their influential conceptual albums "Dark Side of the Moon" (1973) and "The Wall" (1979). 
 
Gilmour has also had a successful solo career as a musician and as a producer.

name: Ray Mancini
about: Ray "Boom Boom" Mancini was an American professional boxer known for becoming the WBA lightweight champion and the dramatic events surrounding one of his title defenses. He was inspired by his father, Lenny Mancini, to reach the boxing heights that the latter could not achieve due to World War II injuries.

name: Tom Cruise
about:
Started his career at age 19 in the 1981 film "Endless Love", and became a full-fledged movie star after starring as Pete "Maverick" Mitchell in "Top Gun". He is well known for his role as secret agent Ethan Hunt in the "Mission: Impossible" film series.  
 
He is also known for his support for the Church of Scientology and its affiliated social programs.

name: Phil McGraw
about: Phil McGraw came to fame after a series of appearances on The   Show from 1998. He had previously helped Oprah Winfrey win a court case through his legal consulting firm Courtroom Sciences, Inc. (CSI). The TV show "Bull" starring Michael Weatherly is based on McGraw's own history as a trial consultant.

name: Youssou N'dour
about: The most popular singer in Senegal, N'dour helped develop the Mbalax sound - popular dance music fusing traditional Senegalese songs with Latin rhythms.

name: Michael Biehn
about: As an actor Michael Biehn has specialized in military characters. His most famous roles include Sergeant Kyle Reese in "The Terminator" (1984) and as Corporal Dwayne Hicks in "Aliens" (1986) both directed by  .

name: Dan Aykroyd
about: Comedian Dan Aykroyd was an original cast member and writer for the influential late-night comedy show "Saturday Night Live" (1975-79) alongside Chevy Chase,   and his close friend  .  On the program he was noted for is impersonations of US Presidents   and  , and TV hosts   and Julia Child. He also created the characters of Beldar Conehead and Yortuk Festrunk.

name: John McEnroe
about:
Former World No. 1 professional tennis player from the United States.  
 
McEnroe won seven Grand Slam singles titles (three at Wimbledon and four at the US Open), nine Grand Slam men's doubles titles, and one Grand Slam mixed doubles title.  
 
He also won a record eight season ending championships.

name: John Travolta
about:
Travolta shot to international stardom in the 1970s with iconic roles in Saturday Night Fever (1977), which precipitated the disco phenomenon on both sides of the Atlantic, and Grease (1978). 
 
Though his career declined throughout the 1980s, he experienced a resurgence in the 1990s with films like   (1994) and later films such as Wild Hogs (2007) and Hairspray (2007).

name: Courtney Love
about: Courtney Love is known for her role in the grunge music scene of the 1990s and her turbulent personal life. She founded the rock band Hole and gained fame for her emotional performances and songwriting.

name: Magic Johnson
about: Magic Johnson was became one of the most influential figures in basketball history. He is known for his exceptional skills on the court as well as his successful business ventures.

name: Mike Myers
about: The Canadian actor rose to fame on Saturday Night Live, appearing from 1989 to 1995.  He became known for his comic characters especially Wayne Campbell. He went on to make that character the basis of his film "Wayne's World" in 1992, with Saturday Night Live co-star Dana Carey playing his best friend Gareth. The film had a successful sequel in 1993.

name: Russell Crowe
about: Came to international attention for his role as the Roman General Maximus Decimus Meridius in the 2000 historical epic film "Gladiator", directed by  , for which Crowe won an Academy Award for Best Actor. His portrayal of mathematician and Nobel Prize winner John F. Nash in the biopic " " also brought him numerous awards.

name: Diana Spencer
about: Diana was the wife of   from 1981 until their divorce in 1996. Their relationship and eventual break-up drew enormous media scrutiny from around the globe. The object of worldwide press attention during and after her marriage, Diana became a media sensation.

name: Dave Stewart
about:
One half of  , in partnership with  . The pair achieved global fame with their second studio album "Sweet Dreams (Are Made of These)" in 1983 with the title single topping the US Billboard Top 100 chart.  
 
In 1987 they won a Grammy award for Best Rock performance by a Duo or Group for their single "Missionary man"

name: Tim Walz
about: Tim Walz is the Governor of Minnesota and the 2024 Democratic vice presidential nominee. He has a background in education, military service, and politics.

name: Whitney Houston
about: One of the most awarded and the best-selling female music artist ever. Houston first came to prominence as a teen model and moved into music full time after she signed a record contract in 1983.

name: Lenny Kravitz
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Known for his elaborate stage performances and music videos.  
 
Kravitz won the Grammy Award for Best Male Rock Vocal Performance four years in a row from 1999 to 2002, breaking the record for most wins in that category as well as setting the record for most consecutive wins in one category by a male.

name: Jeff Bezos
about: Jeffrey Preston Bezos is an American entrepreneur, media proprietor, and investor, best known for founding Amazon, the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company. As of November 2023, with a net worth of approximately $170 billion, Bezos is the third-wealthiest person globally.

name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
about: Erdoğan is the current President of Turkey, having previously served as Prime Minister from 2003 to 2014 and Mayor of Istanbul from 1994 to 1998. He is also the founder of the Justice and Development Party (AKP), which he led from its origin in 2001 until his election as President in 2014.

name: Tilda Swinton
about: Tilda Swinton is a British actress known for her unique style and versatility. She has appeared in both independent and mainstream films, earning critical acclaim and winning an Academy Award for her performance in “Michael Clayton” (2007).

name: Boris Johnson
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Mayor of London between 2008 and 2016, and as well known for his scruffy hairstyle as for his many controversies. Johnson's unique style and active contributions to journalism throughout his tenure as a politician have made him one of the most well-known and visible political figures in modern Britain.

name: Tom Hanks
about: One of the most successful actors of all time. Known for his roles in "Big", "Philadelphia", "Forrest Gump", "Apollo 13", " ", "You've Got Mail", "The Green Mile", "Cast Away", "The Da Vinci Code", "Captain Phillips", and the " " series.

name: Richard Gere
about:
Came to prominence in 1980 for his role in the film "American Gigolo", which established him as a leading man and a Hollywood heartthrob. 
 
Gere went on to star in several hit films, including "An Officer and a Gentleman", "Pretty Woman", "Primal Fear", "Arbitrage", and "Chicago", for which he won a Golden Globe Award as Best Actor.

name: Trisha Yearwood
about: Trisha Yearwood is one of the most successful female country artists of all time. She has sold over 15 million records and has won three Grammy Awards. She is also a successful author and television personality.

name: Elisabeth Shue
about: In the 1980s Shue became a starring actress in such films as "The Karate Kid" (1984) and "Cocktail" (1988) with  . Roles in the blockbuster Back to the Future Part II and III followed.

name: Marla Maples
about: Marla Maples is best known for her high-profile marriage to  . She also had a varied career in entertainment, appearing in films and television shows, as well as on Broadway.

name: Billy Ray Cyrus
about: Although Billy Ray Cyrus has released 16 albums throughout his county music career his debut album "Some Gave All" (1992) remains his most well known. It sold over 20 million copies and included the hit single "Achy Breaky Heart", which went on to become the most successful cross-over hit since   and  's "Islands in the Stream" in 1983.

name: Richard Branson
about: Best known as the founder of the Virgin Group, English entrepreneur Richard Branson has an estimated worth of $5.2 billion (Forbes 2016).

name: Seal
about: Known for his numerous international hits, including "Kiss from a Rose", which appeared on the soundtrack to the 1995 film "Batman Forever".

name: David Hasselhoff
about: Nicknamed "The Hoff", David Hasselhoff is best known for his lead roles as Michael Knight in the popular 1980s US series "Knight Rider" and as L.A. County Lifeguard Mitch Buchannon in the TV series "Baywatch" opposite  .

name: Sheikh Hasina
homePlace: Tungipara, Gopalganj, East Bengal, Pakistan (now Bangladesh)
about: Sheikh Hasina Wazed is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh, having served since January 2009 and before that from June 1996 to July 2001. As the daughter of  , the nation's founding father, Sheikh Hasina's leadership has been influential in shaping modern Bangladesh.

name: Ted Bundy
about:
One of the most infamous serial killers in American history. 
 
He assaulted and murdered numerous young women and girls during the 1970s.  
 
Shortly before his execution, he confessed to 30 homicides committed in seven states between 1974 and 1978.

name: Bill Nye
about: America's most famous science presenter, Bill Nye presented and starred in "Bill; Nye the Science Guy from 1993 to 1999. Afterwards his work has continued with a number of specials and presentations.

name: Mitt Romney
about:
Politician and businessman who was the Republican Party's nominee for President of the United States in the 2012 election.  
 
He was also the 70th Governor of Massachusetts from 2003 to 2007.

name: Michael J. Fox
about:
Famous roles have included Marty McFly from the "Back to the Future" trilogy (1985–1990); Alex P. Keaton from "Family Ties" (1982–1989), for which he won three Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe Award; and Mike Flaherty in "Spin City" (1996–2001), for which he won an Emmy, three Golden Globes, and two Screen Actors Guild Awards. 
 
Diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 1991, he has since become an advocate for research toward finding a cure.

name: Iggy Pop
about: The Stooges vocalist and solo artist known for his stage performances.

name: Ingrid Kristiansen
about: The only person to ever simultaneously hold the world records in the 5000 meters, 10,000 meters and the marathon.

name: Michelle Yeoh
about: Of Malaysian and Chinese descent, Michelle Yeoh started her film career in Hong Kong action and martial arts films, often doing her own stunts. In 1992 she starred alongside   in  "Police Story 3: Super Cop" and in 1993 in "Tai Chi Master" with Jet Li.

name: Randy Travis
about: Randy Travis has recorded twenty studio albums and placed more than forty singles on the Billboard country music charts, including nineteen Number One hits. His songs include the hits "Forever and Ever, Amen," "I Told You So," "Diggin' Up Bones," and "Three Wooden Crosses".

name: Tony Blair
about: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1997 to 2007 and the Leader of the Labour Party from 1994 to 2007.

name: Kathleen Kennedy
about:
Kennedy, now president of   Inc, is known for her many collaborations with director  . With her husband Frank Marshall and   she cofounded Amblin Entertainment, Inc. 
 
In this role she has produced landmark films such as E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982) and the first two   films.

name: David Letterman
about:
Host of late night television talk shows for 33 years including the long running shows "Late Show with David Letterman" first on NBC and then CBS. 
 
He is the longest-serving late-night talk show host in TV history.

name: Joe Montana
about: After winning a college national championship at Notre Dame, he started his NFL career in 1979 with San Francisco, where he played for the next 14 seasons and won four Super Bowls and three Super Bowl Most Valuable Player awards, the only player to have been named Super Bowl MVP three times.

name: Richard Dreyfuss
about: American Graffiti, The Goodbye Girl and Mr. Holland's Opus.

name: Teller
about: Teller is one half of the magician act Penn and Teller, who along with fellow illusionist   has been performing  since 1975. Teller, formally a teacher is known for not speaking during their act, except on rare occasions.

name: Pierce Brosnan
about: Rose to popularity in the television series "Remington Steele" (1982–87). Also appeared in films such as "The Fourth Protocol" and "Mrs. Doubtfire".

name: Kathy Hochul
about: Became the first female governor of New York upon the resignation of   in 2021. She then became the first elected female governor of New York in 2022.

name: Michelle Pfeiffer
about: Scarface, Batman Returns, Hairspray

name: Christopher Dean
about: Christopher Dean is best known for his partnership with  , with whom he won a gold medal at the 1984 Winter Olympics.

name: Hugh Grant
about: Hugh Grant's first leading film role was in "Maurice" (1987) based on the E.M. Forster novel, for which he won Best Actor at the Venice Film Festival. However it was the 1994 romantic comedy "Four Weddings and a Funeral" that propelled Grant to international fame. The film, written by Richard Curtis, was made cheaply but became a worldwide hit.

name: Homer Simpson
about: Homer Simpson is a fictional character and the main protagonist of the long-running animated television series  . Created by cartoonist  , Homer has become one of the most iconic and recognizable characters in popular culture, known for his lovable yet flawed nature.

name: Julianne Moore
about:
Prolific in cinema since the early 1990s, Moore is particularly known for her portrayals of emotionally troubled women.  
 
Moore has also starred in a number of Hollywood blockbusters including "Nine Months" (1995) and "The Lost World:  " (1997) establishing herself as a leading Hollywood actress. 
 
Moore won the Oscar for Best Actress for her role in "Still Alice", after 4 previous nominations.

name: Madonna
about: Madonna is a pop music icon and cultural figure, known as the "Queen of Pop," who has sold over 300 million records worldwide. She is further known for her many reinventions and boundary-pushing works.

name: Gerry Adams
about: Gerry Adams is an Irish republican politician who played a key role in the modern history of Northern Ireland. He is best known for his leadership of Sinn Féin, a political party associated with the Irish Republican Army (IRA) and its campaign to end British rule in Northern Ireland and reunify Ireland.

name: Linda Hamilton
about: Linda Hamilton's most famous role is that of Sarah Connor in the first two Terminator film series opposite   and directed by   and to whom she was married to for two years.

name: Drew Carey
about:
Drew Carey first made a name for himself as a stand-up comedian in the 1980s.  
 
He is most famous though for starring in his own sitcom, "The Drew Carey Show," and serving as host of the U.S. version of the improv comedy show "Whose Line Is It Anyway?", both of which aired on ABC.

name: Steve Jones
about: Guitarist and songwriter for the punk-rock band  . After the band split up in 1978 Jones went on to perform in two other short-lived bands, The Professionals and  Chequered Past.

name: Jon Stewart
about: Stewart was the longtime host of The Daily Show from 1999 to 2016 before he gave up the reigns to  . Under his tenure the satirical news show gained consistent critical acclaim and commercial success as well as numerous Emmy Awards.

name: Stephen Colbert
about: Colbert rose to fame began as a correspondent on The Daily Show, before he was given his own role hosting a satirical news show with The Colbert Report from 2005 to 2014, where he played a character that satirized conservative media pundits. His success in this role led to an appearance at the 2006 White House Correspondents Dinner which was highly controversial for its searing routine targeting President  , sitting a few feet away, and the media.

name: Camilla Parker Bowles
about: Camilla Parker Bowles is best known as the wife of  , the current King of the United Kingdom and the other Commonwealth realms, who ascended to the throne in 2022 following the death of his mother,  .

name: Spike Lee
about: American film director whose production company, 40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks, has produced over 35 films since 1983. His movies have examined race relations, colourism in the black community, the role of media in contemporary life, urban crime and poverty, and other political issues.

name: Kirk Hammett
about:
An American musician, Kirk Hammett is best known as the lead guitarist for the heavy metal band  .  
 
He has been ranked as one of the best guitarists of all time by Rolling Stone magazine and in author Joel McIver's "The 100 Greatest Metal Guitarists."

name: David Lee Roth
about:
Best known as the original (1974–1985) and current (2006–present) lead singer of the Southern California-based hard rock band  .  
 
Also known as a successful solo artist, releasing numerous RIAA-certified Gold and Platinum records.

name: Rigoberta Menchú
about: Rigoberta Menchú is a K'iche' Indigenous woman from Guatemala who gained international prominence as a human rights activist. She rose to prominence in the early 1980s when she began speaking out about the injustices faced by her community during the Guatemalan Civil War, which lasted from 1960 to 1996.

name: Sheryl Crow
about:
Versatile singer whose music incorporates elements of pop, rock, and country. She has released eight studio albums and has sold more than 17 million albums in the U.S. and over 50 million albums worldwide.  
 
She has also won nine Grammy Awards, and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2023.

name: Conan O'Brien
about: Conan O'Brien is an American comedian and television host, best known for his series of late night television shows: Late Night with Conan O'Brien (1993-2009), The Tonight Show with Conan O'Brien (2009-2010), and Conan (2010-2021).

name: John Mellencamp
about: John Mellencamp has sold over 60 million records worldwide, and penned the hits "Pink Houses"; "Jack and Diane", and "Small Town".

name: Sigourney Weaver
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Sigourney Weaver is known as the Sci-fi Queen, especially as the lead role of Ellen Ripley in the four "Alien" films and her role as Dana Barrett in " " and "Ghostbusters II".

name: Mick Fleetwood
about: Mick Fleetwood is a British musician, best known as the drummer and co-founder of  . The group's name comes from a combination of Fleetwood's name with that of bassist John "Mac" McVie.

name: George Clooney
about:
After gaining wide recognition in his role as Dr. Doug Ross on the long-running medical drama "ER", he has starred in numerous critically acclaimed films and received three Golden Globe Awards for his work as an actor and two Academy Awards, one for acting and the other for producing. 
 
He is the only person ever to be nominated for Academy Awards in six categories.

name: Fumio Kishida
about: Kishida was born into a family of politicians in Okayama Prefecture in 1955. He graduated from the University of Tokyo in 1978 with a degree in law. Kishida began his career as a bureaucrat in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

name: Andy Gibb
about: Andy Gibb was an English-Australian singer and actor, best known as younger brother to the  :  ,  , and  .

name: Idriss Déby
homePlace: Berdoba, Northern Chad, French Equatorial Africa
about: Overthrew the regime of Hassène Habre and replaced him as president of the country for more than 20 years.

name: Benjamin Netanyahu
about: The first Israeli prime minister born in Israel after the establishment of the state, he has been elected Prime Minister four times and is the only Prime Minister in Israel's history to have been elected three times in a row.

name: Annie Leibovitz
about: Annie Leibovitz known for her portraits of celebrities. Her most well-known work is a photo of   and   taken on the day Lennon was killed, which was used on the cover of Rolling Stone magazine.

name: Chesley Sullenberger
about: Chesley Sullenberger, known as "Sully," is an American retired airline captain who became a national hero in the United States after successfully carrying out an emergency water landing of US Airways Flight 1549 on the Hudson River in 2009. His quick thinking and calm under pressure saved all 155 passengers on board and led to widespread recognition for his expertise and heroism.

name: RuPaul
about: Known as the "Queen of Drag," RuPaul is a global icon who transformed the art of drag into a worldwide phenomenon. He has had a successful career as a model, recording artist, actor and TV host. His TV show "RuPaul's Drag Race" premiered in 2009, winning 27 Emmy awards over 16 years.

name: Agnetha Fältskog
about: Agnetha is most widely known as member of internationally successful Swedish pop band ABBA (she's the blonde one!).

name: Brian May
about: Brian May is an English musician best known as the lead guitarist for Queen, alongside   and Roger Taylor. The band came to international fame with their album A Night at the Opera (1975), and particularly its hit single "Bohemian Rhapsody."

name: Diego Maradona
about: One of the most famous, talented and controversial football players in history, Maradona was join FIFA Player of the Century with Brazilian footballer Pelé. During his club career he played for Argentinos Juniors, Boca Juniors, Barcelona, Napoli, Sevilla and Newell's Old Boys.

name: José Carreras
about: José Carreras is known for his tenor singing voice and his work as part of the Three Tenors. He has also been recognized for his efforts in leukemia research and treatment.

name: Sharon Osbourne
about:
Came to public prominence after appearing in "The Osbournes", a reality television show that followed her family's daily life.  
 
Later Osborne became a talent show judge on shows such as the British and original version of "The X Factor", from 2004 to 2007; before returning in 2013, and "America's Got Talent" from 2007 to 2012.

name: Jorge Ramos
about: Jorge Ramos is a Mexican-American journalist and author. He is the anchor for the Univision news television program "Noticiero Univision" and the Fusion TV program "América con Jorge Ramos".

name: Meg Ryan
about: Prolific film actress known mostly for her leading roles in romantic comedies of the 1980s and 90s.  After winning some small roles while attending college for journalism, she dropped out of school to take a part in the daytime serial "A the World Turns".

name: Tom Morello
about:
Best known as the guitarist for American rock band "Rage Against the Machine". 
 
Morello went on form the rock group "Audioslave" after Zack de la Rocha's departure from Rage Against the Machine in 2000.

name: Paula Abdul
about:
Began her career as a cheerleader for the Los Angeles Lakers at the age of 18 before rising to prominence in the 1980s as a highly sought-after choreographer at the height of the music video era.  
 
She saw renewed fame and success as an original judge on "American Idol" in the 2000s, which she left after the eighth season.

name: George Thorogood
about: The blues-rock guitarist George Thorogood became successful in the 1980s with his band George Thorogood and the Destroyers. Their debut album was released in 1977 and since then they have released over 20 and sold more than 15 million copies worldwide.

name: Shigeru Miyamoto
about: Shigeru Miyamoto is best known for his work at Nintendo, including Mario, The Legend of Zelda, and Donkey Kong. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in the video game industry.

name: Ed Harris
about: Ed Harris is known for his critically aimly acting career, mostly in film, over the course of which he has received four Academy Award nominations.

name: Garry Kasparov
about: Considered by many to be the greatest chess player of all time, Kasparov was ranked no. 1 for 225 out of 228 months from 1986 until his retirement in 2005. His rating of 2851 was the highest ever recorded until surpassed by   in 2013.

name: Mr. T
about: Mr. T is known for his distinctive mohawk hairstyle, gold chains, and catchphrase "I pity the fool!" He rose to fame in the 1980s through his roles in "Rocky III" (1982) and the television series "The A-Team" (1983-1987).

name: Weird Al Yankovic
about: "Weird Al" Yankovic transformed musical parody into mainstream entertainment through four decades of hit songs and innovative videos. His meticulous approach to parody, always seeking permission from original artists, helped establish new standards for comedy in music while earning him the title of best-selling comedy recording artist.

name: Lionel Richie
about: Starting his music career in the 1970s as a songwriter and the co-lead singer of the R&B band the Commodores ("Easy"; "Three Times a Lady"), he made his solo debut in 1982 with the album "Lionel Richie" and number-one hit "Truly". He co-wrote, with  , the all-star charity single "We Are The World" in 1985. Richie has sold more than 100 million records worldwide, making him one of the best-selling artists of all time.

name: Adam Clayton
about: Adam Clayton is an English-born Irish musician best known as the bass guitarist of the rock band U2. Having won 22 Grammy Awards, Clayton's place in rock history was solidified in 2005 by his induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

name: David Copperfield
about: David Copperfield is an American magician, widely recognized as one of the most commercially successful illusionists in history. His remarkable career spans several decades and is marked by a number of groundbreaking feats and record-breaking performances.

name: Catherine O'Hara
about: Catherine O'Hara is a Canadian-American actress, best known for her comedy work. She started off starring on Second City Television (1976-1984) and then went on to major roles in Beetlejuice (1988) and the first two   films (1990 and 1992) playing the mother of  's character.

name: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot
about: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot is a Kenyan marathon runner, best known for winning the Boston Marathon four times. He also held the record time for the Boston Marathon from 2006, when he broke the record held by Cosmas Ndeti, until 2010, when his record was superseded by Robert Kiprono Cheruiyot.

name: Monica Seles
about: Monica Seles won nine Grand Slam singles titles and was the youngest French Open champion in history.

name: Rachel McAdams
about:
McAdams first came to fame after starring in " " (2004) and "The Notebook" (2005).  
 
She has since gone on to feature in a number of major films including the "Doctor Strange" series, as well as a role in season two of the television series "True Detective".

name: Josh Duhamel
about:
Josh Duhamel is an American actor and model, best known for his television roles as Leu du Pres on the ABC soap opera "All My Children" and on NBC's "Las Vegas" as Danny McCoy.  
 
Subsequently Duhamel has also starred in a number of films, including in the Transformers series such as "Transformers: The Last Knight" (2017).

name: Todd Howard
about: Todd Howard is known for his work on popular game series like The Elder Scrolls and Fallout and for his leadership at Bethesda Game Studios.

name: Olga Kurylenko
about:
Olga was raised by a divorced/single mother in Berdyansk, Ukraine. After a short time in Moscow, she moved to Paris, France as a teen to pursue a career as a fashion model.   
 
Kurylenko later worked in a variety of international films, including "Quantum of Solace" and "Seven Psychopaths".  in 2001, she became a French citizen.

name: Colin Farrell
about: Colin Farrell is an Irish actor known for his versatile and compelling performances over two decades. Early roles in "Tigerland" (2000) and "Minority Report" (2002) were followed by films like "Daredevil" (2003) and "Alexander" (2004).

name: Tiffany Darwish
about: Tiffany Darwish is an American singer and songwriter. Darwish began her career in the early 1980s as a teenage country pop singer.

name: John Romero
about: John Romero co-founded id Software, which created video games series such as Wolfenstein and Doom, helped shape the first-person shooter genre.

name: John Michael McDonagh
about: John Michael McDonagh is an acclaimed Irish-British filmmaker and screenwriter known for his distinct style, blending dark humor and poignant themes in his films.

name: Ellen Pompeo
about: Ellen Pompeo is one of the highest paid actresses on American television, having starred in the hit medical drama "Grey's Anatomy" since 2005.

name: Terrence Howard
about:
Terrence Howard is an American actor who first came to fame in the early 2000s with films such as Crash (2004) and Hustle & Flow (2005). The latter earned him an Academy Award nomination for best actor. 
 
He has also starred in television series such as Empire (2015-2020), as well as having a musical career. Howard released his debut album, Shine Through It, in 2008.

name: Sofía Vergara
about: Colombian-born actress Sofia Vergara rose to fame starring in the American mockumentary "  (2009-2020) opposite Ed O'Neill. She has received critical acclaim for her role, including five nominations for a Golden Globe award and four for an Emmy. In 2019 she was named the highest-paid television actress in the world.

name: Ryan Gosling
about:
After appearing in family entertainment programs, he came to the attention of a wider audience in 2004 with a leading role in the romantic drama "The Notebook".  
 
Other well known roles include "Crazy, Stupid, Love", "Drive", "The Ides of March", and "Gangster Squad".

name: Melanie Brown
about:
Nicknamed "Sporty Spice", Melanie Brown was a member of the phenomenally successful girls group the  .  
 
The Spice Girls sold over 85 million records worldwide and had 9 no. 1 hit singles in the UK.

name: Ronan Keating
about:
Best known as the lead singer of Irish boyband group Boyzone. The band was put together in 1993 by manager Louis Walsh. Boyzone went on to become one of the most successful groups in the UK and Ireland.    
 
After Boyzone broke up in 1999, Keating went on to develop a successful solo career, with his cover of Keith Whitley's song "When You Say Nothing at All", from the soundtrack of the film "Notting Hill", a No. 1 in many countries.

name: David Cameron
about: British Prime Minister from 2010 to 2016 who lead a Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition and after a winning a majority in 2015 a Conservative government. He was known for both his economic and socially liberal policies.

name: Vince Vaughn
about: Best known for comedy films such as Old School, Wedding Crashers and Couple's Retreat.

name: Gerard Butler
about: Gerard Butler is a Scottish actor who gained worldwide recognition for his portrayal of King Leonidas in 300 (2006) and roles in The Phantom of the Opera (2004) and the How to Train Your Dragon series (2010–2019).

name: Brendan Fraser
about:
Versatile screen actor in a variety of film genres. Popular and/or critically acclaimed films include comedy (Encino Man; Monkeybone), adventure (The Mummy trilogy), and drama (Gods and Monsters; The Whale). 
 
His performance in "The Whale" earned him an Academy Award for Best Actor in 2023.

name: Julian Assange
about: Julian Assange is best known for founding WikiLeaks in 2006. He gained worldwide attention in 2010 when WikiLeaks released classified documents provided by Chelsea Manning, a United States Army intelligence analyst.

name: Bashar al-Assad
about:
Rules as the dictator of Syria after taking over from his father,  , in 2000 until his ouster in 2024.  
 
A decade into his reign the Syrian Civil War began as an uprising to topple him from power. More than 350,000 people have been killed since the beginning of the war.

name: Martin Freeman
about: The English actor rose to fame in the original UK version of the mockumentary  "The Office", starring alongside its writer and creator  . He then appeared in a number of films including "Love Actually" (2003) and "Shaun of the Dead" (2004).

name: Queen Latifah
about: She has been considered one of hip-hop's pioneer feminists. Her first album "All Hail to the Queen" (1989) sold more than 1 million copies, and her single U.N.I.T.Y earned her first Grammy Award.

name: Nick Cannon
about: Nick Cannon began his career in music as a rapper before moving into acting, starring in the romantic film "Love Don't Cost a Thing" (2003),

name: Jennifer Love Hewitt
about: Jennifer Love Hewitt is an American actress and singer. She first came to fame as a child actress on the Disney Channel series "Kids Incorporated" (1989-1991), which earned her three Young Artist Award nominations.

name: Eddie George
about: Eddie George is best known for his successful career as a running back in the National Football League (NFL) and for winning the Heisman Trophy in college.

name: Oliver Riedel
about:
Oliver Riedel is a German musician and the bassist for the industrial metal band Rammstein. 
 
Riedel began his musical career in 1990 at the age of 19, playing in a band called Inchtabokatables. In 1994, he joined Till Lindemann, Richard Kruspe, and Christoph Schneider to form Rammstein after winning the Berlin Senate Metro beat contest, with Paul Landers and Christian "Flake" Lorenz later joining the band.

name: Thomas Muster
about: Thomas Muster is an Austrian former professional tennis player. Known for his powerful groundstrokes and incredible determination on the court, he is often considered among the greatest clay-court players in the history of the sport and hence known as "The King of Clay."

name: Jean Dujardin
about: Brice de Nice, OSS 117: Cairo, Nest of Spies, 99 Francs and The Artist.

name: Melissa Mccarthy
about: Melissa McCarthy is an American actress, comedian, writer, producer, and fashion designer. She came to fame with her breakout role in Bridesmaids (2011) and her television work in Gilmore Girls (2000–2007) and Mike & Molly (2010–2016). Her performances have earned her two Academy Award nominations and a Primetime Emmy Award.

name: Amy Adams
about: Adams is an American actress born overseas to a military family, who eventually settled in Colorado. Her career began in dinner theater as a teenager, eventually leading to small film roles.

name: The Notorious B.I.G.
about: Born Christopher Wallace in Bedford-Stuyvesant, New York The Notorious B.I.G. was a pioneering gangsta rapper famous for his rivalry with West Coast rapper   who was shot and killed a mere six months after Tupac himself.

name: David Guetta
about: David Guetta is known for his chart-topping hits and collaborations with major artists, with a lengthy and influential career that has shaped electronic dance music globally. He has had a string of international hits including "When Love Takes Over" and has sold over 10 million albums and 65 million singles worldwide.

name: Sam Rockwell
about: Sam Rockwell is an American actor who won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role in Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri (2017), and was nominated for his portrayal of   in Vice (2018).

name: Brad Paisley
about: Brad Paisley is an American country music singer and songwriter, known for having sold over 11 million albums and won three Grammy Awards. He has also won a large number of other awards: 14 Country Music Association Awards, 14 Academy of Country Music Awards, and 2 American Music Awards.

name: Kate Winslet
about:
The youngest person to acquire six Academy Award nominations, including the 2008 Academy Award for Best Actress which she won for her role in "The Reader".  
 
Winslet is one of the few actresses to have won three of the four major American entertainment awards (EGOT), with her Oscar, Emmy and Grammy wins.

name: Shaquille O'Neal
about:
Won three consecutive NBA championships from 2000-2002 as a member of the Los Angeles Lakers. Won a fourth NBA championship as a member of the Miami Heat in 2006.  
 
Also won the 1999-2000 MVP award and three NBA Finals MVP awards. Ranks 3rd all-time in field goal percentage (58.2%), largely because of his ability to dunk the basketball.

name: DJ Khaled
about: DJ Khaled is an American record producer and rapper. He came to fame as a radio host in the 1990s and then worked as a DJ for the hip hop collective Terror Squad. Subsequently he released his debut album Listennn.... the Album (2006) which went gold and was followed by We the Best (2007).

name: Ben Affleck
about:
First came to attention for his performances in "Dazed and Confused". He later gained recognition as a writer when he won the Academy Award and Golden Globe Award for Best Original Screenplay for "Good Will Hunting", which he co-wrote and starred in alongside childhood friend  .  
 
He directed and starred in "Argo", which won the Academy Award for Best Picture.

name: Zoe Saldaña
about: Known for her role as Anamaria in "Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl" and "Avatar: The Way of Water".

name: Peter Dinklage
about: Born with a common form of achondroplasia, a form of dwarfism, Dinklage is known for his roles in " " (2010-19) as Tyrion Lannister.

name: Owen Wilson
about: Owen Wilson is an American actor, comedian, producer, and screenwriter best known for his frequent collaborations with filmmaker Wes Anderson and for being part of the "Frat Pack" group of comedic actors.

name: Hugh Jackman
about: Best known for his long-running role as Wolverine in the X-Men film series, as well as for his leads in "The Prestige", "Australia", and "Les Misérables", for which he received his first Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.

name: Tim McGraw
about: McGraw first came to fame with his 1994 album 'Not a Moment Too Soon,' which was the top country album of that year. Since then he has had 25 number one country singles, three of which were also the top country songs of the year: 'It's Your Love' (1997), 'Just to See You Smile' (1998), and 'Live Like You Were Dying' (2004).

name: Phil Mickelson
about: Nicknamed "Lefty" for his left-handed swing, he has won 42 events on the PGA Tour including five major championships (the Masters three times, the PGA Championship, and the Open Championship).

name: Todd Beamer
about: Todd Beamer was one of the passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93, which was hijacked as part of the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001. He is known for his heroic actions during the hijacking, which contributed to preventing the plane from reaching its intended target.

name: Toni Braxton
about: Toni Braxton is an American singer, songwriter, pianist, and actress who rose to fame in the early 1990s with her distinctive sultry voice and blend of R&B, pop, and soul music. Her powerful vocals and emotive performances have earned her numerous awards and accolades, and she is considered one of the most successful R&B artists of her generation.

name: Rose McGowan
about: Best known professionally for her role as a witch in the TV series "Charmed," McGowan is an accomplished film and television actress.

name: Louis Theroux
about: Louis Theroux is a documentarian and journalist known for his numerous documentaries with the BBC, such as "Louis Theroux's Weird Weekends," "When Louis Met..." and 50 BBC Two specials. His documentaries follow unusual and often taboo topics of race, religion, crime, and celebrities.

name: Kurt Cobain
about:
Lead singer, guitarist, and primary songwriter of the grunge band Nirvana.  
 
Following the success of the album "Nevermind", Nirvana was labeled "the flagship band" of  , and Cobain hailed as "the spokesman of a generation".

name: Sheryl Sandberg
about: Sheryl Sandberg has been the Chief Operating Officer of social network Facebook since 2008. Prior to this Sandberg worked for Google, becoming its Vice President of Online Sales developing AdSense and AdWords, greatly increasing profitability at the company.

name: Drew Barrymore
about: A descendant of the Barrymore family of well-known American stage and cinema actors, and the granddaughter of film legend  , she first appeared in an advertisement when she was eleven months old, before starring in her breakout role in  's "E.T.".

name: Steffi Graf
about: Graf began her professional tennis career aged 13, coached and managed by her father Peter Graf.

name: James Corden
about: James Corden is an English actor, comedian, and television host. He gained prominence in the UK for co-writing and starring in the BBC sitcom Gavin & Stacey and became widely known in the US as the host of The Late Late Show with James Corden.

name: Matt LeBlanc
about: LeBlanc gained worldwide fame for his role as Joey Tribbiani on the sitcom Friends (1994-2004), which became one of the most popular television shows of all time.

name: Idina Menzel
about:
Rose to prominence when she originated the role of Maureen Johnson in the Broadway musical "Rent", a role which she reprised for the 2005 feature film adaptation of the musical. 
 
Also known for originating the role of Elphaba in the Broadway musical "Wicked", and for providing the voice of Elsa in the Disney film "Frozen".

name: Puff Daddy
about: Sean Combs is best known for founding Bad Boy Records and his successful career in hip-hop. More recently, however, he has been charged with the "creation of a criminal enterprise in which he abused, threatened, and coerced women and others around him."

name: Geri Horner
about:
Geri Horner or Geri Halliwell as she was known before her marriage was a member of the British girls group the  .  
 
The Spice Girls are the most successful girls group ever, and have sold over 85 million records worldwide. While in the Spice Girls Geri was nicknamed "Ginger Spice" in reference to her hair color.

name: Mike Dirnt
about: Mike Dirnt is an American musician, known as co-founder and bassist for the band Green Day. He met fellow founder   in middle school, and the two fast friends began to make music together from an early age.

name: Matt Damon
about: Rose to fame following the success of the drama film "Good Will Hunting" (1997) from a screenplay he co-wrote with friend and actor  . The pair won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay and the Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay for their work.

name: Audra McDonald
about:
Best known for her work on the stage, such as in "Ragtime", "A Raisin in the Sun", and "Porgy and Bess".  
 
She has won six Tony Awards and is the only person to have won a Tony in each of the four acting categories.

name: Gordon Ramsay
about: The Scottish-born chef is as famous for his angry, expletive TV persona as he is for his high class award-winning restaurants.

name: Mark Wahlberg
about: Frontman of the band Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch.

name: Taika Waititi
about: Taika Waititi's successful film career has spanned short films, indie films and taken him all the way to direct the Marvel superhero epic "Thor: Ragnarok" (2019) with  , which Waititi also acted in.

name: Scottie Pippen
about: Scottie Pippen is regarded as one of the greatest small forwards in Basketball history.

name: Natalie Maines
about: Achieved success as the lead vocalist for the female alternative country music band "The Chicks", formerly known as "The Dixie Chicks".

name: Ryan Reynolds
about: Reynolds is the youngest of four brothers. He began acting professionally as a young teenager in Canadian television.  He moved to Hollywood instead of college, and grew into larger roles there, starring in the sitcom series "Two Guys and a Girl".

name: Ronaldinho
homePlace: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
about: Ronaldinho is a Brazilian global soccer icon, famous for his outstanding technical skills and footballing tricks in the midfield.

name: Martina Hingis
about:
Martina Hingis spent a total of 209 weeks as world no. 1 and won five Grand Slam singles titles (three Australian Opens, one Wimbledon, and one US Open).  
 
She also won nine Grand Slam women's doubles titles, winning a calendar-year doubles Grand Slam in 1998, and one Grand Slam mixed doubles title.

name: N. K. Jemisin
homePlace: Iowa City, Iowa, United States of America
about: N. K. Jemisin is a prominent speculative, fantasy, and science fiction author known for her series "The Broken Earth Trilogy." Jemisin is the first African American author to win the Hugo Award for Best Novel, and the first author to win the Hugo Award for Best Novel in three consecutive years.

name: Amy Poehler
about: Amy Poehler's career began in sketch comedy, which she studied in college. She become an early member of the influential improv and sketch group The Upright Citizens Brigade in Chicago. They landed a comedy series on Comedy Central for three years from 1998 and moved to New York. From 2001 Poehler featured on "Saturday Night Live", which she also wrote for. From 2003 she co-hosted the Weekend Update with friend and co-star  .

name: Marion Cotillard
about: Marion Cotillard is a French actress best known for her Oscar-winning performance as Édith Piaf in the 2007 film "La Vie en Rose" (2007), which made her the first and only actor to win an Academy Award for a French-language role.

name: Will Ferrell
about: Will Ferrell rose to prominence on comedy sketch TV show "Saturday Night Live" 1995-2002, alongside Tracy Morgan and  . He went on to star in a series of Hollywood films as one of a new generation of comic actors labelled the "Frat Pack".

name: Didier Deschamps
about:
Deschamps has been the manager of the French national football team since 2012. Prior to this he played as a defensive midfielder for a number of clubs such as Marseilles and Chelsea. In 1993 he was part of the only French team so far to win the UEFA Champions League.  
 
As captain of his team he guided France to victory in the 1998 FIFA World Cup and as manager he won the 2018 FIFA World Cup, thus making him the third person to win the tournament as both a player and a manager.

name: Aaron Paul
about: Aaron Paul is an American actor best known for his role as Jesse Pinkman in the television series   (2008–2013). His performance in the series earned him three Primetime Emmy Awards.

name: Marilyn Manson
about: Marilyn Manson is an American singer, songwriter, actor, and artist. He is best known for his controversial stage persona and image as the lead singer of the band Marilyn Manson, which he co-founded with guitarist Daisy Berkowitz and of which he remains the only constant member.

name: Kylie Minogue
about: The Australian singer and actress came to fame playing the role of Charlene in Australian soap "Neighbours" opposite love interest Jason  , but went on to become an international singing star.

name: Billie Joe Armstrong
about: Billie Joe Armstrong transformed punk rock from underground movement to mainstream phenomenon as the frontman of  . His distinctive guitar style and songwriting helped the band sell over 60 million albums while addressing personal struggles and political issues through music.

name: Seattle Slew
homePlace: White Horse Acres Farm, Texas, USA
about: Seattle Slew was an American Thoroughbred racehorse, best known as the tenth winner of the American Triple Crown (1977). He and his descendant, Justify, who won the Triple Crown in 2018, are the only two horses to have won this title while undefeated in any other race.

name: Dr. Dre
about: Dr. Dre transformed hip-hop through his innovative production techniques and business acumen. From pioneering gangsta rap with N.W.A to developing the G-funk sound and launching multiple superstar careers, he helped shape modern music while building a billion-dollar business empire.

name: Shakira
about: Shakira is known for her unique blend of Latin pop, rock, and world music, as well as her distinctive voice and belly dancing. She has sold over 80 million records worldwide and has won multiple Grammy and Latin Grammy Awards.

name: Gavin Newsom
about:
Gavin Newsom is an American politician, currently serving as governor of California after being elected in 2018. After facing criticism for his behavior and leadership during the COVID-19 pandemic there was an attempt to recall him, although this ultimately failed. 
 
Prior to this, Newsom was elected mayor of San Francisco in 2003; then re-elected in 2007. After this he served two terms as lieutenant governor of California before his 2018 election as governor.

name: Joaquin Phoenix
about: A member of the famous Phoenix family, including brother   and sister Summer Phoenix, he has received international acclaim for films such as To Die For (2005), Quills (2000) and Gladiator (2000).

name: Rachel Weisz
about: Weisz's breakthrough role came in the film "Chain Reaction" (1996), leading to a high-profile role as Evelyn Carnahan-O'Connell in the films "The Mummy" (1999) and "The Mummy Returns" (2001).

name: Kimi Räikkönen
about: Nicknamed "Iceman" for his icy personality and terse responses to questions, Räikkönen is one of the most popular and successful Formula 1 Drivers of the modern era. He is the only driver to take a race win in the V10, V8 and the hybrid V6 engine eras.

name: Katherine Heigl
about: Best known for her role as Dr. Isobel "Izzie" Stevens on ABC's medical drama "Grey's Anatomy" from 2005 to 2010. A role which won her the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series in 2007.

name: Cate Blanchett
about: Cate Blanchett has won two Academy Awards and is recognized as one of the most talented actors of her generation.

name: Pete Sampras
about: Pete Sampras is an American tennis player, known for his lengthy rivalry with   and his formerly holding the number one ranking in 1993 for a total of 286 weeks.

name: Leonardo DiCaprio
about:
Nominated for five Academy Awards and ten Golden Globe Awards, winning for "The Aviator" and "The Wolf of Wall Street".  
 
He has received critical acclaim for his work in many films, including "Catch Me If You Can", "Gangs of New York", "Blood Diamond", " ", and "Inception".

name: Snoop Dogg
about: After being discovered by   in 1992, he rose to a fame as a rapper and has sold over 30 million albums worldwide.

name: Nicole Kidman
about:
Following several films in the early 1990s, she came to worldwide recognition for her performances in "Days of Thunder" (1990), "Far and Away" (1992), and "Batman Forever" (1995). 
 
Her performance as   in the drama film "The Hours" (2002) received critical acclaim and earned her the Academy Award for Best Actress.

name: Mark Ronson
about: Mark Ronson is a British-American musician, DJ, songwriter, and record producer, renowned for his innovative contributions to the music industry. Notably, Ronson's work on  's Back to Black (2006) earned him multiple Grammy Awards, and his single "Uptown Funk" with   (2014) achieved global acclaim. Additionally, he won an Oscar and Golden Globe for co-writing the song "Shallow" for A Star Is Born (2018).

name: Matthew McConaughey
about: Matthew McConaughey is a Texas actor known for his Southern charm and laid-back persona.

name: Kim Kardashian
about: Kim   rose to fame in the reality series " " (2007-) and "Kourtney and Kim Take New York". She is married to rapper  .

name: Edward Norton
about: Edward Norton is an American actor and filmmaker. He has received multiple accolades for his performances in a range of film genres, demonstrating a broad acting range and significant talent. His film credits include major roles in Primal Fear (1996), American History X (1998), Fight Club (1999), and Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance) (2014).

name: Ewan McGregor
about:
Ewan McGregor is a Scottish actor who began his career famous for his roles in a series of   directed films including " ". 
 
McGregor went on to star in 3  : Episode I The Phantom Menace, Episode II - Attack of the Clones and Episode III - Revenge of the Sith.

name: Elizabeth Hurley
about: Associated with the cosmetics company   since the company gave Hurley her first modelling job at the age of 29. It has featured her as a representative and model for its products, especially perfumes such as Sensuous, Intuition, and Pleasures. She also owns an eponymous beachwear line.

name: Jimmy Fallon
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Best known for his work in television as a cast member on "Saturday Night Live" and as the host of late-night talk show "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon."

name: Chris Brown
about: Chris Brown is known for his R&B and pop music, as well as his dancing skills, being labelled by some as the "King of R&B."

name: Guy Sebastian
about: Guy Sebastian is an Australian singer-songwriter best known for winning the first season of Australian Idol in 2003, after which he continued to serve in various roles on reality television. He was a judge on the Australian version of The X Factor from 2010 to 2015, as well as a coach on The Voice Australia.

name: Post Malone
about: Rapper, singer-songwriter and record producer Post Malone has himself called his style of music "genre-less". Malone's father was a DJ and growing up introduced his son to a number of different music styles including country, hip-hop and rock and Malone's own musical style is a melting pot of these and other genres.

name: Dan Reynolds
about: Dan Reynolds is an American musician best known as the lead singer of the rock band Imagine Dragons. Reynolds formed Imagine Dragons while at   University and experienced a surge in popularity following their debut album Night Visions (2012).

name: Alexandre Bilodeau
about: Freestyle skier who won a gold medal in the men's moguls at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver, becoming the first Canadian to win a gold medal at an Olympic Games held in Canada.

name: Greta Gerwig
about: As director and screenwriter of the phenomenally successful "Barbie" film, Greta Gerwig is the first solo female director with a film to gross over $1 billion. Gerwig co-wrote "Barbie" which starred   and   with Noah Baumbach, her frequent collaborator and partner.

name: Jordan Spieth
about:
A winner of three majors, Spieth is the youngest person since   in 1923 to win the US Open. 
 
In 2015 he become the second-youngest person (after  ) to win the Masters.

name: Anne-Marie
about: Anne-Marie is an English singer-songwriter who came to fame on a feature with Clean Bandit, the song "Rockabye," in 2016, alongside Sean Paul. She released her debut album, Speak Your Mind, in 2018 and had several charting singles including "2002" which was co-created with  .

name: Leona Lewis
about: Leona Lewis is a British singer, songwriter, and actress who gained prominence after winning the third season of The X Factor in 2006. Her success on the show led to a recording contract and the release of her debut single, "A Moment Like This," which set a download record at the time.

name: Antoine Griezmann
about: Antoine Griezmann is a French professional footballer renowned for his success as a forward for both his club teams and the French national team. Griezmann began his professional career with Real Sociedad in Spain, where he made his debut in 2009 and scored 52 goals in 201 appearances.

name: Khloé Kardashian
about:
Khloé   is one of the American Kardashian family made famous through their reality TV shows " " (2007-21).  
 
Khloé has gone on to star in "Khloé & Lamar" and "Kourtney and Khloé Take Miami" all on the on the E! cable network.

name: Mary-Kate Olsen
about: Mary-Kate Olsen is best known for her role as Michelle Tanner on the television sitcom " " (1987-1995), which she shared with her twin sister  . The Olsen twins became household names and starred in numerous films and TV shows throughout their childhood and teenage years.

name: Elliot Page
about:
Best known for starring in the 2007 film "Juno". 
 
Page started his career in Canada with roles in the television shows "Pit Pony", "Trailer Park Boys", and "ReGenesis" before venturing into feature films. 
 
Page publicly came out as a gay woman in February 2014 and as transgender in December 2020.

name: Dan Carter
about: Dan Carter is a New Zealand rugby player, best known for his time with the Crusaders (2003-2015) and the All Blacks (2003-2015). He holds the record for the highest point-scorer in test match rugby and is regarded by many as the all-time greatest fly-half in rugby history.

name: Haley Joel Osment
about: One of the most successful child actors in history, Osment appeared in films such as "Forrest Gump" (1994) before his breakout role in "The Sixth Sense" (1999) alongside  . This role earned him a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

name: Andy Roddick
about:
Best known for his fast service and powerful forehand, he became a Grand Slam singles champion when he won the title at the 2003 US Open.  
 
He reached four other Grand Slam finals but famously lost to   every time. 
 
Roddick is currently the last North American male player to win a Grand Slam singles event.

name: Ana Ivanović
about: Ana Ivanović is a Serbian former professional tennis player. She was ranked No. 1 in the world in 2008, after winning the French Open.

name: Freddie Highmore
homePlace: Camden Town, London, England, United Kingdom
about:
Freddie Highmore is an English actor who first came to fame as a child, starring in Finding Neverland (2004) and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (2005). 
 
More recently, Highmore played Norman Bates in the television series Bates Motel (2013-2017). He has also starred in The Good Doctor since 2017.

name: DeMarcus Cousins
about: DeMarcus Cousins is an American professional basketball player, widely recognized for his tenure in the NBA and his current playing for the Taiwan Beer Leopards of the T1 League. Notable for his dominant role as a center, Cousins earned accolades such as being a four-time NBA All-Star and twice named to the All-NBA Second Team.

name: Taylor Kitsch
about:
The actor rose to fame in the teen drama "Saturday Night Lights" (2006-11) playing troubled fullback/running back Tim Riggins. 
 
Since then Kitsch has appear in Oliver Stones film "Savages" (2012) alongside  , film "American Assassin" (2017) and the mini series "Waco" (2018) as the cult leader David Koresh.

name: Gedhun Choekyi Nyima
about: The 11th Panchen Lama of Tibetan Buddhism as recognised by the   and various other Tibetan Buddhist leaders. After his selection, he was detained by authorities of the People's Republic of China and has not been seen in public since 17 May 1995.

name: Kaká
about: Kaká is a Brazilian professional footballer widely regarded as one of the finest attacking midfielders of his generation. Starting his career with São Paulo FC in Brazil, he quickly made a name for himself. His nickname Kaká comes from his brother Digão, also a professional football player, who could not pronounce Ricardo when he was a child.

name: Aaron Rodgers
about: Aaron Rodgers is an American football quarterback currently playing for the New York Jets of the National Football League (NFL). Rodgers distinguished himself early in his career, setting several college records with the California Golden Bears. His professional journey commenced when the Green Bay Packers picked him in the first round of the 2005 NFL Draft, setting the stage for a career including a Super Bowl victory and multiple MVP awards.

name: Morgan Wallen
about: Morgan Wallen is an American country music singer and songwriter, best known for having competed on The Voice, first as a part of Usher's team and then Adam Levine's, during the sixth season. He was eliminated in the playoffs but managed to get a record deal, then released his debut EP in 2015.

name: Brian Chesky
about: Brian Chesky is an American entrepreneur best known as a co-founder of Airbnb, the online marketplace for lodgings and tourism. After experiencing the difficulties of paying rent in San Francisco, he and his roommate, Joe Gebbia, conceived of Airbnb in 2007. The idea started with hosting guests in their apartment on air mattresses, hence the name "AirBed and Breakfast."

name: Caroline Wozniacki
about: Caroline Wozniacki is a Danish professional tennis player. She is a former world No. 1 in singles, and has won 30 WTA singles titles and one WTA doubles title.

name: Megan Fox
about: Considered one of the modern female sex symbols (appeared in magazines such as Maxim, Rolling Stone and FHM), she is best known for her role as Mikaela Banes, the love interest of  's character, in the blockbuster film "Transformers".

name: Craig David
about: Craig David achieved international success with his debut album and has maintained a career in the music industry for over two decades.

name: Keira Knightley
about: English actress known for her roles in the Pirates of the Caribbean film series opposite   and   and for historical films such as Joe Wright's " " (2007) and his adaptation of  's novel " " (2005).

name: Rose McIver
about: Rose McIver is a New Zealand actress known for her lead role in the television series iZombie (2015–2019) and for her portrayal of Amber Moore in the A Christmas Prince film series. She began her acting career as a child, appearing in notable projects like The Piano (1993) when she was only three years old.

name: Jessica Alba
about: Jessica Alba's break-out role was playing Max Guevara in  's sci-fi tv programme "Dark Angel". Before this Alba had been acting since her teens, her first role was in 1994's "Camp Nowhere".

name: Ashley Olsen
about: Ashley Olsen is best known for her role as Michelle Tanner on the sitcom " " (1987-1995), which she shared with her twin sister  .

name: Amber Heard
about: Amber Heard is an American actress, having played supporting roles in a number of major films including Pineapple Express (2008) and Magic Mike XXL (2015). She is also a part of the DC Extended Universe, particularly having played Mera in the Aquaman series of films.

name: Tyler Joseph
about: Joseph is the singer of the musical duo Twenty One Pilots, alongside the drummer Josh Dun. At the 59th Grammy Awards the band won the award for Best Duo/Group Performance.

name: Lana Del Rey
about: Del Rey's music has been noted by critics and fans for its cinematic quality, with references to 1950s and 1960s Americana and pop culture prevalent throughout lyrics about romance, glamour and melancholy. Her breakthrough success began in 2011 when her song "Video Games" became a viral hit.

name: Tyson Fury
about: Tyson Fury, known worldwide as the "Gypsy King," is a two-time world heavyweight champion and one of the most prominent figures in modern boxing. His career is marked by high-profile victories, notable comebacks, and open discussion of mental health issues.

name: Jodie Comer
about: Jodie Comer is an English actress, best known for her starring role in the television series   (2018-2022) for which she won an Emmy Award. She has also starred in films such as Free Guy (2021) and The Last Duel (2021).

name: Palmer Luckey
about: Palmer Luckey is best known founding Oculus VR and creating the Oculus Rift virtual reality headset. He later established Anduril Industries, a defense technology company.

name: Kate Mara
about:
American actress best known for her role in the Netflix political drama "House of Cards" where she played Zoe Barnes.  
 
Mara also appeared in the Fox TV series "24" as computer analyst Shari Rothenberg.

name: Chris Evans
about: Chris Evans is best known for his portrayal of   in the Marvel Cinematic Universe films. He has become one of Hollywood's leading men and has expanded his career to include directing.

name: Josh Groban
about: Josh Groban is an American singer, songwriter, and actor. He has sold over 25 million records worldwide and has won multiple awards, including four Grammy Awards.

name: Harry Kane
about: Considered one of the world's best football strikers, Harry Kane continues to set goalscoring records throughout his career.

name: Hope Solo
about:
Regarded as one of the top female goalkeepers in the world, Solo is a two-time Olympic gold medalist and holds the US record for the most clean sheets. 
 
After controversy in the 2007  's World Cup, she helped the US team win gold at the 2008 and 2012 Summer Olympics.

name: Karen Gillan
about: Karen Gillan is a Scottish actress, director, and screenwriter. She is best known for her roles as Amy Pond in the BBC series Doctor Who (2010–2013), Nebula in the Marvel Cinematic Universe films   (2014), Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017),  : Infinity War (2018), and   (2019), and Ruby Roundhouse in the Jumanji franchise (2017–present).

name: Anya Taylor-Joy
about: American-born but of Argentine, British and Spanish heritage, Anya Taylor-Joy. left school to act aged 16 and her first success was in Robert Eggers' horror "The Witch" (2015). She starred in another horror M. Night Shyamalan's "Split" (2016) and its sequel "Glass" (2019). She was awarded the Trophée Chopard, given to a promising young actress, at Cannes in 2017.

name: Michael van Gerwen
about: Michael van Gerwen is a Dutch professional darts player who has won multiple titles, including three PDC World Championships, and is recognized for his fast-paced playing style and exceptional skill. Additionally, van Gerwen has held the world No. 1 position and is the second most successful PDC player after Phil Taylor.

name: Felicity Jones
about: Felicity Jones is a British actress who garnered critical acclaim for her role in Like Crazy (2011) and was nominated for an Academy Award for her portrayal of Jane Hawking in The Theory of Everything (2014). She also played a lead role in Rogue One: A   Story (2016), which was a commercial success.

name: Matt Smith
about: The stage, screen and TV actor shot to international fame as the youngest actor to take on the "Doctor Who" role, replacing   as the Eleventh Doctor aged 26.

name: Richard Madden
about: Scottish actor Richard Madden came to prominence playing Robb Stark in the HBO series "Games of Thrones" from 2011-13.

name: Duhan van der Merwe
about: Duhan van der Merwe is a South African-born Scottish professional rugby union player known for his remarkable try-scoring ability. Major highlights include playing for Scotland internationally, joining the British & Irish Lions, and being the top try scorer in several competitions.

name: Cardi B
about: Cardi B first rose to fame through social media and reality television before becoming one of the most successful female rappers in the music industry.

name: Miranda Cosgrove
about: Miranda Cosgrove is best known for her roles in the Nickelodeon series "Drake & Josh" (2004-2007) and "iCarly" (2007-2012), as well as voicing the character Margo in the " " franchise.

name: Kaya Scodelario
about: Kaya Scodelario is a British actress who first came to fame as Effy Stonem in the TV series "Skins" (2007-2010, 2013), which she was cast in at age 14 with no prior acting experience. Scodelario has since starred in major film franchises like "The Maze Runner" series (2014-2018) and "Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales" (2017).

name: Logan Paul
about: One of the most successful YouTubers, he and his younger brother   gained fame initially on the short-video service Vine, and then eventually on YouTube. He currently has 15 million subscribers.

name: Kane Brown
about: Kane Brown is an American singer, who was the first artist to have simultaneous number ones on all five of the main Billboard country charts. He later released his second studio album, Experiment (2018), which reached number one of the Billboard 200.

name: Patrick J. Adams
about: Patrick J. Adams is a Canadian actor, best known for his role as Mike Ross in Suits (2011-2019). He played the main character in the series, a hyper-intelligent college dropout who goes on to work as an unlicensed lawyer. He was nominated for a Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Drama Series for this role.

name: Katie Cassidy
about: Katie Cassidy is an American actress, model and singer from Los Angeles, California. She is best known for her roles as Laurel Lance/Black Canary in the television series Arrow, and as Juliet Sharp in Gossip Girl (2007-2012). She has also appeared in films such as A Nightmare on Elm Street (2010) and When a Stranger Calls (2006).

name: Kacey Musgraves
about: Country singer songwriter Kacey Musgrave was discovered aged 19 in Austin Texas. She released her debut single "Merry Go 'Round" in 2012 and her debut album "Same Trailer Different Park" in 2013, which included the single "Follow Your Arrow" and notable for its progressive lyrics. The album went on to win Best Country Album at the 2014 Grammy Awards.

name: Lily Allen
about:
English recording artist, actress and television presenter. Her first mainstream single, "Smile", reached number one on the UK Singles Chart in July 2006.  
 
Her debut record, Alright, Still, was well received, selling over 2.6 million copies worldwide and brought her a nomination at the Grammy Awards.

name: Hope Hicks
about: Hope Hicks was an American public relations executive and political advisor best known for her roles in the Trump administration, serving in high-level communications positions and her involvement in  's presidential campaigns. Hicks was one of the key figures in Trump's rise to the presidency.

name: Michael Essien
about: Michael Essien is a Ghanaian professional footballer and coach best known for his time as a player with Chelsea, where he won multiple Premier League titles, FA Cups, a League Cup, and the UEFA Champions League. Essien also played for the Ghanaian national team, including representing Ghana in the World Cup.

name: John Mulaney
about: John Mulaney is an American stand-up comedian, actor, and writer. He first came to fame as a writer for Saturday Night Live from 2008 to 2013, and he has returned to host the show several times since.

name: Breanna Stewart
about: Breanna Stewart is one of the most decorated players and dominant power forwards in women's basketball.

name: Megan Rapinoe
about: Soccer star Megan Rapinoe had the year of her life professionally in 2019, leading the US side as co-captain, to win the  's World Cup. The winger went on to be awarded FIFA's Best Women's Player (2019), the Ballon d'Or Féminin and Sports Illustrated Sportsperson of the Year.

name: Fernando Alonso
about: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish racing driver who won the World Drivers' Championship titles in 2005 and 2006 with the Renault team, breaking several records along the way including becoming the youngest double world champion.

name: Leelee Sobieski
about: Leelee Sobieski is an American artist and retired actress. She was discovered by a talent scout at a young age and landed her first roles in "Interview with the Vampire" (1994) and TV movies like "Reunion" (1994) and "A Horse for Danny" (1995).

name: Zoë Kravitz
about: Zoë Kravitz is an American actress and model, as well as the daughter of singer   and actress  . She came to fame with her role as Angel Salvadore in X-Men: First Class (2011) and later continued with roles in the Divergent series (2014-2016) and the Fantastic Beasts series (2016-2022).

name: Kendall Jenner
about: First coming to prominence with her role in the reality series   (2007-present), her and her sister   showed an early interest in fashion by producing a line of clothes in 2012.

name: Draymond Green
about: Draymond Green is an American basketball player, best known as power forward for the Golden State Warriors. He is a four-time NBA champion, as well as a four-time NBA All-Star and has twice been selected for the All-NBA Team.

name: Lil Wayne
about: Dwayne Michael Carter Jr., better known as Lil Wayne, is an American rapper, singer, and songwriter who rose to prominence as one of the most influential hip hop artists of his generation. He is also the founder of Young Money Entertainment.

name: Kate Middleton
about: Catherine, Princess of Wales, is the wife of  , who is heir to the British throne. She is well known and favoured for her charitable work and public service.

name: Sebastian Stan
about: Famous for his portrayal of the character of Bucky Barnes/The Winter Soldier in the Marvel Cinematic Universe films. Cast as the character in the 2011 film "Captain America: The First Avenger", he took more of a starring role opposite   in the follow-up "Captain America: The Winter Soldier" (2014).

name: Zara Phillips
about:
British equestrian and the second-eldest grandchild of   and  ,  .  
 
Phillips is the second child and only daughter from the marriage of Anne, Princess Royal and her first husband, Captain Mark Phillips.  
 
She is 15th in the line of succession.

name: Sean McColl
about: Sean McColl is a Canadian rock climber known for his versatility and success across the lead, speed, and bouldering disciplines. His career is marked by victories in competitions and impressive ascents in outdoor climbing.

name: Robert Pattinson
about: Robert Pattison came to prominence as Edward Cullen in the film adaptations of the Twilight novels.

name: Margot Robbie
about: Margot Robbie studied drama in Australia and appeared on local soap Neighbours before moving to America to work.

name: Hasan Minhaj
about:
While most famous for his Netflix show (Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj), Minhaj started out as a stand-up comedian. He first came into the spotlight as a correspondent on 'The Daily Show.'  
 
After this his career accelerated into major stand-up comedy specials, starting with 'Homecoming King.' For this and 'Patriot Act,' his weekly comedy show on Netflix, Minhaj has won two Peabody Awards.

name: Ciara
about: R&B singer-songwriter Ciara got her start as part of girl group Hearsay before going solo. She released her debut solo album "Goodies" in 2004 with the hit single of the same name. The album went on to be nominated for four Grammys.

name: Jennifer Lawrence
about: Silver Linings Playbook,  : Catching Fire

name: Seth Rogen
about:
Rogen rose to fame after his major supporting role in "The 40-Year-Old Virgin", which he was also credited for co-producing. His performance was critically acclaimed, and he was cast as a lead in "Knocked Up" and "Funny People".  
 
He also co-wrote the films "Superbad", "Pineapple Express", and "This Is the End" with Evan Goldberg.

name: Andrew Garfield
about: Andrew Garfield is a British-American actor, best known for his performances in the Spider-Man series and for winning an Academy Award for his role as   in the film Hacksaw Ridge (2016).

name: Carrie Underwood
about: Carrie Underwood first rose to fame after winning the fourth season of "American Idol" in 2005 and has since had a highly successful solo career.

name: Liam Payne
about: Liam Payne was an English singer who came to fame as a member of   alongside Niall Horan,  ,  , and  . The group were an all-time best-selling boy band prior to their indefinite hiatus in 2016.

name: Rita Ora
about:
Rita Ora is a British singer-songwriter who first came to fame with her feature on DJ Fresh's single "Hot Right Now" (2012). She has since released her debut album Ora (2012), which featured a number of major singles including "R.I.P" and "How We Do (Party)."  
 
She has been in a relationship with New Zealand filmmaker   since 2021, and the couple are reported to have married in 2022.

name: Rebecca Ferguson
about: Rebecca Ferguson is a Swedish actress, best known for playing Elizabeth Woodville in the series The White Queen (2013). She was nominated for the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Miniseries or Television Film for this role, but the award went to   for her role in Burton and Taylor.

name: Kendrick Lamar
about:
Labelled the "new king of hip hop", Kendrick Lamar has won 17 Grammy awards and in 2018 became the first rapper to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music for his album "Damn", marking a significant milestone for the music genre.  
 
In 2022, he co-headlined the Emmy Award-winning Super Bowl half-time show.

name: Adrienne Bailon
about: Adrienne Bailon is an American television personality, singer, and actress, known for her involvement with the girl groups 3LW and The Cheetah Girls. She has also made a name for herself as a co-host of the daytime talk show The Real, earning a Daytime Emmy Award for her role, and as a co-anchor on E! News since 2022.

name: Dominic Thiem
about: Won the US Open in 2020 and made the ATP Finals in 2019.

name: Lil Baby
about: Lil Baby is an American rapper and singer-songwriter who came to fame in 2017 with the release of a mixtape titled Perfect Timing. He then released his debut studio album Harder Than Ever in 2018, which included the top 10 single "Yes Indeed" featuring Drake.

name: Christina Perri
