about: Christina Perri gained fame with her song "Jar of Hearts" and achieved diamond certification for "A Thousand Years."

name: Chris Froome
about: Chris Froome is one of the most accomplished riders of his generation, best known for his Tour de France victories and Grand Tour success.

name: Amanda Seyfried
about: Although acting and modelling since the age of 11, Amanda Seyfried came to fame as an actress in  's 2004 film "Mean Girls" opposite  . Further prominent roles followed in "Mama Mia!" (2008) with  , its sequel in 2018 and Les Misérables (2012).

name: Mo Farah
about: Mo Farah is a British long-distance runner, known for having won ten gold medals in global championships including the Olympic and World titles. He is the all-time most successful male track distance runner, as well as the most successful British athlete in the modern Olympic Games.

name: Neymar
homePlace: Mogi das Cruzes, São Paulo, Brazil
about:
Forward/winger for FC Barcelona. Known for his acceleration, dribbling skills, finishing and ability with both feet.  
 
His playing style has earned him critical acclaim, with fans, media and former players drawing comparison to former Brazil forward Pelé.

name: Lauren Cohan
about:
Lauren Cohan is an American-British actress, best known for her role as Maggie Greene in The Walking Dead (2011-18; 2020-22).  
 
She has also had roles in Supernatural (2007-08) and The Vampire Diaries (2010-12).

name: Ashley Tisdale
about:
Tisdale achieved mainstream success with her role as Maddie Fitzpatrick on the Disney Channel television series The Suite Life of Zack and Cody (2005-08) and later in the High School Musical where she played Sharpay Evans.  
 
After this she released several studio albums and started her own makeup brand.

name: Lewis Hamilton
about:
Regarded by many as the greatest driver in the history of Formula One, Hamilton has won more F1 victories than any other British race driver. 
 
Hamilton won his first title with McLaren in 2008, before winning back-to-back titles in 2014 and 2015 with Mercedes.

name: Agnieszka Radwańska
about: Agnieszka Radwańska is a Polish professional tennis player who achieved a career-high ranking of world No. 2 and was the first Polish player to reach a Grand Slam singles final in the Open Era at Wimbledon 2012. Radwańska has won 20 career singles titles.

name: Astronaut Michael Collins
about: Michael Collins was an American astronaut, best known for flying the Apollo 11 command module during the 1969 landing of   and   on the Moon. He was also the fourth person to perform a spacewalk.

name: Marc Garneau
about:
A navy man by training, Garneau joined Canada’s fledgling space program in 1983, and in 1984 became the first Canadian in outer space when he served as crew on U.S. Shuttle Mission 41-G.  
 
After venturing to space a few more times, he went on to serve as head of the Canadian Space Agency from 2001 to 2005.  
 
In 2008 he was elected to Parliament as a Liberal representing Quebec.

name: John Glenn
about:
John Glenn became a national hero when he became the first American to orbit the earth in 1962 aboard the Friendship 7 spacecraft. 
 
As a politician Glenn served 4 terms as the Democratic Senator for Ohio and in 1984 ran for the Democratic nomination for President. 
 
In 1998 Glen became the oldest person in space at 77 aboard the space shuttle Discovery.

name: Chris Hadfield
about: Chris Hadfield was the first Canadian to command the International Space Station, as well as the first Canadian to walk in space. He is well-known for his efforts to make space exploration accessible to the public through social media.

name: Jim Lovell
about: Jim Lovell went from model building youth to Apollo mission commander, ultimately leading the first lunar orbit with Apollo 8 as well as the ill-fated Apollo 13 mission.

name: Frank Borman
about: As the commander of Apollo 8, NASA astronaut Frank Borman, along with crew mates   and Bill Anders were the first to fly around the Moon in 1968. They orbited the moon ten times during the six-day mission and were the first humans to see and take pictures of the far side of the moon.

name: Alan Shepard
about: Alan Bartlett Shepard Jr. an American astronaut and the first American to travel into space, as well as one of the few individuals to have walked on the Moon. He was the second person to travel into space after the Soviet cosmonaut  .

name: Buzz Aldrin
about: Buzz Aldrin was the second person to walk on the Moon. He is best known for his role in the Apollo 11 mission in 1969, where he and   became the first humans to set foot on the lunar surface.

name: Neil Armstrong
about: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon. He is best known for this feat and his role as commander of the Apollo 11 mission in 1969.

name: Scott Kelly
about:
Kelly began a year-long mission to the International Space Station in March 2015. He has served previously on three different missions. 
 
His identical twin brother is also an astronaut, and the two are the only siblings to have traveled to outer space.

name: Joseph A. Walker
about: Joseph A. Walker was the American pilot and physicist that first flew an airplane to space in 1963, a feat achieved in the North American X-15 experimental space plane. He flew this plane three times to over 50 miles.

name: Scott Carpenter
about: Scott Carpenter was an American astronaut, test pilot, and aquanaut who played a significant role in the early years of the United States' space program. As one of the original Mercury Seven astronauts, Carpenter was among the first Americans to venture into space.

name: Byron de la Beckwith
about: Byron de la Beckwith is an American white supremacist and Klansman, best known for assassinating  , a civil rights leader, in 1963. He was charged but after two hung juries, was initially let off; only to be later successfully convicted in 1994 for murder.

name: Mehmet Ali Ağca
about: Ağca is infamous for having murdered left-wing journalist Abdi İpekçi in 1979 and then, in 1981, for shooting and wounding Pope  .

name: Gavrilo Princip
homePlace: Obljaj, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Austro-Hungarian Empire, officially the Ottoman Empire
about: Princip was a Bosnian-Serb and a member of the group Young Bosnia, who were dedicated to ending the rule of Austria-Hungary in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which had been in place since 1878.

name: Lee Harvey Oswald
about:
Oswald assassinated   on November 22, 1963, in Dallas, Texas.  
 
Though numerous conspiracy theories exist in regard to the killing, Oswald is generally taken to have fired the fatal shots from the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository along Kennedy's parade route in Dealey Plaza. 
 
Two days later, Oswald was himself shot dead by  , live on television.

name: James Earl Ray
about: Prior to his infamy, Ray left school at fifteen and was briefly in the United States Army, serving in Germany at the end of World War Two.

name: Sirhan Sirhan
about: Sirhan Sirhan, a Palestinian born in Jerusalem, is the individual found guilty of the 1968 assassination of Senator  .

name: Charles J. Guiteau
about: Charles J. Guiteau was the assassin of President  . He shot Garfield on July 2, 1881, at a train station in Washington, D.C.

name: John Bellingham
about: On a trip to Russia in 1803, Bellingham was involved in revealing an apparent insurance scam for which, in retaliation, he was accused of a debt. As a result, his travel papers were cancelled and he was imprisoned after pressure from Soloman Van Brienen, who had lost money in the insurance issue.

name: John Wilkes Booth
about: Booth was an American stage actor and Confederate sympathizer who is infamous for his assassination of President  . Booth's act marked the first time a sitting U.S. president was assassinated, and his deed significantly altered the course of Reconstruction and the aftermath of the Civil War.

name: Akira Toriyama
about: Akira Toriyama is a renowned Japanese manga artist and character designer. He is best known for creating the widely popular manga and anime series, Dragon Ball.

name: Frederick Catherwood
about: Frederick Catherwood was an English artist and explorer who played a significant role in documenting ancient Maya sites in Central America. Known for combining scientific precision with artistic skill, Catherwood’s illustrations have remained influential in archaeological studies.

name: Tarsila do Amaral
about: Tarsila do Amaral, often known by her first name Tarsila, was a leading modernist artist in Latin America.

name: Arthur Wesley Dow
about: Arthur Wesley Dow was an American artist and educator, known for his innovative ideas about the teaching of visual arts. His philosophies and teaching methodologies helped shape the development of modern art education in the United States.

name: Ai Weiwei
about: Ai Weiwei is a Chinese contemporary artist, documentarian, and activist known for his bold commentary on social and political issues. i faced early adversity due to his father, Ai Qing's, exile during the Anti-Rightist Movement, which influenced his perspective and work.

name: David Hockney
about:
An important 20th century artist, Hockney came to prominence in the 1960s as a pop artist and is known for his colorful and bold paintings. He is also famous for his portraits. 
 
Hockney has for many years worked both in California and in the UK and the landscapes and color of both places are reflected in his work.  
 
In 2017 Hockney was the subject of a major comprehensive retrospective at Britain's Tate Gallery.

name: Andy Warhol
about: Andy Warhol was an American artist who was a leading figure in the pop art movement of the 1960s. He is known for his artworks in a wide variety of mediums which drew on influences from advertising and celebrity culture.

name: Ben Enwonwu
about: Often called 'Africa's greatest artist' Ben Enwonwu was the most well known and one of the most influential African artists of the 20th century. Born in Nigeria, he studied in England before returning to his home country.

name: Stan Lee
about: Lee was for many decades Marvel Comics' primary creative leader, and he was responsible for transforming the company from a small family-run business to a creative and publishing empire responsible for some of the most famous comics and characters of all time.

name: Peter Max
about: Peter Max is an American artist and prominent figure in the pop art movement who is known for his colorful psychedelic art style.

name: Fernando Botero
about: Fernando Botero is a Colombian artist whose signature style is known as "Boterismo." His characters are depicted as extremely rotund, a stylistic quirk which is read as a commentary on contemporary excess.

name: William Blake
about: Largely unrecognised and often considered a lunatic during his lifetime the visionary poet engraver and painter William Blake is now considered the first poet of the Romantic age and one of the finest English artists and engravers.

name: Ilya Repin
about: Ilya Repin was a Ukrainian-born Russian painter, one of the best known artists in nineteenth-century Russia. He is known especially for works like Barge Haulers on the Volga (1873) and Religious Procession in Kursk Province (1880-1883).

name: Jack Kirby
about: Jack Kirby worked with both of the industry’s main publishers - Marvel and DC, and was responsible for the creation of many of the format’s best-known characters, including  , Iron Man, Fantastic Four, X-Men and The Hulk.

name: Karl Polanyi
about: Karl Polanyi was a Hungarian economic anthropologist and social philosopher. He is known for his opposition to traditional economic thought and for his book, The Great Transformation, published in 1944. This book discusses the economic and social changes that occurred in England during the rise of the market economy.

name: Rudolf Virchow
about: Rudolf Virchow made significant contributions to medicine and public health. He is known as the father of modern pathology and cellular theory.

name: Margaret Mead
about:
A popularizer of the insights of anthropology into modern American and Western culture, she was a respected and often controversial academic anthropologist.  
 
Her reports about the attitudes towards sex in South Pacific and Southeast Asian traditional cultures helped shapd the 1960s sexual revolution.

name: Raymond Dart
about: Discovered the first Australopithecus africanus, an extinct hominin species that is closely related to humans that lived 2-3 million years ago.

name: Davidson Black
about: Davidson Black was a Canadian paleoanthropologist noted for his work in the early 20th century on the evolutionary origins of humans. His substantial contributions to the field include the discovery and naming of the Peking Man fossil (Homo erectus pekinensis), a landmark achievement that significantly advanced the understanding of human evolution.

name: Louis Leakey
about: Louis Leakey is best known for his part in demonstrating that humans evolved in Africa. He and his wife   made important discoveries at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania which changed how we understand human origins.

name: Jane Goodall
about: Jane Goodall was an English primatologist and anthropologist. She is best known for her groundbreaking research on the social and family interactions of wild chimpanzees in Gombe Stream National Park, Tanzania. Goodall's work has significantly transformed scientific understanding of chimpanzees and redefined the relationship between humans and animals in the field of ethology.

name: Henry Schoolcraft
about: Henry Rowe Schoolcraft was an American geographer, geologist, and ethnologist, best known for his extensive studies of Native American cultures and for his discovery of the source of the Mississippi River in 1832. Schoolcraft initially studied glassmaking, as his father had, and his first work was published in this field. He left the family business to explore the frontier at the age of twenty-five.

name: Mary Leakey
about: Mary Leakey’s most notable achievements include the discovery of the first fossilized Proconsul skull and the robust Zinjanthropus skull at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania.

name: Ian McKellen
about: Considered one of the greatest British actors of all time, Ian McKellen has played various roles ranging from popular science fiction and fantasy films to Shakespearean dramas and modern theatre. McKellen was knighted by   in 1991, cementing his legacy as one of the greats.

name: Mahmoud Abbas
about: Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen, is the president of the State of Palestine and the Palestinian National Authority. He is also the chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization and a member of the Fatah party.

name: Diana Ross
about: Diana Ross rose to fame as the lead singer of The Supremes, Mototown's most successful act, and one of the most successful female groups ever.

name: Phil Jackson
about: Widely considered one of the greatest coaches in NBA history, Jackson won six NBA Championships as head coach of the Chicago Bulls and five NBA Championships as head coach of the Los Angeles Lakers.

name: Mick Jagger
about:
Best known as the lead singer and a founding member of  .  
 
His career has spanned over 50 years, and he is one of the most influential people in the history of rock & roll.

name: Neil Young
about: Co-founded the band Buffalo Springfield along with Stephen Stills and Richie Furay, later joining Crosby, Stills & Nash as a fourth member in 1969. His work is characterized by his deeply personal lyrics, distinctive guitar work and signature alto or high tenor singing voice.  He also plays piano, harmonica, and pump organ.

name: Judea Pearl
about: Judea Pearl is an Israeli-American computer scientist and philosopher, widely recognized for his pioneering work in the fields of artificial intelligence, probabilistic reasoning, and causality. His groundbreaking contributions to the development of Bayesian networks have had a significant impact on the way researchers approach problems involving uncertainty, and have enabled more effective decision-making and reasoning in various domains, including medicine, economics, and engineering.

name: Danny DeVito
about:
DeVito first came to fame as part of the television series 'Taxi' (1978-1983), in which he played dispatcher Louie De Palma; and for which he won a Golden Globe and an Emmy. 
 
Since then, DeVito has been a mainstay in countless popular films: 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest' (1975), 'Batman Returns' (1992), 'Matilda' (1996), and many more. 
 
Since 2006, he has returned to television, starring as Frank Reynolds in 'It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia.'

name: John Williams
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: John Williams is an American composer, conductor, and pianist, widely regarded as one of the greatest film composers of all time. His career spans over six decades, during which he has composed some of the most popular, recognizable, and critically acclaimed film scores in cinematic history.

name: Elizabeth Taylor
about: Elizabeth Taylor is regarded as the epitome of a film star - for her beauty, glamorous lifestyle and for her acting. She came to fame as a child actress in the film "National Velvet" aged 12 before moving on to adult roles such as "A Place in the Sun" before she was 20. She was nominated for an Oscar 4 years in a row, winning for Butterfield 8 and also for "Who's Afraid of  ". She was the first actress to receive  $1 million, for her role in " ".

name: Ali MacGraw
about: Ali MacGraw is an American actress known for her roles in iconic films of the 1960s and 1970s. She gained international fame and earned an Academy Award nomination for her role as Jenny Cavalleri in the 1970 romantic drama Love Story.

name: Anne Frank
about:
Aged 13, German born Dutch Jewish national Anne Frank and her family went into hiding in Amsterdam in 1942 to escape persecution under Nazi occupation. 
 
Betrayed two years later they were sent to concentration camps where Anne later died from Typhus.  
 
Anne's diary from June 1942 to August 1944 is regarded as the most famous personal account of the Holocaust and has been turned into a play and film.

name: George Lucas
about: George Lucas is an film director, scriptwriter and producer associated with some of the most successful films ever made.

name: Margrethe II
about:
Margrethe has been the reigning Queen of Denmark since her ascension to the throne on 14 January 1972, upon the death of her father Frederick IX. 
 
In this role she is also the supreme authority of the Church of Denmark and Commander-in-Chief of the Danish Defence.

name: Sally Jessy Raphael
about: Sally Jessy   is an American talk show host. She is best known for hosting "Sally" (originally called "The Sally Jessy Raphael Show"), where she discussed relationship problems and offered advice. Raphael is recognized for her trademark oversized red-framed glasses.

name: Enzo Maiorca
about: Enzo Maiorca was an Italian free diver known for his numerous world records and environmental advocacy. He set his first world record in free diving in 1960 and eventually retired from competitive diving in 1988 after setting a record dive of 101 meters.

name: John Madden
about: As head coach of the Oakland Raiders John Madden won the 1976 Super Bowl.

name: Nancy Pelosi
about: Nancy Pelosi is the highest-ranking woman to be elected in US history. She has been elected Speaker of the House of Representatives twice, serving 2007-11 and re-elected in 2019. She is the first Speaker to be elected to a second term since 1955.

name: Alexei Leonov
homePlace: Listvyanka, West Siberian Krai, Soviet Union
about: Leonov was the first person to do a 'spacewalk' - that is conducting extra-vehicular activity while in space. He achieved this feat with the Soviet space program on March 18, 1965, when he went outside his capsule on the Voshkod 2 program for 12 minutes and nine seconds.

name: Joe Gibbs
about: The 20th and 26th head coach in the history of the Washington Redskins (1981–1992, 2004–2007), he built championship teams with many players who have had mediocre to average careers while playing for other NFL teams.

name: Sophia Loren
about:
International film star and Italy's most renowned and honored actress.  
 
Her deglamorized performance as Cesira in Vittorio De Sica's "Two Women" earned her the Academy Award for Best Actress in 1962 and made her the first artist to win an Oscar for a foreign-language performance.

name: Stanley Kubrick
about: Stanley Kubrick was an American film director, screenwriter, and producer, widely regarded as one of the most influential filmmakers in the history of cinema. Known for his meticulous attention to detail, visual style, and innovative storytelling, Kubrick collaborated with a diverse array of talented actors and actresses, including  ,  ,  ,  ,  , and

name: Al Pacino
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Al Pacino is an American actor who has won an Academy Award, two Tony Awards, and two Primetime Emmy Awards—taken together, having earned the Triple Crown of Acting. He has also been honored with the   Award, the AFI Life Achievement Award, the National Medal of Arts, and the Kennedy Center Honors

name: Jack Nicholson
about: Widely regarded as one of the greatest actors of his generation.  Known particularly for playing dark, neurotic characters, such as in "The Shining", "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" and " ".

name: Elvis Presley
about: One of the most significant cultural icons of the 20th century, Elvis helped establish the emerging Rock and Roll sound, incorporating blues and gospel influences. He was also a leader in popularizing both the rockabilly sound and the four-man band line-up which would later dominate the music industry.

name: Chinua Achebe
about: Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian author best known for his debut novel Things Fall Apart (1958), which is widely read and studied in schools across the globe. The book, set in pre-colonial Nigeria, narrates the life of Okonkwo, a respected warrior, his struggles with the changing society, and eventual downfall with the arrival of European colonizers.

name: Sharon Tate
about:
An American sex symbol of the 1960s, she played small television roles before appearing in several motion pictures, and appeared regularly in fashion magazines as a model and cover girl. 
 
In 1969 she was brutally murdered while 8½ months pregnant by cult leader   and his group, the "Manson Family".

name: Joni Mitchell
about: Joni helped define an era and a generation with popular songs like "Big Yellow Taxi", "Woodstock", "Both Sides Now", and "A Case Of You".

name: Joan A. Steitz
about: Joan Steitz is an American biochemist and molecular biologist who has made important discoveries about RNA and how it works in cells. Her research has informed our understanding of genes and the roles these play in disease.

name: Morgan Freeman
about: Known for his distinctively smooth, deep voice, he has received Academy Award nominations for his performances in "Street Smart", "Driving Miss Daisy", "The Shawshank Redemption" and "Invictus", and won the Best Supporting Actor Oscar in 2005 for Million Dollar Baby.

name: Björn Ulvaeus
about: Björn Ulvaeus began his music career as a member of a folk and schlager group called the Hootenany Singers.  After meeting keyboardist  , he began co-writing songs that Andersson's band recorded.

name: Bernie Ecclestone
homePlace: St Peter South Elmham, Suffolk, England, United Kingdom
about: Bernie Ecclestone is British businessman known as the former chief executive of the Formula One Group, which manages Formula One motor racing. He began as a driver in 1958, though failing to qualify, and went own to manage other drivers; then to controlling the sport as a whole.

name: George Soros
about: One of the world's most successful investors, in February 2018 Soros had a net worth of $8 billion after donating $18 billion to his Open Society Foundation.

name: Louis Farrakhan
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
The leader of the Nation of Islam religious group, Farrakhan has been a controversial figure in black civil rights history. He is widely thought to have been involved in the assassination of  .  
 
In 1995 he organised the Million Man March in Washington, D.C.

name: Bob Dylan
about: An influential American singer-songwriter who began as a folk singer associated with the protest movements of the 1960s with folk songs "Blowin' in the Wind" and "The Times They Are a-Changin".

name: Carl Bernstein
about: Carl Bernstein won a Pulitzer Prize for his and  's investigation of the Watergate scandal for the Washington Post. Their investigation was a major factor that led to the resignation of  .

name: Bette Midler
about:
A star of rare talent, Midler has won three Grammy Awards, four Golden Globes, three Emmy Awards and a special Tony Award. She has also been nominated for two Academy Awards. 
 
Midler has sold over 30 million albums worldwide.

name: William Peter Blatty
about: William Peter Blatty is known for the novel and Academy Award-winning screenplay of " ".

name: Mary Quant
about: Mary Quant is an English fashion icon, synonymous with the swinging 1960s. She lead the youth quake in fashion in London, liberating women from the stuffy, more formal clothing that was usually their only option up until then.

name: Roger Waters
about: The lead vocalist, songwriter and bassist for the British rock band  . Waters was one of the original founders of the band in 1965 alongside   (guitar, lead vocals), Nick Mason (drums) and Richard Wright, with   joining in 1967.

name: Tim Rice
about: His collaborations with   led to "Joseph & the Technicolor Dreamcoat", "Jesus Christ Superstar" and "Evita".

name: Pattie Boyd
about: Pattie Boyd was a successful English model when she married Beatles member   in 1966.

name: Hunter S. Thompson
about: Hunter S. Thompson was an American journalist and author who is widely credited as the founder of gonzo journalism. He rose to prominence in the 1960s as a writer for Rolling Stone magazine and was most famously known for his novel Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (1971).

name: Juvénal Habyarimana
about: Juvénal Habyarimana was the president of Rwanda from 1973 to 1994. He led the country during a period of significant political and social change, culminating in his assassination and the subsequent Rwandan genocide.

name: Smokey Robinson
about: Smokey Robinson is an American singer, songwriter, record producer, and former record executive. Robinson was the founder and front man of the Motown vocal group the Miracles, for which he also served as the group's chief songwriter and producer.

name: Scotty Bowman
about:
Holds the record for most wins in NHL history with 1,244 regular season wins and 223 Stanley Cup playoff wins.  
 
Combined, as a player, coach, and executive, he has won 13 Stanley Cups.

name: Paul McCartney
about: McCartney grew up in Liverpool, and was introduced to future song-writing partner   aged 15 by mutual friend Ivan Vaughan. McCartney joined Lennon's skiffle band, the Quarrymen.

name: Osamu Tezuka
about: Osamu Tezuka was a Japanese manga artist and animator, often dubbed as the "Father of Manga" for his groundbreaking contributions to the medium. His prolific output and innovative techniques have made him one of the most influential figures in the world of comics and animation.

name: Pope Francis
about: Pope Francis was the 266th Pope of the Roman Catholic Church, elected on March 13, 2013. He was the first Latin American Pope and the first born outside Europe since the 8th-century Syrian Pope Gregory III.

name: Tom Brokaw
about: Tom Brokaw is an American television journalist and author best known for his time as anchor and managing editor of NBC Nightly News from 1982 to 2004. He is a recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the highest civilian honor in the United States.

name: Mario Andretti
about: He won the Indianapolis 500, the Daytona 500, the Formula One World Championship and the Pikes Peak Hillclimb.

name: Priscilla Presley
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Priscilla Presley is an American businesswoman, actress, and the former wife of  . Her story includes her marriage to the "King of Rock and Roll," her transition to a career in the entertainment industry, and her successful management of Elvis Presley's legacy.

name: Yuri Gagarin
about: Yuri Gagarin was a Soviet and pilot, best known as the first human to venture into outer space. This feat was first achieved by Gagarin aboard the Vostok 1 capsule in April 1961. As a result, he became an international celebrity and was made a Hero of the Soviet Union by  .

name: Joe Gallo
about: Nicknamed "Crazy Joe", Joe Gallo was a well known New York City gangster for the Profaci crime family, which later became the Colombo crime family.

name: George Takei
about:
Born to Japanese American parents in Los Angeles, George Takei and his family were interred during WWII. 
 
As an actor Takei is most famous for his role as  Lt. Hikaru Sulu in the "Star Trek" TV series opposite   and Leonard Nimroy 1966-69. He went on to feature in the animated series and several Star Trek films. 
 
Takei is also a successful writer and activist, speaking out on immigration and LGBT rights

name: Susan Sontag
about: Susan Sontag is best known for her essays, novels, films, and activism.

name: John Fogerty
about: Best known as the primary songwriter, guitarist and singer of the American swamp rock band   (CCR), from 1968-72. The popular band  was formed of high school friends, and John's older brother Tom. They had many hit songs during their brief existence, including "Proud Mary", "Bad Moon Rising", "Fortunate Son", and "Have You Ever Seen the Rain?".

name: George Harrison
about: English musician, singer and songwriter who became famous as the lead guitarist of the Beatles.

name: Lech Wałęsa
about:
Co-founded and headed Solidarity (Solidarność), the Soviet bloc's first independent trade union. 
 
Wałęsa won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1983 and served as President of Poland from 1990 to 1995.

name: Ringo Starr
about: Ringo Starr, a featured member of Rory Storm and The Hurricanes, became the final piece of the Beatles puzzle when he replaced drummer   in 1962.

name: Joanne Woodward
about: Award-winning actress who establish a career during the Golden age of Hollywood but also went on to become an acclaimed TV actress.

name: Tommie Smith
about:
In 1968, at the Summer Olympics, a 24-year old Smith was the first person to break the 20-second barrier for the 200-meter sprint–winning gold in the process.  
 
After winning this, Smith and   celebrated atop the podium with the Black Power salute. This controversy, and Smith's record-breaking talent, set him on the path to be not only a star athlete but also a civil rights icon.

name: Audrey Hepburn
about: A film and fashion icon during Hollywood's Golden Age, Hepburn is one of the few people to have won an Academy Award, Emmy, Grammy, and Tony award.

name: Roger Hargreaves
about: Roger Hargreaves is best known for creating the Mr. Men and Little Miss series of children's books. These simple stories with their colourful characters have sold over 85 million copies worldwide in 20 languages.

name: Jocelyn Bell Burnell
about: Jocelyn Bell Burnell was still a research student at Cambridge University when she was part of the team that was the first to detect a radio pulsar in 1967. It is now considered to be one of the greatest astronomical discoveries of the 20th century. The discovery won the 1974 Nobel Prize for Physics, but was controversially awarded to just her supervisor Antony Hewish and astronomer Martin Ryle, despite Burnell Bell being the first to spot the pulsar in the data .

name: Nolan Bushnell
about: Nolan Bushnell is best known for founding Atari and Chuck E. Cheese's. He is often called the father of the video game industry due to his early work in arcade and home video games.

name: Clint Eastwood
about: Clint Eastwood is an American actor, filmmaker, and political figure. He rose to prominence in the 1960s with the television show Rawhide and then as the 'Man with No Name' in  's 'Dollars Trilogy' of spaghetti Westerns during the 1960s. These early roles established Eastwood's on-screen persona as a rugged, stoic, and tough antihero.

name: Betty Cuthbert
about: Betty Cuthbert was an Australian athlete who won four Olympic gold medals across the 1956 and 1964 Games and set multiple world records. Her career featured an exceptional rise to prominence, becoming an Olympic champion and earning the nickname "Australia's Golden Girl."

name: Robert Hanssen
about:
A FBI agent who spied for Soviet and Russian intelligence services against the United States for 22 years.  
 
His activities have been described by the US Department of Justice's Commission for the Review of FBI Security Programs as "possibly the worst intelligence disaster in U.S. history".

name: Sandra Day O'Connor
about: In 1981 Sandra Day O'Connor  became the first woman to be nominated and confirmed to the US Supreme Court. She was nominated by President  , who had made a campaign pledge to elect the first woman to the court.

name: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf
about: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is a Liberian politician recognized as the first elected female head of state in Africa, serving as the 24th president of Liberia from 2006 to 2018. Her presidency marked significant steps towards peace and rebuilding in Liberia after years of civil unrest and conflict.

name: Anni-Frid Lyngstad
about: "Frida" is most widely known as member of internationally successful Swedish pop band ABBA (she's the brunette one!).

name: Griselda Blanco
about: Griselda Blanco Restrepo was a Colombian drug lord who played a significant role in the cocaine trafficking industry in Miami from the 1970s to the early 2000s. Her life was marked by crime and violence until her death by assassination in Medellín, Colombia.

name: Yoko Ono
about: The second wife of  , from 1969 until his death, was initially criticized for her influence over Lennon and his music, and blamed for the breakup of the Beatles.

name: Gene Hackman
about:
American stage and screen actor Gene Hackman enjoyed a film career of over forty years, appearing in over 75 movies. He was nominated for five Academy Awards, winning Best Actor for the thriller "The French Connection" (1971),  and Best Supporting Actor for the Western film "Unforgiven" (1992).  He also won  BAFTA and Golden Globe Awards for those performances. 
 
After retiring from acting in the mid-2000s, he wrote several novels.

name: Huey P. Newton
about: Huey Newton was an African-American revolutionary and activist, best known as co-founder of   Party. Together with  , the two first constituted the party according to a ten-point manifesto of their design.

name: Barbra Streisand
about: American singer-songwriter, actress, film producer and director Barbra Streisand has sold over 145 million albums worldwide. She is one of the few people to have won an Oscar, Tony, Emmy and a Grammy award.

name: Michael Palin
about:
Known for being one of the members of the comedy group   and for his travel documentaries.  
 
His journeys have taken him across the world, including the North and South Poles, the Sahara Desert, the Himalayas, Eastern Europe and Brazil.

name: Mario Vargas Llosa
about: Mario Vargas Llosa is one of the leading writers of the Latin American Boon generation. His considerable body of work includes novels, short stories, plays, non fiction works and literary criticism.

name: Wangari Maathai
about:
Internationally renowned environmentalist and political activist, Dr. Maathai became the 1st African woman to win a Nobel Peace Prize in 2004 for her work against environmental degradation and poverty. 
 
After founding the Green Belt Movement in 1977, Maathai was responsible for planting over 30 million trees in Africa, and helping provide employment for nearly 900,000 women.

name: Joe Biden
about: US President (2021-25), who won election with a record 81 million popular votes, becoming the oldest sitting president.

name: Tim Horton
about:
Played 24 seasons in the NHL for the Toronto Maple Leafs, New York Rangers, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Buffalo Sabres.  
 
He also co-founded Tim Hortons, a doughnut chain, which currently has over 3,000 locations across Canada.

name: Willie Nelson
about: An American country music singer and songwriter, Willie Nelson is also an author, poet, actor, and activist.

name: Julie Andrews
about: Eternally best known for her portrayals of Mary Poppins (showing remarkable forbearance in the face of  's much maligned cockney accent) and Maria in "The Sound of Music".

name: Charlie Watts
about: Best known as the drummer of British rock group The Rolling Stones, his first musical love was jazz. While still a teenager, he moved from playing jazz to the more lucrative genres of blues and rock, and joined the then newly formed group in 1963.

name: Bob Marley
about: Born to a mother of African and a father of European descent in rural Jamaica, Marley moved with his mother to the ghetto Trench Town in Kingston in 1957. In 1963 he formed a singing group called "The Wailing Wailers" with friends (later "The Wailers") achieving local success.

name: Sylvia Plath
about: Sylvia Plath is known for her confessional style of writing and her struggles with mental health. She began her literary career early, publishing her first poem at age eight in a local newspaper.

name: Jimmie Lee Jackson
about:
Civil rights protester and church deacon who was shot and killed by Alabama State Trooper James Bonard Fowler in 1965 during a peaceful march for voting rights in his home town of Marion, Alabama. 
 
His death inspired the   marches a month later that ultimately led to the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

name: Eric Clapton
about: Eric Clapton is an English rock and blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter, widely considered one of the greatest guitarists of all time. With a career spanning over five decades, Clapton has been a member of several influential bands and has also had a highly successful solo career.

name: Marvin Gaye
about: Marvin Gaye was an important Motown singer in the 1960s. His initial solo recording were not successful but he found success as a songwriter and session musician.

name: Slobodan Milošević
about: A Serbian and Yugoslav politician who was the President of Serbia from 1989 to 1997 and President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia from 1997 to 2000.

name: Rupert Murdoch
about: Rupert Murdoch owns a global media empire and is known for his influence in print, television, and online media across multiple countries.

name: Jayne Mansfield
about: Film actress Jayne Mansfield was a leading sex symbol of the 1950s and 60s and was often compared to  . Mansfield epitomized the image of the blonde bombshell with a voluptuous figure and limited intelligence, although her IQ was supposedly 163.

name: Frank Gehry
about: Frank Gehry was a Canadian-American architect known for his innovative and often unconventional designs. His unique approach to architecture, which often involved the use of unconventional materials and bold, sculptural forms, earned him a place among the most influential architects of the 20th and 21st centuries.

name: Valentina Tereshkova
about: First woman in space, having been selected from more than four hundred applicants and five finalists to pilot Vostok 6 on the 16th June 1963.

name: James Watson
about: James Dewey Watson is an American molecular biologist, geneticist, and zoologist. He is co-credited with the discovery of the double helix structure of DNA, along with  . This groundbreaking discovery, made in 1953, was pivotal in the field of genetics and earned Watson and Crick (along with  ) the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962.

name: Mikhail Gorbachev
about: Seventh and last leader of the Soviet Union, having served as General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from 1985 until 1991, and as the country's head of state from 1988 until its dissolution in 1991.

name: Glenn Hall
about: During his NHL career he seldom missed a game and was a consistent performer, winning the Vezina Trophy three times, and the Calder Memorial Trophy. Nicknamed "Mr. Goalie", he was the first goaltender to develop and make effective use of the butterfly style of goalkeeping.

name: Chubby Checker
about: Chubby Checker will forever be remembered for kicking off a dance craze that took hold of the early countercultural generation in the 1960s. In 1960 he released "The Twist", a cover of a song by Hank Ballard & The Midnighters.

name: Mark Hamill
about:
Hamill is best known for his role as Luke Skywalker in the original   trilogy and in the sequel trilogy of films. 
 
In addition to these films he is known for his voice-over work as the Joker, beginning with the Batman: The Animated Series.

name: Twiggy
about: One of the iconic images of the swinging sixties, Twiggy became famous worldwide as a model for her slim waif-like appearance, following in the footsteps of fellow model  . She got her break after having her hair cropped by a famous hairdresser, and Twiggy went on to be named the face of 1966 in the UK.

name: Mae Jemison
about: Mae Jemison was the 1st African American woman in space in 1993 as a Mission Specialist on the Endeavour (STS-47). An employee of NASA since 1987 Jemison resigned in 1993 to form her own technology company.

name: Michael Keaton
about: Michael Keaton has become a Hollywood icon through his roles in blockbuster films and critically acclaimed productions. He has received various award nominations, as well as winning an Emmy and two Golden Globes.

name: William H. Macy
about: William H. Macy is an American actor, director, and writer known for his versatile performances in film and television. He gained recognition in the 1990s for his work in independent films, including Fargo (1996) and Boogie Nights (1997).

name: Simon Cowell
about: Famous for his role as a talent judge on TV shows such as "Pop Idol," "The X Factor," "Britain's Got Talent" and "American Idol."

name: Jerry Seinfeld
about:
Seinfeld began his career as a stand up comedian before creating the TV sitcom " " with   in 1988.  
 
The show (1989-98) in which Seinfeld played a caricature of himself became one of the most popular sitcoms ever in America.  
 
The comedy was famously called "a show about nothing" and was the winner of a Grammy (1993) and a Golden Globe (1994).

name: Michael Jackson
about: One of the most successful and popular entertainers in music history, Jackson began his musical career as a child, performing with his brothers in Jackson 5 before going solo in 1971. The Jackson 5 had numerous hits, including "ABC" and "I'll Be There".

name: Jayne Torvill
about: Jayne Torvill is best known for her partnership with  . She achieved worldwide fame for their perfect-scoring performance of Bolero at the 1984 Winter Olympics in Sarajevo.

name: Jeff Goldblum
about: Goldlbum's career has seen a number of varied and wide-ranging roles, but is best known for his starring turns in the many blockbusters of his day. These include   (1993), The Lost World: Jurassic Park (1997) and   (1996), as well as their sequels, Independence Day: Resurgence (2016) and Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom (2018).

name: Gloria Estefan
about: Gloria Estefan rose to fame with her band The Miami Sound Machine, drawing on her Cuban roots to become one of the biggest Latino musical acts in the world by the 1980s.

name: George W. Bush
about: Previously serving as the Governor of Texas from 1995 to 2000, Bush was the son of   who served as President from 1989 to 1993. His election win in 2000 was a close and highly controversial victory over  .

name: Kamala Harris
about: Kamala Harris made history in 2020 when she became the first Indian and the first woman of African American heritage to be elected as Vice President of the United States on the Democratic ticket with  , defeating Republicans   and  .

name: Kris Jenner
about: Jenner is an American media personality who rose to fame with the television show Keeping Up with the Kardashians (2007–2021). The show followed her and her children from her marriage to Robert  : Kourtney Kardashian,  ,  , Robert Kardashian—and her children from her marriage to  : Kendall Kardashian and Kylie Kardashian.

name: Tom Waits
about: Tom Waits is an American singer-songwriter, musician, and actor known for his distinctive raspy voice, eclectic musical style, and vivid storytelling. Throughout his career, Waits has explored various genres, including blues, jazz, rock, and experimental music, creating a unique sound that has earned him a dedicated fan base and critical acclaim.

name: Maureen McGovern
about: Maureen McGovern is an American singer and actress best known for recording the Oscar-winning songs "The Morning After" from "The Poseidon Adventure" (1972) and "We May Never Love Like This Again" from "The Towering Inferno" (1974).

name: Barbara Bach
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Barbara Bach's career started in the mid-1960's as a fashion model, which led to acting in Italian films. She landed her best known role when cast as the Bond girl Anya Amasova in the 1977 James Bond film "The Spy Who Loved Me". Entertainment Weekly ranks her as the fifth best Bond girl.

name: Terry Pratchett
about:
Pratchett was an author of fantasy novels, especially comical works who was best known for his "Discworld" series of about 40 volumes.  
 
Pratchett at the time of his death had sold more than 85 million books worldwide in 37 languages. He was also the UK's best-selling author of the 1990s.

name: Tim Allen
about:
Famous for his starring role in the sitcom "Home Improvement".  
 
Allen is also known for his roles in several popular films, including the " " film series (as the voice of Buzz Lightyear), "The Santa Clause" film series, and "Galaxy Quest".

name: Sharon Stone
about:
Sharon Stone is an American actress, best known for her role as the femme fatale Catherine Tramell in Basic Instinct (1992). This role earned Stone her first Golden Globe nomination for best actress. 
 
Stone made her film debut as an extra in  's Stardust Memories (1980). Starring in major films like Total Recall (1990) and Casino (1995), she has since won an Emmy, a Golden Globe, and was nominated for an Academy Award.

name: Eddie Murphy
about: Rose to fame and received Golden Globe Award nominations for his performances in "48 Hrs.", "Beverly Hills Cops", "Trading Places", and "The Nutty Professor". Won the Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actor for his performance in "Dreamgirls". Also was a regular cast member on Saturday Night Live from 1980-1984.

name: Keir Starmer
about: Keir Starmer is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and leader of the Labour Party. He succeeded   after Labour’s success in the 2024 election.

name: Chrissie Hynde
about: Chrissie Hynde is a founding member and driving force of rock band  .

name: Bruce Willis
about: Best known for his role as John McClane in the "Die Hard" series. He has appeared in over 60 films, including " ", "Armageddon", "The Sixth Sense", and "Sin City".

name: Colin Firth
about: Colin Firth gained international recognition for his portrayal of Mr. Darcy in the BBC adaptation of " " (1995) and won an Academy Award for his role as King   in "The King's Speech" (2010).

name: Keanu Reeves
about:
Born in Beirut to an American father and an English mother, but identifying as Canadian, Reeves is perhaps best recognized for his role as Neo in   series (1999-2003), but has appeared in several high profile films such as the Bill and Ted franchise (1989-1991), Speed (1994), Dangerous Liaisons (1988) and My Own Private Idaho (1991). 
 
His later film roles include the John Wick films and The Day the Earth Stood Still (2008).

name: Peter Jackson
about: Best known as the director and producer of his adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien's   trilogy, which won 17 out of 30 total Academy Award nominations.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
about: Inventor of the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee implemented the first successful communication between a Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) client and server via the Internet.

name: Al Gore
mainType: Vice President of the United States
about: Al Gore is an American politician who served as the 45th vice president of the United States from 1993 to 2001 in the administration of President  . Prior to his vice presidency, he served both in the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives.

name: Andrew Lloyd Webber
about: Andrew Lloyd Webber is an English composer best known for his involvement in musical theatre, with several productions seeing major long-term success in the West End and on Broadway. Some of his musical compositions have also been successful outside of the musical in which they initially featured.

name: Barry Gibb
homePlace: Douglas, Isle of Man, United Kingdom
about: Known as the falsetto voice of the  , Gibb co-founded and co-wrote many of the group's enduring hits along with brothers   and  .

name: Jordan Peterson
about: Peterson, a clinical psychologist at the University of Toronto, first came to public prominence in 2016 after posting a series of YouTube videos criticizing political correctness and the introduction of a law that would add gender identity as protected grounds for discrimination in Canada.

name: Vince Gill
about: Vince Gill is an American country singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. He has achieved commercial success and fame both as a solo artist and as a member of the country rock band Pure Prairie League. In his career, Gill has won 20 Grammy Awards, more than any other male country artist.

name: Charles III
about: King Charles III is the monarch of the United Kingdom and Commonwealth realms. He became king in 2022 after serving as heir apparent for over 70 years.

name: Michael Jordan
about:
Widely considered the greatest basketball player of all, Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984, rapidly establishing himself as a leading NBA player known for his high scoring and leaping.  
 
Jordan helped the bulls win the national championship in 1991, 1992 and 1993. He was also won two Olympic gold medals as part America's dream team.

name: Andrés Manuel López Obrador
about:
Andrés Manuel López Obrador, also known by his initials AMLO, was President of Mexico between 2018 and 2024.  
 
AMLO also server as the Head of Government of Mexico City between 2000 and 2005.

name: Jon Bon Jovi
about: Jon   is an American singer and songwriter, best known as founder of the band Bon Jovi. The band, which formed in 1983, has released 15 studio albums and Bon Jovi himself has released two solo albums.

name: Sting
about: Gordon Matthew Thomas Sumner, known professionally as Sting, first came to fame as the frontman of the rock band The Police and later established a successful solo career.

name: Chaka Khan
about: Chaka Khan has won ten Grammy Awards and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2023.

name: Bono
about: The lead singer of the Irish rock group U2 alongside band members Larry Mullen,  , and the Edge. The group formed as teenagers in 1976 and released their first album "Boy" in 1980.

name: Ken Follett
about:
Ken Follett is a British author known for his best-selling thrillers and historical novels, which have sold over 160 million copies worldwide.  
 
His works have regularly reached the number-one position on the New York Times Best Seller list, including "A Dangerous Fortune" (1993) and "The Key to Rebecca" (1980).

name: Whoopi Goldberg
about: Whoopi Goldberg is one of only 16 people to achieve EGOT status, winning Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards. Goldberg's career spans decades, marked by her comedic talent and dramatic performances.

name: Peter Agre
about: Peter Agre is an American physician and molecular biologist best known for his discovery of aquaporins, proteins that allow water to move through cell membranes. This earned Agre the 2003 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, which he shared with Roderick MacKinnon.

name: Steve Wozniak
about:
Wozniak played an important part in the personal computer revolution of the 1970s. 
 
With  , "Woz" co-founded Apple Computer in the garage of Jobs' parents house in Cupertino, California  
 
The company's first product was the Apple I personal computer kit that Wozniak single handedly-designed and built by hand.

name: Vladimir Putin
about: Putin has been in his second term as the President of Russia since 2012, having served a previous term from 2000 until 2008. Between 2008 and 2012 he served as prime minister in the cabinet of President  .

name: Billy Joel
about: Billy Joel was born and raised in New York City.  He started piano lessons at age 4.  His parents divorced when he was 8, leaving his mother to raise him and his sister alone, as his father relocated to Vienna, Austria.  Seeing The Beatles on The   Show inspired him to pursue a career in pop music.

name: Robert Plant
about:
Lead vocalist and lyricist of the rock band Led Zeppelin.  
 
With a career spanning more than 40 years and possessing a powerful wide vocal range (particularly using his trademark high-pitched vocals), he is regarded as one of the greatest singers in the history of rock and roll.

name: Quentin Tarantino
about: Widely regarded as one of the best filmmakers of his generation, Tarantino's popular career began with the success of Reservoir Dogs in 1992. The release of   in 1994 boosted his career and the film was a major commercial and critical success.

name: Stevie Wonder
about: Blind soon after birth, Stevland Morris (Wonder) was a child prodigy, signed to Motown records in 1961 at age 11 and given the stage name 'Little Stevie Wonder'. He gained fame in 1963 with the No. 1 hit 'Fingertips - Part 2".

name: Douglas Adams
about: Douglas Adams was an English author best known for 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy' which began as a BBC radio series before becoming first a novel. In 2005 it was made into a major film featuring   and  , among others.

name: Benazir Bhutto
about: Benazir Bhutto served as Prime Minister of Pakistan for two non-consecutive terms. She was the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country, breaking new ground in a conservative society.

name: Olga Korbut
about: Olga Korbut burst onto the world gymnastic scene at the 1972 Munich Olympics and revolutionizing women's gymnastics in the process.

name: Paul Krugman
about: Paul Krugman is an American economist and public intellectual. He is a professor at the City University of New York and writes a column for The New York Times. In 2008, Krugman won the Nobel Prize in Economics for his work on international trade and economic geography.

name: Bill Belichick
about:
Coaching continuously in various roles in the NFL since 1975, he earned his first head coaching job with the Cleveland Browns in 1991.  
 
In 2000, he became head coach of the New England Patriots, a team he has coached to five Super Bowl appearances and three victories.  
 
He also won two Super Bowls as the defensive coordinator of the New York Giants.

name: Osama bin Laden
about: Born into a wealthy Saudi Arabian family bin Laden joined and helped fund mujahideen forces in Afghanistan against the Soviets before founding al-Qaeda in 1988.

name: Jack Ma
about: Jack Ma is a Chinese business magnate, philanthropist, and former executive chairman of Alibaba Group, a multinational conglomerate specializing in e-commerce, retail, internet, and technology. Ma co-founded Alibaba with 17 other people in 1999, creating one of the world's most impactful e-commerce platforms, which significantly revolutionized the way business is done in China and beyond.

name: Hugo Chávez
about: Hugo Chávez rose to prominence as a military officer before founding the Revolutionary Bolivarian Movement-200 in an attempt to overthrow the government in 1992. After a jail sentence he formed the socialist political party the Fifth Republic Movement and was elected President in 1998.

name: James Hetfield
about: James Hetfield founded heavy metal band   with   in Los Angeles in 1981. He performs as lead vocalist and on rhythm guitar. As the bands main songwriter he is responsible for such anthems as "Enter Sandman" and "The Memory Remains".

name: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar is an American basketball player known for his prolific career in the NBA, winning six championships and until 2023 holding the record for the league's all-time leading scorer when he was overtaken by  .

name: Viktor Yushchenko
homePlace: Khoruzhivka, Sumy Oblast, Ukrainian SSRSoviet Union, Soviet Union
about: Viktor Yushchenko is a Ukrainian politician best known for serving as the third President of Ukraine from 2005 to 2010. Yushchenko was a significant figure during a turbulent period in Ukrainian history, characterized by his struggle for democratic values, economic reforms, and stronger ties with the West.

name: Linda Ronstadt
about: Ronstadt retired in 2011 after an immensely popular career in which she won, among others, twelve Grammy Awards (including Lifetime Achievement), an Emmy, and two American Country Music awards. She has released 24 studio albums and 14 compilation albums, including many top-40 singles and a single number one: "You're No Good".

name: Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán
about: Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán is best known for leading the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking organizations in the world, and for his several high-profile prison escapes. Since 2016, however, he has been incarcerated in the United States.

name: Bryan Adams
about: One of the world's best-selling music artists and Canadian rock artist of all time. Reckless and (Everything I Do) I Do It for You, best-selling singles.

name: Andrea Bocelli
about: Andrea Bocelli is an Italian tenor and multi-instrumentalist, known for his massive popular success and for the fact that he has been blind since age 12 when he suffered a brain hemorrhage after a football accident.

name: Brian Kobilka
about: Brian Kobilka is an American physician and scientist recognized for his significant contributions to understanding G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with   for their work on these crucial proteins. GPCRs are a large family of receptors that play a fundamental role in many biological processes and are targets for a large portion of modern medicinal drugs.

name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
about:
Austrian-born, becoming a naturalised US Citizen in 1983 Arnold Schwarzenegger won Mr Olympia 7 times.  
 
A successful business man he became a film star in action films, including the Conan and Terminator series.  
 
As a Republican he became Governor of California in 2003 and served 2 terms until 2011. Hasta la vista, baby.

name: Jamie Dimon
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Jamie Dimon is an influential American banker and the current Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan Chase, one of the largest and most prominent banks in the United States.

name: Phil Collins
about: Phil Collins began his career as the drummer and occasional singer for the progressive rock band Genesis alongside Mike Rutherfield and  .

name: Elle MacPherson
about: Elle Macpherson is an Australian supermodel, businesswoman, television host, and actress best known for her record five cover appearances for the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue in the 1980s. These features earned her the nickname "The Body" from Time magazine in 1989.

name: Steve Jobs
about: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple Inc and played a key role in revolutionizing personal computing, mobile phones, and digital animation. As CEO of Apple, he oversaw the introduction of the iMac, iTunes, iPod, iPad and the iPhone—and under his leadership they became the most valuable company in the world.

name: Bruce Springsteen
about: Nicknamed "The Boss", Springsteen is an iconic fixture of American music. His style concentrates on his distinctive voice and lyrics often concerning working class Americans. His tours, often with the E Street Band, are noted for their energetic performances and often long length.

name: Liza Minnelli
about:
Rose to international stardom for her appearance as Sally Bowles in the 1972 film version of the Broadway musical "Cabaret", for which she won the Academy Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role.  
 
In total, Minnelli has won four Tony Awards, an Oscar, the Emmy Award, and two Golden Globes.

name: Jet Li
about:
Won great acclaim in China as an actor making his debut with the film "Shaolin Temple" (1982). He went on to star in many critically acclaimed martial arts epic films such as "Hero" (2002) and the "Once Upon a Time in China" series (1991–1993). 
 
His first role in a Hollywood film was as a villain in "Lethal Weapon 4" (1998), and his first leading role in a Hollywood film was as Han Sing in "Romeo Must Die" (2000).

name: Narendra Modi
about: The 15th and current Prime Minister of India. Prior to holding this office he was the Chief Minister of Gujarat from 2001 to 2014. Modi was a highly controversial figure in this role, particularly over allegations that he was complicity in the 2002 riots in which over 1,000 Muslims were killed.

name: Sid Meier
about: Sid Meier is best known for creating the Civilization series, which lets players guide a civilization from ancient times to the future.

name: Bill Gates
about: Gates co-founded Microsoft in 1975 along with  .

name: Sally Ride
about: Sally Ride was the first American woman in space and the youngest American astronaut, a feat which she achieved in 1983 at the age of 32.

name: Bobby Sands
homePlace: Newtownabbey, County Antrim,, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom
about: Bobby Sands was an Irish revolutionary who was a member of the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) and a leader among political prisoners during the Troubles in Northern Ireland. His conviction for firearms possession in 1977 led to a prison sentence at the Maze Prison. In prison, Sands led the prisoners in a protest against the removal of Special Category Status for convicted paramilitary prisoners, a change which meant they would be treated as ordinary criminals rather than prisoners of war.

name: Elton John
about: Elton John is an iconic English singer, songwriter, pianist, and composer. With a career spanning more than five decades, he's one of the best-selling music artists in the world, boasting numerous hit singles and albums.

name: Enya
about: Enya is an Irish singer, songwriter, and musician, celebrated for her unique blend of Celtic, ambient, and pop music. Her ethereal melodies and multilayered vocals have captivated audiences worldwide, making her one of the best-selling music artists of all time.

name: Jeremy Clarkson
about: Jeremy Clarkson is known for his work in automotive television. He gained worldwide fame as a presenter on the BBC show "Top Gear" (2002-2015).

name: Joy Harjo
about: Joy Harjo is a Native American poet, musician, and author whose poetry explores Native American identity, history, and spirituality. She has served as the United States Poet Laureate and received prestigious awards such as the Bollingen Prize for American Poetry.

name: Bill Clinton
about: Governor of Arkansas he became the first two-term Democratic President since FDR serving 1993-2001. Oversaw a period of strong economic prosperity in the US, and signed the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).

name: Jason Newsted
about: Known for playing bass guitar with the bands  , Voivod and Flotsam and Jetsam. Joining Metallica in 1986 after Cliff Burton's death, he remained a member until 2001, making him the band's longest-serving bassist.

name: Al Unser Jr.
about: Nicknamed "Little Al" to distinguish him from his father  , Al Unser Jr. is an American racing driver, best known for winning the Indianapolis 500 twice.

name: Cher
about: A hugely successful American entertainer, Cher is a pop singer, TV host, nightclub star and acclaimed actress.

name: Barack Obama
about: Barack Obama served as the 44th President of the United States (2009-2017). Previously he was a Senator from Illinois before a 2004 speech at the Democratic National Convention cast him into the spotlight, leading to a successful 2008 presidential campaign.

name: Matt Groening
about: Matt Groening is an influential American cartoonist, writer, and producer, best known as the creator of the animated television series  , the longest-running American sitcom and animated program. His distinct art style, humor, and storytelling approach have made him a significant figure in modern pop culture.

name: Pete Farndon
about: Pete Farndon was one of the founding members of American British rock band The  , along with  , James Honeyman-Scott and Martin Chambers.

name: Ray Kurzweil
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Ray Kurzweil is an American inventor, futurist, and computer scientist who has made significant contributions to the fields of artificial intelligence, pattern recognition, and technology forecasting. He is best known for his predictions about the future of technology and human society, as well as his development of various groundbreaking technologies, including optical character recognition (OCR), text-to-speech synthesis, and speech recognition systems.

name: Carole Bayer Sager
about: Carole Bayer Sager has written hit songs for many famous performers and won multiple awards for her work.

name: Cat Stevens
about: English singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, humanitarian, and education philanthropist.

name: Ayrton Senna
about:
Widely regarded as one of the greatest Formula 1 drivers of all time, Senna won three Formula One world championships for McLaren in 1988, 1990 and 1991, as well as a slew of other victories in various races. 
 
His death during a race in 1994 led to widespread global mourning and was considered by many Brazilians to be a national tragedy. Almost three million people gathered in São Paulo during his funeral, the largest gathering of mourners in modern times.

name: Donald Trump
about: Trump gained fame as a real estate developer and a reality television host. He was previously chairman of The Trump Organization and the host of The Apprentice. Long expressing an interest in national politics, he announced his run for President of the United States in 2015. Despite a campaign that courted numerous controversies, he was selected as the Republican presidential candidate in July 2016. After an exceptionally bitter and divisive election campaign, he then went on to beat   in a huge upset.

name: Xi Jinping
about: General Secretary of the Communist Party of China from 2012 and President of the People's Republic of China from 2013.

name: Keith Haring
about: Social activist and artist whose work responded to the New York City street culture of the 1980s by expressing concepts of birth, death, sexuality, and war, and was often heavily political.

name: Dave Winfield
about: Dave Winfield was a star outfielder in Major League Baseball during the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s.

name: Fred Couples
about: Fred Couples is an American professional golfer who made his mark in both the PGA Tour and the PGA Tour Champions, earning the nickname "Boom Boom" for his the accuracy and distance of his driving.

name: Al Sharpton
about: Al Sharpton is an American civil rights activist, Baptist minister, and media personality. He is a founder of the National Action Network and campaigned for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2004. He also hosts a radio show, Keepin' It Real, and a television program on MSNBC, PoliticsNation.

name: Tommy Lee
about:
Tommy Lee is an American musician known as a founding member and drummer of the heavy-metal band Mötley Crüe, alongside bassist  , guitarist Mick Mars, and lead singer Vince Neil.  
 
The group has sold over 100 million albums worldwide since their formation in 1981.

name: Linus Torvalds
about: Linus Torvalds is the creator of the Linux operating system kernel, which forms the core of many computer systems worldwide. He is also known for developing Git, a widely used version control system.

name: Charlize Theron
about: Born in South Africa, Theron emigrated to Italy and worked as model, and then to America to pursue a career in film. She worked in a variety of genres, garnering praise in "Cider House Rules" (1999), and winning an Academy Award for Best Actress in "Monster" (2003).  She continues to work in film on screen, and occasionally as a producer.

name: Lisa Marie Presley
about:
The only child of  , she has conducted a long career in the music business and has issued several albums and videos.  
 
Her work as a vocalist and lyricist has ranged across rock, country, blues and folk.

name: Salma Hayek
about: Salma Hayek is known for her breakthrough role in the 1995 film "Desperado" and her Academy Award-nominated portrayal of artist   in the 2002 biopic "Frida."

name: P!nk
about:
One of the most successful artists of her generation, having sold over 45 million albums, including nearly 16 million in the United States, and 65 million singles worldwide as of 2014.  
 
Career accolades include three Grammy Awards, a Brit Award, and six MTV Video Music Awards.

name: Vitali Klitschko
about: Klitschko first came to world renown with his brother   as half of a star-studded pair in the world of professional heavyweight boxing. The two hold the Guinness World Record for brothers with the most heavyweight title wins: 40 as of 2020.

name: Thalía
about: One of the most influential and famous Mexican artists in the world, Thalía has not limited herself to Spanish, also singing songs in English, French, Portuguese and Tagalog. She has often been referred to as the "Queen of Latin Pop" as a result of her success.

name: Timothy McVeigh
about: A veteran of the Gulf War, McVeigh was convicted of carrying out he 1995 Oklahoma City bombing in which 168 people were killed.

name: Claudia Schiffer
about: Claudia Schiffer was one of the most recognizable faces in fashion during the 1990s. She holds a Guinness World Record for appearing on the most magazine covers.

name: Catherine Zeta-Jones
about: Catherine Zeta-Jones has won an Academy Award for her performance in "Chicago" (2002) and a Tony Award for her role in "A Little Night Music" (2009).

name: Faith Hill
about: Faith Hill is an American country and pop singer who rose to fame in the 1990s with her debut album Take Me as I Am (1993). This was followed by a string of other successful albums including Faith (1998) and Breathe (1999), as well as hit singles including "This Kiss," "Breathe," and "The Way You Love Me."

name: Julia Roberts
about:
Became a Hollywood star after headlining the romantic comedy "Pretty Women", which grossed $464 million worldwide.  
 
She also won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her performance in "Erin Brockovich".

name: Sachin Tendulkar
about: Sachin Tendulkar is widely regarded as one of the greatest batsmen in the history of cricket. He holds numerous records in both Test and One Day International (ODI) cricket.

name: Johnny Galecki
about: Johnny was a child actor with a long career in film and television before landing the part of Leonard Hofstadter in the TV sitcom "The  " which ran for 12 seasons between 2007 to 2019.

name: Tonya Harding
about: Harding is an American figure skater, best known for her controversial involvement in an attack on her rival,  , which was carried out by her ex-husband.

name: Alison Krauss
about:
Tied with   as the most awarded living recipient of Grammys - 27 in total - Krauss performs bluegrass and country with her band Union Station.  
 
Her soundtrack to the hit film "O Brother, Where Art Thou?" sparked a revival in American blugrass, and in 2007 she won Album of the Year for "Raising Sand", a duet with Led Zeppelin lead singer  .

name: J. J. Abrams
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about:
Known for his high quality work in the genres of action, science fiction and drama. He was the co-creator of a number of several television series, including Felicity, Alias, Lost and Fringe. 
 
His work as a director includes Mission: Impossible III (2006), Star Trek (2009), its sequel Star Trek: Into Darkness (2013), Super 8 (2011) and the first film in the   reboot, The Force Awakens (2015).

name: Nelly Furtado
about: Nelly Furtado is a Canadian singer-songwriter and record producer. She is a multi-platinum and Grammy Award-winning artist who has sold over 20 million albums worldwide.

name: John Carmack
about: John Carmack is renowned for his work in video game development and virtual reality. He co-founded id Software and served as the lead programmer for groundbreaking games such as Wolfenstein, Doom, and Quake.

name: Jack Dorsey
about: Jack Dorsey is an American entrepreneur who co-founded two major platforms, Twitter and Square. As a young man, Dorsey developed a keen interest in computers and programming, paving the way for him to create Twitter, a platform that reshaped the world of communication.

name: John Mayer
about: John Mayer is an American singer-songwriter and musician. Mayer achieved commercial success with early albums such as Room for Squares (2001) and Heavier Things (2003) and went on to win seven Grammy Awards. He formed the John Mayer Trio, exploring blues traditions, and later collaborated with surviving members of the Grateful Dead in Dead & Company.

name: Tammy Duckworth
about: Tammy Duckworth is an American politician and retired military officer who has served as the junior United States Senator from Illinois since 2017. A member of the Democratic Party, she was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2012 and to the U.S. Senate in 2016, becoming the first Thai-American woman to be elected to Congress.

name: Mike Tyson
about: Michael Tyson is a former undisputed heavyweight champion of the world and holds the record as the youngest boxer to win the WBC, WBA and IBF heavyweight titles at 20 years, 4 months, and 22 days old.

name: Usher
about:
Rose to fame in the late 1990s with the release of his second album "My Way".  
 
His 2004 album, "Confessions", sold over 20 million copies worldwide, and established him as one of the best-selling musical artist of the 2000s decade.

name: Fergie
about: Fergie is an American singer, songwriter, and actress best known as the female vocalist for the hip-hop group The Black Eyed Peas. She joined the group in 2002, and her presence was pivotal in catapulting the band to international fame with hits like Where Is the Love? and My Humps.

name: Sadiq Khan
about: Sadiq Khan is a British politician and current Mayor of London, having served in this role since 2016 when he defeated Zac Goldsmith, the Conservative candidate, in the election. Prior to this, Khan had been a Member of Parliament and member of the Shadow Cabinet under Ed Miliband.

name: Brooke Shields
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Initially a child model, she gained critical acclaim for her leading role in Louis Malle's controversial film Pretty Baby, in which she played a child prostitute in New Orleans at the turn of the 20th century.

name: Lennox Lewis
homePlace: West Ham, London, England, United Kingdom
about:
Regarded by many as one of the greatest heavyweight boxers of all time. 
 
As an amateur he won gold representing Canada at the 1988 Olympic Games after defeating future heavyweight champion   in the final.  
 
Lewis became the undisputed world heavyweight champion in 1999 after he defeated  .

name: Lance Armstrong
about:
American professional road cyclist who won a (then) record 7 Tour de France titles between 1999 and 2005.  After several investigations, he was stripped of his competitive achievements and barred from all professional sport for using illicit performance-enhancing drugs. 
 
Also known for founding the Lance Armstrong Foundation (now Livestrong) for people affected by cancer after surviving metastatic testicular cancer himself.

name: Jada Pinkett Smith
about:
Jada Pinkett Smith is an American actress who has featured in more than 20 films including "Set it Off", "Nutty Professor" and "Menace II Society."  
 
Pinkett Smith is also a voice actor and features in the "Madagascar" films. She is also well known for her marriage to fellow actor  .

name: Adam Sandler
about: Adam Sandler is an American comedian who came to fame with Saturday Night Live during the 1990s, and has since starred in a number of major films. His best known roles include Billy Madison (1995), Happy Gilmore (1996), The Waterboy (1998), and Click (2006).

name: Dwayne Johnson
about: He is widely considered one of the all-time greatest professional wrestlers. The Rock wrestled for eight years for the World Wrestling Federation (WWF, now WWE) before beginning his film career.

name: Macaulay Culkin
homePlace: New York City, New York, USA
about: Macaulay Culkin gained worldwide fame as a child star in the 1990s. He is best known for his role as Kevin McCallister in the " " film series.

name: Jennifer Lopez
about: American entertainer who started as a dancer on television's "In Living Color" before branching out into acting and music. Known familiarly as J. Lo", she has recorded pop-dance songs in English and Spanish, selling over 70 million records worldwide.

name: Travis Barker
about: Travis Barker is an American musician best known as the drummer of rock band Blink 182. He joined the band in 1998, a year before it achieved major mainstream success with Enema of the State (1999).

name: Christina Applegate
about: Christina Applegate is best known for her work in television and film, for which she has won an Emmy Award and received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

name: Jennifer Garner
about: Gained recognition for her performance as CIA officer Sydney Bristow in the ABC thriller drama series "Alias", which aired for five seasons from 2001 to 2006. For her work on the series, she won a Golden Globe.

name: Noel Gallagher
about:
Served as the lead guitarist, occasional lead singer and principal songwriter of the British rock band Oasis.  
 
Gallagher is often regarded as the spear-head of the Britpop movement.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
about: Has hosted the eponymous late-night television talk show "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" on ABC since 2003.

name: Harry Connick Jr
about: American singer, musician and actor Harry Connick, Jr. was born in New Orleans to two lawyers that also owned a record store.  He was a prodigy at the piano, first performing in public at age 5, with the New Orleans Symphony at 9, and recording with a jazz band at 10.   Connick has sold over 28 million albums worldwide. Ranked among the top 60 best-selling male artists in the United States by the Recording Industry Association of America, with 16 million in certified sales.

name: John Cena
about: Cena is considered by many to be the greatest and most popular wrestler in the history of the WWE, though he has many supporters and detractors. The winner of 25 championships in his career, he was the sport's most prolific figure and franchise player for many years in the 2000s and 2010s.

name: Enrique Iglesias
about: Enrique Iglesias is a Spanish singer, songwriter, actor, and record producer. Known for his romantic ballads and energetic dance tracks, Iglesias has been referred to as the "King of Latin Pop."
