about: George Hamilton-Gordon, 4th earl of Aberdeen was British Prime Minister for just 3 years 1852-55, before this he served as diplomat and in various ministerial posts.

name: Alec Douglas-Home
about: Alec Douglas-Home became Prime Minister unexpectedly in 1963 when   resigned in the wake of the Profumo affair.

name: Harold Wilson
about: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1964 to 1970 and 1974 to 1976, Wilson was a moderate socialist who placed emphasis on increasing opportunity within society,

name: Charles Watson-Wentworth
about: Charles Watson-Wentworth, commonly known as the Marquess of Rockingham, was a British statesman and two-time Prime Minister in the mid-18th century. He first served as Prime Minister from 1765 to 1766 and then again in 1782, though his second term was cut short by his sudden death.

name: Bonar Law
homePlace: Kingston, Colony of New Brunswick, Canada
about: Bonar Law was a British Conservative politician who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from October 1922 to May 1923. Despite his relatively brief term, he is notable for being the only Prime Minister to have been born outside the British Isles, in New Brunswick, which was then a British colony in North America.

name: Henry John Temple
about: British statesman who served twice as Prime Minister in the mid-19th century. Nicknamed "Pam" and "The Mongoose", he was in government office almost continuously from 1807 until his death in 1865.

name: Thomas Pelham-Holles
about: Thomas Pelham-Holles, 1st Duke of Newcastle, dominated Whig politics in the 18th century. He served in various high offices for over 40 years and became Prime Minister twice.

name: Edward Heath
about: Heath served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1970 to 1974, and was leader of the Conservative Party from 1965 to 1975 when he was replaced by  .

name: William Grenville
homePlace: Wotton Underwood, Buckinghamshire, England, United Kingdom
about: William Grenville was the son of an earlier British Prime Minister   (1763-65) and the cousin of William Pitt.

name: William Gladstone
about: Glastone served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for twelve years through four non-consecutive times between 1868 and 1894. Prior to this he served as Chancellor of the Exchequer. His popularity among the working classes earned him the nickname 'The People's William.'

name: Spencer Perceval
about: Perceval served as British Prime Minister from 1809 until his assassination in 1812; he is to date the only British PM to have been murdered. Prior to serving in this position he was the Chancellor of the Exchequer.

name: William Pitt the Younger
about: The second son of Prime Minister  , William Pitt the Younger is the youngest ever British Minister, aged just 24, when he was appointed by King  .

name: Robert Peel
about: Peel served twice as Prime Minister of Britain (1834-1835, 1841-1846) and as Home Secretary (1822-1827, 1828-30), Widely regarded as the father of modern British policing and as one of the founders the modern Conservative Party, he is immortalized by the affectionate slang expressions 'bobby' and 'peeler' due to his creating the modern concept of the police force whilst Home Secretary.

name: Benjamin Disraeli
about: British statesman who twice served as Prime Minister, Disraeli played a central role in the creation of the modern Conservative Party.

name: Harold Macmillan
about: After serving in the First World War Harold Macmillan entered parliament in 1924. He served in  's war cabinet and opposed appeasement of Nazi Germany.

name: Clement Attlee
about: Attlee served as the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1945 to 1951, and as the Leader of the Labour Party from 1935 to 1955. He came into office months after the end of World War II in Europe after an unexpected landslide victory forced   from office.

name: George Grenville
homePlace: Wotton Underwood, Buckinghamshire, England, United Kingdom
about: George Grenville was born into a political family. His father was an MP and Grenville entered parliament himself in 1741 as MP for Buckingham, a seat he held until his death in 1770.

name: Ramsay MacDonald
about: Elected in 1924 as the first British Labour Party Prime Minister with Liberal Party support. In government he was widely applauded for his moderation and his support of the League of Nations winning the Labour Party praise for its competency.

name: William Pitt the Elder
about: William Pitt the Elder served as Prime Minister from 1766 to 1768. He is best known for leading Britain to victory in the Seven Years' War, establishing British global dominance. Pitt was a gifted orator, earning the nickname "The Great Commoner" for his ability to sway public opinion and parliament with his speeches.

name: Anthony Eden
about: Anthony Eden became British Prime Minister after  's resignation in 1955. Prior to this he had been Foreign Secretary during the Second World War and the Cold War.

name: David Lloyd George
about: As British Prime Minister from 1916 to 1922 he helped laid the foundations of the modern welfare state.

name: Robert Walpole
about: One of the greatest politicians in British history, Walpole served as the first Prime Minister of Great Britain and dominated the government from 1721 to 1742.

name: H. H. Asquith
about: Herbert Henry Asquith, commonly known as H. H. Asquith, was a British statesman and a member of the Liberal Party who served as the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1908 to 1916. He was a key figure in the early 20th century British politics and played a significant role in the reform of the British parliamentary system and shaping of the modern welfare state.

name: Robert Gascoyne-Cecil
about: Commonly known as Lord Salisbury, he served a total of thirteen years as Prime Minister across three different terms. Before being Prime Minister, Salisbury served in a series of high profile positions, including Secretary of State for India and Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs.

name: Henry Addington
about: The son of a physician, Henry Addington's rise in political life after becoming an MP in 1789 was aided by his childhood friendship with  .

name: Charles Grey
about: Charles Grey, 2nd Earl Grey, served as Prime Minister from 1830 to 1834. He is known for his role in passing the Reform Act of 1832 and for the tea that bears his name.

name: Neville Chamberlain
about: Chamberlain served as British Prime Minister from 1937 to 1940, and his government was dominated by the crisis over Nazi Germany's aggressive moves in Europe. He is remembered today principally for his failed efforts to appease  , particularly through signing the Munich Agreement in 1938 which ceded parts of Czechoslovakia to Germany.

name: William Cavendish-Bentinck
about: William Cavendish-Bentinch, Duke of Portland was a Whig politician who was Prime Minister twice, with a record 24 years between each term of office.

name: Arthur Wellesley
about:
Commonly known as the Duke of Wellington, Wellesley was a leading military and political figure of the 19th century. His defeat of   in 1815 at Waterloo made him a heroic national figure and top military hero in British history. 
 
He was less successful as prime minister, though he did pass the Catholic Relief Act of 1829. He served two terms - between 1828 and 1830, and for one month in 1834.

name: Margaret Thatcher
about: First female British Prime Minister, known as 'The Iron Lady'. While in office her policies became known as Thatcherism, with an emphasis on deregulation, free markets and the privatization of state-owned companies. While support for her government fell in the first term due to high unemployment and recession, her victory in the 1982 Falklands War with Argentina brought her into power in the following year's election.

name: Arthur Balfour
homePlace: Whittingehame House, East Lothian, Scotland, United Kingdom
about:
British Conservative politician who was Prime Minister from July 1902 to December 1905. 
 
As Foreign Secretary he became famous for writing the Balfour Declaration which proclaimed support for a Jewish state in Palestine.

name: Winston Churchill
about: Regularly regarded as one of the greatest British prime ministers, Churchill led Britain to victory against the Axis Powers during World War II, and served a second term in office from 1951 to 1955.

name: Hudson Fysh
about: Co-founder of QANTAS (Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services Limited) and World War I veteran.

name: Sergei Korolev
homePlace: Zhytomyr, Volhynian Governorate, Russian Empire (now Ukraine)
about: Sergei Korolev was a Soviet engineer and pioneering figure in space exploration, leading the Soviet Union's space program during the height of the Space Race. As the lead rocket engineer and spacecraft designer, he played a pivotal role in launching the first human-made object, Sputnik, into space in 1957, and subsequently the first human,  , in 1961.

name: Walter Mittelholzer
about:
Walter Mittelholzer was a Swiss aviation pioneer, who first earned his pilot's license in 1917. He then founded a photography and passenger flight business, which would after later mergers go on to become Swissair. 
 
Mittelholzer was the first pilot to complete a north-south flight across the whole of Africa, a feat which took him 77 days. He was also the first person to fly over Mount Kilimanjaro, and intended to fly over Mount Everest also in 1930.

name: Wiley Post
homePlace: Corinth, Van Zandt County, Texas, USA
about: Wiley Post was the first pilot to fly solo around the world. He made significant contributions to high-altitude flight and helped develop one of the first pressure suits. Post also discovered the jet stream, a fast-flowing air current in the atmosphere.

name: Noel Wien
about: The founder of Wien Air Alaska, Alaska's first airline, he introduced the airplane to Alaska, which over the years became the primary mode of transport in the vast and thinly populated state.

name: Francis Chichester
about: Francis Chichester was a British aviator and sailor known for his daring feats of navigation in the mid-20th century. His love for adventure and challenge was evident early on, as he became a pioneer in aviation and later turned to sailing as a profession.

name: Pappy Boyington
about: Pappy Boyington was a United States Marine Corps officer who was a fighter pilot during World War II. He was awarded the Medal of Honor for leading his squadron in combat against Japanese forces in the Pacific theater.

name: David McCampbell
about: David McCampbell was an American naval aviator and war hero best known for being the United States Navy's all-time leading flying ace and top F6F Hellcat ace. He was awarded the Medal of Honor for his exploits in World War II, and his leadership played a significant role in the success of Air Group 15 in the Pacific War.

name: Billy Bishop
about:
The top Canadian flying ace during World War One, Billy Bishop is officially credited with 72 victories.  
 
During World War Two, he was instrumental in establishing the British Commonwealth Air Training Plan.

name: William Boeing
about: Boeing founded The Boeing Company in 1916, which today has grown to be among the largest aircraft producers in the world, with iconic aircraft such as the Boeing 747.

name: Howard Hughes
about: Howard Hughes is known for his eccentricities as much as for his achievements, which were many. Hughes was a Hollywood filmmaker, an aviator, real estate mogul and philanthropist.

name: Robert H. Goddard
about: Robert H. Goddard is the father of modern rocketry. He made many fundamental contributions to rocket science that ultimately laid the foundation for space exploration in the long-term.

name: Orville Wright
about: Orville Wright, together with his brother  , revolutionized transportation with the invention of the airplane.

name: Amy Johnson
about: Amy Johnson was an English pilot, best known as the first woman to fly solo from London to Australia. She set a number of records, many solo but also with her husband Jim Mollison, as well as flying in the Second World War.

name: Richard E. Byrd
about: A pioneering American aviator and polar explorer, Richard E. Byrd claimed that his expeditions had been the first to reach both the North Pole and the South Pole by air.

name: Eugene Bullard
about: Eugene Bullard was an African American pilot who flew for the French during World War I. He was one of the first black military pilots in the world.

name: Jean Batten
about: Jean Batten set several long-distance flight records in the 1930s. She became famous for her solo flights between England and Australia, and later for her flight from England to New Zealand.

name: Wilbur Wright
about: Wilbur Wright, in collaboration with his younger brother  , changed the course of human history with the invention of the first successful airplane. Together, the Wright brothers' tenacity, curiosity, and mechanical ingenuity pioneered the dawn of aviation.

name: Claude Grahame-White
about: Grahame-White was an early aviation pioneer, one of the first people to qualify as a pilot in England after training at Louis Blériot’s flying school. He entered in a number of competitions, including a 1910 Daily Mail-sponsored air race between London and Manchester.

name: Jimmy Doolittle
about: One of the most famous pilots during the inter-war period, he made many pioneering flights. During the Second World War, he served as an officer in the United States Army Air Forces, and earned the Medal of Honor for his valor and leadership.

name: Anne Morrow Lindbergh
about: Anne Morrow Lindbergh is a renowned 20th century aviator and author. She was born in 1906 in Englewood, New Jersey, to a wealthy and influential family. She attended Smith College and graduated with a degree in history in 1928.

name: Chuck Yeager
about: Chuck Yeager was a United States Air Force officer, flying ace, and test pilot. He was the first pilot to exceed the speed of sound in level flight, a feat which he achieved in October 1947.

name: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
about: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry is best known for his novella "The Little Prince" (1943) and for his lyrical aviation writings, including "Wind, Sand and Stars" (1939) and "Night Flight" (1931).

name: Charles Lindbergh
about: Charles Lindbergh was an American aviator celebrated for conducting the first solo, non-stop flight across the Atlantic Ocean. This significant achievement occurred in 1927 when Lindbergh successfully piloted the Spirit of St. Louis from New York to Paris. The flight took 33.5 hours and made Lindbergh an international hero.

name: Harry Ferguson
about: Henry George "Harry" Ferguson was an Irish mechanic and inventor. He played a pivotal role in the development of the modern agricultural tractor, invented the three-point linkage system, and was the first person in Ireland to build and fly his own aeroplane. He also developed the Ferguson P99, which was the first four-wheel-drive Formula One car.

name: The Red Baron
about:
German World War I fighter ace, credited with 80 air combat kills.  
 
Richthofen is considered the top fighter ace of the war. He was widely respected by his enemies and regarded as a national hero in Germany by 1918. 
 
History has recorded "The Red Baron" as one of the top fighter pilots of all time and thus he has become the subject of various books, songs and films.

name: Henri Farman
about:
Farman set several important records in the pioneering years of aviation, including the first officially observed circuit flight of 1km, 2km and the first cross-country flight from Châlons to Reims, all in the year 1908. 
 
He would later become a successful aircraft engineer and designer, making several important milestone development in aviation construction.

name: Anthony Fokker
homePlace: Blitar, East Java, Dutch East Indies
about: Anthony Fokker was a Dutch aviation pioneer and aircraft manufacturer who played a significant role in the development of military and civil aviation during the early 20th century. He founded Fokker Aeroplanbau, later known as Fokker Aircraft Company, which became one of the world's leading aircraft manufacturers during the first half of the 20th century.

name: Amelia Earhart
about: Amelia Earhart was an American aviator, whose pioneering efforts included being the first female pilot to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean. She further promoted commercial air travel as well as writing popular books about her flying experiences.

name: Sheila Scott
about:
Scott was the first British pilot to fly solo around the world, and broke more than 100 light-aircraft records between 1965 and 1972.  
 
Beginning her career as a nurse during WWII, Scott also worked as a model and an actress until 1960, when she earned her pilot’s license and bought an old biplane from the Royal Air Force. 
 
Scott first flew around the world in 1966, completing the trip in 189 flying hours. She was made an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 1968.

name: Guy Gibson
about: Guy Penrose Gibson was a British bomber pilot in the Royal Air Force during the Second World War. He was the first Commanding Officer of No. 617 Squadron, leading the "Dam Busters" raid in 1943, which breached two large dams in the Ruhr area of Germany. Gibson was awarded the Victoria Cross, the highest military decoration for valor. Over his career, he completed over 170 war operations before his death at age 26.

name: Harriet Quimby
about: Harriet Quimby was an American aviator, journalist, and screenwriter. She is best known for being the first woman in the United States to receive a pilot's license and the first woman to fly across the English Channel. Despite dying young at 37 in a flying accident, Quimby significantly impacted women's roles in aviation.

name: Igor Sikorsky
about: Designed and flew the world's first multi-engine fixed-wing aircraft and helicopter.

name: Bessie Coleman
about: Bessie Coleman was born in Atlanta, Texas, in 1892. Her parents were sharecroppers, and she was the tenth of their thirteen children. When she was two years old her family moved to Waxahachie, Texas.

name: Donald Wills Douglas
about: Douglas was an aviation pioneer who built the Douglas Cloudster, the first aircraft to have a payload greater than its own weight, but which failed in its intent to be the first to fly non-stop across the United States.

name: Adam Opel
about: Adam Opel founded the company Adam Opel AG. The business first made sewing machines and later moved into making bicycles, it would not make its first car until after Opel’s death.

name: W. O. Bentley
about: Founder of Bentley Motors Limited in London which he later sold to  .

name: William Lyons
about: Co-founder of the Swallow Sidecar Company in 1922, as Chairman William Lyons announced the company change of name to Jaguar Cars in 1945

name: Louis Chevrolet
about: Louis Chevrolet is best known for co-founding the Chevrolet Motor Car Company in 1911, which later became a part of General Motors.

name: Alec Issigonis
about: Alec Issigonis was a British-Greek automotive designer, best known for designing the Mini. This car, which has become iconic worldwide as a symbol of the British automotive industry, was created by Issigonis and launched in 1959 by the British Motor Corporation.

name: Ettore Bugatti
about: Ettore Bugatti founded the luxury car company Automobiles E. Bugatti in 1909 in Molsheim, France, which became renowned for its high-performance and technologically advanced vehicles.

name: Ferruccio Lamborghini
about: Ferruccio Lamborghini founded Lamborghini, the famous maker of sports cars and luxury vehicles. He was born into a family of grape farmers but he was more interested in mechanics than farming.

name: Armand Peugeot
about: Armand Peugeot played a key role in the development of the automobile industry in France. He came from a family of metalworkers and graduated from a prestigious engineering school. After a trip to England in 1881, Peugeot recognized the potential of bicycles and introduced their manufacture to his family's company.

name: Édouard Michelin
about: Édouard Michelin and his brother André turned their family's struggling business into a successful tire company.

name: Soichiro Honda
about: Soichiro Honda founded the Honda Motor Company, which became one of the world's largest motorcycle and automobile manufacturers.

name: Ferdinand Porsche
about: Ferdinand Porsche is best known for creating the Volkswagen Beetle, the Lohner-Porsche hybrid vehicle, and the Auto Union racing cars, as well as founding Porsche AG, the famous sports car company.

name: Nicolaus Otto
homePlace: Holzhausen an der Haide, Duchy of Nassau, German Confederation
about: Nicolaus August Otto invented the compressed charge internal combustion engine, which paved the way for the modern automobile engine.

name: Harlow Curtice
about:
After starting at the company aged 20, Harlow Curtice rose to become President of General Motors (GM), serving from 1953 to 1958.  
 
Under his leadership General Motors sold five million vehicles and became the first corporation to earn US$1 billion in a single year in 1955. A feat that saw Curtice named Time magazine's person of the year in 1955.

name: Enzo Ferrari
about: Enzo Ferrari was an Italian motor racing driver and entrepreneur, best known for founding the Scuderia Ferrari Grand Prix motor racing team and then the Ferrari automobile brand.

name: Henry Royce
about: Co-founder of car manufacturing and aerospace firm Rolls-Royce Limited with  .

name: Charles Rolls
about: Charles Rolls co-founded the Rolls-Royce company, along with  , and also set records as a pioneer in both ballooning and powered flight.

name: Karl Benz
about: Karl Benz was a German engine designer and engineer, regarded as the inventor of the first automobile powered by an internal combustion engine.

name: Elon Musk
about: Elon Musk is a billionaire entrepreneur and business magnate known for pushing the boundaries of technology. He has been instrumental in the success of several high-profile technology companies, beginning with Zip2, a company he co-founded with his brother Kimbal Musk in the late 1990s, and PayPal, a payment system company that was later sold to eBay for $1.5 billion in 2002.

name: Henry Ford
about: Henry Ford introduced the Model T Ford automobile in October 1908, the world's first mass-produced car. In producing an automobile for the middle classes instead of just for the wealthy, Henry Ford help change American society forever.

name: Gottlieb Daimler
about: Gottlieb Daimler had been working for the firm of the inventor of the internal-combustion engine Nikolaus A. Otto before he and colleague Wilhelm Maybach set out of their own in 1882.

name: August Horch
about: August Horch founded the company that eventually became Audi and played a significant role in the early German automotive industry.

name: Rudolf Diesel
about: Rudolf Diesel created the diesel engine. This engine, which bears his name, remains widely used in various forms of transportation and industrial machinery.

name: André Michelin
about:
Together with his brother  , André founded the Michelin Tyre Company in 1888 and revolutionized the automotive industry where their detachable-pneumatic automobile tires. 
 
He went on to publish the first Michelin Guide in 1900, a now famous hotel and restaurant reference guide.

name: Walter Chrysler
about: Walter Chrysler spent nearly 20 years of his working life working on the railways in ever more senior positions until Charles Nash, President of General Motors hired him to manage the Buick factory in Flint, Michigan.

name: John Curtin
about: John Curtin was an Australian politician who served as the 14th Prime Minister of Australia, from 1941 to 1945. He is widely regarded as one of the country's greatest leaders, and played a pivotal role in leading Australia during the Second World War.

name: Edmund Barton
homePlace: Glebe, Colony of New South Wales, British Empire
about: Edmund Barton was an Australian politician and judge best known as the first Prime Minister of Australia. He was also a founding member of the High Court, and had a lasting impact on the nation’s political and judicial systems.

name: Robert Menzies
about: The 12th Prime Minister of Australia, he served over 18 collective years, and is Australia's longest-serving prime minister.
